examples.en: I have a coupon, so the coffee is cheap.

examples.ko: 이 쿠폰은 이번 달까지 쓸 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can use this coupon until the end of this month.

explain: 가게나 앱에서 할인이나 선물을 받을 때 쓰는 표나 코드예요. '쿠폰을 쓰다'라고 말해요.
explain_en: A ticket or code that gives a discount or a free item at a shop or in an app. The usual verb is 쓰다 (to use).

examples.en: One cappuccino, please.
I drink a cappuccino in the morning.

explain: 에스프레소에 우유 거품을 올린 커피예요. 카페에서 주문할 때 자주 써요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 카페에서 주문할 때 '한 잔'을 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add 'han jan' (one cup) when ordering at a cafe.

phrases.en: A warm cappuccino is good on a cold day.
phrases.nuance_ko: '따뜻한'을 앞에 붙여 온도를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put 'ttatteuthan' in front to say the temperature.

phrases.en: I drink a cappuccino in the afternoon.
phrases.nuance_ko: '마시다'와 함께 쓰는 기본적인 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The basic phrase with 'drink'.

explain_en: Espresso topped with milk foam. You will often say it when ordering at a cafe.

examples.en: A cafe latte, please.
A cafe latte has a lot of milk in it.

explain: 에스프레소에 따뜻한 우유를 많이 넣은 커피예요. '라떼'라고 줄여서 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: Espresso with a lot of steamed milk. People often shorten it to 라떼.

examples.en: One cheesecake, please.
I had cheesecake for dessert.

explain: 치즈로 만든 케이크예요. 카페에서 디저트로 많이 시켜요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 케이크는 '한 조각'으로 세는 경우가 많아요.
phrases.nuance_en: Cake is often counted as 'han jogak' (one piece).

phrases.nuance_ko: 카페에서 주문할 때 '시키다'를 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: 'Sikida' is often used when ordering at a cafe.

phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 가게의 대표 메뉴를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe a shop's signature item.

explain_en: A cake made with cheese. It is a common dessert to order at a cafe.

examples.en: Yesterday I ate sushi with a friend.
This sushi place is very famous.

explain: 일본식 음식이에요. 한국어에서는 '초밥'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: A Japanese dish. In Korean it is also called 초밥.

examples.en: I get nervous before an exam.
Don't be too nervous.

explain: 마음이 불안하고 몸이 굳는 느낌이에요. 보통 '긴장하다', '긴장되다'로 써요.

phrases.en: to relax; to ease the tension
phrases.en_equiv: to relax; to ease the tension

explain_en: The feeling of being nervous and tense. It is usually used as 긴장하다 or 긴장되다.

examples.en: I eat cheese in the morning.
This pizza has a lot of cheese.

explain: 우유로 만든 음식이에요. 피자, 샌드위치 등에 많이 들어가요.

phrases.en: I put cheese in the sandwich.
phrases.nuance_ko: 요리나 음식에 넣을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when adding it to food.

phrases.nuance_ko: 음식 이름 앞에 '치즈'를 붙여서 종류를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put 'chijeu' before a food name to name the type.

phrases.en: I put a slice of cheese on the bread.
phrases.nuance_ko: 얇은 슬라이스 치즈는 '한 장'으로 세요.
phrases.nuance_en: Thin sliced cheese is counted as 'han jang'.

explain_en: A food made from milk. It goes into pizza, sandwiches, and more.

examples.en: My younger sibling is doing homework.
I'll do my homework after dinner.

explain: '숙제'에 '하다'가 붙은 말이에요. '숙제를 하다'라고 띄어 써도 같은 뜻이에요.

phrases.en: to assign homework; to hand in homework
phrases.en_equiv: to assign homework; to hand in homework

explain_en: 숙제 (homework) plus 하다. 숙제를 하다 with a space means the same thing.

examples.en: This food is incredibly good.
It's really cold today.

explain: '아주', '매우'보다 편한 말이에요. 친구와 말할 때 많이 쓰고, 공식적인 글에서는 잘 안 써요.

phrases.en: to be enormous; to be tremendous
phrases.en_equiv: to be enormous; to be tremendous

explain_en: A casual word for 'very', softer than 아주 or 매우. Common in speech with friends, but not in formal writing.

examples.en: Thank you very much for your help.
This task is extremely important.

explain: '아주'보다 격식 있는 말이에요. 인사말이나 글에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: A more formal way to say 'very'. It often appears in greetings and writing.

dis.h: formal very; for serious or impressive things

p.n: Both are formal; 대단히 sounds more weighty and respectful.

examples.en: Today is a special day.
There is a special discount during the holidays.

explain: 보통과 다르다는 뜻이에요. '특별한 날', '특별히'처럼 모양을 바꿔서 많이 써요.
explain_en: Means different from the usual. It is mostly used in forms like 특별한 날 or 특별히.

dis.h: special as in exceptional, out of ordinary

p.n: 특수한 날 sounds odd. 특별 means a day that stands out, while 특수 means a day of a specialized kind.

en: to be sultry; to be sweltering; to be stuffy

examples.en: The weather is sultry in the rainy season.
The room was stuffy, so I opened the window.

explain: 덥고 습해서 답답한 날씨나 방 안 느낌이에요. 장마철에 많이 써요.
explain_en: Describes hot, humid, stuffy air, in weather or in a room. Common in the rainy season.

en: to take a walk; to stroll

examples.en: I take a walk in the park in the evening.
I'll walk the dog this weekend.

explain: 운동이나 기분 전환으로 천천히 걷는 것이에요. 그냥 길을 가는 '걷다'와 달리 걷는 일 자체가 목적이에요.
explain_en: Walking slowly for exercise or relaxation. Unlike 걷다, the walk itself is the purpose.

examples.en: I lost my phone.
I take photos with my phone.

explain: 손에 들고 다니는 전화기예요. '휴대폰'과 같은 말이고, 둘 다 많이 써요.
explain_en: A phone you carry with you. It means the same as 휴대폰, and both are common.

examples.en: I had malatang for lunch today.
Malatang is a little spicy.

explain: 중국 쓰촨 지역에서 온 맵고 얼얼한 국물 요리예요. 원하는 재료를 골라서 넣어 먹어요.

phrases.en: I'm going to eat malatang with a friend on the weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: '마라탕'과 '먹으러 가다'를 붙여 식당에 갈 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Pairs the word with 'go to eat' for when you head out to a restaurant.

phrases.en: There is a malatang restaurant near the school.
phrases.nuance_ko: 마라탕을 파는 가게를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to talk about a restaurant that sells malatang.

phrases.en: My friend asks, "Do you want to eat malatang today?"
phrases.nuance_ko: 친한 친구에게 반말로 같이 먹자고 제안할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A casual way to invite a close friend to eat malatang.

explain_en: A spicy, numbing soup from China's Sichuan region. You pick your own ingredients to put in.

en: going and returning in one day; finishing on the same day

examples.en: I took a day trip to Busan on the weekend.
It's a bit far for a day trip.

explain: 하루 안에 갔다 오거나 끝내는 것이에요. 여행이나 일에 모두 쓰고, 보통 '당일치기 여행'으로 말해요.
explain_en: Doing something within a single day, such as a round trip or a task. Most often heard as 당일치기 여행 (day trip).

examples.en: I watch videos of daily life in Korea.
The trip ended and I went back to my daily life.

explain: 매일 반복되는 평범한 생활을 말해요. '일상생활', '일상적이다'처럼 이어서 많이 써요.
explain_en: Means ordinary life that repeats every day. It often appears in '일상생활' and '일상적이다'.

examples.en: I put on sunscreen before going out.

examples.ko: 바다에 갈 때 선크림이 꼭 필요해요.
examples.en: You really need sunscreen when you go to the beach.

explain: 햇빛에서 피부를 지키려고 바르는 크림이에요. '선크림을 바르다'라고 말해요.
explain_en: A cream you put on to protect your skin from the sun. The verb is '바르다' (to apply).

examples.en: I need motivation when I study.
Kind words became a big motivation for me.

explain: 무엇을 하고 싶은 마음이 생기게 하는 것이에요. '동기부여가 되다', '동기부여를 하다'로 써요.
explain_en: Something that makes you want to do something. Use '동기부여가 되다' (to be motivating) or '동기부여를 하다' (to motivate).

examples.en: I started preparing to get a job.
I want to get a job within this year.

explain: 일자리를 얻는 것이에요. '취업하다'로 동사처럼 쓰고, '취업 준비'처럼 앞에 붙여도 써요.

phrases.en: to succeed in getting a job
phrases.en_equiv: to succeed in getting a job

explain_en: Getting a job. It works as a verb with '하다' (취업하다) and as a prefix in phrases like '취업 준비'.

en: to be cozy; to be snug

examples.en: This cafe is small but cozy.
The room is cozy, so I want to stay a long time.

explain: 공간이 작고 편안하고 따뜻한 느낌일 때 써요. 주로 방, 카페, 집에 말해요.
explain_en: Used when a place feels small, comfortable and warm. Mostly said about rooms, cafes and homes.

examples.en: The situation is a little difficult right now.
I speak differently depending on the situation.

explain: 어떤 일이 되어 가는 모습이나 형편이에요. '상황이 좋다/나쁘다', '상황에 따라 다르다'로 많이 써요.
explain_en: The state of things at a certain moment. Common in '상황이 좋다/나쁘다' and '상황에 따라 다르다' (it depends on the situation).

examples.en: The director is in a meeting now.
I greeted the director.

explain: 학원, 병원 같은 곳의 가장 높은 사람을 높여 부르는 말이에요. 이름 대신 '원장님'이라고 불러요.
explain_en: A respectful title for the head of an academy, clinic or similar place. People call them '원장님' instead of using their name.

examples.en: I go to work at 9 in the morning.
I went to work early today.

explain: 일하려고 직장에 가는 것이에요. 장소 앞에는 '에'를 쓰고, 반대말은 '퇴근하다'예요.
explain_en: To go to your workplace to work. Use '에' with the place (회사에 출근하다). Its opposite is '퇴근하다' (to leave work).

examples.en: I like salmon.
I had a salmon salad for lunch.

explain: 분홍색 살을 가진 생선이에요. 회로도 먹고 구워서도 먹어요.
explain_en: A fish with pink flesh. People eat it raw as sashimi or cooked.

examples.en: I put bell pepper in the salad.
Red bell peppers are sweet.

explain: 색이 여러 가지인 달고 아삭한 채소예요. 맵지 않아서 샐러드나 볶음에 넣어요.

phrases.en: I bought a red bell pepper.
phrases.nuance_ko: 색 이름을 앞에 붙여서 어떤 파프리카인지 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put a color word in front to say which kind of bell pepper.

phrases.en: I slice the bell pepper to put in the salad.
phrases.nuance_ko: 요리할 때 재료를 준비하는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes preparing the ingredient when cooking.

phrases.nuance_ko: 파프리카의 식감을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe the crunchy texture of bell pepper.

explain_en: A sweet, crunchy vegetable that comes in many colors. It isn't spicy, so it goes into salads and stir-fries.

examples.en: Korean food uses a lot of garlic.
I chop the garlic finely.

explain: 한국 요리에 가장 많이 들어가는 양념 채소예요. 한 개는 '쪽'으로 세요.
explain_en: A seasoning vegetable used in a huge number of Korean dishes. One clove is counted with '쪽'.

examples.en: I put lemon in water and drink it.
I squeeze lemon over the fish.

explain: 노랗고 신 과일이에요. 차나 음료, 요리에 넣어요.
explain_en: A yellow, sour fruit. It goes into tea, drinks and cooking.

examples.en: I sprinkle salt and pepper on the meat.
Please add just a little pepper.

explain: 맵고 향이 강한 검은 가루 양념이에요. 보통 소금과 같이 써요. 고추와 달라요.
explain_en: A black, sharp-flavored spice, usually used with salt. Not the same as '고추' (chili pepper).

examples.en: I bake bread in the oven.
The oven is still hot.

explain: 음식을 안에 넣고 뜨겁게 굽는 기계예요. '오븐에 굽다'라고 말해요.
explain_en: A machine that heats food inside to bake or roast it. Say '오븐에 굽다' (to bake in the oven).

examples.en: I had grilled fish for dinner.
This restaurant's grilled ribs are delicious.

explain: 고기나 생선을 구운 음식이에요. 보통 재료 뒤에 붙여서 '생선구이', '연어구이'처럼 써요.
explain_en: A dish of grilled or roasted meat or fish. It usually follows the ingredient, as in '생선구이' or '연어구이'.

en: to grill; to roast; to bake

examples.en: I grill the meat in a frying pan.
I baked bread yesterday.

explain: 불이나 오븐에서 음식을 익히는 것이에요. 'ㅂ 불규칙'이라서 '구워요', '구웠어요'가 돼요.
explain_en: To cook food over fire or in an oven. It is a ㅂ-irregular verb: 구워요, 구웠어요.

examples.en: I drink protein after working out.
This snack has a lot of protein.

explain: 운동할 때 많이 챙기는 단백질을 말해요. '단백질'과 같은 뜻이지만 보충제나 음료를 말할 때 '프로틴'을 많이 써요.
explain_en: Protein, especially as people take it for exercise. It means the same as '단백질', but '프로틴' is common for supplements and drinks.

examples.en: I eat a chicken breast salad for dinner.
I boiled the chicken breast and ate it.

explain: 닭의 가슴 부분 고기예요. 지방이 적어서 운동하는 사람들이 많이 먹어요.

phrases.en: I grill chicken breast in a pan.
phrases.nuance_ko: 닭가슴살을 요리하는 방법 중 하나로 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common way to say how you cook chicken breast.

phrases.en: I eat a chicken breast lunch box after working out.
phrases.nuance_ko: 닭가슴살이 들어간 도시락을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a lunch box that has chicken breast in it.

phrases.en: I often cook chicken breast dishes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 닭가슴살로 만든 여러 음식을 한꺼번에 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for any dish made with chicken breast.

explain_en: Meat from the breast of a chicken. It is low in fat, so people who exercise eat it a lot.

examples.en: I think this method is good.
When I think of my family, I feel strong.

explain: 머릿속으로 어떤 것을 따져 보는 것이에요. 의견을 말할 때 '-다고 생각해요'로 많이 써요.
explain_en: To think about something in your mind. To give an opinion, use '-다고 생각해요' (I think that...).

examples.en: I exercised and lost a lot of weight.
I think you've lost weight lately.

explain: 몸무게가 줄었을 때 써요. 반대는 '살이 찌다'예요. '살을 빼다'는 내가 일부러 뺀다는 뜻이에요.
explain_en: Used when your body weight has gone down. The opposite is '살이 찌다'. '살을 빼다' means you lose weight on purpose.

examples.en: I looked around the market.
I'm going to see the sights of Seoul this weekend.

explain: 재미있는 것이나 처음 보는 것을 둘러보는 것이에요. '구경하러 가다', '구경 잘 했어요'처럼 써요.
explain_en: To look around at something interesting or new, like sightseeing or browsing. Used in '구경하러 가다' (to go and look around).

examples.en: I like seafood.
Tonight's dinner is seafood pasta.

explain: 바다에서 나는 먹을 것이에요. 생선, 새우, 조개 등을 모두 말해요.
explain_en: Food that comes from the sea, such as fish, shrimp and shellfish.

examples.en: I have a peanut allergy.

examples.ko: 알러지 때문에 이 음식을 못 먹어요.
examples.en: I can't eat this food because of an allergy.

explain: 몸이 어떤 음식이나 물질에 안 맞아서 아픈 것이에요. '알러지가 있다'라고 말하고, 표준 표기는 '알레르기'예요.
explain_en: A bad bodily reaction to a food or substance. Say '알러지가 있다' (to have an allergy). The standard spelling is '알레르기'.

examples.en: My friend is a vegetarian.
Do you have a menu for vegetarians?

explain: 고기를 먹지 않고 채소 중심으로 먹는 사람이에요. 식당에서 '저는 채식주의자예요'라고 말할 수 있어요.
explain_en: A person who doesn't eat meat and eats mainly plants. At a restaurant you can say '저는 채식주의자예요' (I'm a vegetarian).

examples.en: It's the same for me.
Korean needs practice just like English.

explain: 앞의 말과 같은 상황이라고 말할 때 써요. 보통 '~도 마찬가지예요' 모양으로 말해요.
explain_en: Use it to say the situation is the same as what was just mentioned. It usually appears as '~도 마찬가지예요'.

examples.en: The timing was really good.
I missed the moment to speak.

explain: 어떤 일을 하기에 알맞은 때를 말해요. '타이밍이 좋다/나쁘다'처럼 자주 써요.
explain_en: It means the right moment to do something. Often used as '타이밍이 좋다/나쁘다'.

en: to fit together; to adjust; to match

examples.en: I match my schedule with my friend's.
I set the alarm for six o'clock.

explain: 서로 어긋나지 않게 딱 맞게 해요. 시간, 알람, 퍼즐에 써요. '맞다(be right)'와 헷갈리지 마세요.
explain_en: To make things fit or line up with each other without a gap. Used for schedules, alarms and puzzles. Don't confuse it with 맞다 (to be right).

examples.en: I rented a surfboard.
Standing on a surfboard is hard.

explain: 파도를 탈 때 쓰는 판이에요. '서핑'과 '보드'가 합쳐진 낱말이에요.

phrases.en: I'm going to buy a surfboard this summer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서핑보드를 새로 장만할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when getting your own surfboard.

phrases.en: I carry my surfboard and go to the sea.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서핑보드를 손에 들고 이동하는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes carrying the board to the beach.

phrases.en: Riding waves on a surfboard is fun.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서핑보드를 쓰는 목적인 파도 타기를 함께 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Links the board to its purpose, riding waves.

explain_en: The board you ride on waves. It combines '서핑' (surfing) and '보드' (board).

examples.en: The apple pie is delicious.
I'm going to make a pie this weekend.

explain: 밀가루 반죽에 과일이나 고기를 넣어 구운 음식이에요. 사과파이, 호박파이처럼 써요.

phrases.en: I bake a pie in the oven.
phrases.nuance_ko: 파이를 직접 만들 때 '굽다'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 'bake' with pie when making it yourself.

phrases.en: Please give me a piece of pie.
phrases.nuance_ko: 파이를 잘라서 주문하거나 나눌 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when ordering or sharing a slice of pie.

phrases.en: I eat pumpkin pie in the fall.
phrases.nuance_ko: 재료 이름을 앞에 붙여 파이 종류를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put an ingredient before 'pie' to name the kind.

explain_en: A baked dish with a dough crust and a fruit or meat filling, as in 사과파이 (apple pie).

en: to party; to have a party

examples.en: I party together with my friends.
We had a party at home on my birthday.

explain: '파티'에 '하다'가 붙은 동사예요. '파티를 하다'라고도 말해요.
explain_en: A verb made from '파티' plus '하다'. You can also say '파티를 하다'.

examples.en: My friend is British.
A British teacher teaches English.

explain: 나라 이름 뒤에 '-인'을 붙이면 그 나라 사람이라는 뜻이에요. 영국인, 미국인, 중국인처럼 써요.

phrases.nuance_ko: '영국인'과 뜻이 같고 말할 때 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as '영국인' and more common in speech.

phrases.nuance_ko: '영국인' 뒤에 친구, 선생님 같은 사람 말을 붙여 어떤 사람인지 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add a word for a person, like friend or teacher, after '영국인' to say who they are.

phrases.nuance_ko: 국적이 영국이 아니라고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say someone's nationality is not British.

explain_en: Adding '-인' after a country name means a person from that country, as in 영국인, 미국인, 중국인.

examples.en: I'm very busy at the end of the month.
I'm going to travel at the end of the month.

explain: 한 달의 끝 무렵이에요. 반대말은 '월초'예요.
explain_en: The last part of a month. The opposite is '월초' (beginning of the month).

en: to sprinkle; to scatter; to spray; (of rain) to fall lightly

examples.en: I sprinkle cheese on the pizza.
I sprayed water on the flowers.

explain: 작은 것들을 여기저기 흩어지게 놓거나 던져요. 요리에서는 치즈나 소금을 위에 올릴 때 써요.
explain_en: To scatter small things around. In cooking it's used for sprinkling cheese or salt on top.

dis.h: rain that sprinkles or blows in spray

p.n: 내리다 just states that it rains; 뿌리다 describes the way the rain falls.

en: meat broth; stock (for soup or noodles)

examples.en: I boil the broth first.
I made stock with anchovies.

explain: 고기나 멸치, 채소를 끓여 낸 국물이에요. 국이나 국수의 바탕이 돼요.

phrases.en: I make broth with anchovies and kelp.
phrases.nuance_ko: 재료를 끓여서 국물을 만든다는 뜻으로 가장 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common phrase for making stock by boiling ingredients.

phrases.en: I put anchovy broth in the noodles.
phrases.nuance_ko: 재료 이름을 앞에 붙여 육수 종류를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put the ingredient before it to name the broth.

phrases.en: Please pour the broth into the pot.
phrases.nuance_ko: 완성된 육수를 냄비나 그릇에 넣을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when pouring finished broth into a pot or bowl.

explain_en: Broth made by boiling meat, anchovies or vegetables. It is the base for soups and noodle dishes.

examples.en: I store food in the fridge.
I saved the photo on my phone.

explain: 나중에 쓰려고 모아 두거나 보관해요. 음식, 파일, 사진에 모두 쓸 수 있어요.

phrases.en: Please keep this file saved on your computer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나중에 쓰려고 미리 보관해 둘 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you keep something saved for later use.

phrases.en: The photo was saved on my phone.
phrases.nuance_ko: '저장하다'의 피동형으로, 저장된 상태나 결과를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The passive form of '저장하다'; describes the state or result of being saved.

phrases.en: I did not save the file.
phrases.nuance_ko: 저장을 안 했다고 말하는 부정 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A negative form to say you did not save.

explain_en: To keep something for later use. It works for food, files and photos.

examples.en: I mix the eggs and flour.
Please mix the ingredients well.

explain: 둘 이상을 한데 합쳐서 어우러지게 해요. 요리할 때 자주 써요.
explain_en: To combine two or more things together. Very common when cooking.

examples.en: I make a seasoning sauce and put it on the tofu.
I dip it in the seasoning sauce and eat.

explain: 간장, 고춧가루, 마늘 등을 섞어 만든 소스예요. 음식에 넣거나 찍어 먹어요.

phrases.en: I make a soy sauce seasoning and mix it into rice.
phrases.nuance_ko: 간장을 바탕으로 만든 양념장을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A seasoning sauce made with soy sauce as the base.

phrases.en: I add the seasoning sauce to the noodles.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음식에 양념장을 더할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when adding the sauce to food.

phrases.en: I mix the rice with the seasoning sauce and eat it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 밥이나 국수와 양념장을 섞어 먹을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when mixing rice or noodles with the sauce.

explain_en: A sauce made by mixing soy sauce, chili powder, garlic and so on. It is added to food or used for dipping.

examples.en: Don't add too much seasoning.
I season the meat.

explain: 음식에 맛을 더하려고 넣는 재료예요. 소금, 후추, 마늘, 고춧가루 등이 있어요.
explain_en: Ingredients added to give food flavor, such as salt, pepper, garlic and chili powder.

examples.en: I go on a picnic to the park on weekends.
I had a picnic with friends at the Han River.

explain: 밖에 나가 음식을 먹으며 노는 일이에요. '피크닉을 가다', '피크닉을 하다'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: The weather is nice, so we are going on a picnic.
phrases.nuance_ko: '피크닉'과 비슷한 뜻이고, 학교나 가족 나들이에도 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 'picnic', and also used for school or family outings.

phrases.en: I prepared a picnic lunch box.
phrases.nuance_ko: 피크닉 때 가져가는 도시락을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The lunch box you take on a picnic.

phrases.en: Shall we go on a picnic together tomorrow?
phrases.nuance_ko: 존댓말로 같이 가자고 부드럽게 제안할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite way to suggest going together.
phrases.en_equiv: shall we go on a picnic?

explain_en: An outing where you eat and relax outdoors. Used as '피크닉을 가다' or '피크닉을 하다'.

examples.en: I drank a lot yesterday, so I have a hangover.
Soup is good for curing a hangover.

explain: 술을 마신 다음 날 머리가 아프고 속이 안 좋은 상태예요. '숙취가 있다', '숙취 해소'처럼 자주 써요.
explain_en: The headache and upset stomach you get the day after drinking. Common patterns are '숙취가 있다' and '숙취 해소' (hangover cure).

examples.en: I bought a triangular rice ball at the convenience store.
For lunch I had a rice ball and ramen.

explain: 편의점에서 파는 삼각형 모양 김밥이에요. 보통 간단한 식사로 먹어요.

phrases.en: I like the tuna rice ball the most.
phrases.nuance_ko: 안에 들어간 재료 이름을 앞에 붙여 맛을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put the filling in front to name the flavor.

phrases.en: I heat the rice ball in the microwave.
phrases.nuance_ko: 차가운 삼각김밥을 따뜻하게 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when warming up a cold rice ball.

phrases.nuance_ko: 가게에서 개수를 말하며 살 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when buying a certain number at a store.

explain_en: A triangle-shaped rice ball wrapped in seaweed, sold at convenience stores. People often eat it as a quick meal.

en: to become close; to get friendly

examples.en: I quickly became close with my new friend.
We will get closer next time.

explain: 처음엔 어색하던 사람과 가까워진다는 뜻이에요. '-와/과 친해지다'로 써요.

phrases.en: I want to get close (to you)
phrases.en_equiv: I want to get close (to you)

explain_en: To go from being strangers to being close with someone. Use it as '-와/과 친해지다' (become close with).

examples.en: I like mushrooms.
I put mushrooms in the stew.

explain: 요리에 많이 쓰는 재료예요. 표고버섯, 느타리버섯처럼 종류 이름 뒤에 붙여 써요.

phrases.en: I put shiitake mushrooms in the soup.
phrases.nuance_ko: 버섯 중에서 표고라는 종류를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Names one specific kind of mushroom, shiitake.

phrases.nuance_ko: 버섯 요리에서 가장 흔한 조리법이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A very common way to cook mushrooms.

phrases.en: I bought oyster mushrooms at the market.
phrases.nuance_ko: 종류 이름 뒤에 '버섯'을 붙인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A kind name followed by 'mushroom'.

explain_en: A common cooking ingredient. It follows the type name, as in 표고버섯 (shiitake) and 느타리버섯 (oyster mushroom).

examples.en: I ate a lot, so I'm full.
I'm too full to eat dessert.

explain: 많이 먹어서 더 먹기 힘든 상태예요. '배가 부르다'라고도 하고, '배불러요'처럼 한 단어로도 써요.
explain_en: You have eaten so much that you can't eat more. You can say '배가 부르다' or use it as one word, as in '배불러요'.

examples.en: This character is the cutest.
I bought a doll of my favorite character.

explain: 만화, 게임, 영화에 나오는 인물이나 동물이에요. 사람의 성격을 말할 때는 보통 '성격'을 써요.
explain_en: A figure in a cartoon, game, or movie. For a person's personality, Koreans usually say '성격' instead.

examples.en: I went to a restaurant a local recommended.
I want to travel like a local.

explain: 그 지역에 사는 사람이에요. 여행 이야기에서 '현지인 맛집'처럼 자주 써요.
explain_en: A person who lives in the place you are visiting. Often used in travel talk, like '현지인 맛집' (a place locals love).

en: to hang (be hanging); to cling to

examples.en: The child is hanging from the tree.
My younger sibling clings to Mom.

explain: 무엇에 붙어서 아래로 달려 있다는 뜻이에요. '나무에 매달리다'처럼 장소에 '-에'를 써요. 어떤 일이나 사람에게 계속 매달린다는 뜻도 있어요.
explain_en: To hang from something, using '-에' for what it hangs from. It can also mean clinging to a person or task.

dis.h: be hanging or cling on (intransitive)

p.n: 매달다 takes an object (hang something), but 매달리다 describes something already hanging.

examples.en: I checked in at the airport.
Admission procedures are done on the first floor.

explain: 어떤 일을 하려고 거치는 절차예요. '수속을 밟다', '입국 수속'처럼 공항이나 병원에서 많이 써요.
explain_en: The formal steps you go through to get something done. Common in '수속을 밟다' (go through the procedure) and '입국 수속' (immigration).

examples.en: The children are on the swings.
There is a swing in the park.

explain: 놀이터에서 앉아서 앞뒤로 흔들며 노는 기구예요. '그네를 타다'라고 말해요.
explain_en: A playground swing. The verb is '타다': '그네를 타다' (ride a swing).

examples.en: I got a restaurant recommendation from a friend.

examples.ko: 이게 추천을 제일 많이 받은 거예요.
examples.en: This is the one that got the most recommendations.

explain: 좋은 것을 다른 사람에게 알려 주는 일이에요. '추천을 받다', '추천하다'로 자주 써요.
explain_en: Telling someone about something good. Common as '추천을 받다' (get a recommendation) and '추천하다' (to recommend).

examples.en: It's raining, so it can't be helped.
I had no choice but to stay home.

explain: 다른 방법이 없다는 뜻이에요. 포기하거나 받아들일 때 '어쩔 수 없어요'라고 말해요.
explain_en: There is no other way, so you accept the situation. Say '어쩔 수 없어요' when you give in or accept something.

examples.en: I don't really have any allergies.

examples.ko: 오늘은 딱히 하고 싶은 게 없어요.
examples.en: There's nothing in particular I want to do today.

explain: 주로 뒤에 '없다, 아니다, 않다'가 와서 '특별히 그렇지는 않다'는 뜻이에요. 긍정문에는 잘 안 써요.
explain_en: Usually followed by a negative like '없다' or '않다', meaning 'not especially'. It is rarely used in positive sentences.

examples.en: Did you heat up lunch?
I warmed the milk and drank it.

explain: 식은 음식이나 물을 다시 따뜻하게 만든다는 뜻이에요. 전자레인지나 냄비로 해요. '데워지다'는 저절로 따뜻해진다는 뜻이에요.
explain_en: To make cold food or liquid warm again, in a microwave or pot. '데워지다' means it becomes warm on its own.

examples.en: I'll have cake for dessert.
The desserts at this restaurant are delicious.

explain: 식사 뒤에 먹는 단 음식이에요. 케이크, 아이스크림, 과일 등이 있어요.
explain_en: A sweet food eaten after a meal, such as cake, ice cream, or fruit.

en: to be sunny; to be bright

examples.en: The weather is sunny today.
We went on a picnic on a sunny day.

explain: 날씨가 맑고 따뜻하고 밝다는 뜻이에요. 주로 '날씨가 화창하다'로 써요.

phrases.nuance_ko: '화창하다'를 '-ㄴ' 형태로 바꿔 '날씨' 앞에 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: The '-ㄴ' form placed before 'weather'.

phrases.nuance_ko: 지난 날씨를 말할 때 과거형으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Past tense for talking about earlier weather.

phrases.en: The weather is not sunny today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 날씨가 맑지 않을 때 쓰는 부정 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A negative form for when the weather is not bright.

explain_en: Describes weather that is clear, warm, and bright. Mostly used as '날씨가 화창하다'.

examples.en: I made porridge with pumpkin.
I made a pumpkin-shaped pizza.

explain: 둥글고 노랗거나 초록색인 채소예요. 애호박, 단호박처럼 다른 낱말에도 들어가요.
explain_en: A round yellow or green vegetable. It appears in other words like 애호박 (zucchini) and 단호박 (sweet pumpkin).

examples.en: I made dough with flour.
You have to knead the dough for a long time.

explain: 밀가루에 물 등을 섞어 만든 덩어리예요. 빵, 피자, 수제비를 만들 때 써요. '반죽하다'는 동사예요.
explain_en: A lump of flour mixed with water, used for bread, pizza, and 수제비. The verb is '반죽하다' (to knead).

en: to put on; to place on top

examples.en: I put an egg on top of the rice.
I put a hat on my head.

explain: 무엇 위에 올려 놓는다는 뜻이에요. '-을/를 -에 얹다'로 써요. 요리에서 재료를 위에 올릴 때 많이 써요.
explain_en: To put something on top of something else, as in '-을/를 -에 얹다'. Often used for putting ingredients on top of a dish.

examples.en: I put olives on the pizza.
We make the eyes and mouth with olives.

explain: 작고 동그란 열매예요. 피자나 샐러드에 넣어요. 올리브 기름은 '올리브유'라고 해요.
explain_en: A small round fruit used on pizza and in salads. Olive oil is called '올리브유'.

examples.en: We used an oven at the academy.
I use this app every day.

explain: 무엇을 쓴다는 뜻이에요. '쓰다'보다 조금 격식 있는 말이에요. 대화에서는 '쓰다'를 더 자주 말해요.
explain_en: To use something. It is a bit more formal than '쓰다', which people say more often in conversation.

dis.h: general word for using tools or things

p.n: 이용하다 sounds like using a shared or public facility. 사용하다 is plain use of a thing.

en: to band together; to clump (lump together)

examples.en: The dough is clumped together.
If we all band together, we can do it.

explain: 여러 개가 한데 붙어 덩어리가 된다는 뜻이에요. 사람들이 힘을 모을 때도 써요. 근육이 뭉치다처럼 몸에도 써요.
explain_en: For separate things to stick together into a lump. It also means people joining forces, and muscles can '뭉치다' (knot up).

dis.h: casual: band together, or clump up

p.n: 뭉치다 is casual and warm; 단결하다 is formal solidarity.

examples.en: I cut the onion.
I put onion in the fried rice.

explain: 요리에 자주 쓰는 채소예요. 썰 때 눈이 매워서 눈물이 나요.
explain_en: A common cooking vegetable. Cutting it makes your eyes sting and water.

examples.en: I go to a pojangmacha after work.
I ate fish cake at a pojangmacha.

explain: 길가에서 천막을 치고 음식과 술을 파는 가게예요. 밤에 많이 가요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 포장마차에서 파는 음식을 한꺼번에 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the food sold at these tents in general.

phrases.en: Let's meet at the pojangmacha nearby.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가까운 곳에서 만나자고 약속할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when arranging to meet at a nearby place.

phrases.en: I ate tteokbokki at a pojangmacha.
phrases.nuance_ko: 포장마차에서 흔히 먹는 음식과 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Pairs the place with a food people often eat there.

explain_en: A tented street stall that sells food and drinks. People mostly go at night.

examples.en: I ordered a cocktail.
This cocktail is sweet.

explain: 술과 주스 등을 섞어 만든 음료예요. 보통 바에서 마셔요.

phrases.en: I want to have a cocktail.
phrases.nuance_ko: '한 잔'으로 마시는 양을 세어요.
phrases.nuance_en: 'Han jan' counts one glass of the drink.

phrases.en: I went to a cocktail bar on Friday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 칵테일을 파는 술집을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A bar that serves cocktails.

phrases.en: I drank a cocktail with a friend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 칵테일과 가장 자주 쓰는 동사 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common verb pairing for cocktail.

explain_en: A mixed drink made from liquor and juice or other ingredients. Usually ordered at a bar.

en: to hike; to climb a mountain

examples.en: I hike every weekend.
I hiked on Bukhansan with a friend.

explain: 산에 올라가는 것을 말해요. '산에 가다'보다 운동의 느낌이 강해요.
explain_en: It means going up a mountain. It sounds more like exercise than just 'going to a mountain'.

examples.en: Our group has five people.
I like that group's songs.

explain: 사람이나 물건의 모임이에요. 가수 팀이나 회사 묶음에도 써요.

phrases.en: We did a group activity in class today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 사람이 모여 같이 하는 활동을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: An activity done together by several people.

phrases.en: The teacher divided us into three groups.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람들을 여러 모임으로 나눌 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when splitting people into several groups.

phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 명이 함께 활동하는 가수 팀을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A singing team of several members.

explain_en: A set of people or things. Also used for music groups and company groups.

examples.en: This app is really useful.
Please tell me some useful information.

explain: 쓸모가 있어서 도움이 된다는 뜻이에요. 정보, 앱, 물건에 자주 써요.

phrases.en: The explanation I heard yesterday was really useful.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이미 쓸모 있었던 일을 말할 때 과거형으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Past tense for something that turned out useful.

phrases.en: This feature is not very useful.
phrases.nuance_ko: 쓸모가 적다고 말하는 부정 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A negative form to say something is not very useful.

phrases.en: I know a useful way to learn Korean.
phrases.nuance_ko: '유용한' 뒤에 명사를 붙여 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Place a noun after the '-ㄴ' form to describe it.

explain_en: It means something has a use and helps you. Often used for information, apps and tools.

en: to be beneficial; to be useful; to be helpful

examples.en: Yesterday's lecture was very beneficial.
Reading is a beneficial hobby.

explain: 배울 것이 있거나 몸과 마음에 좋다는 뜻이에요. '유용하다'는 쓸모, '유익하다'는 얻는 이로움에 가까워요.

phrases.en: Today was a very beneficial time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 배운 것이 많았던 시간을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for time in which you gained a lot.

phrases.en: This program is beneficial for children.
phrases.nuance_ko: 현재 이로움이 있다고 말하는 해요체예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Polite present form saying something is beneficial.

phrases.example: 밤에 늦게 먹는 것은 몸에 유익하지 않아요.
phrases.en: Eating late at night is not good for your body.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이로움이 없다고 말하는 부정 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A negative form saying something is not beneficial.

explain_en: It means something teaches you or is good for you. 유용하다 stresses usefulness; 유익하다 stresses the benefit you gain.

examples.en: I need help right now.
There's no need to worry.

explain: 꼭 있어야 하는 것을 말해요. 보통 '필요하다', '필요 없다'로 써요.
explain_en: Something that must be there. Usually used as 필요하다 or 필요 없다.

en: to shell; to peel by hand (egg, tangerine, nut)

examples.en: I peel a tangerine and eat it.
Please peel the boiled egg.

explain: 껍질을 손으로 벗기는 것이에요. 귤, 달걀, 밤에 써요. 사과는 '깎다'예요. 헷갈리지 마세요.
explain_en: It means removing a shell or peel by hand, like with tangerines, eggs and chestnuts. Apples are 깎다, so don't mix them up.

dis.h: peel off shell or skin by hand

p.n: You do not cut a tangerine's peel off with a knife, so 깎다 is not natural.

examples.en: I eat sundae, a Korean sausage.
I ordered tteokbokki and sundae, the Korean sausage.

explain: 돼지 창자에 당면, 채소, 피 등을 넣어 만든 음식이에요. 떡볶이와 같이 많이 먹어요.

phrases.en: One plate of sundae (Korean blood sausage), please.
phrases.nuance_ko: 접시 단위로 주문할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when ordering by the plate.

phrases.en: On cold days I eat sundae soup (blood sausage soup).
phrases.nuance_ko: 순대를 넣어 끓인 국이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A soup boiled with blood sausage in it.

phrases.en: I dip sundae (blood sausage) in salt and eat it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 순대를 먹는 흔한 방법이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common way of eating sundae.

explain_en: A Korean sausage made by stuffing pig intestine with noodles, vegetables and blood. Often eaten with tteokbokki.

examples.en: Do you like jokbal?
Let's have jokbal for dinner tonight.

explain: 돼지 발을 간장 양념에 오래 삶은 음식이에요. 보통 배달로 많이 시켜요.

phrases.en: There is a famous jokbal restaurant in our neighborhood.
phrases.nuance_ko: 족발을 파는 가게를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A restaurant that sells jokbal.

phrases.nuance_ko: 배달이나 식당에서 주문할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when ordering by delivery or at a restaurant.

phrases.nuance_ko: 접시 단위로 주문할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when ordering by the plate.

explain_en: Pig's feet simmered for a long time in soy sauce seasoning. Commonly ordered for delivery.

en: to look forward to; to be anticipated

examples.en: I'm looking forward to tomorrow's trip.
I'm really looking forward to the new movie.

explain: 앞으로 일어날 일이 좋을 것 같아서 마음이 설레는 것이에요. '○○이/가 기대돼요'로 말해요.
explain_en: You feel excited because something good is coming. Say '○○이/가 기대돼요'.

examples.en: It's before dinner, so I'm a bit hungry.
I'm a little hungry. Shall we eat ramyeon?

explain: 밥때가 아닌데 배가 조금 고픈 느낌이에요. 간단히 먹고 싶을 때 써요.

phrases.en: I'm a little hungry, so shall we eat something?
phrases.nuance_ko: '-ㄴ데'로 뒤에 제안이나 질문을 이어 갈 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The '-ㄴ데' ending leads into a suggestion or question.

phrases.en: I was a bit hungry, so I ate some bread.
phrases.nuance_ko: 배가 고파서 한 행동의 이유를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Gives the reason for something you did.

phrases.nuance_ko: 배가 고프지 않다는 부정 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A negative form saying you are not hungry.

explain_en: A slight hunger between meals. Used when you want a small snack.

examples.en: Light reflects off the window.
The glare from the sunlight is too strong.

explain: 빛이나 소리가 어떤 면에 부딪혀 되돌아오는 것이에요. '반사하다', '빛 반사'로 써요.
explain_en: Light or sound hitting a surface and bouncing back. Used as 반사하다 or 빛 반사.

examples.en: I made a monthly plan.
This magazine is monthly.

explain: 한 달에 한 번 나오거나 한 달 단위로 하는 것을 말해요. 잡지, 계획표 앞에 붙여요.
explain_en: Something that comes out or is done once a month. Put before words like magazine or schedule.

examples.en: We're moving to the meeting room.
We traveled by bus.

explain: 한 곳에서 다른 곳으로 옮겨 가는 것이에요. 사람, 물건 모두에 써요.
explain_en: To go from one place to another. Used for people and objects.

dis.h: travel to another place; formal, has destination

p.n: 움직이다 stresses the motion itself and sounds less formal than 이동하다.

en: to ostracize; to shut out; to shake off

examples.en: You shouldn't shut a friend out.
He left his rivals behind and came first.

explain: 사람을 무리에서 빼고 같이 안 놀아 주는 것이에요. 쫓아오는 사람을 멀리 떼어 놓을 때도 써요.

phrases.en: to be ostracized; to be left out
phrases.en_equiv: to be ostracized; to be left out

explain_en: To leave someone out of a group and not include them. Also means to shake off someone chasing you.

examples.en: My younger sibling plays pranks.
I'm just kidding, don't be mad.

explain: 재미로 하는 가벼운 행동이나 말이에요. '장난치다', '장난이다'로 자주 써요.

phrases.en: to be no joke; to be amazing
phrases.en_equiv: to be no joke; to be amazing

explain_en: A light action or remark done for fun. Often used as 장난치다 or 장난이다.

examples.en: I'm not a fool.
Silly, you should take an umbrella!

explain: 어리석거나 순진한 사람을 가리켜요. 친한 사이에서는 장난으로도 써요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이나 행동이 어리석게 보인다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a person or action seems foolish.

phrases.en: He is smiling like a fool.
phrases.nuance_ko: 장난스럽거나 순진하게 웃는 모습에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a playful or innocent-looking smile.

phrases.en: Sorry, it is a silly question.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자기 질문을 낮춰 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used to be modest about your own question.

explain_en: A foolish or naive person. Between close people it can be said jokingly.

examples.en: We hold the ancestral rite this evening.
We made food for the rite at Grandmother's house.

explain: 돌아가신 조상을 기리며 음식을 차려 지내는 의식이에요. '제사를 지내다'로 써요.

phrases.en: My mother sets up the ritual table.
phrases.nuance_ko: 제사 때 음식을 올리는 상이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The table on which food is placed for the rite.

phrases.en: Today is my grandfather's memorial day.
phrases.nuance_ko: 제사를 지내는 날을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The day the ancestral rite is held.

phrases.en: The family gathers and prepares for the ancestral rite.
phrases.nuance_ko: 제사 전에 음식을 만들고 정리하는 일이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The work of cooking and arranging before the rite.

explain_en: A ritual honoring deceased ancestors with a table of food. Used as 제사를 지내다.

examples.en: A new neighbor moved into the house across from us.
The dog from the house across the street is cute.

explain: 내 집 바로 앞쪽에 있는 집이에요. 옆에 있는 집은 '옆집'이라고 해요.
explain_en: The house directly in front of yours. A house beside yours is 옆집.

examples.en: A friend lives in the house behind mine.
The dog from the house behind barks often.

explain: '뒤'와 '집'이 합쳐진 말로, 내 집 바로 뒤에 있는 집을 가리켜요. 앞에 있는 집은 '앞집'이라고 해요.
explain_en: A compound of 뒤 (back) and 집 (house): the house right behind yours. The one in front is 앞집.

examples.en: I played games with a friend on the weekend.
I like playing games at night.

explain: '게임'에 '하다'가 붙은 동사예요. 컴퓨터나 휴대폰 게임을 할 때 써요. '게임을 하다'처럼 띄어 써도 돼요.
explain_en: A verb made of 게임 plus 하다, used for computer or phone games. You can also say 게임을 하다 with a space.

examples.en: If you exercise, you get stronger.
The wind gets stronger at night.

explain: '세다(힘이 강하다)'에 '-아/어지다'가 붙어 '더 강해지다'라는 뜻이에요. 시간이 지나면서 변할 때 써요.
explain_en: From 세다 (strong) plus -아/어지다, meaning to become stronger over time.

examples.en: It was a bit hard in the beginning.
The first part of this movie is fun.

explain: 어떤 일이나 기간의 처음 부분이에요. 반대말은 '후반'이고, 가운데는 '중반'이에요.
explain_en: The early part of an event or period. The opposite is 후반 (late stage), and the middle is 중반.

examples.en: Adjectives modify nouns.
Adverbs modify verbs.

explain: 한 말이 다른 말을 꾸며서 뜻을 더해 주는 것이에요. 문법에서 '형용사는 명사를 수식한다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: When one word describes or qualifies another. In grammar, adjectives modify nouns.

examples.en: The parts of speech are noun, verb, adjective and adverb.
What part of speech is this word?

explain: 단어를 문법적 성질에 따라 나눈 종류예요. 명사, 동사, 형용사, 부사 같은 것이 있어요.

phrases.en: I divide the words of a sentence by part of speech.
phrases.nuance_ko: 단어를 종류별로 가를 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when sorting words by their kind.

phrases.example: 이 문장에서 각 단어의 품사를 찾아 보세요.
phrases.en: Try finding the part of speech of each word in this sentence.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문장에서 각 단어의 종류를 알아낼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when working out each word's type in a sentence.

phrases.en: I studied parts of speech today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 품사를 배우는 공부를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to studying parts of speech.

explain_en: The grammatical category a word belongs to, such as noun, verb, adjective or adverb.

examples.en: My older brother went into the military.
I learned a lot in the military.

explain: 나라를 지키는 조직이에요. 한국에서는 '군대에 가다'가 병역 의무를 하러 간다는 뜻으로 많이 쓰여요.

phrases.en: to enlist; to go to the army
phrases.en_equiv: to enlist; to go to the army

explain_en: The armed forces. In Korea, 군대에 가다 commonly means going to do mandatory military service.

examples.en: I will give you one apple each.
Please come in one person at a time.

explain: '하나'에 '-씩'이 붙어 하나하나, 또는 각각 하나라는 뜻이에요. '둘씩', '셋씩'처럼 다른 수에도 써요.

phrases.en: two each; two at a time
phrases.en_equiv: two each; two at a time

explain_en: 하나 plus -씩, meaning one at a time or one each. It also works with other numbers, like 둘씩.

examples.en: My father reads books in the study.
There are two desks in the study.

explain: 집에서 책을 읽거나 일을 하는 방이에요. 여러 사람이 가는 '도서관'과 달라요.

phrases.en: I tidied my study on the weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 책과 물건을 깔끔하게 둘 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when putting books and things in order.

phrases.en: There are many books in our home study.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서재에 있는 것을 말하는 가장 흔한 문장이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A very common sentence about what is in a study.

phrases.en: I wish I had a small study.
phrases.nuance_ko: 크기를 나타내는 말을 앞에 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put a size word before it to describe the room.

explain_en: A room in a home for reading or working. It is different from a library (도서관).

examples.en: The washing machine is in the laundry room.
I do the laundry in the laundry room.

explain: 세탁기가 있어서 빨래를 하는 공간이에요. 집이나 건물 안에 있는 작은 방을 말해요.

phrases.en: I take the laundry and go to the laundry room.
phrases.nuance_ko: '세탁실' 뒤에 '에 가다'를 붙여 그 장소로 갈 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add '에 가다' to say you go to the laundry room.

phrases.en: Our apartment building has a shared laundry room.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 사람이 같이 쓰는 세탁실을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is a laundry room that many people share.

phrases.en: The laundry room door is open.
phrases.nuance_ko: 세탁실의 문을 말할 때 '세탁실'을 앞에 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put '세탁실' before a word to talk about a part of the room.

explain_en: A space with a washing machine where you do laundry, usually a small room in a home or building.

examples.en: My younger sibling goes to medical school.
It is hard to get into medical school.

explain: '의과 대학'을 줄인 말이에요. 의사가 되려는 사람이 다니는 대학이에요.
explain_en: Short for 의과 대학. It is the university school where people study to become doctors.

examples.en: I am studying psychology now.
The psychology class is interesting.

explain: 사람의 마음과 행동을 연구하는 학문이에요. 전공을 말할 때 '심리학을 공부하다'라고 해요.
explain_en: The study of the human mind and behavior. You say 심리학을 공부하다 when talking about your major.

examples.en: I hold the handle and turn it.
Please hold the handle tightly on the bus.

explain: 문이나 가방, 컵 등을 손으로 잡는 부분이에요. 버스나 지하철의 손잡이도 같은 말을 써요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 문을 열 때 잡는 손잡이를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the handle you hold to open a door.

phrases.nuance_ko: 가방을 들 때 잡는 부분이에요. 앞에 물건 이름을 붙이면 어떤 손잡이인지 알 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Putting an object's name before the word tells which handle you mean.

phrases.en: I pull the handle to open the door.
phrases.nuance_ko: '잡고 돌리다' 말고 손잡이를 내 쪽으로 끌 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this when you pull the handle toward you, not turn it.

explain_en: The part of a door, bag, cup and so on that you hold. The grab handle on a bus or subway is also 손잡이.

examples.en: I pull the door open.

examples.ko: 줄을 뒤로 당겼다가 놓으면 앞으로 가요.
examples.en: If you pull the string back and let go, it moves forward.

explain: 물건을 내 쪽으로 끌어오는 것이에요. 반대말은 '밀다'예요. 문에 '당기시오'라고 쓰여 있으면 끌어서 열어요.
explain_en: To draw something toward yourself. The opposite is 밀다 (to push). A door marked 당기시오 means pull.

en: to turn off a light; to put out a fire

examples.en: I turn off the light before I sleep.
The firefighter put out the fire.

explain: 전등을 끌 때도, 타는 불을 끌 때도 같이 써요. 반대말은 '불을 켜다'예요.
explain_en: Used both for turning off a light and for putting out a fire. The opposite is 불을 켜다.

examples.en: I draw a square on the paper.
This box is square.

explain: 모서리가 네 개인 모양이에요. 쉬운 말로 사각형을 '네모'라고 해요.
explain_en: A shape with four corners. It is the everyday word for 사각형.

examples.en: I drew a triangle on the board.
There is a triangle-shaped snack.

explain: 모서리가 세 개인 모양이에요. 쉬운 말로 삼각형을 '세모'라고 해요.
explain_en: A shape with three corners. It is the everyday word for 삼각형.

examples.en: I need ten pencils.
I bought a sack of rice.

explain: 연필, 볼펜처럼 긴 물건을 셀 때 '한 자루, 두 자루'라고 써요. 큰 주머니(포대)라는 뜻도 있어요.
explain_en: Use it to count pencils, pens and other long objects: 한 자루, 두 자루. It also means a sack.

examples.en: We do a quiz at the end of class.
I prepared a quiz.

explain: 짧게 보는 문제나 맞히기 놀이를 말해요. '퀴즈를 내다', '퀴즈를 풀다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: A short set of questions or a guessing game. Say 퀴즈를 내다 (to give a quiz) and 퀴즈를 풀다 (to solve a quiz).

en: watch someone's reaction; read the mood

examples.en: I watch my boss's mood.
The child is watching Mom's reaction.

explain: 다른 사람의 기분이나 반응을 살피는 것이에요. 보통 조심스럽거나 불편한 마음이 들어 있어요.

phrases.en: to be quick to read the situation
phrases.en_equiv: to be quick to read the situation

explain_en: To watch other people's mood or reaction, usually because you feel careful or uneasy.

dis.h: be wary of someone's mood

p.n: 살피다 is a more careful, deliberate check of the mood.

en: to feel awkward about others' eyes

examples.en: I feel awkward leaving work early.
I feel awkward resting by myself.

explain: 다른 사람의 시선 때문에 마음이 불편하다는 뜻이에요. '눈치 보다'는 내가 살피는 것이고, '눈치 보이다'는 저절로 신경 쓰이는 것이에요.

phrases.en: I feel awkward when I come late.
phrases.nuance_ko: '눈치 보이다'에 조사 '가'를 넣은 말이에요. 뜻은 같고 더 자주 들어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning with the particle '가' added; very common in speech.

phrases.example: 눈치 보여서 먼저 집에 못 가요.
phrases.en: I feel awkward, so I can't go home first.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이유를 말할 때 써요. 뒤에 하지 못하는 일이 자주 와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this to give a reason; what you can't do usually follows.

phrases.en: Here I don't feel awkward even when I rest.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반대로 마음이 편하고 신경 쓰이지 않을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite: you feel comfortable and don't worry about others.

explain_en: To feel uncomfortable because of how others might see you. 눈치 보다 is you actively watching; 눈치 보이다 is the feeling that arises on its own.

examples.en: I do Pilates on weekends.
I signed up for a Pilates class.

explain: 몸의 중심 근육을 키우는 운동이에요. '필라테스를 하다'라고 써요.

phrases.en: I am learning Pilates these days.
phrases.nuance_ko: '하다'보다 처음 배우는 중일 때 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: More fitting than '하다' when you are still learning.

phrases.en: There is a Pilates studio near my house.
phrases.nuance_ko: 필라테스를 가르치는 곳을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is a place that teaches Pilates.

phrases.en: I will start Pilates next month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 운동을 처음 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this when you begin the exercise.

explain_en: An exercise that builds core strength. Say 필라테스를 하다.

examples.en: That's a good choice.
The choice is too hard.

explain: 여러 개 중에서 하나를 고르는 것이에요. '선택하다'로도 많이 써요.
explain_en: Picking one from several options. Often used as 선택하다 (to choose).

en: to have an affair; to cheat

examples.en: My boyfriend cheated on me.
I don't like people who cheat.

explain: 연인이나 부부 사이에 다른 사람을 몰래 만나는 것이에요. 붙여 쓰고, '바람을 피우다'로 띄워 써도 돼요.
explain_en: To secretly see someone else while in a relationship or marriage. Written as one word, or as 바람을 피우다.

examples.en: The teacher is in the teachers' office.
I went to the teachers' office to hand in homework.

explain: 학교에서 선생님들이 일하는 방이에요. 학생은 '교무실에 가다'처럼 말해요.

phrases.en: I wait for my friend in front of the teachers' office.
phrases.nuance_ko: 교무실 가까운 곳을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this for the place near the teachers' office.
phrases.en_equiv: in front of the teachers' office

phrases.en: I met my teacher in the teachers' office.
phrases.nuance_ko: 교무실 안에서 한 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this for something that happened inside the office.

phrases.en: Please come to the teachers' office tomorrow morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 선생님이 학생에게 오라고 할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A teacher often says this to ask a student to come.
phrases.en_equiv: please come to the teachers' office

explain_en: The room where teachers work at a school. Students say 교무실에 가다.

examples.en: Exam season feels like hell.
The commute is hell.

explain: 나쁜 사람이 죽은 뒤에 간다는 곳이에요. 아주 힘든 상황을 말할 때도 써요.
explain_en: The place where bad people are said to go after death. Also used for a terribly hard situation.

examples.en: We should respect each other.
Please respect my opinion too.

explain: 다른 사람의 생각이나 사람 자체를 소중하게 대하는 것이에요. '존중하다', '존중을 받다'로 써요.
explain_en: Treating another person or their opinion as valuable. Used as 존중하다 and 존중을 받다.

en: broth; the liquid part of soup or stew

examples.en: The broth is delicious at this restaurant.
I drank even all the broth.

explain: 국이나 찌개에서 건더기를 뺀 물이에요. '국물이 시원하다', '국물이 진하다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: The liquid in soup or stew, apart from the solid ingredients. Say 국물이 시원하다 or 국물이 진하다.

examples.en: Please add more kimchi.
Is there an extra charge?

explain: 이미 있는 것에 더하는 것이에요. 식당에서 '추가해 주세요'라고 자주 말해요.
explain_en: Something added to what already exists. At restaurants you often say 추가해 주세요.

examples.en: The student walks with a bag on their shoulder.
I traveled with a backpack on.

explain: 가방이나 짐을 어깨에 걸치는 것이에요. '가방을 메다'로 써요. 손에 들면 '들다'예요.

phrases.en: to carry a bag on the shoulder
phrases.en_equiv: to carry a bag on the shoulder

explain_en: To carry a bag or load over the shoulder: 가방을 메다. If you hold it in your hand, use 들다.

examples.en: I ate rice noodles for lunch.
Rice noodle soup has a warm broth.

explain: 쌀로 만든 국수예요. 베트남 음식인 쌀국수 국물 요리를 가리킬 때가 많아요.

phrases.en: One bowl of rice noodles, please.
phrases.nuance_ko: 식당에서 주문할 때 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Very common when ordering at a restaurant.

phrases.nuance_ko: 국물이 있는 베트남식 쌀국수를 분명하게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this to clearly mean the Vietnamese noodle soup.

phrases.en: There is a rice noodle shop nearby.
phrases.nuance_ko: 쌀국수를 파는 가게를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is a shop that sells rice noodles.

explain_en: Noodles made from rice. It often refers to the Vietnamese noodle soup.

examples.en: Stars shine in the night sky.
A smiling face shines.

explain: 빛이 나서 환하게 보이는 것이에요. 사람이나 재능이 훌륭하게 보일 때도 써요.
explain_en: To give off light and look bright. Also used when a person or talent stands out.

examples.en: The night view of Seoul is really pretty.
I watched the night view from the mountain.

explain: 밤에 보이는 도시의 모습이에요. '야경이 예쁘다', '야경을 보다'로 써요.
explain_en: The view of a city at night. Say 야경이 예쁘다 or 야경을 보다.

en: to announce; to present; to make public (results, a work)

examples.en: I'm presenting in class tomorrow.
They announced the exam results.

explain: 여러 사람 앞에서 생각이나 결과를 말하거나 알리는 것이에요. 수업 발표도, 결과 발표도 모두 써요.
explain_en: To tell people your ideas or results in front of others. Used for class presentations and for announcing results.

examples.en: I ate dakgalbi.

examples.ko: 닭갈비를 먹고 남은 양념에 밥을 볶아 먹어요.
examples.en: After eating dakgalbi, we stir-fry rice in the leftover sauce.

explain: 닭고기를 매운 양념에 채소와 함께 볶은 음식이에요. '닭'은 chicken, '갈비'는 rib이에요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 식당에서 사람 수에 맞춰 주문할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this to order by the number of people at a restaurant.

phrases.nuance_ko: 춘천은 닭갈비로 유명한 도시예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Chuncheon is a city famous for dakgalbi.

phrases.en: I went to a dakgalbi restaurant with my friend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 닭갈비를 파는 식당을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is a restaurant that sells dakgalbi.

explain_en: Chicken stir-fried with vegetables in spicy sauce. 닭 means chicken and 갈비 means rib.

examples.en: I'm traveling tomorrow, so I have to pack.
I arrived at the hotel and unpacked.

explain: 여행이나 이사 전에 물건을 가방이나 상자에 넣는 것이에요. 반대로 풀 때는 '짐을 풀다'라고 해요.
explain_en: To put things in bags or boxes before a trip or move. The opposite is 짐을 풀다 (to unpack).

en: to pick; to pluck; to get (a certificate, a score)

examples.en: Grandmother picks apples in the field.
I want to get a driver's license.

explain: 열매나 꽃을 가지에서 떼어 낼 때 써요. 시험에서 점수를 얻거나 자격증을 얻을 때도 '따다'를 써요.
explain_en: Used for picking fruit or flowers off a plant. It is also used for earning a score or a certificate.

en: to be abundant; to be plentiful; to be ample

examples.en: The Chuseok table is very abundant.
Fruit is plentiful in autumn.

explain: 음식이나 물건이 넉넉하고 많을 때 써요. '풍성한 한가위'처럼 명절 인사에도 자주 써요. 관형형은 '풍성한'이에요.
explain_en: Used when food or things are plentiful and generous. It often appears in holiday greetings such as '풍성한 한가위'.

examples.en: I share photos with my friend.
This file can't be shared.

explain: 파일, 정보, 위치 등을 다른 사람과 함께 쓰는 것을 말해요. 동사는 '공유하다'예요.
explain_en: Means using files, information or a location together with others. The verb form is '공유하다'.

en: go for it!; you can do it! (cheer)

examples.en: Good luck on tomorrow's exam!
Go, our team!

explain: 누군가를 응원하거나 힘을 줄 때 외치는 말이에요. 시험, 경기, 일을 앞둔 사람에게 써요. 영어 fighting과 뜻이 조금 달라요.

phrases.en: Cheer up, you can do it!
phrases.en_equiv: Cheer up, you can do it!

explain_en: A shout used to cheer someone on before an exam, a game or a task. Its meaning is a bit different from English 'fighting'.

examples.en: I eat jajangmyeon for lunch.
One jajangmyeon, please.

explain: 검은 춘장 소스를 올린 국수예요. '자장면'도 표준어예요. 식당에서 '짜장면 하나 주세요'라고 주문해요.
explain_en: Noodles topped with a black bean sauce. '자장면' is also an accepted standard spelling. You order it with '짜장면 하나 주세요'.

examples.en: I saw a lion at the zoo.
Lions are very strong.

explain: 동물원에서 볼 수 있는 큰 동물이에요. 갈기가 있고 '동물의 왕'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: There is one lion at the zoo.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동물은 '마리'로 세요.
phrases.nuance_en: Animals are counted with '마리'.

phrases.en: There is a big lion over there.
phrases.nuance_ko: '큰'을 앞에 붙여 사자의 크기를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put '큰' before the word to describe its size.

phrases.en: The lion is sleeping under the tree.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사자가 하는 일을 말하는 간단한 문장이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A simple sentence about what the lion does.

explain_en: A big animal you can see at the zoo. It has a mane and is called the 'king of animals'.

examples.en: I swim at the pool on weekends.
It's cold, so I can't swim.

explain: 물에서 헤엄칠 때 써요. '수영을 하다'처럼 띄어 쓸 수도 있어요. 장소는 '에서'와 함께 써요.
explain_en: Used for swimming in water. You can also say '수영을 하다'. The place is marked with '에서'.

examples.en: I go to a jjimjilbang with my family on weekends.
I ate eggs at the jjimjilbang.

explain: 뜨거운 방에서 땀을 내고 쉬는 한국식 목욕 시설이에요. 친구나 가족과 같이 가서 먹고 쉬기도 해요.
explain_en: A Korean bathhouse with hot rooms for sweating and resting. People go with friends or family to eat and relax too.

en: to be pleasantly salty; to be savory

examples.ko: 이 반찬은 짭짤해서 밥이랑 잘 어울려요.
examples.en: This side dish is salty and goes well with rice.
The Spam is salty.

explain: 음식이 알맞게 짜서 맛있을 때 써요. 너무 짤 때는 '짜다'를 써요. 관형형은 '짭짤한'이에요.
explain_en: Used when food is pleasantly salty and tasty. If it is too salty, use '짜다' instead.

examples.en: I play the piano.
I perform at the concert hall tonight.

explain: 악기로 음악을 들려줄 때 써요. '피아노를 연주하다'처럼 '을/를'과 함께 써요. 운동이나 게임에는 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: Used for playing music on an instrument, as in '피아노를 연주하다'. It is not used for sports or games.

en: to experiment; to conduct an experiment

examples.en: We experiment with water in science class.
I tried out a new recipe.

explain: 무언가를 알아보려고 직접 해 볼 때 써요. 과학 수업뿐 아니라 새 방법을 시험해 볼 때도 써요.
explain_en: Used when you try something out to find an answer. It fits science class and also trying a new method.

examples.en: I eat roasted sweet potatoes in winter.
I bought sweet potatoes at the mart.

explain: 달고 부드러운 뿌리 채소예요. 구워 먹거나 쪄서 먹어요. 겨울 간식으로 인기가 많아요.
explain_en: A sweet, soft root vegetable. It is roasted or steamed and is a popular winter snack.

en: to be annoyed; to get irritated

examples.en: I'm annoyed because of the traffic.
I got irritated because there was so much homework.

explain: 일이 마음에 안 들어서 기분이 나쁠 때 써요. '짜증(이) 나다'로 띄어 쓰기도 해요. 사람에게 쓰면 강하게 들릴 수 있어요.
explain_en: Used when something bothers you and puts you in a bad mood. It can also be written '짜증(이) 나다'. Said about a person, it can sound harsh.

examples.en: I've been stressed lately, so I'm getting counseling.
There is a counseling center at school.

explain: 마음의 고민을 전문가와 이야기하는 것을 말해요. '심리상담을 받다'로 자주 써요.
explain_en: Talking through worries with a professional. It is commonly used as '심리상담을 받다'.

examples.en: I watched a parade at the theme park.
There is a big parade during the festival.

explain: 사람들이 줄지어 거리를 행진하는 행사예요. 놀이공원이나 축제에서 자주 볼 수 있어요.

phrases.nuance_ko: '보다'보다 재미있게 구경할 때 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Fits better than '보다' when you watch for fun.

phrases.nuance_ko: 행사가 시작될 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this when the event begins.

phrases.en: They hold a parade in the evening.
phrases.nuance_ko: 행사를 하는 쪽에서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this from the side of those holding the event.

explain_en: An event where people march in a line along a street. You often see them at theme parks and festivals.

examples.en: I go camping with my family on weekends.
I want to camp in the mountains.

explain: 텐트를 치고 밖에서 자며 즐기는 여행이에요. '캠핑을 가다', '캠핑하다'로 써요.
explain_en: A trip where you set up a tent and stay outdoors. Use it as '캠핑을 가다' or '캠핑하다'.

en: to be gentle; to be mild

examples.en: This cream is gentle on the skin.
My dog has a very gentle nature.

explain: 맛, 화장품, 사람의 성격이 자극적이지 않고 부드러울 때 써요. '순한 맛'처럼 '순한'으로도 자주 써요.
explain_en: Used for food, skincare, or a person's nature that is not harsh or irritating. It often appears as 순한, as in 순한 맛 (mild flavor).

examples.en: I wipe my face gently.
Please hold the baby gently.

explain: 힘을 약하게 주고 조심스럽게 할 때 써요. 닦다, 만지다, 걷다 같은 동작과 자주 같이 써요.
explain_en: Used when doing something with little force and with care. It often goes with actions like wiping, touching, or walking.

examples.en: My friend wrote a letter by hand.
My handwriting is pretty.

explain: 컴퓨터로 치지 않고 손으로 쓴 글씨예요. '글씨'만 쓰면 쓴 모양을 말하고, '손글씨'는 손으로 썼다는 점을 강조해요.
explain_en: Writing done by hand rather than typed. 글씨 alone means the look of writing, while 손글씨 stresses that it is handwritten.

examples.en: Stars twinkle in the night sky.
I cleaned the floor, so it's shiny.

explain: 별, 눈, 보석처럼 작은 빛이 계속 나타났다 사라질 때 써요. 깨끗하게 닦아서 윤이 나는 모습에도 써요.
explain_en: Describes small lights that keep flickering, like stars, eyes, or jewels. It also describes something that shines because it is clean.

examples.en: Lightning flashed in the sky.
The student raised a hand quickly.

explain: 큰 빛이 갑자기 나타날 때 써요. 또 손이나 물건을 갑자기 높이 들 때도 '번쩍 들다'라고 해요.
explain_en: Used for a bright light that appears suddenly. It also describes lifting a hand or object up quickly, as in 번쩍 들다.

en: to work out at a gym

examples.en: I work out at the gym every weekend.
I worked out at the gym yesterday evening.

explain: 헬스장에서 운동기구로 운동할 때 써요. 달리기나 요가에는 쓰지 않아요.

phrases.en: to go to the gym regularly
phrases.en_equiv: to go to the gym regularly

explain_en: Used for working out with equipment at a gym. It is not used for running or yoga.

examples.en: I add sesame oil to bibimbap.
The sesame oil smells nutty.

explain: 참깨로 만든 기름이에요. 비빔밥이나 나물에 넣어요. 냄새와 맛이 '고소하다'고 말해요.
explain_en: Oil made from sesame seeds, added to dishes like bibimbap and seasoned vegetables. Its taste and smell are described as 고소하다 (nutty).

examples.en: The baby looks like an angel when sleeping.
Our teacher is an angel.

explain: 하늘에 사는 착한 존재예요. 아주 착하고 친절한 사람을 '천사 같아요'라고 칭찬할 때도 써요.

phrases.en: That child smiles like an angel.
phrases.nuance_ko: 모습이나 행동이 천사와 같다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this to say someone looks or acts like an angel.

phrases.en: My mom is an angelic person.
phrases.nuance_ko: '천사 같아요'를 사람 앞에 붙이는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This puts '천사 같다' before a noun.

phrases.example: 그림 속 천사의 날개는 하얗고 커요.
phrases.en: The angel's wings in the picture are white and big.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그림이나 이야기 속 천사를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this for angels in pictures or stories.

explain_en: A kind being from heaven. You can also praise a very kind person by saying they are like an angel (천사 같아요).

examples.en: Let's split the bill today.
We paid by splitting the bill with friends.

explain: 밥값을 각자 나눠서 내는 것이에요. 보통 '더치페이하다'로 써요.
explain_en: Each person paying their own share of a meal. It is usually used as the verb 더치페이하다.

en: to be pricked; to feel guilty

examples.en: My finger was pricked by a thorn.
I feel guilty because I lied.

explain: 뾰족한 것에 찔릴 때 써요. '양심이 찔리다'처럼 잘못한 일 때문에 마음이 불편할 때도 써요. 대화에서는 '찔려요'라고 자주 말해요.

phrases.en: to feel a pang of conscience
phrases.en_equiv: to feel a pang of conscience

explain_en: Used when something sharp pricks you. It also means feeling guilty about something you did wrong, as in 양심이 찔리다. In conversation, 찔려요 is common.

examples.en: I lost my wallet. I'm in big trouble!
Marriage is a major event in life.

explain: '큰일 났다'는 문제가 생겨서 걱정될 때 해요. '큰일을 하다'처럼 중요한 일이라는 뜻도 있어요. 붙여 써요.
explain_en: 큰일 났다 means something bad has happened and you are worried. It can also mean an important task, as in 큰일을 하다. It is written without a space.

examples.en: An iced latte, please.
I drink iced coffee even in winter.

explain: 카페에서 차가운 음료를 주문할 때 써요. 뜨거운 음료는 '따뜻한' 또는 '핫'이라고 해요.
explain_en: Used when ordering a cold drink at a cafe. A hot drink is 따뜻한 or 핫.

examples.en: The children play wearing masks.
I wore a mask at the party.

explain: 얼굴을 가리려고 쓰는 물건이에요. '가면을 쓰다'로 써요. 위생용 마스크는 '마스크'라고 해요.
explain_en: An item worn to cover the face, used as 가면을 쓰다. A hygiene mask is called 마스크 instead.

en: to sink; to subside; to settle down

examples.en: The ship sank into the sea.
The swelling went down after I took medicine.

explain: 물 아래로 내려갈 때 써요. 또 붓기, 흥분, 분위기가 줄어들거나 차분해질 때도 써요.
explain_en: Used for going down under water. It also means swelling, excitement, or a mood calming down.

en: to be pierced; to be cleared

examples.en: A hole was made in the wall.
My nose cleared up after I took medicine.

explain: 구멍이 생길 때 써요. 막혔던 것이 풀릴 때도 써요. 예를 들어 막힌 길이나 코가 시원하게 열릴 때 말해요.
explain_en: Used when a hole is made. It also means something that was blocked becomes clear, such as a road or a stuffy nose.

en: owner (esp. of a lost or found item); the right person or match

examples.en: This umbrella has no owner.
You've finally met your match.

explain: 물건의 주인을 말해요. '임자 없는 물건'처럼 자주 써요. '임자를 만나다'는 어울리는 사람이나 상대를 만났다는 뜻이에요.
explain_en: Means the owner of an item. 임자를 만나다 means meeting the right person or a worthy match. It often appears in phrases about ownerless items.

en: to pay; to make a payment

examples.en: I'll pay by card.
I paid right away in the app.

explain: 카드나 앱으로 돈을 낼 때 써요. '카드로 결제하다'처럼 방법을 같이 말해요.
explain_en: Used when paying by card or app. The payment method is usually stated, as in 카드로 결제하다.

dis.h: settle payment, esp. card or accounts

p.n: 결제하다 means completing the payment transaction; 지불하다 stresses handing over the money.

examples.en: Small habits change your life.
We can change the world.

explain: 무엇을 다르게 만들 때 써요. '변하다'는 저절로 달라지는 것이고, '변화시키다'는 누가 일부러 바꾸는 거예요.

phrases.en: I changed the mood of the room.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻이 비슷하지만 더 쉽고 일상에서 많이 써요. '변화시키다'는 조금 더 큰 일에 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar meaning but simpler and more everyday; '변화시키다' suits bigger changes.

phrases.en: I changed my hairstyle a little.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조금 다르게 만들 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used for making a small difference.

phrases.nuance_ko: 이미 바꾼 일을 말하는 과거형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The past form for something already changed.

explain_en: Used when someone makes something different on purpose. 변하다 changes by itself, while 변화시키다 needs someone doing the changing.

dis.h: cause a deep change in something

p.n: 바꾸다 is plainer; 변화시키다 stresses causing a deep, lasting change.

examples.en: Your pronunciation is perfect.
I made a perfect plan.

explain: 부족하거나 틀린 곳이 없을 때 써요. 사람, 발음, 계획 모두에 쓸 수 있어요. '완벽한'으로 명사를 꾸며요.
explain_en: Used when nothing is lacking or wrong. It works for people, pronunciation, or plans, and 완벽한 modifies a noun.

examples.en: I'm doing an internship at a company this summer.
The internship experience was helpful.

explain: 학생이 회사에서 일을 배우는 경험이에요. '인턴십을 하다', '인턴십에 지원하다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: Work experience where a student learns at a company. Used as 인턴십을 하다 or 인턴십에 지원하다.

examples.en: I'm stressed because of the exam.
I was stressed because I had a lot of work.

explain: 힘들거나 걱정돼서 마음이 불편할 때 써요. 원인 뒤에 '때문에'나 '-아/어서'를 써요. '스트레스를 받다'라고도 해요.
explain_en: Used when you feel pressured or worried. Put the cause before 때문에 or -아/어서. You can also say 스트레스를 받다.

en: come on; go for it; cheer up

examples.en: Good luck on tomorrow's exam!
Go team!

explain: 응원하거나 힘을 줄 때 외쳐요. 시험, 운동 경기, 일을 앞둔 사람에게 말해요. 바른 표기는 '파이팅'이고, '화이팅'도 많이 써요.

phrases.en: Cheer up, you can do it!
phrases.en_equiv: Cheer up, you can do it!

explain_en: Shouted to cheer someone on, such as before an exam, a match, or a task. The standard spelling is 파이팅, but 화이팅 is also common.

examples.en: This is the so-called popular menu.
The so-called expert was wrong.

explain: 사람들이 흔히 그렇게 부르는 것을 말할 때 써요. 보통 '소위 말하는', '소위 ~라는'으로 써요.
explain_en: Used for something people commonly call by a certain name. It usually appears as 소위 말하는 or 소위 ~라는.

en: hotteok; Korean pancake with sweet fillings

examples.en: In winter, I want to eat hotteok.
The hotteok is hot, so be careful.

explain: 기름에 구운 둥근 반죽 안에 설탕과 견과류를 넣은 간식이에요. 겨울에 길거리에서 많이 팔아요.
explain_en: A round pancake fried in oil with a sweet sugar and nut filling. It is a popular street snack in winter.

examples.ko: 이 웹사이트에서 표를 살 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can buy tickets on this website.
Please tell me the school's website.

explain: 인터넷 주소로 들어가서 보는 페이지 모음이에요. 줄여서 '사이트'라고도 해요.
explain_en: A set of pages you visit through an internet address. It is often shortened to '사이트'.

en: to jot down; to take notes

examples.en: I jot down the phone number in my notebook.
I took notes on what the teacher said.

explain: '메모'에 '하다'가 붙은 동사예요. 보통 '~을/를 메모하다'나 '~에 메모하다'로 써요.
explain_en: A verb made from '메모' plus '하다'. Use it as '~을/를 메모하다' or '~에 메모하다'.

examples.en: I reviewed the words I learned yesterday.
After class, I review at home.

explain: 배운 내용을 다시 공부한다는 뜻이에요. 앞으로 배울 것을 미리 공부하는 '예습하다'와 반대예요.
explain_en: It means to study again what you already learned. It is the opposite of '예습하다', which is to prepare before class.

examples.en: I lost face in front of everyone.

examples.ko: 체면 때문에 도와 달라고 말을 못 했어요.
examples.en: Because of my pride, I couldn't ask for help.

explain: 다른 사람 앞에서 지키고 싶은 자존심이나 위신이에요. '체면을 차리다', '체면을 잃다'처럼 자주 써요.
explain_en: The pride or standing you want to keep in front of others. It often appears as '체면을 차리다' or '체면을 잃다'.

examples.en: Depression is an illness that can be treated.
My friend goes to the hospital for depression.

explain: 기분이 오랫동안 아주 나쁜 병을 말해요. 잠깐 기분이 안 좋은 '우울하다'와는 달라요.
explain_en: An illness where a person feels very low for a long time. It is different from '우울하다', which can be a short-term mood.

examples.en: Korean culture was influenced by Confucianism.
In Confucianism, people respect their elders.

explain: 공자의 가르침을 따르는 사상이에요. 한국의 예절과 가족 문화에 영향을 많이 줬어요.
explain_en: The way of thought based on Confucius's teachings. It has strongly influenced Korean manners and family culture.

examples.en: There were many uphill roads, so it was tiring.
I ride my bike up the hill.

explain: 위로 올라가는 길이에요. 반대말은 '내리막길'이에요.
explain_en: A road that goes up. Its opposite is '내리막길'.

examples.en: On a downhill road, the bike goes fast.
It's a downhill road, so I walk slowly.

explain: 아래로 내려가는 길이에요. 반대말은 '오르막길'이에요.

phrases.en: Because it's raining, I walk carefully down the downhill road.
phrases.nuance_ko: '내려가다'와 '내리막길'은 뜻이 겹쳐서, 내리막길에서는 '걷다'나 '달리다'를 붙여 쓰는 게 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: '내려가다' repeats the meaning of '내리막길', so verbs like '걷다' or '달리다' sound more natural with it.

phrases.en: This road has many downhill parts.
phrases.nuance_ko: 길의 모습을 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this to describe the shape of a road.

phrases.en: A mountain has uphill and downhill roads.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반대말인 '오르막길'과 함께 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used together with its opposite, '오르막길'.

explain_en: A road that goes down. Its opposite is '오르막길'.

examples.en: I often eat plums in summer.
This plum is a little sour.

explain: 여름에 먹는 작고 새콤달콤한 과일이에요. 복숭아와 모양이 비슷하지만 더 작고 껍질이 매끈해요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 과일은 보통 '개'로 세요.
phrases.nuance_en: Fruit is usually counted with '개'.

phrases.en: The plum tastes sweet and sour.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자두의 맛을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this to talk about how a plum tastes.

phrases.nuance_ko: 자두가 먹기 좋게 되었다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means the plums became ready to eat.

explain_en: A small, sweet-and-sour summer fruit. It looks a bit like a peach but is smaller with smooth skin.

examples.en: The toilet is clogged.
The bathroom has a toilet and a bathtub.

explain: 화장실에서 용변을 볼 때 쓰는 기구예요. 장소를 말하는 '화장실'과 구별해요.
explain_en: The fixture you use to go to the toilet. Don't confuse it with 화장실, which is the room.

examples.en: I floss before going to bed.
I cleaned between my teeth with floss.

explain: 이 사이를 닦는 가는 실이에요. '치실을 하다'나 '치실로 닦다'처럼 말해요.

phrases.en: I use dental floss every day.
phrases.nuance_ko: '치실을 하다'와 비슷하지만 물건을 사용한다는 느낌이 더 커요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to '치실을 하다' but focuses on using the item.

phrases.en: I bought dental floss at the mart.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건으로서의 치실을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this when you talk about floss as a thing.

phrases.en: I put dental floss and a toothbrush in my bag.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이를 닦는 물건끼리 함께 자주 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often mentioned together with other tooth-cleaning items.

explain_en: A thin thread for cleaning between teeth. Say '치실을 하다' or '치실로 닦다'.

examples.en: If I take a walk in the morning, I feel refreshed.
The air is fresh after the rain.

explain: 몸이나 기분, 공기가 맑고 개운하다는 뜻이에요. '기분이 상쾌하다', '공기가 상쾌하다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It means feeling clean and fresh in body, mood, or air. Use it like '기분이 상쾌하다' or '공기가 상쾌하다'.

en: to be depressed; to be depressing

examples.en: I feel gloomy on rainy days.
I've been a bit down lately, so I met a friend.

explain: 마음이 어둡고 기운이 없다는 뜻이에요. 사람의 기분뿐 아니라 날씨나 분위기에도 써요.
explain_en: It means feeling low and heavy-hearted. It can describe a person's mood, and also weather or atmosphere.

examples.en: A family photo hangs on the living room wall.
We took a family photo on New Year's Day.

explain: '가족'과 '사진'이 합쳐진 한 낱말이에요. 붙여 써요.
explain_en: A single compound word made from '가족' and '사진'. It is written without a space.

examples.en: This pizza is too greasy.

examples.ko: 느끼한 음식을 먹어서 김치가 먹고 싶어요.
examples.en: I ate greasy food, so I want kimchi.

explain: 기름기가 많아서 먹기 부담스러운 맛을 말해요. 이럴 때 김치나 콜라를 같이 먹는 사람이 많아요.

phrases.en: to feel queasy from rich food
phrases.en_equiv: to feel queasy from rich food

explain_en: Describes food so oily or rich that it feels heavy. Many Koreans eat kimchi or drink cola to cut that taste.

examples.en: This neighborhood is quiet and peaceful.
I had a peaceful weekend.

explain: 조용하고 걱정이 없어서 편안하다는 뜻이에요. 'ㅂ' 불규칙이라서 '평화로워요'가 돼요.
explain_en: It means calm and free of worry. It is a ㅂ-irregular adjective, so it becomes '평화로워요'.

dis.h: calm place or scene, without conflict

p.n: Almost the same; 평화롭다 is more common.

examples.en: The new shop was a big hit.
Wow! You passed the exam?

explain: 크게 성공하거나 운이 좋은 일을 말해요. 대화에서는 놀랐을 때 '대박!'이라고 짧게 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: A big success or stroke of luck. In conversation, people also say '대박!' alone to react with surprise.

examples.en: That person must have gone to heaven.
This island is paradise for a vacation.

explain: 종교에서 좋은 사람이 간다고 하는 곳이에요. 아주 좋은 장소를 비유할 때도 써요.
explain_en: In religion, the place good people are said to go. It is also used figuratively for a wonderful place.

examples.en: I hug my friend tightly.
The baby sleeps hugging a doll.

explain: 두 팔로 사람이나 물건을 꼭 감싸 안을 때 써요. '안다'보다 더 꼭 안는 느낌이에요.
explain_en: Use it when you wrap both arms tightly around a person or thing. It feels tighter than '안다'.

dis.h: wrap both arms tightly around someone

p.n: 껴안다 is wrapping the arms around; 끌어안다 adds pulling the person close to your chest.

examples.en: I'm going to a department store event this weekend.
This store often runs promotions.

explain: 행사나 특별한 활동을 말해요. 가게의 할인 행사도 이벤트라고 해요.

phrases.en: to take part in an event
phrases.en_equiv: to take part in an event

explain_en: It means an event or special activity. A store sale promotion is also called an 이벤트.

examples.en: That little kid is five years old.
The little kid runs around in the park.

explain: 나이가 어린 아이를 편하게 부르는 말이에요. 어른에게는 쓰지 않아요. 'ㄲ'은 'ㅋ'처럼 숨을 내보내지 않고 세게 소리 내요.

phrases.en: A little customer came to the shop.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어린 손님을 귀엽게 부를 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A cute way to call a young customer.

phrases.en: The kids in the neighborhood are playing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 동네에 사는 어린아이를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: This means young kids who live in the same neighborhood.

phrases.en: The little kids sing a song.
phrases.nuance_ko: '들'을 붙여 여러 아이를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '들' makes it plural.

explain_en: A casual word for a small child. Don't use it for adults. Pronounce 'ㄲ' tensely without a puff of air, unlike 'ㅋ'.

examples.en: I ate steak.
How would you like your steak cooked?

explain: 두껍게 구운 고기 요리예요. '스테이크를 먹다', '스테이크를 굽다'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: I ordered steak at the restaurant.
phrases.nuance_ko: 식당에서 음식을 주문할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this when ordering food at a restaurant.

phrases.en: I pour the steak sauce on the meat.
phrases.nuance_ko: 스테이크와 함께 먹는 소스를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the sauce eaten with steak.

phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 고기인지 말할 때 고기 이름을 앞에 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put the meat name before the word to say what kind it is.

explain_en: A thick grilled cut of meat. Use it as '스테이크를 먹다' or '스테이크를 굽다'.

examples.en: I meditate every morning.
Meditating makes my mind feel at ease.

explain: 조용히 앉아서 마음을 가라앉히는 일이에요. '명상하다'라고 동사로도 써요.
explain_en: Sitting quietly to calm the mind. It also works as a verb: '명상하다'.

examples.en: I listen to jazz.
This cafe plays jazz.

explain: 음악 종류 이름이에요. '재즈를 듣다', '재즈를 좋아하다'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: I feel relaxed when I listen to jazz music.
phrases.nuance_ko: '음악'을 붙여 음악이라는 뜻을 분명히 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '음악' makes it clear you mean music.

phrases.en: I often go to jazz cafes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 재즈가 나오는 카페를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is a cafe that plays jazz.

phrases.en: I am going to a jazz concert on the weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 재즈를 직접 들려주는 공연을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is a live performance of jazz.

explain_en: The name of a music genre. Use it as '재즈를 듣다' or '재즈를 좋아하다'.

examples.en: I listen to hip-hop.
My younger sibling is learning hip-hop dance.

explain: 음악 종류 이름이에요. 랩이 들어간 음악을 말해요.
explain_en: The name of a music genre, music built around rap.

examples.en: She went home.
She is wearing a blue skirt.

explain: 앞에서 말한 여자를 가리켜요. 글에서 많이 쓰고, 말할 때는 이름이나 '그 사람'을 더 자주 써요.

phrases.nuance_ko: '그녀'와 뜻이 같고 말할 때 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as '그녀' and more common in speech.

phrases.en: That person is at home now.
phrases.nuance_ko: 남자와 여자 모두에게 쓸 수 있어서 말할 때 편해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Works for men and women, so it is handy in speech.

phrases.nuance_ko: '그녀' 뒤에 '의'를 붙여 '그 여자의'라는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: '의' added to '그녀' means 'her'.

explain_en: Refers to a woman already mentioned. It's common in writing; in speech people more often use a name or '그 사람'.

examples.en: The goat eats grass.
Have you tried goat meat?

explain: 뿔이 있고 풀을 먹는 동물이에요. 고기는 '염소고기'라고 해요.
explain_en: An animal with horns that eats grass. Its meat is called '염소고기'.

examples.en: I cut the carrot and stir-fry it.
Rabbits like carrots.

explain: 주황색 채소예요. 요즘은 중고 거래 앱 '당근마켓'을 줄여서 '당근'이라고도 말해요.

phrases.en: I bought a chair on Danggeun (the app).
phrases.en_equiv: I bought a chair on Danggeun (the app).

explain_en: An orange vegetable. These days '당근' is also short for the secondhand-trading app Danggeun Market.

examples.en: I'm making gukbap today.
Gukbap tastes good on a cold day.

explain: 뜨거운 국에 밥을 말아 먹는 음식이에요. 돼지국밥, 소고기국밥처럼 종류가 많아요.
explain_en: A dish of rice served in hot soup. There are many kinds, such as pork or beef gukbap.

examples.en: This shirt is yellow.
I wore a white shirt.

explain: 단추가 있는 윗옷이에요. '셔츠를 입다'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: I wear short-sleeved shirts in summer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 소매가 짧은 셔츠예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A shirt with short sleeves.

phrases.en: A button came off my shirt.
phrases.nuance_ko: 셔츠에 달린 단추를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: This means the buttons on a shirt.

phrases.nuance_ko: 옷가게에서 셔츠를 살 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this when buying a shirt at a clothing store.

explain_en: A top with buttons. Use it as '셔츠를 입다'.

examples.en: She wears a pink dress.
I wore a dress at the wedding.

explain: 결혼식이나 파티에서 입는 멋진 원피스예요. 평소에 입는 원피스는 보통 '원피스'라고 해요.

phrases.en: My older sister wore a wedding dress.
phrases.nuance_ko: 결혼식에서 신부가 입는 드레스예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The dress a bride wears at a wedding.

phrases.en: I picked out a dress with my friend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 드레스 중에서 마음에 드는 것을 찾을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this when choosing one you like among many.

phrases.nuance_ko: 길이를 앞에 붙여 드레스 모양을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put the length before the word to describe the dress.

explain_en: A fancy dress for weddings or parties. An everyday dress is usually called '원피스'.

examples.en: I go hiking on weekends.
Autumn is a good time for hiking.

explain: 산이나 길을 따라 걷는 운동이에요. '하이킹을 가다', '하이킹하다'로 써요.
explain_en: Walking along mountain trails or paths for exercise. Use '하이킹을 가다' or '하이킹하다'.

examples.en: I feel refreshed after a shower.
I slept well, so my body feels refreshed.

explain: 씻거나 자고 나서 몸이 가볍고 상쾌할 때 써요. 국물 맛이 깔끔할 때도 써요.

phrases.en: The broth tastes clean and refreshing.
phrases.en_equiv: The broth tastes clean and refreshing.

explain_en: Use it when your body feels light and fresh after washing or sleeping. It also describes a clean, light-tasting broth.

examples.en: I rinse my hands well.
I washed my hair and rinsed it with water.

explain: 비누나 세제를 물로 씻어 내는 것이에요. 손, 머리, 빨래, 그릇에 써요. '행구다'로 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: To wash off soap or detergent with water. Used for hands, hair, laundry, and dishes. The spelling is '헹구다', not '행구다'.

examples.en: I'm learning the cello.
The sound of the cello is really soft.

explain: 바이올린보다 크고 낮은 소리가 나는 악기예요. 악기는 '연주하다'나 '켜다'와 함께 써요.
explain_en: A string instrument bigger than a violin with a lower sound. Pair it with '연주하다' or '켜다'.

examples.en: My dad plays the trumpet.
The trumpet is very loud.

explain: 입으로 불어서 소리를 내는 금속 악기예요. '트럼펫을 불다'라고 해요.
explain_en: A metal instrument you blow into. Say '트럼펫을 불다'.

examples.en: My older sister plays the flute.
The flute sounds clear.

explain: 옆으로 들고 입으로 부는 악기예요. '플루트를 불다'라고 해요.
explain_en: An instrument held sideways and blown into. Say '플루트를 불다'.

examples.en: I do yoga in the morning.
I did yoga with a friend.

explain: '요가'에 '하다'가 붙은 말이에요. '요가를 하다'라고 띄어 써도 돼요.
explain_en: '요가' plus '하다'. You can also say '요가를 하다' with a space.

examples.en: I go to an amusement park on Children's Day.
I give my child a gift on Children's Day.

explain: 5월 5일, 어린이를 위한 날이에요. 이날은 쉬는 날이라서 가족과 함께 나들이를 많이 가요.

phrases.en: I bought a toy as a Children's Day gift.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어린이날에 아이에게 주는 선물을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A gift given to a child on Children's Day.

phrases.en: There is a Children's Day event in the park.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어린이날에 열리는 행사를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: This means events held on Children's Day.

phrases.nuance_ko: 날짜와 함께 어린이날을 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this to explain the day together with its date.
