explain_en: A holiday for children on May 5th. It's a day off, so many families go on outings.

examples.en: I express my feelings well.
This painting expresses sadness.

explain: 생각이나 느낌을 말, 글, 그림, 행동으로 나타내는 것이에요. 보통 '감정을 표현하다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: To show thoughts or feelings through words, writing, art, or actions. Typically used as '감정을 표현하다'.

examples.en: I respect my friend's privacy.
We have to respect each other's opinions.

explain: 사람이나 그 사람의 생각을 소중하게 여기는 것이에요. '의견을 존중하다'처럼 목적어와 함께 써요.
explain_en: To value a person or their ideas. It takes an object, as in '의견을 존중하다'.

examples.en: My phone and computer are synced.
My photos sync to the cloud automatically.

explain: 기기나 파일의 내용이 서로 같아지도록 맞출 때 써요. 휴대폰, 컴퓨터, 클라우드에 많이 써요.
explain_en: Used when the contents of devices or files are matched so they are the same. Often used for phones, computers, and the cloud.

en: to ignore; to look down on

examples.en: My friend ignored my message.
Please ignore that noise.

explain: 일부러 신경 쓰지 않거나 낮게 볼 때 써요. 사람을 무시하면 기분 나쁜 말이 될 수 있어요.
explain_en: Means to deliberately pay no attention to something, or to look down on someone. Used about a person, it can sound offensive.

examples.en: I'm sincerely thankful.
Sincerity matters in relationships.

explain: 겉으로 하는 말이 아니라 마음속의 진짜 생각이나 감정이에요. '진심으로'의 형태로 자주 써요.
explain_en: The real feeling or thought inside, not just words on the surface. It is often used as '진심으로' (sincerely).

examples.en: I comforted my crying friend.
My friend's words were a great comfort.

explain: 슬프거나 힘든 사람의 마음을 편하게 해 줄 때 써요. 위로를 받는 사람은 '위로받다'라고 해요.
explain_en: Used when you ease the feelings of someone sad or struggling. The person who receives comfort uses '위로받다'.

examples.en: Let's overcome hard times together.
He overcame his fear.

explain: 어려움, 약점, 문제를 이겨 낼 때 써요. '어려움을 극복하다'처럼 목적어로 어려운 일이 와요.
explain_en: Used for beating a difficulty, weakness, or problem. The object is usually something hard, as in '어려움을 극복하다'.

examples.en: I have to take care of this today.
I'll take care of the documents tomorrow.

explain: 일, 서류, 문제를 맡아서 끝낼 때 써요. 회사나 관공서에서 많이 써서 조금 딱딱하게 들려요.
explain_en: Used for dealing with a task, document, or problem until it is done. It is common at work and in offices, so it sounds a bit formal.

examples.en: There are ducks in the pond.
The duck swims in the water.

explain: 동물 오리도 되고 음식 오리고기도 돼요. 음식으로 말할 때는 '오리 먹어요'보다 '오리고기 먹어요'가 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: It means the animal, and it can also stand for the meat. When talking about food, '오리고기' sounds more natural than just '오리'.

examples.en: I made gochujang stew on the weekend.
The gochujang stew is a bit spicy.

explain: 고추장을 풀어 끓인 찌개예요. 김치찌개, 된장찌개처럼 재료 이름 뒤에 '찌개'를 붙여요.
explain_en: A stew made by dissolving gochujang in broth. Like 김치찌개 and 된장찌개, it is the main ingredient plus '찌개'.

examples.en: The staff are wearing uniforms.
Our team's uniform is pretty.

explain: 같은 일이나 팀의 사람들이 함께 입는 옷이에요. 학교 옷은 보통 '교복'이라고 해요.
explain_en: Clothes worn together by people in the same job or team. A school uniform is usually called '교복'.

examples.en: This city is really dynamic.
The movie scenes were dynamic.

explain: 활기차고 변화가 많은 모습을 말해요. 보통 '다이내믹하다'로 써요.
explain_en: Describes something lively and full of change. It is usually used as '다이내믹하다'.

examples.en: I spread cream cheese on a bagel.
The cream cheese is smooth.

explain: 빵에 발라 먹는 부드러운 치즈예요. 베이글과 함께 자주 먹어요.

phrases.en: to spread cream cheese on bread
phrases.en_equiv: to spread cream cheese on bread

explain_en: A soft cheese spread on bread. It is often eaten with bagels.

examples.en: The sauce is so good.
I pour sauce on the meat.

explain: 음식에 더하거나 찍어 먹는 액체 양념이에요. 샐러드에 뿌리는 것은 '드레싱'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: A liquid seasoning added to or dipped with food. The kind poured on salad is also called '드레싱'.

examples.en: I had a salad for lunch.
I put tomatoes in the salad.

explain: 채소를 주재료로 한 음식이에요. 점심에 가볍게 먹는 메뉴로 자주 말해요.
explain_en: A dish made mainly of vegetables. People often mention it as a light lunch.

en: to like; to be to one's liking

examples.en: I like this outfit.
I don't like the new house.

explain: 마음에 드는 물건이나 사람이 있을 때 써요. 좋아하는 대상에는 '이/가'를 붙여요. 예: 이 옷이 마음에 들어요.
explain_en: Use it when you like something or someone. The thing you like takes 이/가, as in '이 옷이 마음에 들어요'.

en: family genealogy record; (slang) collection of past exam questions

examples.en: My grandfather's house has an old family genealogy book.
I got the past exam papers.

explain: 한 집안의 역사를 적은 책이에요. 대학생들은 지난 시험 문제 모음을 '족보'라고도 불러요.

phrases.en: to look at the family tree
phrases.en_equiv: to look at the family tree

explain_en: A record of a family's lineage. College students also call a collection of past exam questions a '족보'.

examples.en: By the way, what did you do yesterday?
It's good. But it's too expensive.

explain: '그런데'를 줄인 말로, 말할 때 자주 써요. 앞말과 다른 내용을 말하거나 화제를 바꿀 때 써요.
explain_en: A spoken short form of '그런데'. Use it to contrast with what came before or to change the topic.

dis.h: casual spoken short form of 'but/by the way'

p.n: Same meaning; 근데 is the casual spoken shortening, 그런데 is the fuller, more standard form.

examples.en: Repairing my phone cost money.
I'm going to get my computer repaired.

explain: 고장 난 물건을 고칠 때 써요. 말할 때는 '고치다'를 더 자주 쓰고, '수리하다'는 조금 공식적이에요.
explain_en: Used for fixing broken things. In speech '고치다' is more common; '수리하다' sounds a bit more formal.

dis.h: formal repair of machines or buildings

p.n: Same meaning; 고치다 is more casual and also covers correcting.

examples.en: I drive carefully at night.
Get home safe.

explain: 위험하지 않게 주의하며 행동할 때 써요. 헤어질 때 '조심히 가세요'라고도 자주 말해요.
explain_en: Means acting with care to avoid danger. It is also a common farewell: '조심히 가세요'.

examples.en: I bought fruit at the traditional market on the weekend.
The traditional market is cheaper than the supermarket.

explain: 옛날 방식으로 물건을 파는 시장이에요. 마트와 달리 상인과 이야기하고 값을 깎기도 해요.

phrases.en: I bought vegetables at the market.
phrases.nuance_ko: 더 짧고 쉬운 말이에요. '전통시장'은 옛날 방식의 시장을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: A shorter, simpler word; '전통시장' means the old-style market.

phrases.en: I go to the traditional market every Saturday.
phrases.nuance_ko: '전통시장' 뒤에 '에 가다'를 붙여 장을 보러 갈 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add '에 가다' to say you go shopping there.

phrases.en: The local traditional market is close.
phrases.nuance_ko: 우리 동네에 있는 전통시장을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: This means the traditional market in your own neighborhood.

explain_en: A market where goods are sold in the old style. Unlike a supermarket, you chat with the vendors and sometimes bargain.

examples.en: I've been tired lately, so I go to bed early.
Even when I drink coffee, the tiredness doesn't go away.

explain: 몸이 힘들고 쉬고 싶은 느낌이에요. 보통 '피곤하다'로 써요.
explain_en: The feeling of being worn out and wanting to rest. It is usually used as the verb-like form 피곤하다.

en: to be sour; to be tart

examples.en: This lemon tea is tangy.
The tangy tangerines are delicious.

explain: 상큼하고 기분 좋게 신맛이 나는 거예요. 아주 시면 '시다'를 써요.
explain_en: Describes a pleasantly sour, fresh taste. For something very sour, use 시다.

examples.en: Populist policies are policies meant to win popularity.
That politician was criticized as populist.

explain: 인기를 얻으려고 사람들이 좋아할 정책만 내세우는 정치 방식이에요. 보통 비판하는 뜻으로 써요.

phrases.example: 포퓰리즘 공약은 나중에 문제가 될 수 있어요.
phrases.en: Populist promises can become a problem later.
phrases.nuance_ko: 인기를 얻으려고 내세운 약속을 비판하는 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: It criticizes promises made only to win popularity.

phrases.en: Politics should not fall into populism.
phrases.nuance_ko: 포퓰리즘을 너무 따라간다고 비판할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this to criticize going too far into populism.

phrases.en: People criticize that policy as populism.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 정책을 포퓰리즘이라고 부르며 나쁘게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this when calling a policy populism as criticism.

explain_en: A political style that pushes only popular policies to win support. It is usually used critically.

examples.en: He finished his military service last year.
Korean men have to do military service.

explain: 군대에서 일정 기간 나라를 지키는 일이에요. 보통 '군복무를 하다/마치다'로 써요.

phrases.en: I'm in the middle of military service
phrases.en_equiv: I'm in the middle of military service

explain_en: Serving for a set period in the military. Commonly used as 군복무를 하다 or 군복무를 마치다.

examples.en: I go to the hospital every month.
Every payday, I have a meal with my family.

explain: 한 달 한 달마다라는 뜻이에요. 말할 때는 '매달'을 더 자주 써요.
explain_en: Means every single month. In speech, 매달 is more common.

examples.en: I put the car in the garage.
Our house has a big garage.

explain: 자동차를 넣어 두는 곳이에요. 집에 붙어 있는 차고도 있고 따로 있는 차고도 있어요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 차고의 문을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this for the door of a garage.

phrases.en: I take the car out of the garage.
phrases.nuance_ko: 차를 차고 밖으로 가져올 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this when bringing the car out of the garage.
phrases.en_equiv: take the car out of the garage

phrases.en: It rained, so I parked in the garage.
phrases.nuance_ko: 차를 차고 안에 세울 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this when you park the car inside the garage.

explain_en: A place to keep a car. It can be attached to a house or separate.

examples.en: I put red pepper powder in the kimchi stew.
I sprinkle red pepper powder on the food.

explain: 말린 고추를 곱게 간 가루예요. 맞춤법은 '고추가루'가 아니라 '고춧가루'예요.

phrases.en: I put one spoonful of red pepper powder in the soup.
phrases.nuance_ko: 요리할 때 양을 말하는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An expression for the amount when cooking.
phrases.en_equiv: a spoonful of red pepper powder

phrases.en: I use coarse red pepper powder for kimchi.
phrases.nuance_ko: 곱지 않고 알갱이가 큰 고춧가루예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Red pepper powder with large flakes, not fine.

phrases.en: This red pepper powder is too spicy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 고춧가루의 매운 맛을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this to talk about how spicy the powder is.
phrases.en_equiv: the red pepper powder is spicy

explain_en: Powder made from ground dried chili peppers. The correct spelling is 고춧가루, not 고추가루.

en: to be spicy; to be piquant

examples.en: This tteokbokki is nicely spicy, so it's delicious.
I like spicy food.

explain: 기분 좋게 매운맛이 나는 거예요. 아주 매워서 힘들면 '맵다'를 써요.
explain_en: Describes a pleasant, appetizing spiciness. For painfully hot food, use 맵다.

examples.en: I checked in at the hotel.
From what time can I check in?

explain: 호텔이나 공항에서 도착을 알리고 확인받는 일이에요. 보통 '체크인(을) 하다'로 써요.
explain_en: Registering your arrival at a hotel or airport. Usually used as 체크인(을) 하다.

examples.en: That puppy is really lovely.
I bought a lovely dress.

explain: 귀엽고 사랑스러운 느낌을 말해요. 사람, 옷, 분위기에 두루 써요.

phrases.en: It's a café with a lovely atmosphere.
phrases.nuance_ko: '러블리하다'를 '-ㄴ' 형태로 바꿔 장소나 물건의 분위기를 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form of 러블리하다, used to describe the mood of a place or thing.

phrases.example: 그 옷을 입으면 더 러블리해 보여요.
phrases.en: You look even lovelier in that outfit.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉모습이 러블리하게 느껴진다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when something or someone looks lovely from the outside.

phrases.en: The baby is really lovely when it smiles.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻이 비슷한 우리말이에요. '러블리하다'보다 조금 더 부드럽고 일상적이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A similar native Korean word, a bit softer and more everyday than 러블리하다.

explain_en: Describes something cute and charming. It can be used for people, clothes, or a mood.

examples.en: I saw fish at the aquarium on the weekend.
I want to go to the aquarium.

explain: 물고기와 바다 생물을 모아 놓고 보여 주는 곳이에요.

phrases.en: I saw pretty fish at the aquarium.
phrases.nuance_ko: '수족관'과 같은 뜻이에요. 크고 새로운 시설에 '아쿠아리움'을 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 수족관. 아쿠아리움 is often used for big, modern facilities.

phrases.en: I bought the aquarium tickets in advance.
phrases.nuance_ko: 수족관에 들어갈 때 필요한 표를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the ticket you need to enter the aquarium.

phrases.en: I went to see the aquarium with the kids.
phrases.nuance_ko: 수족관에서 물고기를 둘러보는 일을 가볍게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A casual way to say looking around an aquarium.

explain_en: A place that displays fish and other sea creatures.

examples.en: I ordered and got a pager.
When the pager buzzes, I go pick up my food.

explain: 카페나 식당에서 주문하면 받는 기계예요. 음식이 다 되면 울리고 불빛이 켜져요.
explain_en: The buzzer you get after ordering at a cafe or restaurant. It vibrates and lights up when your order is ready.

examples.en: People all over the world watch the World Cup.
We have to solve global problems together.

explain: 전 세계를 한 마을처럼 가깝게 보고 부르는 말이에요. 뉴스나 글에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: A word for the whole world seen as one close-knit village. It often appears in news and writing.

examples.en: Oh my goodness, it's raining!
Oh my, it's so pretty.

explain: 놀랐을 때 나오는 말이에요. 주로 여자들이 쓰고, 좋은 일과 나쁜 일 모두에 써요.
explain_en: What you say when surprised. It is used mostly by women, for both good and bad surprises.

examples.en: I'm really going to Korea.
Really? I didn't know.

explain: '정말로'와 비슷한 말이에요. 끝을 올려서 '진짜로?' 하면 놀라서 되묻는 말이 돼요.
explain_en: Similar to 정말로. With rising intonation, 진짜로? is a surprised 'Really?'

en: no (polite, short spoken form of 아니요)

examples.en: No, it's okay.
No, I'm not a student.

explain: '아니요'를 말할 때 줄여서 써요. 윗사람에게도 쓸 수 있는 공손한 말이에요. '아냐'는 친구에게만 써요.
explain_en: A spoken short form of 아니요. It is polite. 아냐 is only for friends.

dis.h: spoken, shortened polite no

p.n: Same politeness; 아뇨 is the quicker spoken form.

examples.en: I took photos with my friend in a photo booth.
We go to a photo booth on birthdays.

explain: 돈을 내고 친구들과 사진을 찍는 작은 방이에요. 한국에서는 '인생네컷'을 많이 찍어요.

phrases.en: I took Life Four Cuts photos with my friends.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한국에서 많이 쓰는 포토부스 브랜드 이름이에요. 포토부스 사진을 가리킬 때도 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A popular Korean photo booth brand name, often used for photo booth pictures in general.

phrases.en: There are many people in front of the photo booth.
phrases.nuance_ko: '앞'을 붙여 포토부스 앞에서 기다리는 상황을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 앞 describes waiting or standing in front of the photo booth.
phrases.en_equiv: in front of the photo booth

phrases.en: I put the photo booth picture in my wallet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 포토부스에서 찍은 사진을 가리킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the pictures taken in a photo booth.

explain_en: A small booth where you pay to take photos with friends. In Korea, 인생네컷 booths are popular.

examples.en: I study Korean at a language school.
I want to attend a language school.

explain: 외국어를 가르치는 학원이에요. 한국에서 한국어를 배울 때 대학교 어학당이나 어학원에 다녀요.
explain_en: A private school that teaches foreign languages. In Korea, people study Korean at a university language center or 어학원.

examples.en: I'm going to Korea as an exchange student.
I made an exchange student friend.

explain: 다른 나라 대학에서 일정 기간 공부하는 학생이에요. 보통 한두 학기 동안 가요.
explain_en: A student who studies at a university abroad for a set period, usually one or two semesters.

en: to be excited; to be in high spirits

examples.en: I'm excited to go to Korea.
I get excited when I listen to music.

explain: 기분이 좋아서 들뜨는 것을 말해요. '신나요'처럼 현재형으로 지금 기분을 말하는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: To feel excited and in high spirits. It is often used in the present tense, like 신나요, to describe how you feel now.

examples.en: The pineapple is sweet.
I drink pineapple juice.

explain: 노랗고 달콤한 열대 과일이에요. 피자나 주스에도 넣어요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 파인애플을 올린 피자를 말해요. 좋아하는 사람도 싫어하는 사람도 많아요.
phrases.nuance_en: Pizza topped with pineapple. Some people love it and some hate it.

phrases.en: Do you want a piece of pineapple?
phrases.nuance_ko: 자른 파인애플을 셀 때 '한 조각'이라고 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: 한 조각 is used to count cut pieces of pineapple.

phrases.en: I cut the pineapple with a knife.
phrases.nuance_ko: 먹기 전에 과일을 준비하는 동작을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes preparing the fruit before eating.

explain_en: A yellow, sweet tropical fruit, also used on pizza and in juice.

examples.en: I like mangoes.
I eat mango bingsu.

explain: 노랗고 부드러운 열대 과일이에요. 빙수에 넣어서도 많이 먹어요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 카페에서 음료를 주문할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used when ordering a drink at a café.

phrases.nuance_ko: 망고의 맛을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe how the mango tastes.

phrases.en: I bought one mango at the market.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과일을 하나씩 셀 때 '한 개'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: 한 개 is added when counting fruit one by one.

explain_en: A soft, yellow tropical fruit. It is also popular in bingsu.

examples.en: Kiwis are a little sour.
I ate a kiwi in the morning.

explain: 초록색 속에 작은 씨가 있는 과일이에요. 맛이 새콤해요.

phrases.en: I drink kiwi juice in the morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 키위를 갈아서 만든 음료를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A drink made by blending kiwi.

phrases.en: I cut one kiwi in half.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과일을 하나씩 셀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when counting fruit one by one.

phrases.en: I cut the kiwi to eat it with a spoon.
phrases.nuance_ko: 먹기 전에 키위를 준비하는 동작을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes preparing the kiwi before eating.

explain_en: A fruit with green flesh and tiny seeds. It tastes a little sour.

examples.en: Grapefruit tastes bitter.
One grapefruit ade, please.

explain: 크고 새콤쌉싸름한 과일이에요. 카페에서 자몽 에이드를 많이 마셔요.

phrases.en: I drank grapefruit juice this morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: '자몽 에이드'보다 탄산이 없는 음료를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A drink without the fizz of 자몽 에이드.

phrases.en: When it's cold, I drink warm grapefruit tea.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자몽을 설탕에 절여 뜨거운 물에 타서 마시는 차예요. 카페에서 많이 팔아요.
phrases.nuance_en: A tea made by mixing grapefruit preserved in sugar with hot water. Many cafés sell it.

phrases.en: This grapefruit is tangy and delicious.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자몽의 맛을 말할 때 써요. '쓰다'와 함께 쓰면 맛을 더 잘 설명할 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the taste of grapefruit. Using it with '쓰다' explains the taste even better.

explain_en: A large, sour and slightly bitter fruit. Grapefruit ade is popular at cafes.

examples.en: I boil eggs.
I boiled potatoes and ate them.

explain: 재료를 물에 넣고 끓여서 익히는 거예요. 달걀, 감자, 빨래도 삶아요.
explain_en: To cook something by putting it in water and boiling it. You boil eggs and potatoes, and also laundry.

dis.h: cook food in boiling water

p.n: 끓이다 is for liquids, so 달걀을 끓이다 is unnatural.

examples.en: I wrap the boiled pork in kimchi and eat it.
Tonight's dinner is boiled pork.

explain: 돼지고기를 삶아서 얇게 썬 음식이에요. 보통 김치나 새우젓과 같이 먹어요.
explain_en: Pork that is boiled and sliced thin. It is usually eaten with kimchi or salted shrimp.

examples.en: The chick peeps.
Chicks are yellow.

explain: 닭의 새끼예요. 노란색이고 '삐약삐약' 하고 울어요.

phrases.example: 상자 안에 병아리 한 마리가 있어요.
phrases.en: There is one chick in the box.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동물은 '마리'로 세요.
phrases.nuance_en: Animals are counted with 마리.

phrases.en: The baby is as small as a chick.
phrases.nuance_ko: 작고 귀여운 것을 병아리에 비유할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to compare something small and cute to a chick.

phrases.en: A chick comes out of an egg.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병아리가 태어나는 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a chick being born.
phrases.en_equiv: a chick hatches from an egg

explain_en: A baby chicken. It is yellow and goes 삐약삐약.

examples.en: There are many people at the cafe.
People are lining up.

explain: '사람'에 복수 '-들'이 붙은 말이에요. 사람이 여러 명일 때 써요.

phrases.en: There are many people in the park.
phrases.nuance_ko: '많은'이 '사람들'을 꾸며요. 사람이 많을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: 많은 describes 사람들. Used when there are lots of people.

phrases.nuance_ko: 나 말고 다른 사람이 여럿일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for several people other than yourself.

phrases.nuance_ko: '하고'가 붙어서 '여러 사람과 함께'라는 뜻이 돼요.
phrases.nuance_en: With 하고, it means 'together with several people'.

explain_en: 사람 plus the plural -들. Use it when there are several people.

examples.en: I'm late, so I'm hurrying.
Don't rush.

explain: 빨리 하려고 급하게 움직이는 거예요. '서둘러요', '서둘러서'로 바뀌는 불규칙 활용이에요.
explain_en: To move quickly to get something done. It is irregular: 서둘러요, 서둘러서.

examples.en: I got a boyfriend.
I watch a movie with my boyfriend.

explain: 사귀는 남자예요. 줄여서 '남친'이라고도 해요. 남자인 친구는 그냥 '남자 친구'라고 띄어 써요.
explain_en: A male partner you are dating. It is shortened to 남친. A friend who is male is written with a space: 남자 친구.

examples.en: I got a girlfriend.
I go to a cafe with my girlfriend.

explain: 사귀는 여자예요. 줄여서 '여친'이라고도 해요. 여자인 친구는 '여자 친구'라고 띄어 써요.
explain_en: A female partner you are dating. It is shortened to 여친. A friend who is female is written with a space: 여자 친구.

examples.en: I listen to podcasts on my way to work.
Korean podcasts are fun.

explain: 인터넷으로 듣는 방송이에요. '듣다'와 같이 써서 '팟캐스트를 듣다'라고 해요.
explain_en: An audio show you listen to online. It goes with 듣다: 팟캐스트를 듣다.

examples.en: Get ready quickly.
We're late. Let's hurry!

explain: '빨리'를 두 번 말해서 서두르라고 재촉하는 느낌을 더해요. 친한 사이에서 많이 쓰고, 윗사람에게는 '빨리 해 주세요'가 더 공손해요.

phrases.nuance_ko: '빨리빨리'보다 덜 재촉하는 느낌이에요. 윗사람에게도 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Less pushy than 빨리빨리. You can also use it with someone older or senior.

phrases.en: Sorry, but please do it quickly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 윗사람이나 처음 만난 사람에게 서두르라고 공손하게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite way to ask an older or unfamiliar person to hurry.

phrases.nuance_ko: '빨리빨리'와 비슷하게 서두르라는 뜻이지만 조금 더 부드럽게 들려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Also means 'hurry', but sounds a little softer than 빨리빨리.

explain_en: Doubling 빨리 adds urgency, like 'hurry up'. Use it with friends; with elders, 빨리 해 주세요 is more polite.

dis.h: repeated for urgency; hurry-up, impatient

p.n: The repeated form adds impatience or urgency.

examples.en: I have a lot on my schedule today.
My schedule changed.

explain: 하루나 일주일 동안 할 일의 계획을 말해요. '일정'도 비슷한 뜻이고, 보통 '스케줄이 있다/없다'로 말해요.
explain_en: Means the plan of things to do in a day or week. 일정 is a similar word; you usually say 스케줄이 있다/없다.

examples.en: I did my makeup today.
Your makeup is really pretty.

explain: 얼굴을 꾸미는 화장을 말해요. '메이크업을 하다'로 쓰고, 같은 뜻의 '화장'도 자주 써요.
explain_en: Refers to putting makeup on your face. Say 메이크업을 하다; 화장 is a common word with the same meaning.

examples.en: The store manager isn't here today.
Manager, do you have a moment?

explain: 가게를 책임지는 사람 '점장'에 높임 '님'을 붙인 말이에요. 직접 부를 때도 '점장님'이라고 해요.

phrases.nuance_ko: '께'는 '에게'의 높임말이에요. 점장님처럼 높여야 하는 사람에게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: 께 is the honorific form of 에게. Used for someone you must show respect to, like a manager.

phrases.en: I listened carefully to what the manager said.
phrases.nuance_ko: 점장님이 한 말을 높여서 '말씀'이라고 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The manager's words are raised with the honorific 말씀.

phrases.en: Excuse me, is the store manager here?
phrases.nuance_ko: '있다'의 높임말 '계시다'를 써서 점장님이 있는지 공손하게 물어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses 계시다, the honorific of 있다, to politely ask if the manager is there.

explain_en: 점장 means the person in charge of a store, and 님 makes it respectful. You also use it to address the manager directly.

examples.en: I make a list of things to buy.
My name isn't on the list.

explain: 순서대로 적어 놓은 목록을 말해요. '목록'과 비슷하고, '리스트를 만들다'로 자주 써요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻이 같은 한자어예요. 글이나 공식적인 자리에서 더 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A Sino-Korean word with the same meaning. More common in writing or formal settings.

phrases.en: I write my to-do things on the list.
phrases.nuance_ko: 목록에 내용을 쓸 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when writing items down on a list.

phrases.nuance_ko: 살 물건을 적은 목록을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A list of things to buy.

explain_en: A written list of items. Similar to 목록; commonly used as 리스트를 만들다.

examples.en: I like corn soup.
I eat warm corn soup.

explain: 옥수수로 만든 걸쭉한 수프예요. '수프'는 '스프'라고도 쓰지만 표준어는 '수프'예요.

phrases.nuance_ko: '콘수프'와 뜻이 같아요. 우리말로 풀어서 쓴 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 콘수프, written with the Korean word for corn.

phrases.en: One bowl of corn soup, please.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음식점에서 주문할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when ordering at a restaurant.

phrases.en: On cold days, I cook corn soup and eat it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 수프를 직접 만들 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for making soup yourself.

explain_en: A thick soup made from corn. The standard spelling of 'soup' is 수프, though 스프 is also heard.

examples.en: I put pepperoni on the pizza.
One pepperoni pizza, please.

explain: 피자 위에 올리는 매콤한 얇은 소시지예요. 보통 '페퍼로니 피자'로 많이 말해요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 피자를 주문할 때 토핑을 더 달라고 하는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when ordering pizza to ask for extra topping.

phrases.en: This pepperoni is a little spicy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 페퍼로니의 맛을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the taste of pepperoni.

phrases.en: I'll eat just one piece of pepperoni.
phrases.nuance_ko: 작게 자른 페퍼로니를 셀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to count small slices of pepperoni.

explain_en: A spicy, thinly sliced sausage used on pizza. Most often heard in 페퍼로니 피자.

examples.en: I grill sausage in the morning.
I put sausage in the gimbap.

explain: 고기를 갈아서 만든 긴 음식이에요. 구워서 먹거나 반찬, 요리에 넣어요.

phrases.en: I put stir-fried sausage in the lunch box.
phrases.nuance_ko: 소시지를 볶아서 만든 반찬이에요. 도시락 반찬으로 인기가 많아요.
phrases.nuance_en: A side dish of stir-fried sausage, popular in lunch boxes.

phrases.en: I bought a sausage bun at the convenience store.
phrases.nuance_ko: 소시지가 들어간 빵을 말해요. 한 단어로 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Bread with sausage inside. It is written as one word.

phrases.en: This sausage is a little salty.
phrases.nuance_ko: 소시지의 맛을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the taste of sausage.

explain_en: A long food made from ground meat. It's grilled or used in side dishes and cooking.

examples.en: Which airline is cheaper?
I called the airline.

explain: 비행기로 사람이나 짐을 나르는 회사예요. 비행기표를 살 때 '어느 항공사'인지 물어봐요.

phrases.en: I asked a staff member of the airline.
phrases.nuance_ko: 항공사에서 일하는 사람을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A person who works for an airline.

phrases.nuance_ko: 값이 싼 항공사를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: An airline with low prices.

phrases.nuance_ko: 공항에서 표를 확인하고 짐을 맡기는 곳을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The counter at the airport where you check in and drop off your bags.

explain_en: A company that carries people or cargo by plane. When buying tickets you ask which 항공사.

examples.en: I wash the spinach.
The seasoned spinach is delicious.

explain: 초록색 잎채소예요. 데쳐서 '시금치나물'로 먹거나 김밥, 국에 넣어요.
explain_en: A green leafy vegetable. It's blanched and seasoned as 시금치나물, or put in gimbap and soup.

examples.en: I eat banquet noodles for lunch.
The broth of janchi-guksu is refreshing.

explain: 멸치 국물에 가는 국수를 말아 먹는 음식이에요. 예전에 잔치 때 먹어서 이런 이름이 됐어요.

phrases.en: One bowl of janchi guksu, please.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음식점에서 주문할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when ordering at a restaurant.

phrases.example: 비 오는 날에는 따뜻한 잔치국수가 좋아요.
phrases.en: On rainy days, warm janchi guksu is nice.
phrases.nuance_ko: 국물이 따뜻한 잔치국수의 느낌을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the feel of janchi guksu with warm broth.

phrases.en: I eat janchi guksu with kimchi on top.
phrases.nuance_ko: 국수와 김치를 함께 먹는 방법이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common way of eating the noodles together with kimchi.

explain_en: Thin wheat noodles in a light anchovy broth. It got its name because it was traditionally served at celebrations.

examples.en: I receive New Year money on Seollal.
Grandma gave me New Year money.

explain: 설날에 세배를 하면 어른들이 주시는 돈이에요. 발음은 [세배똔/세밷똔]이고 '세뱃돈'으로 써요.

phrases.en: to bow to elders at New Year
phrases.en_equiv: to bow to elders at New Year

explain_en: Money elders give you at Lunar New Year after you bow to them. It's spelled 세뱃돈, with ㅅ in the middle, and pronounced 세배똔.

examples.en: I like shrimp.
I eat shrimp fried rice.

explain: 바다에 사는 작은 동물이고 음식 재료예요. 튀기거나 구워서 먹고 '새우튀김', '새우볶음밥'처럼 써요.
explain_en: A small sea animal and common ingredient. Often fried or grilled, as in 새우튀김 and 새우볶음밥.

examples.en: I bought new running shoes.
I wear running shoes and go to the park.

explain: 달리기할 때 신는 운동화예요. '러닝'과 신발을 뜻하는 '-화'가 합쳐진 말이에요.

phrases.nuance_ko: '러닝화'보다 넓은 말이에요. 운동할 때 신는 신발을 모두 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: A broader word than 러닝화. It covers all shoes worn for exercise.

phrases.en: My running shoe lace came undone.
phrases.nuance_ko: 신발 끈을 말할 때 '러닝화'를 앞에 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put 러닝화 in front to talk about the shoe's lace.

phrases.en: I bought a pair of running shoes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 신발은 '켤레'로 세요.
phrases.nuance_en: Shoes are counted with 켤레.

explain_en: Shoes made for running. It combines 러닝 with -화, meaning 'shoes'.

examples.en: Our house is a new house.
We are moving to a new house next month.

explain: 새로 지었거나 새로 이사 간 집이에요. '새 집'처럼 띄어 쓰기도 하고, '새집'은 새가 사는 집(둥지)을 뜻하기도 해요.
explain_en: A house that was newly built or that you just moved into. 새집 can also mean a bird's nest.

examples.en: I installed a shower booth in the bathroom.
I cleaned the shower booth glass.

explain: 욕실 안에서 유리나 벽으로 따로 막아 놓은 샤워 공간이에요. 샤워기만 말할 때는 '샤워기'라고 해요.

phrases.en: The shower booth door won't open.
phrases.nuance_ko: 샤워부스의 유리문을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the glass door of the shower booth.

phrases.en: I clean the shower booth on weekends.
phrases.nuance_ko: 욕실의 샤워 공간을 깨끗하게 하는 일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Cleaning the shower space in the bathroom.

phrases.en: I hung a towel inside the shower booth.
phrases.nuance_ko: '안'을 붙여 샤워 공간 속을 가리킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 안 points to the inside of the shower space.

explain_en: The enclosed space in a bathroom, walled off with glass or panels, where you take a shower. The shower head itself is 샤워기.

examples.en: This piece of clothing is easy to wash.
I do the laundry on weekends.

explain: 옷이나 이불을 물로 빠는 일이에요. 보통 '세탁하다', '세탁기', '세탁소'처럼 다른 말과 함께 써요.

phrases.en: to take to the dry cleaner
phrases.en_equiv: to take to the dry cleaner

explain_en: The act of washing clothes or bedding. It is usually used in words like 세탁하다, 세탁기 and 세탁소.

dis.h: formal; washing, cleaning service

p.n: 세탁 is the act or service; 세탁물 is the items themselves.

examples.en: The air is dry in winter.
Drying takes one hour.

explain: 물기가 없이 마르는 것, 또는 말리는 일이에요. 날씨가 '건조하다'처럼 쓰고, 빨래를 말릴 때도 '건조'라고 해요.
explain_en: Being free of moisture, or the act of drying something. It is used for dry weather (건조하다) and for drying laundry.

examples.en: A new era has arrived.
The age of AI is arriving.

explain: 어떤 시기나 때가 오는 것을 말해요. 사람이 오는 것에는 쓰지 않고, '시대', '시기', '때'와 함께 써요.

phrases.example: 우리는 도래한 새 시대에 적응해야 해요.
phrases.en: We have to adapt to the new era that has arrived.
phrases.nuance_ko: '도래하다'를 '-ㄴ' 형태로 바꿔 '시대'를 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form of 도래하다, used to describe an era.

phrases.nuance_ko: 앞으로 올 시기를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a time that will come in the future.

phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻이 비슷하지만 '도래하다'는 주로 글에서 쓰고, '다가오다'는 말과 글에서 모두 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar in meaning, but 도래하다 is mostly for writing, while 다가오다 works in speech and writing.

explain_en: Used when a period or time arrives. It is not used for people coming; it goes with words like 시대, 시기 and 때.

examples.en: Some people oppose that plan.
This is just the tip of the iceberg.

explain: 전체 가운데 한쪽, 일부분을 뜻해요. 뉴스에서 '일각에서는 ~라고 말해요'처럼 자주 써요.
explain_en: One part or corner of a larger whole. In the news it often appears as 일각에서는 ~, meaning 'some people say ~'.

examples.en: I sent an email to the client.
The lawyer meets the client.

explain: 변호사나 전문가에게 일을 맡기는 사람이에요. 가게의 '손님'과 달리, 일을 부탁한 사람을 가리켜요.

phrases.en: A lawyer keeps the client's secrets.
phrases.nuance_ko: '의'가 붙어서 의뢰인에게 속한 것을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: With 의, it refers to something that belongs to the client.

phrases.en: I asked an expert to do the work.
phrases.nuance_ko: '의뢰인'이 하는 행동이에요. 전문가에게 일을 맡길 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The action a client does: asking an expert to take on a job.

phrases.nuance_ko: 물건이나 서비스를 사는 사람이에요. '의뢰인'은 일을 부탁한 사람이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A person who buys goods or services. 의뢰인 is a person who asks for work to be done.

explain_en: A person who asks a lawyer or other professional to handle something for them. Unlike 손님 (a shop customer), it means the one who commissioned the work.

examples.en: I watched the sunrise at the sea on New Year's Day.
What time is sunrise?

explain: 아침에 해가 떠오르는 모습이에요. 새해 첫날에 해돋이를 보러 가는 문화가 있어요.
explain_en: The sight of the sun rising in the morning. In Korea, many people go to watch the sunrise on New Year's Day.

examples.en: I film a vlog every weekend.
I am watching a travel vlog.

explain: 자기 일상을 찍어서 올리는 영상이에요. 영어 vlog를 한국어 소리로 읽은 말이에요.
explain_en: A video that shows your daily life, posted online. It is the English word 'vlog' read in Korean sounds.

en: to conclude; to sign (a contract or treaty)

examples.en: The company concluded a new contract.
The two countries signed an agreement.

explain: 계약이나 조약을 정식으로 맺는다는 뜻이에요. '계약을 체결하다'처럼 주로 계약·협정과 함께 써요.
explain_en: To formally enter into a contract or treaty. It is mostly used with words like 계약 and 협정.

examples.en: You must carry out the terms of the contract.
He did not fulfill his promise.

explain: 약속, 계약, 의무를 말한 대로 실제로 하는 것을 뜻해요. '약속을 지키다'보다 딱딱한 말이에요.
explain_en: To actually do what you promised or are obliged to do, such as a promise, contract or duty. It sounds more formal than 약속을 지키다.

examples.en: Korea exports a lot of semiconductors.
He works at a semiconductor company.

explain: 전기가 통하는 정도가 도체와 부도체 사이인 물질이에요. 컴퓨터와 휴대폰에 들어가고, 한국의 대표 수출품이에요.
explain_en: A material whose electrical conductivity lies between a conductor and an insulator. It goes into computers and phones, and it is one of Korea's main exports.

examples.en: Members of the National Assembly are chosen by election.
A lawmaker proposed a new law.

explain: 국민이 선거로 뽑아 국회에서 법을 만드는 사람이에요. 줄여서 '의원'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: A person elected by the people to make laws in the National Assembly. It is also shortened to 의원.

examples.en: The US Senate passed the bill.
There are 100 senators.

explain: 의회가 두 곳으로 나뉜 나라에서 위쪽 의회예요. 미국의 Senate를 말할 때 많이 써요. 한국 국회는 한 곳뿐이라 상원이 없어요.
explain_en: The upper chamber in a country with a two-chamber legislature. It is often used for the US Senate. Korea has a single-chamber National Assembly, so it has no 상원.

en: lower house; the House of Representatives

examples.en: The House voted first.
A member of the House serves a two-year term.

explain: 의회가 두 곳으로 나뉜 나라에서 아래쪽 의회예요. 미국의 House of Representatives를 말할 때 많이 써요. 보통 '상원'과 짝으로 외워요.
explain_en: The lower chamber in a country with a two-chamber legislature. It is often used for the US House of Representatives, and is usually learned as a pair with 상원.

examples.en: He is my business partner.
I am looking for a dance partner.

explain: 함께 일하거나 운동하고 춤을 추는 짝이에요. 회사에서는 지분을 가진 공동 경영자를 뜻하기도 해요.
explain_en: Someone you work, exercise or dance with. In a firm it can also mean a co-owner who holds a share of the business.

examples.en: My grandfather left his last words.
The funeral was held according to their last wishes.

explain: 세상을 떠나기 전에 남기는 말이에요. 보통 '유언을 남기다'로 써요. 재산을 나누는 법적 문서는 '유언장'이라고 해요.
explain_en: Words a person leaves behind before dying. It is usually used as '유언을 남기다'. The legal document dividing property is called '유언장'.

en: note left before death; suicide note

examples.en: He left a note for his family.
This is a temple with a long history.

explain: 죽기 전에 남기는 편지예요. 무겁고 감정이 큰 말이라 일상 대화에서는 조심해서 써요. '유서 깊다'의 유서(由緖)는 한자와 뜻이 완전히 달라요.

phrases.en: to have a long, distinguished history
phrases.en_equiv: to have a long, distinguished history

explain_en: A letter left behind before death. It is heavy and emotional, so use it carefully in everyday talk. The 유서 in '유서 깊다' (由緖) is a different word with a different meaning.

examples.en: Korea was called a single-ethnicity nation for a long time.

examples.ko: 요즘은 단일민족국가라는 말이 잘 맞지 않아요.
examples.en: These days the term single-ethnicity nation doesn't fit well.

explain: 한 민족으로만 이루어진 나라를 말해요. 한국을 설명할 때 자주 쓰지만, 요즘은 다문화 가정이 늘어서 맞지 않는다는 의견도 있어요.

phrases.en: The idea of being a single ethnic group is changing.
phrases.nuance_ko: '단일민족국가'를 줄인 말처럼 쓰여요. 한 민족이라는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used as a shortened form meaning 'one single ethnic group'.

phrases.en: The United States is a multiethnic country.
phrases.nuance_ko: '단일민족국가'와 반대로 여러 민족이 사는 나라를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of 단일민족국가: a country where many ethnic groups live.

phrases.en: Korea is known as a single-ethnicity nation.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한국을 소개하는 글이나 말에서 자주 나오는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A phrase often seen when introducing Korea in writing or speech.

explain_en: A country made up of a single ethnic group. It is often used to describe Korea, though many now say it no longer fits as multicultural families increase.

examples.en: This puppy has a good pedigree.
That family carries on a line of artists.

explain: 조상에서 이어지는 피의 계통이에요. 사람뿐 아니라 동물에게도 써요. '혈통을 이어받다'처럼 써요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 다른 피가 섞이지 않은 혈통을 말해요. 동물에게 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A line with no mixing of other blood. Often used for animals.

phrases.en: Those two people are of the same lineage.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조상이 같은 사람들을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for people who share the same ancestors.

phrases.en: That family is carrying on its lineage.
phrases.nuance_ko: '이어받다'는 받는 쪽, '이어가다'는 계속 지키는 쪽을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: 이어받다 focuses on receiving, while 이어가다 focuses on continuing it.

explain_en: The blood line passed down from ancestors. It is used for animals as well as people, as in '혈통을 이어받다'.

examples.en: That group is too closed to outsiders.
An exclusionary attitude isn't good.

explain: 자기 편이 아닌 사람을 받아들이지 않는 태도를 말해요. '배타적인 문화'처럼 '-인'을 붙이거나 '배타적이다'로 써요.
explain_en: An attitude of refusing to accept outsiders. Use it as '배타적인 + noun' or '배타적이다', as in '배타적인 문화'.

examples.en: My father turns 60 in August.
I gave a watch as a 60th birthday gift.

explain: 만 예순 살 생일이에요. 십이지와 십간이 합쳐 60년마다 한 바퀴 돌아서 생긴 말이에요. 요즘은 칠순이나 팔순을 더 크게 챙기기도 해요.
explain_en: The 60th birthday. The word comes from the 60-year cycle of 12 zodiac signs combined with 10 heavenly stems. Nowadays some families celebrate 70th or 80th birthdays more grandly.

examples.en: My younger sibling acted cute and got some allowance.
Our cat is very affectionate and charming.

explain: 귀엽고 사랑스러운 말투나 행동이에요. '애교를 부리다'로 자주 쓰고, '애교가 많다'는 그런 성격을 말해요.
explain_en: A cute, endearing way of speaking or acting. Commonly used as '애교를 부리다'; '애교가 많다' describes someone with that personality.

en: dropping out of school; voluntary withdrawal

examples.en: My older brother dropped out of university.
After dropping out, I started working.

explain: 학생이 스스로 학교를 그만두는 거예요. '자퇴하다'로 쓰고, 학교에서 내보내는 '퇴학'과 달라요.
explain_en: A student leaving school of their own will. Used as '자퇴하다'; it differs from '퇴학', where the school expels the student.

examples.ko: 그는 힘든 일을 겪고 스스로 목숨을 끊었어요.
examples.en: After going through hard times, he took his own life.

examples.ko: 스스로 목숨을 끊는 일은 막아야 해요.
examples.en: Suicide must be prevented.

explain: '자살하다'를 돌려서 말하는 표현이에요. 뉴스나 글에서 쓰고, 일상 대화에서는 아주 조심해서 써야 해요.

phrases.example: 뉴스에서 극단적인 선택을 한 사람의 이야기가 나왔어요.
phrases.en: The news reported the story of a person who took their own life.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스에서 자주 쓰는 더 돌려 말하는 표현이에요. 조심스럽게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A more indirect expression often used in the news, for speaking carefully about the topic.

phrases.en: Articles sometimes use the word 'committed suicide'.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가장 직접적인 말이에요. 뉴스나 글에서 쓰고, 대화에서는 조심해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most direct word. Used in news and writing, and handled with care in conversation.

phrases.en: There is a suicide prevention hotline.
phrases.nuance_ko: 도움을 주고 막는 활동을 말할 때 쓰는 말이에요. 뉴스와 공공 안내에 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for activities that help and prevent it. Often seen in the news and public notices.

explain_en: A euphemism for '자살하다' (to commit suicide). It appears in news and writing; use it very carefully in everyday conversation.

en: to splash; to bounce; to stand out

examples.en: Oil splashed and burned my hand.
That outfit stands out too much.

explain: 물이나 공이 튀기도 하고, 사람이나 옷이 눈에 띌 때도 써요. '너무 튀지 마'는 눈에 띄지 말라는 뜻이에요.
explain_en: It means water or a ball splashing or bouncing, and also a person or outfit standing out. '너무 튀지 마' means don't stand out too much.

examples.ko: A: 도와주실 수 있어요? B: 그럼요!
examples.en: A: Can you help me? B: Of course!
Sure, of course we should go.

explain: 상대의 질문이나 부탁에 확실히 '그렇다'고 답할 때 써요. 윗사람에게도 쓸 수 있는 부드러운 말이에요.

phrases.en: A: Do you want to go together? B: Of course!
phrases.nuance_ko: '그럼요'와 뜻이 비슷하고 정중해요. 조금 더 글 같은 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 그럼요 and polite, but sounds a little more formal.

phrases.example: A: 도와줄 수 있어요? B: 당연하죠!
phrases.en: A: Can you help me? B: Of course!
phrases.nuance_ko: '그럼요'와 뜻이 비슷하지만 '당연히 그렇다'는 느낌이 더 강해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 그럼요, but with a stronger feeling of 'obviously'.

phrases.nuance_ko: '그럼요'의 반말이에요. 친한 친구나 아랫사람에게만 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The casual form of 그럼요. Use it only with close friends or people younger than you.

explain_en: Used to answer a question or request with a firm yes. It is polite enough to use with elders.

examples.en: That restaurant went under because it had no customers.
I totally bombed this exam.

explain: 가게나 계획이 크게 실패할 때 써요. 말할 때는 시험이나 하루가 엉망일 때도 '망했다'고 가볍게 말해요.
explain_en: Used when a business or plan fails badly. In casual speech, people also say '망했다' when a test or a day goes terribly.

examples.en: The baby next door is so cute.
The baby is sleeping.

explain: '아기'를 편하게 말하는 형태예요. 글에서는 '아기'가 표준이고, 말할 때는 '애기'도 많이 써요.

phrases.en: The baby's mother is pushing a stroller.
phrases.nuance_ko: '애기'와 같이 쓰는 대표적인 짝말이에요. 아기를 키우는 엄마를 편하게 부를 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing with '애기'. It casually refers to a mother with a baby.

phrases.en: The mother is holding the baby.
phrases.nuance_ko: '애기'를 목적어로 쓰는 기본 동작이에요. '안고 있어요'처럼 연결해서 많이 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The basic action with '애기' as the object. It is often used in forms like '안고 있어요'.

phrases.nuance_ko: '애기'의 표준 형태예요. 글이나 공식적인 자리에서는 '아기'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The standard form of '애기'. Use it in writing and formal situations.

explain_en: A casual form of '아기'. In writing '아기' is standard, but '애기' is very common in speech.

en: to work; to function; to operate

examples.en: This machine doesn't work well.
It starts running as soon as you press the button.

explain: 기계나 프로그램이 움직일 때 써요. 기계가 주어면 '작동하다', 사람이 움직이게 하면 '작동시키다'예요.
explain_en: Used when a machine or program runs. With the machine as subject use '작동하다'; when a person makes it run, use '작동시키다'.

dis.h: a device works or functions properly

p.n: 가동하다 needs an operator or object and does not fit this sentence.

examples.en: Seoul is a really dynamic city.
The dance was very dynamic.

explain: 힘이 있고 활발하게 움직이는 느낌이에요. 변화가 많고 에너지가 넘치는 도시, 춤, 분위기에 써요.
explain_en: Describes something full of energy and movement. Used for lively cities, dances, or atmospheres with a lot of change.

examples.en: I get competitive when I play games.
My friend's words fired up my competitive spirit.

explain: 이기고 싶은 마음이에요. '승부욕이 강하다', '승부욕을 자극하다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: The urge to win. Used in phrases like '승부욕이 강하다' and '승부욕을 자극하다'.

en: to foul; to break the rules (in a game or sport)

examples.en: That player fouled and was sent off.
Peeking is against the rules.

explain: 경기나 게임에서 규칙을 어길 때 써요. '반칙을 하다'로도 많이 말하고, 친구끼리 '그건 반칙이야'라고 자주 해요.
explain_en: Used when someone breaks the rules in a game or sport. Also said as '반칙을 하다'; friends often say '그건 반칙이야' (that's cheating).

en: to close the door; to shut down (a business)

examples.en: It's cold, so please close the door.
Business was slow, so the shop closed down.

explain: 말 그대로 문을 닫는 뜻이 있고, 가게나 회사가 영업을 끝내고 없어진다는 뜻으로도 써요. 직원이 회사를 그만두는 '퇴사'와는 달라요.

phrases.en: to open (a shop) / to open the door
phrases.en_equiv: to open (a shop) / to open the door

explain_en: It literally means closing a door, and it also means a shop or company shuts down for good. This differs from an employee leaving a company.

examples.en: That company went bankrupt last year.
They filed for bankruptcy because of heavy debt.

explain: 빚을 갚지 못해 재산을 잃는 거예요. '파산하다', '파산 신청'으로 써요. '파'는 깨진다는 뜻으로 파괴, 파손에도 있어요.
explain_en: Losing everything because you can't repay debts. Used as '파산하다' or '파산 신청'. The 파 means 'break', as in 파괴 and 파손.

examples.en: The athlete came home in glory after winning a gold medal.
I want to return home in triumph after finishing my studies.

explain: 성공한 뒤에 멋지게 고향이나 집으로 돌아오는 것을 말하는 사자성어예요. 보통 '금의환향하다'로 써요.
explain_en: A four-character idiom for coming home successful and honored. It is usually used as '금의환향하다'.

examples.ko: 할머니가 치매에 걸리셔서 가족이 많이 걱정해요.
examples.en: My grandmother has dementia, so the family is very worried.

examples.ko: 치매를 막으려면 운동을 하는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: Exercise is good for preventing dementia.

explain: 기억력과 판단력이 점점 약해지는 병이에요. '치매에 걸리다'라고 말해요.
explain_en: A disease where memory and judgment gradually decline. The set phrase is '치매에 걸리다'.

examples.ko: 유튜브 알고리즘이 제가 좋아하는 영상을 계속 보여 줘요.
examples.en: The YouTube algorithm keeps showing me videos I like.
This program uses a new algorithm.

explain: 문제를 푸는 순서나 방법이에요. 요즘은 SNS나 유튜브가 영상을 추천하는 방식을 말할 때도 많이 써요.
explain_en: A step-by-step method for solving a problem. It is also often used for how social media or YouTube recommends videos.

en: to grant; to give; to assign

examples.en: The company assigned new roles to the employees.

examples.ko: 사람들은 이 날에 특별한 의미를 부여해요.
examples.en: People give special meaning to this day.

explain: 권리, 의미, 역할, 번호 같은 것을 공식적으로 주는 거예요. 물건을 직접 주는 '주다'와 달리 추상적인 것에 써요. '의미를 부여하다'가 자주 나와요.
explain_en: To formally give something abstract like a right, meaning, role, or number. Unlike '주다', it is not used for physical objects. '의미를 부여하다' is a common phrase.

examples.en: I got a Jeju Island brochure from the travel agency.
The school brochure has class information.

explain: 회사, 학교, 여행지를 소개하는 얇은 책자예요. 비슷한 말로 '팸플릿'이 있어요.

phrases.en: I got a pamphlet at the hotel.
phrases.nuance_ko: '브로슈어'와 거의 같은 뜻이에요. 팸플릿이 조금 더 얇고 간단한 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Almost the same meaning as '브로슈어'. A pamphlet feels a bit thinner and simpler.

phrases.en: I made a company introduction brochure.
phrases.nuance_ko: 소개 책자를 직접 만들 때 써요. 회사나 학교에서 자주 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when making an introductory booklet. Common in companies and schools.

phrases.en: I saw the brochure and called.
phrases.nuance_ko: 책자를 읽고 정보를 얻을 때 써요. 뒤에 '-고'를 붙여 이유나 순서를 말할 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when getting information from a brochure. Adding '-고' links it to a reason or sequence.

explain_en: A thin booklet that introduces a company, school, or travel spot. A similar word is '팸플릿'.

examples.en: I tanned at the beach on vacation.
My skin is sensitive, so I shouldn't tan.

explain: 피부를 갈색으로 태우는 것을 말해요. 햇볕이나 기계로 해요. '선탠하다'도 비슷하게 써요.
explain_en: To darken your skin to a brown color, by sunlight or a machine. '선탠하다' is used in a similar way.

en: hill; small mountain; movable property (動産)

examples.en: The children are running around on the little hill.
A house is real estate and a car is movable property.

explain: 집 근처의 작은 언덕이나 낮은 산이에요. 한자어 '동산(動産)'은 돈이나 물건처럼 옮길 수 있는 재산을 뜻하고, 땅이나 건물인 '부동산'과 반대예요.

phrases.en: I take a walk on the hill behind my house.
phrases.nuance_ko: 집이나 마을 뒤에 있는 작은 언덕을 말해요. 동산보다 위치가 분명해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A small hill behind a house or village. The location is clearer than with plain '동산'.

phrases.en: I climbed the hill in the morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 작은 언덕에 올라갈 때 쓰는 짝말이에요. 높은 산에는 보통 '산에 오르다'라고 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for going up a small hill. For high mountains, people usually say '산에 오르다'.

phrases.en: Movable property and real estate are different.
phrases.nuance_ko: 재산의 뜻일 때는 '부동산'과 함께 자주 말해요. 옮길 수 있는 재산이 동산이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: In the property sense, it is often paired with '부동산'. Movable property is '동산'.

explain_en: A small hill or low mountain near a home. The Sino-Korean '동산 (動産)' means movable property like money or goods, the opposite of '부동산' (real estate).

examples.en: A salary is earned income.
It is hard to save money with earned income alone.

explain: 직접 일해서 버는 돈이에요. 월급이 대표적이에요. 사업수익, 금융수익과 같이 자주 비교해요.

phrases.en: My earned income increased this year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 월급이나 일해서 버는 돈이 많아졌을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the money earned from working has increased.

phrases.nuance_ko: 직접 일해서 돈을 번다는 뜻을 분명히 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to make clear that the money comes from working directly.

phrases.en: I write down earned income and business income separately.
phrases.nuance_ko: 두 가지 수익을 구별해서 말할 때 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used together when distinguishing the two kinds of income.

explain_en: Money you earn by working yourself, such as a salary. It is often compared with business income and financial income.

examples.en: My online shop started making business income.
Business income is different every month.

explain: 가게나 회사를 운영해서 얻는 돈이에요. 월급인 근로수익과 구별해서 말해요.

phrases.en: My business income decreased this month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가게나 회사에서 버는 돈이 적어졌을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the money earned from a shop or company has decreased.

phrases.en: I wrote down my business income separately.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다른 돈과 나누어 기록할 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when recording it apart from other money.

phrases.en: Business income and earned income are different.
phrases.nuance_ko: 월급과 구별해서 설명할 때 같이 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Said together when explaining the difference from salary.

explain_en: Money earned by running a shop or company. It is distinguished from a salary, which is earned income.

examples.en: Bank interest is also financial income.
I bought stocks and earned financial income.

explain: 예금 이자나 주식 배당금처럼 돈을 굴려서 얻는 수익이에요. 근로수익과 달라요.

phrases.en: Interest went up, so my financial income increased.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이자나 배당금으로 얻는 돈이 많아졌을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when money from interest or dividends has increased.

phrases.en: I don't have any financial income yet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 예금이나 주식으로 번 돈이 없을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you have no money earned from deposits or stocks.

phrases.en: I compared financial income and earned income.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돈을 굴려서 번 돈과 일해서 번 돈을 비교할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when comparing money earned by investing with money earned by working.

explain_en: Income from money working for you, like bank interest or stock dividends. It is different from earned income.

examples.en: On cold days I want to eat bungeoppang.
The child is the spitting image of their dad.

explain: 붕어 모양 틀에 반죽과 팥을 넣어 구운 겨울 간식이에요. 또 부모와 아주 닮은 아이를 '붕어빵'이라고 놀리듯 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: A winter snack baked in a fish-shaped mold, usually filled with red bean. You can also call a child who looks just like their parent a '붕어빵'.

examples.en: I put cream in my coffee.
I put cream on my face before bed.

explain: 우유로 만든 크림도 있고 피부에 바르는 크림도 있어요. 둘 다 '크림'이라고 해요.
explain_en: '크림' means both cream you eat and cream you put on your skin.

examples.en: I do volunteer work every weekend.
The students did volunteer work at a nursing home.

explain: 돈을 받지 않고 다른 사람을 돕는 활동이에요. '봉사활동을 하다'라고 써요. 줄여서 '봉사'라고도 해요.
explain_en: Activities where you help others without pay. Say '봉사활동을 하다'. It is often shortened to '봉사'.

examples.en: My grandfather goes to the senior center every day.
We served lunch to the elders at the senior center.

explain: 동네에서 어르신들이 모여 쉬고 이야기하고 식사도 하는 곳이에요. 한국 동네마다 있어요.

phrases.en: There are many elderly people at the neighborhood senior center.
phrases.nuance_ko: 우리 마을에 있는 경로당을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to talk about the senior center in your own neighborhood.

phrases.en: My grandmother rests at the senior center.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어르신들이 경로당에서 시간을 보낼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when elderly people spend time at the senior center.
phrases.en_equiv: to rest at the senior center

phrases.en: The elderly gather at the senior center.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 사람이 함께 모인다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say that several people gather together.
phrases.en_equiv: to gather at the senior center

explain_en: A neighborhood place where older people gather to rest, chat, and eat. Almost every Korean neighborhood has one.

examples.en: You shouldn't talk behind a friend's back.
I had a hard time at work because of gossip.

explain: 그 사람이 없는 곳에서 그 사람을 나쁘게 말하는 거예요. '뒷담화하다' 또는 '뒷담화를 하다'로 써요. 편한 말이라 격식 있는 자리에서는 잘 안 써요.
explain_en: Speaking badly about someone when they are not there. Use '뒷담화하다' or '뒷담화를 하다'. It is casual, so avoid it in formal settings.

examples.en: I put a bookmark in the book.

examples.ko: 친구가 한글이 쓰여 있는 책갈피를 선물했어요.
examples.en: A friend gave me a bookmark with Hangul on it.

explain: 읽던 곳을 표시하려고 책 사이에 끼우는 얇은 물건이에요. '책갈피를 끼우다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: I put a bookmark in the page I was reading.
phrases.nuance_ko: '끼우다'와 같은 뜻으로 써요. 책 사이에 넣는 동작이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as '끼우다'. It is the action of putting it between pages.

phrases.en: I made a bookmark out of paper.
phrases.nuance_ko: 직접 만들 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for making one yourself.

phrases.en: I use a pretty card as a bookmark.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다른 물건을 책갈피 대신 쓸 때 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when using another object in place of a bookmark.

explain_en: A thin item you slip into a book to mark your place. Say '책갈피를 끼우다'.

examples.en: I turned forty this year.
I started a new job at forty.

explain: 나이 마흔 살을 가리키는 말이에요. 공자의 말에서 나왔고, 마흔이 되면 흔들리지 않는다는 뜻이에요. 40대를 '불혹의 나이'라고 해요.
explain_en: A word for age forty. It comes from Confucius and means that at forty you are no longer swayed by doubt. The forties are called '불혹의 나이'.

examples.en: My father turns fifty this year.
My mind has become calmer now that I am fifty.

explain: 나이 쉰 살을 가리키는 말이에요. 하늘의 뜻을 안다는 뜻이고, 불혹 다음 나이예요. 50대를 '지천명의 나이'라고 해요.
explain_en: A word for age fifty, meaning knowing heaven's will. It comes after '불혹'. The fifties are called '지천명의 나이'.

en: to become stable; to settle down

examples.en: My life has settled down at my new job.
My mind calmed down after taking the medicine.

explain: 흔들리거나 불안하던 것이 차분하고 일정해지는 거예요. 마음, 생활, 물가, 직장에 두루 써요. 반대는 '불안하다'예요.
explain_en: To go from shaky or uneasy to calm and steady. It works for feelings, life, prices, and jobs. The opposite is '불안하다'.

en: to talk down to; to treat with disrespect

examples.en: You shouldn't talk down to customers.
Don't look down on me just because I'm young.

explain: 상대를 낮춰 보고 반말이나 무례한 태도로 대하는 거예요. 반대말은 '존대하다'예요. 보통 '~을/를 하대하다'로 써요.
explain_en: To look down on someone and treat them with casual speech or rude manners. The opposite is '존대하다'. It is used as '~을/를 하대하다'.

examples.en: My little brother got sulky over a toy.
Why are you in a huff? Tell me.

explain: 작은 일로 기분이 상해서 말을 안 하거나 토라지는 거예요. 친한 사이에서 가볍게 써요. 표준어는 '삐치다'이지만 '삐지다'도 많이 써요.
explain_en: To get upset over something small and go quiet or pout. It is used lightly between close people. The standard form is '삐치다', but '삐지다' is very common.

en: to boast; to brag; to show off

examples.en: My friend showed off a new bag.
My father often brags about his son.

explain: 자기나 가족이 잘한 일, 가진 것을 다른 사람에게 말하거나 보여 줄 때 써요. '-을/를 자랑하다'로 쓰고, 듣는 사람에게는 얄밉게 들릴 때도 있어요.
explain_en: Used when you tell or show others about something you or your family did well or own. It takes '-을/를', and it can sound annoying to the listener.

en: to sympathize with; to empathize with

examples.en: I really relate to that story.
I listened and empathized with my friend's worries.

explain: 다른 사람의 생각이나 기분이 이해되고 나도 그렇게 느낀다는 뜻이에요. '-에 공감하다'로 써요. '동정하다'와 달리 같은 마음이 되는 거예요.
explain_en: It means you understand someone's feelings or opinion and feel the same way. Use '-에 공감하다'. It is closer to 'relate to' than to 'pity'.

en: to be pitiful; to feel sorry for

examples.en: I feel sorry for my younger sibling working all night.
It pained me to see them moving alone.

explain: 힘들어 보이는 사람이 불쌍하고 마음이 아플 때 써요. 가까운 사람이나 아랫사람에게 쓰는 말이라 윗사람에게는 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: Used when someone's hardship makes you feel sorry and a bit pained. It is for people close to you or below you, not for superiors.

examples.en: The person who set up the blind date contacted me first.
The organizer of this gathering is a senior.

explain: 만남이나 일을 마련해 주는 사람이에요. 소개팅을 이어 주는 사람을 말할 때 많이 써요. '주선하다'에 '-자'가 붙은 말이에요.
explain_en: A person who sets up a meeting or an event. It is often used for the person who arranges a blind date. It comes from '주선하다' plus '-자'.

examples.en: I got the key from the caretaker.
The building superintendent cleans every day.

explain: 건물이나 시설을 맡아서 돌보는 사람이에요. 아파트나 건물에서 많이 들어요. 회사의 '관리자'와는 조금 달라요.

phrases.en: The building manager opens the door every day.
phrases.nuance_ko: 건물을 돌보는 사람을 분명히 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to clearly refer to the person who looks after a building.

phrases.en: I greeted the apartment building manager.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아파트를 돌보는 사람을 말해요. 높일 때는 '관리인께'라고 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the person who looks after an apartment building. '관리인께' is the polite form.

phrases.en: If there is a problem, contact the manager.
phrases.nuance_ko: 고장이나 문제가 생겼을 때 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used when something is broken or there is a problem.

explain_en: A person who looks after a building or facility, as in an apartment complex. It differs from '관리자', which is a manager in a company.

examples.en: The owner gave me a discount.

examples.ko: 이 가게는 오늘 디스카운트 행사를 해요.
examples.en: This shop has a discount sale today.

explain: 값을 깎아 주는 것이에요. 보통 '할인'이라고 하고, '디스카운트'는 가게에서 가끔 써요. '디스카운트(를) 해 주다'로 써요.
explain_en: It means a reduction in price. Koreans usually say '할인', and '디스카운트' is a loanword sometimes used in shops. Use '디스카운트(를) 해 주다'.

en: to manage; to take care of

examples.en: I manage my health by exercising every day.
My younger sibling is managing the shop.

explain: 어떤 일이나 물건, 건강이 좋은 상태가 되도록 맡아서 돌보는 일이에요. '건강을 관리하다', '가게를 관리하다'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: to take care of one's skin
phrases.en_equiv: to take care of one's skin

explain_en: It means to look after something so it stays in good condition or runs well. Used with health, shops, money, files and more.

dis.h: look after and keep in good condition

p.n: 운영하다 only works for running an organization, so it is wrong for health.

examples.en: The new model phone came out yesterday.
This car is a new model released last year.

explain: 기계나 물건의 새로운 모양이나 종류예요. 반대말은 '구형'이에요. 새 휴대폰이나 자동차를 말할 때 많이 써요.
explain_en: A new model or type of a machine or product. Its opposite is '구형' (old model). Common for phones and cars.

en: to to pour; to to swell

examples.en: Please pour water into the cup.
My face is swollen from eating ramen.

explain: '붓다'는 뜻이 두 가지예요. 물 같은 것을 어디에 쏟아 넣을 때도 쓰고, 몸이 부풀어 오를 때도 써요. 활용은 '부어요'로 같아요.
explain_en: '붓다' has two meanings: to pour liquid into something, and to swell up (the body). The conjugation is the same: 부어요.

examples.en: Please keep the room temperature at 20 degrees.
I want to maintain a good relationship with my friend.

explain: 지금의 상태를 바꾸지 않고 그대로 이어 가는 것이에요. '관계를 유지하다', '온도를 유지하다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It means to keep something in its current state without change. Used in phrases like 'maintain a relationship' or 'keep a temperature'.

dis.h: keep a state or condition as it is

p.n: 건강 is a state, not a process, so 지속시키다 sounds unnatural.

examples.en: That accident was a great misfortune for the family.
They say misfortune comes all at once.

explain: 행복하지 않은 상태나 나쁜 일이 생기는 것이에요. 반대말은 '행복'이에요. '불행하다'는 형용사로 써요.

phrases.en: a silver lining; lucky in the midst of misfortune
phrases.en_equiv: a silver lining; lucky in the midst of misfortune

explain_en: A state of not being happy, or a bad event happening. The opposite is '행복'. The adjective is '불행하다'.

examples.en: My anxiety grows before an exam.
He felt anxious about the future.

explain: 마음이 편하지 않고 걱정되는 느낌이에요. '불안을 느끼다', '불안이 크다'처럼 써요. '불안하다'는 형용사예요.
explain_en: A feeling of worry and not being at ease. Say '불안을 느끼다' or '불안이 크다'. The adjective form is '불안하다'.

en: to to curse; to to swear at; to to badmouth

examples.en: Please don't swear while driving.
I was upset that my friend badmouthed me behind my back.

explain: 다른 사람에게 또는 다른 사람에 대해 나쁜 말을 하는 것이에요. 앞에서 직접 할 수도 있고, 없는 곳에서 흉볼 때도 써요. '욕을 하다'와 같아요.
explain_en: To say bad words about or at someone. It can be to their face or behind their back. It is the same as '욕을 하다'.

examples.en: The company analyzed customer data.
Let's analyze the cause of the failure together.

explain: 어떤 것을 여러 부분으로 나누어 자세히 살펴보는 것이에요. 자료, 원인, 결과를 말할 때 많이 써요.
explain_en: To break something into parts and examine it closely. Often used with data, causes and results.

examples.en: That person keeps stalking me.
My ex-boyfriend stalked me on social media.

explain: 싫다고 해도 한 사람을 계속 따라다니거나 몰래 지켜보는 것이에요. 온라인에서 정보를 계속 찾아보는 것에도 써요. 범죄가 될 수 있어요.
explain_en: To keep following or secretly watching a person who does not want it. It is also used for checking someone's information online. It can be a crime.

examples.en: This company has a clear hierarchy.

examples.ko: 위계가 있는 곳에서는 더 조심해야 해요.
examples.en: You have to be more careful in places with a hierarchy.

explain: 지위나 계급에 따라 위아래가 나뉜 순서예요. 회사나 군대처럼 위아래가 분명한 곳에서 말할 때 써요.
explain_en: The order of higher and lower positions based on rank. Used for places with clear levels, like companies or the military.

examples.en: The teacher pointed out my pronunciation.

examples.ko: 문제를 지적만 하지 말고 같이 고쳐 봐요.
examples.en: Don't just point out the problem; let's fix it together.

explain: 잘못이나 문제를 집어서 말하는 것이에요. 도움말 없이 사실만 말할 때 써요. 고쳐 보라고 알려 주는 '조언하다'와 달라요.
explain_en: To name a mistake or problem. It just states the issue without offering help, unlike '조언하다', which also suggests a fix.

examples.ko: 선배가 면접 준비에 대해 조언해 줬어요.
examples.en: My senior gave me advice on preparing for the interview.
The doctor advised me to exercise more.

explain: 어떻게 하면 좋을지 도움이 되는 말을 해 주는 것이에요. 문제를 말하는 '지적하다'와 달리 고치는 방법도 같이 알려 줘요.
explain_en: To give helpful words on what to do. Unlike '지적하다', which only names the problem, it also suggests how to improve.

en: to be shabby; to be squalid; to be grubby

examples.en: The room was grubby, so I cleaned it.
I hate clinging in a pathetic way.

explain: 지저분하고 초라해 보일 때 써요. 사람의 행동이 깔끔하지 못하고 계속 매달리는 모습에도 써요. 조금 거친 말이에요.
explain_en: Used for things that look dirty and shabby, and for people who act unclean or keep clinging. It is a rather blunt word.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 일할 때 아주 진지해요.
examples.en: He is very serious when he works.
I'm not joking, I'm speaking seriously.

explain: 말이나 태도가 가볍지 않고 진심일 때 써요. 나쁜 상황을 말하는 '심각하다'와 달리 사람의 태도에 써요.
explain_en: Describes a sincere, non-joking attitude. Unlike 심각하다, it is about a person's manner, not a bad situation.

examples.en: I sent the contract to the legal team.
The legal team is checking it.

explain: 회사에서 계약이나 법 문제를 맡는 팀이에요. '인사팀', '재무팀'처럼 '-팀'을 붙여 부서를 말해요.

phrases.en: I asked the legal team about the contract.
phrases.nuance_ko: 법 문제를 확인하려고 법무팀에 질문할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when asking the legal team a question to check a legal issue.

phrases.en: There is a legal team meeting this afternoon.
phrases.nuance_ko: 팀 이름 뒤에 다른 명사를 붙여 쓰는 방법이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Shows how to attach another noun after a team name.

phrases.en: A legal team employee looked at the contract.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그 팀에서 일하는 사람을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to refer to a person working in that team.

explain_en: The team in a company that handles contracts and legal issues. Like 인사팀 or 재무팀, -팀 names a department.

examples.en: I took annual leave for tomorrow.
I used my leave and went on a trip.

explain: 회사에서 일정 기간 일하면 받는 유급 휴가예요. '연차를 내다', '연차를 쓰다'로 자주 말해요.
explain_en: Paid leave an employee earns by working. It is commonly used as 연차를 내다 or 연차를 쓰다.

examples.en: I joined this company last year.
I've learned a lot since joining.

explain: 회사에 직원으로 들어갈 때 써요. 반대말은 '퇴사하다'예요.

phrases.en: I want to join that company.
phrases.nuance_ko: 회사에 들어가고 싶은 마음을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to express a wish to get into a company.
phrases.en_equiv: to want to join a company

phrases.en: It has been one year since I joined the company.
phrases.nuance_ko: 회사에 들어온 뒤 시간이 얼마나 지났는지 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say how much time has passed since joining a company.
phrases.en_equiv: it has been one year since joining

phrases.en: I was very nervous on my first day at the company.
phrases.nuance_ko: '입사' 뒤에 명사를 붙여 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing where a noun follows '입사'.

explain_en: Used when you start working at a company as an employee. The opposite is 퇴사하다.

en: to be devout; to be deeply religious

examples.en: He is a devout believer.
My grandmother's faith is very devout.

explain: 종교에 대한 믿음이 깊고 성실할 때 써요. 보통 '독실한 신자'처럼 사람을 꾸며요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 해요체 활용형이에요. 사람의 믿음이 깊다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The polite conjugated form. Used to say that a person's faith is deep.

phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형이에요. 종교 생활을 열심히 하지 않는다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form. Used to say you are not very active in your religion.

phrases.en: They are a family with deep faith.
phrases.nuance_ko: '신앙'을 꾸밀 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing used to modify '신앙' (faith).

explain_en: Describes deep, sincere religious faith. Usually modifies a person, as in 독실한 신자.

en: to to fall into ruin; to to collapse

examples.en: The big company suddenly collapsed.
That family fell into ruin long ago.

explain: 잘나가던 회사·집안·나라가 무너질 때 써요. 일시적인 실패보다 크게 망하는 느낌이에요.

phrases.nuance_ko: '-고 말다'는 나쁜 결과로 끝났다는 느낌을 더해요.
phrases.nuance_en: '-고 말다' adds the feeling that it ended in a bad result.

phrases.en: That shop is gradually going downhill.
phrases.nuance_ko: 천천히 무너지는 과정을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe a slow process of falling apart.

phrases.nuance_ko: 비슷한 뜻이지만 더 일상적이고 편한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar in meaning, but more everyday and casual.

explain_en: Used when a once-thriving company, family or nation falls apart. It implies a major collapse, not a small setback.

en: to to climb up; to to get cheeky with

examples.en: The child climbed up onto the sofa.
You shouldn't get cheeky with adults.

explain: 손발로 기어서 올라간다는 뜻이에요. 아랫사람이 윗사람에게 버릇없이 굴 때도 써요.

phrases.en: The cat climbed up the tree.
phrases.nuance_ko: 손발로 붙잡고 위로 올라가는 모습을 말할 때 써요. 한 단어로 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe going up while gripping with hands and feet. It is written as one word.

phrases.en: The child is climbing onto the chair.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 올라가는 중이라는 진행형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A progressive form meaning the climbing is happening now.

phrases.en: The child got scolded for getting cheeky with an adult.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아랫사람이 윗사람에게 버릇없이 굴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone of lower status is cheeky or disrespectful to someone of higher status.
phrases.en_equiv: to get cheeky with an adult

explain_en: Literally to crawl or scramble up. Also used when someone of lower rank acts disrespectfully toward a superior.

examples.en: The tenant moved out.
The tenant pays monthly rent to the landlord.

explain: 돈을 내고 남의 집에 사는 사람이에요. 집을 가진 사람은 '집주인'이에요.

phrases.en: The landlord is looking for a new tenant.
phrases.nuance_ko: 집을 빌려 줄 사람을 찾을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when looking for someone to rent a home to.

phrases.example: 이번 달부터 이 집의 세입자가 됐어요.
phrases.en: I became a tenant of this house from this month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 남의 집을 빌려서 살기 시작할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you start renting and living in someone else's home.

phrases.en: The new tenant is moving in tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이전 사람 다음에 들어오는 사람을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the person who comes after the previous one.

explain_en: A person who pays to live in someone else's home. The owner is called 집주인.

examples.en: I called the landlord.
Our landlord is kind.

explain: 집을 가지고 있는 사람이에요. 집을 빌려 사는 사람은 '세입자'예요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 여자 집주인을 친근하게 부를 때 써요. 남자는 '집주인 아저씨'라고 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A friendly way to refer to a female landlord. For a man, say '집주인 아저씨'.

phrases.en: I pay rent to the landlord every month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 집을 빌려 살 때 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A phrase often used when renting a home.
phrases.en_equiv: to pay rent to the landlord

phrases.nuance_ko: 집을 가진 사람이 달라졌을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the owner of the house has changed.

explain_en: The person who owns the home. The person renting it is 세입자.

en: new member of the workforce; young professional

examples.en: I became a new working adult this year.
I learned money management tips for young professionals.

explain: 학교를 졸업하고 처음 일을 시작한 사람이에요. 줄여서 '초년생'이라고도 해요.

phrases.en: I am still a newcomer at work.
phrases.nuance_ko: '사회초년생'을 줄인 말처럼 써요. 앞에 말을 붙여 쓸 수도 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used like a short form of '사회초년생'. You can also put another word before it.

phrases.en: My salary was small when I was new to working life.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일을 처음 시작했던 시기를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to talk about the period when you first started working.
phrases.en_equiv: when I was a new worker

phrases.en: Since I'm new to working life, there is a lot I don't know.
phrases.nuance_ko: 경험이 적은 이유를 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to explain a reason for having little experience.

explain_en: Someone who has just graduated and started working. It can be shortened to 초년생.

en: beginner; newcomer (to a field or activity)

examples.en: He is still new to the workforce.
I'm a new driver, so I'm careful.

explain: 어떤 일이나 생활을 막 시작한 사람이에요. '운전 초년생'처럼 앞에 말을 붙여 써요.

phrases.en: I am a beginner at cooking.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞에 활동 이름을 붙여 그 일을 막 시작한 사람을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put an activity name before it to mean someone who just started that activity.

phrases.en: Since I'm a beginner, I make a lot of mistakes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 경험이 적은 이유를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to give the reason for having little experience.

phrases.en: I was very nervous when I was a new driver.
phrases.nuance_ko: 처음 시작했던 시기를 되돌아볼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when looking back at the time you first started.

explain_en: A person who has just started something. Often preceded by a noun, as in 운전 초년생.

examples.en: I've gotten much busier since starting work.
Relationships matter in working life.

explain: 학교 밖에서 일하고 사람을 만나며 사는 생활이에요. 보통 직장 생활을 가리켜요.

phrases.example: 저는 삼 년째 사회생활을 하고 있어요.
phrases.en: I have been working for three years.
phrases.nuance_ko: 직장에서 일하며 지낸다는 뜻으로 가장 많이 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing, meaning to live and work in a job setting.

phrases.en: Working life is harder than I thought.
phrases.nuance_ko: 직장 생활의 어려움을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to talk about the difficulty of working life.

phrases.en: I don't have much work experience.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일하며 쌓은 경험을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to talk about experience gained from working.

explain_en: Life outside school, working and dealing with people. It usually refers to life at work.

examples.en: I was born in 1995.
What year were you born?

explain: 숫자 뒤에 붙어서 태어난 해를 말해요. 나이를 물을 때 '몇 년생이세요?'라고 해요.
explain_en: Attached after a number to give someone's birth year. To ask age, say 몇 년생이세요?

examples.en: I guarantee the quality.
I co-signed my friend's loan.

explain: 품질이나 사람이 믿을 만하다고 책임지고 말할 때 써요. 돈 문제에서는 빚을 대신 책임진다는 뜻이에요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 상대에게 믿어도 된다고 공손하게 약속할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to politely promise someone that they can trust it.

phrases.en: The company does not guarantee that.
phrases.nuance_ko: 책임지지 않는다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say that you do not take responsibility.

phrases.en: I stood as guarantor for my friend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돈 문제에서 다른 사람의 빚을 책임진다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in money matters to mean taking responsibility for someone else's debt.

explain_en: To take responsibility for the quality or reliability of something or someone. With money, it means to back someone's debt.

examples.en: I bought bread at a bakery near my house.
This bakery's cakes are delicious.

explain: 빵과 케이크를 파는 가게예요. '빵집'과 거의 같지만 베이커리가 조금 더 세련된 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: I bought bread at the bakery in the morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 더 일상적이고 편한 말이에요. 동네 가게 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: A more everyday, casual word. It feels like a neighborhood shop.

phrases.en: I had coffee at a bakery cafe.
phrases.nuance_ko: 빵도 팔고 앉아서 마실 수도 있는 카페를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A cafe that sells bread and also lets you sit and drink.

phrases.en: A new bakery opened in the neighborhood.
phrases.nuance_ko: 집 가까이에 있는 베이커리를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to talk about a bakery near your home.

explain_en: A shop selling bread and cakes. It means about the same as 빵집, but sounds a bit more stylish.

en: to be shiny; to be flashy; to be superficially attractive

examples.en: It's a shop that's all show.
He's all talk and no action.

explain: 겉만 반짝이고 좋아 보이는데 속은 별로일 때 써요. '말만 번지르르하다'처럼 자주 말해요.

phrases.en: I was fooled by smooth talk.
phrases.nuance_ko: 듣기에는 좋지만 믿을 수 없는 말을 가리킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to words that sound good but cannot be trusted.

phrases.example: 그 가게는 번지르르해 보여도 음식이 별로예요.
phrases.en: That shop looks flashy, but the food isn't great.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉모습만 화려하게 보일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when something only looks fancy on the outside.

phrases.example: 그 사람은 말이 번지르르하지 않지만 믿을 수 있어요.
phrases.en: He isn't a smooth talker, but you can trust him.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형이에요. 겉만 좋게 꾸미지 않았다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form. It means something is not dressed up only on the surface.

explain_en: Looks shiny and impressive on the outside but lacks substance. Common in 말만 번지르르하다.

examples.en: This game ended in defeat.
It isn't easy to admit defeat.

explain: 경기나 싸움에서 지는 것이에요. '패배하다'로도 쓰고, 반대말은 '승리'예요.
explain_en: Losing a game or battle. It also works as 패배하다; the opposite is 승리.

en: to be itchy; to feel ticklish

examples.en: My throat tickles and I'm coughing.
My back is itchy.

explain: 몸의 한 부분이 살살 가려워서 긁고 싶거나 기침이 나올 것 같을 때 써요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 더 흔하게 쓰는 말이에요. 몸이 가려운 느낌을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A more common word for the itchy or ticklish feeling on the body.

phrases.en: My nose tickles, so I sneeze.
phrases.nuance_ko: 재채기가 나올 것 같은 느낌에 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used for the feeling that you are about to sneeze.

phrases.en: I have a tickling feeling in my throat.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-ㄴ'을 붙여 '느낌'을 꾸미는 쓰임이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses '-ㄴ' to modify the noun '느낌' (feeling).

explain_en: Describes a light tickling or itching feeling in part of the body, like an urge to scratch or cough.

examples.ko: 어릴 때부터 파리에 대한 동경이 있었어요.
examples.en: Since I was little, I've had a longing for Paris.

examples.ko: 그 배우는 많은 청소년의 동경의 대상이에요.
examples.en: That actor is an object of admiration for many teenagers.

explain: 어떤 사람이나 곳을 멋있다고 느끼고 닮고 싶거나 가 보고 싶어 하는 마음이에요. 보통 '동경하다', '동경의 대상'으로 써요.

phrases.en: to yearn for; to look up to
phrases.en_equiv: to yearn for; to look up to

explain_en: A feeling of admiring someone or something and wanting to be like them or go there. Usually used as 동경하다 or 동경의 대상.

examples.en: This year I switched from sales to marketing.
I went to the sea to change my mood.

explain: 방향, 방법, 상태가 다른 것으로 바뀌는 것을 말해요. '~(으)로 전환하다', '전환되다'로 자주 써요.

phrases.en: a change of mood; a refresher
phrases.en_equiv: a change of mood; a refresher

explain_en: A change of direction, method, or state to something different. Often used as ~(으)로 전환하다 or 전환되다.

examples.en: The chicks are peeping.

examples.ko: 아이들이 병아리 소리를 삐약삐약 따라 했어요.
examples.en: The children imitated the chicks, going peep-peep.

explain: 병아리가 우는 소리예요. 소리를 흉내 내는 말이라서 '삐약삐약 울어요'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: I can hear a peep-peep sound.
phrases.nuance_ko: '소리' 앞에 붙여 병아리 소리를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put before '소리' to refer to the sound of chicks.

phrases.nuance_ko: '하고'를 넣어 소리를 그대로 옮기는 말투예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '하고' repeats the sound as it is made.

phrases.en: The peeping chicks follow their mother.
phrases.nuance_ko: 소리를 넣어서 병아리를 귀엽게 말하는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A cute way to refer to chicks by including their sound.

explain_en: The sound a chick makes. It imitates the sound, so it is used like 삐약삐약 울어요.

examples.en: A calf was born on the farm.
The calf follows its mother.

explain: 소의 새끼예요. 말의 새끼는 '망아지', 개의 새끼는 '강아지'예요.

phrases.en: There is one calf on the farm.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동물을 셀 때는 '마리'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '마리' when counting animals.

phrases.en: The baby calf is eating grass.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어린 송아지를 귀엽게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to refer to a young calf in a cute way.

phrases.nuance_ko: 동물을 돌보며 기른다는 뜻의 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing meaning to care for and raise an animal.

explain_en: A baby cow. A baby horse is 망아지 and a baby dog is 강아지.

examples.en: I was born in the year of the pig.
They say people born in the year of the pig have good luck this year.

explain: 돼지해에 태어난 사람의 띠예요. 한국에서는 나이를 물을 때 '무슨 띠예요?'라고 자주 물어요.
explain_en: The zodiac sign of a person born in the year of the pig. Koreans often ask 무슨 띠예요? when talking about age.

examples.en: That actor has a puppy-like face, so he's very popular.
I like the cat-like look better than the puppy-like look.

explain: 강아지처럼 둥글고 순하고 귀여운 인상의 얼굴이에요. 사람의 얼굴을 말할 때 써요.

phrases.en: My friend has a puppy-like face.
phrases.nuance_ko: '이에요'를 붙여서 사람의 얼굴 인상을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add '이에요' to say what kind of face a person has.

phrases.en: I feel comfortable with people who have puppy-like faces.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-인'으로 뒤에 오는 사람을 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '-인' to describe the person that follows.
phrases.en_equiv: a person with a puppy-like face

phrases.en: He has a puppy-like face, so he looks kind.
phrases.nuance_ko: '얼굴'을 붙이면 얼굴 인상을 말한다는 것이 더 분명해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '얼굴' makes it clear you are talking about the face.

explain_en: A face with a round, gentle, cute look like a puppy. Used to describe a person's face.

examples.ko: 눈이 길어서 고양이상이라는 말을 자주 들어요.
examples.en: My eyes are long, so I often hear that I have a cat-like face.

examples.ko: 고양이상은 조금 차가워 보일 수 있어요.
examples.en: A cat-like face can look a little cold.

explain: 고양이처럼 눈매가 길고 선이 또렷하고 날카로운 인상의 얼굴이에요. 강아지상과 같이 많이 써요.

phrases.en: My younger sibling has a cat-like face.
phrases.nuance_ko: '이에요'를 붙여서 사람의 얼굴 인상을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add '이에요' to say what kind of face a person has.

phrases.en: An actor with a cat-like face is in this movie.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-인'으로 뒤에 오는 사람을 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '-인' to describe the person that follows.
phrases.en_equiv: an actor with a cat-like face

phrases.en: She has a cat-like face, so she looks cool.
phrases.nuance_ko: '얼굴'을 붙이면 얼굴 인상을 말한다는 것이 더 분명해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '얼굴' makes it clear you are talking about the face.

explain_en: A face with long eyes and sharp, clear features like a cat. Often used together with 강아지상.

examples.en: When I go to the seaside, I always eat haemultang.
On a cold day, hot haemultang is the best.

explain: 게, 조개, 오징어 같은 여러 해산물을 넣고 얼큰하게 끓인 국물 요리예요. 보통 여럿이 함께 먹어요.

phrases.en: Excuse me, one seafood stew, please.
phrases.nuance_ko: 식당에서 음식을 주문할 때 바로 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A handy phrase for ordering at a restaurant.

phrases.en: It's cold, so I want to eat a spicy seafood stew.
phrases.nuance_ko: 해물탕의 맛을 말할 때 '얼큰한'을 자주 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: '얼큰한' is the word often used to describe the taste of this stew.

phrases.en: On the weekend, my family and I cooked and ate seafood stew.
phrases.nuance_ko: 집에서 직접 만들 때는 '끓이다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '끓이다' when you cook it yourself at home.

explain_en: A spicy stew with many kinds of seafood such as crab, clams, and squid. It is usually shared by a group.

examples.en: I had a grilled mackerel set meal for lunch.
Grilled mackerel goes really well with rice.

explain: 고등어를 소금을 뿌려 불에 구운 요리예요. 밥과 같이 먹는 흔한 반찬이에요.

phrases.en: I ordered the grilled mackerel set meal at the restaurant.
phrases.nuance_ko: 밥, 국, 반찬이 같이 나오는 한 상 메뉴를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a set meal that comes with rice, soup, and side dishes.

phrases.en: I made grilled mackerel at home for dinner.
phrases.nuance_ko: 집에서 직접 요리할 때는 '만들다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '만들다' when you cook the dish yourself at home.

phrases.en: Today's side dish is grilled mackerel.
phrases.nuance_ko: 밥상에 나오는 반찬으로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when talking about it as a side dish on the table.
phrases.en_equiv: grilled mackerel as a side dish

explain_en: Mackerel salted and grilled over heat. It is a common side dish eaten with rice.

examples.en: I mixed rice with the soy sauce marinated crab and ate it.
