Soy sauce marinated crab is salty, so you need a lot of rice.

explain: 날게를 간장 양념에 담가 숙성한 음식이에요. 밥도둑이라고 불러요.

phrases.en: a dish that makes you eat lots of rice
phrases.en_equiv: a dish that makes you eat lots of rice

explain_en: Raw crab aged in a soy sauce marinade. It is nicknamed 밥도둑 (rice thief) because it makes you eat a lot of rice.

examples.en: I tried live octopus at the market.

examples.ko: 산낙지는 꿈틀거려서 천천히 씹어 먹어야 해요.
examples.en: Live octopus wriggles, so you have to chew it slowly.

explain: 살아 있는 낙지예요. 보통 참기름장에 찍어 바로 먹어요.

phrases.en: Excuse me, one plate of live octopus, please.
phrases.nuance_ko: 식당에서 양을 말해 주문할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to order a portion at a restaurant.

phrases.en: There is a lot of fresh live octopus at the market.
phrases.nuance_ko: 신선한 정도를 말할 때 '싱싱한'과 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Pairs with '싱싱한' to say it is fresh.

phrases.en: I dip the live octopus in sesame oil sauce and eat it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 산낙지를 먹는 방법을 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to explain how to eat live octopus.
phrases.en_equiv: to dip live octopus in sesame oil sauce

explain_en: A small octopus that is still alive, usually dipped in sesame oil sauce and eaten right away.

examples.en: I bought and ate kimchi jeonbyeong at the market.
Buckwheat jeonbyeong is eaten together with acorn jelly.

explain: 쌀가루나 메밀가루 반죽을 얇게 부쳐서 속을 넣고 만 음식이에요. 강원도 전병이 유명해요.

phrases.en: My mother pan-fried jeonbyeong for me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 전병의 얇은 반죽을 팬에 익힐 때는 '부치다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '부치다' for cooking the thin batter in a pan.

phrases.example: 전병 한 접시를 시켜서 나눠 먹었어요.
phrases.en: We ordered a plate of jeonbyeong and shared it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 식당이나 시장에서 양을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to say the amount at a restaurant or market.

phrases.en: The jeonbyeong with filling is really delicious.
phrases.nuance_ko: 전병은 속을 넣어 말아서 먹는 음식이라는 점을 말해 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: Shows that jeonbyeong is rolled up with a filling inside.

explain_en: A thin pancake made from rice or buckwheat batter, often rolled around a filling. The ones from Gangwon-do are famous.

examples.en: I drank sikhye at the jjimjilbang.
On holidays, we make sikhye at home.

explain: 엿기름과 밥으로 만든 달콤한 전통 음료예요. 차갑게 마시고, 찜질방에서 맥반석 계란과 같이 먹는 경우가 많아요.

phrases.en: On a hot day, cold sikhye is good.
phrases.nuance_ko: 식혜는 차갑게 마시는 음료라서 '시원한'과 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Sikhye is drunk cold, so it goes well with '시원한'.

phrases.en: Do you want to have a glass of sikhye before you go?
phrases.nuance_ko: 음료는 '한 잔'으로 양을 세요.
phrases.nuance_en: Drinks are counted with '한 잔'.

phrases.nuance_ko: 식혜의 맛을 말할 때 '달콤한'을 자주 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: '달콤한' is often used to describe the taste of sikhye.

explain_en: A sweet traditional drink made from malt and rice. It is drunk cold and often paired with baked eggs at a jjimjilbang.

examples.en: I put braised quail eggs in my lunch box.

examples.ko: 메추리알은 작아서 한입에 먹을 수 있어요.
examples.en: Quail eggs are small, so you can eat one in a bite.

explain: 메추리의 작은 알이에요. 장조림이나 간식으로 많이 먹어요.

phrases.en: I boiled quail eggs and ate them as a snack.
phrases.nuance_ko: 알을 물에 익힐 때는 '삶다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '삶다' for boiling eggs in water.

phrases.en: I bought a pack of quail eggs at the mart.
phrases.nuance_ko: 마트에서 포장된 것을 살 때 '한 팩'으로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '한 팩' for the packaged ones sold at a mart.

phrases.example: 메추리알 껍질을 까는 게 조금 어려워요.
phrases.en: Peeling the shells of quail eggs is a little hard.
phrases.nuance_ko: 삶은 알의 껍질을 벗길 때는 '까다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '까다' for peeling the shell off a boiled egg.

explain_en: The small egg of a quail. It is often eaten braised in soy sauce or as a snack.

en: al dente; slightly firm and chewy

examples.en: I cooked the ramyeon al dente.
I like slightly firm noodles.

explain: 밥이나 면이 약간 단단하고 쫄깃하게 익은 느낌이에요. '꼬들꼬들하다'로도 쓰고, 보통 일부러 덜 익혔을 때 좋은 뜻으로 말해요.
explain_en: Describes rice or noodles cooked slightly firm and chewy. Also used as 꼬들꼬들하다, usually in a good sense.

en: (of cooked rice) fluffy and firm, grains separate

examples.en: The rice came out fluffy and well cooked.
Fried rice tastes best when made with fluffy, separate-grained rice.

explain: 밥이 질지 않고 알알이 떨어지며 잘 지어진 모양이에요. '고슬고슬하다'로도 써요. 볶음밥에 특히 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: Describes rice that is not sticky, with grains that stay separate. Also used as 고슬고슬하다. It suits fried rice especially.

examples.ko: 오래된 한옥 마을에는 옛 정취가 남아 있어요.
examples.en: The old hanok village still has its old-time charm.
I felt the charm of the season in the autumn mountains.

explain: 어떤 곳이나 계절에서 느껴지는 멋과 분위기예요. '정취가 있다', '정취를 느끼다'로 자주 써요.
explain_en: The charm and mood you feel from a place or season. Often used as 정취가 있다 or 정취를 느끼다.

examples.ko: 이 동네는 상권이 좋아서 가게가 많아요.
examples.en: This neighborhood has a good commercial district, so there are many shops.
The trade area grew after the new subway station opened.

explain: 가게들이 모여 있어서 손님이 오가는 지역이나 장사가 이루어지는 범위예요. '상권이 좋다', '상권이 발달하다'로 써요.

phrases.en: for a commercial area to develop
phrases.en_equiv: for a commercial area to develop

explain_en: An area where shops cluster and customers come and go, or the range a business draws from. Used as 상권이 좋다 or 상권이 발달하다.

examples.en: It was hot, so I bought a handheld fan.
I carry a handheld fan in my bag.

explain: 손에 들고 쓰는 작은 선풍기예요. 여름에 밖에서 많이 써요.

phrases.en: to turn on a handheld fan
phrases.en_equiv: to turn on a handheld fan

explain_en: A small fan you hold in your hand. People use it a lot outdoors in summer.

examples.en: I traveled around Jeju for six days.
The exam is in six days.

explain: 여섯 날 동안, 또는 그달의 여섯째 날을 뜻해요. 이틀·사흘·나흘·닷새·엿새처럼 고유어로 날수를 세요.
explain_en: Means six days, or the sixth day of a month. It belongs to the native Korean day-counting series: 이틀, 사흘, 나흘, 닷새, 엿새.

examples.en: I'm busy the day after tomorrow, so let's meet three days from now.
My friend's birthday is three days from now.

explain: 모레의 다음 날이에요. 오늘, 내일, 모레, 글피 순서로 말해요.

phrases.en: I have to hand in my homework by two days after tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기한을 말할 때 '까지'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add '까지' to give a deadline.

phrases.en: I take a plane the morning of two days after tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그날의 시간대를 같이 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to name a time of day on that date.
phrases.en_equiv: the morning two days after tomorrow

phrases.en: I'll contact you again around two days after tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: '쯤'을 붙이면 정확하지 않은 때를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '쯤' makes it approximate.

explain_en: The day after the day after tomorrow. The order is 오늘, 내일, 모레, 글피.

examples.en: I bought tableware for my new home.
The tableware is in this drawer.

explain: 그릇, 수저, 컵처럼 식사에 쓰는 물건을 모두 묶어 부르는 말이에요. '-류'는 '종류'라는 뜻이에요.

phrases.en: I organized the tableware on the weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그릇과 수저를 한꺼번에 정리할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it for tidying dishes and utensils all at once.

phrases.nuance_ko: 부엌에서 쓰는 식사 도구를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it for the dining items used in the kitchen.

phrases.en: I received a tableware set as a gift.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그릇, 수저, 컵을 묶어서 팔 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it for dishes, utensils, and cups sold together.

explain_en: A group word for bowls, spoons, cups and other things used for meals. The suffix -류 means 'kind' or 'category'.

examples.en: I have a lot to study these days.
I increase my study load before exams.

explain: '공부'와 '양'이 합쳐진 말이에요. 보통 '많다', '적다', '늘리다'와 함께 써요.
explain_en: A compound of 공부 (study) and 양 (amount). It usually goes with 많다, 적다 or 늘리다.

en: children's song (童謠); agitation, unrest (動搖)

examples.en: I sang a lot of children's songs when I was little.
The child sings along to nursery rhymes.

explain: 아이들이 부르는 노래를 뜻해요. 같은 소리의 '동요(動搖)'는 마음이나 사회가 흔들리는 것이라 뜻이 달라요.
explain_en: Means a song for children. The same-sounding 동요 (動搖) means agitation or unrest, which is a different word.

examples.en: I bought clothes for my nephew at a children's clothing store.
This brand sells children's clothing too.

explain: 아이들이 입는 옷이에요. '남성복', '여성복'처럼 '-복'이 붙은 말과 같이 알아 두면 좋아요.
explain_en: Clothes for children. Learn it together with 남성복 and 여성복, which also use -복 for 'clothing'.

examples.en: I rode the Ferris wheel at the amusement park.
You can see the night view well from the Ferris wheel.

explain: 놀이공원에서 천천히 돌아가는 큰 바퀴 모양의 놀이기구예요. '타다'와 함께 써요.

phrases.en: I rode the Ferris wheel with my friend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 놀이기구는 '타다'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Rides are used with '타다' (to ride).

phrases.en: I took photos inside the Ferris wheel.
phrases.nuance_ko: 관람차 칸 안쪽을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it for the inside of the Ferris wheel car.

phrases.example: 이 공원에는 아주 높은 관람차가 있어요.
phrases.en: This park has a very tall Ferris wheel.
phrases.nuance_ko: 관람차의 크기를 말할 때 '높은'과 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Pairs with '높은' to describe its height.

explain_en: The big slowly turning wheel ride at an amusement park. It goes with the verb 타다.

examples.en: There is a restaurant area in the department store basement.

examples.ko: 이 동네 식당가는 저녁에 사람이 많아요.
examples.en: The restaurant row in this neighborhood is crowded in the evening.

explain: 식당이 모여 있는 거리나 층이에요. '-가'는 '거리, 지역'이라는 뜻이에요.

phrases.en: Shall we eat lunch at the restaurant area?
phrases.nuance_ko: '에서'를 붙여 식사하는 장소를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add '에서' to name the place where you eat.

phrases.en: There are many good restaurants in the restaurant alley.
phrases.nuance_ko: 식당이 모인 작은 길을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it for a small street lined with restaurants.

phrases.en: This is a famous restaurant district in Seoul.
phrases.nuance_ko: 식당이 모인 곳이 유명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when a restaurant area is well known.

explain_en: A street or floor where many restaurants are clustered. The suffix -가 means 'street' or 'district'.

examples.en: The school lunch is tasty.
I eat the school-provided meal for lunch.

explain: 학교나 회사에서 단체로 주는 밥이에요. '급식을 먹다', '급식실'처럼 써요.
explain_en: Meals served to a group at a school or workplace. Used as 급식을 먹다 or 급식실 (lunchroom).

examples.en: Volunteers served the food.
We lined up and got our food.

explain: 많은 사람에게 음식을 나눠 주는 일이에요. '배식을 하다', '배식을 받다'로 써요.

phrases.en: The food distribution time is twelve o'clock.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음식을 나눠 주는 때를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it for the time food is handed out.

phrases.en: They give out free meals at the park.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돈을 받지 않고 음식을 나눠 줄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when food is given out for free.

phrases.en: People are waiting for the food distribution.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음식을 받으려고 기다리는 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it for people waiting to receive food.
phrases.en_equiv: to wait for food to be served

explain_en: Handing out food to many people. Used as 배식을 하다 (to serve) and 배식을 받다 (to receive a serving).

examples.en: I lived in a boarding house when I was a college student.
The landlady of the boarding house cooked for us.

explain: 남의 집에서 돈을 내고 방을 빌리고 밥도 먹는 것이에요. '하숙하다', '하숙집'으로 써요.
explain_en: Renting a room in someone's house with meals included. Used as 하숙하다 or 하숙집 (boarding house).

en: homestay; lodging in a private house

examples.en: I stayed at a homestay in a country village.
Homestays by the sea are cheap.

explain: 호텔이 아니라 보통 사람이 사는 집에서 돈을 내고 하룻밤 자는 것이에요. '민박하다'로도 써요.
explain_en: Paying to stay overnight in an ordinary person's home rather than a hotel. Also used as the verb 민박하다.

en: accommodations for students studying for exams

examples.en: I studied at a gosiwon.
The room in the gosiwon is very small.

explain: 작은 방이 많은 값싼 숙소예요. 원래 시험 준비생이 살았지만 지금은 학생이나 직장인도 살아요.

phrases.en: I live in a gosiwon right now.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사는 곳을 말할 때 '에 살다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '에 살다' to say where you live.

phrases.en: The gosiwon monthly rent is cheap, which is good.
phrases.nuance_ko: 매달 내는 방값을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it for the rent paid each month.

phrases.en: Life in a gosiwon is a little hard.
phrases.nuance_ko: 고시원에서 지내는 생활을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it for the experience of living in a gosiwon.

explain_en: A cheap lodging with many tiny rooms. It was first for exam candidates, but now students and workers live there too.

examples.en: I will stay a few more days.
I stayed at the hotel for two days.

explain: 한 곳에 잠시 있는 것을 말해요. '머물다'와 같은 말이에요. '머물러요', '머무를 거예요'처럼 써요.
explain_en: To stay in one place for a while. It is the same as 머물다; forms include 머물러요 and 머무를 거예요.

examples.en: I went to the OB-GYN.
I made an appointment at the OB-GYN.

explain: 임신, 출산, 여성의 몸을 보는 병원 진료과예요. '산부인과에 가다'로 써요.

phrases.en: The OB-GYN appointment is at two in the afternoon.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병원에서 의사에게 보는 진료를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it for a medical visit with the doctor.

phrases.nuance_ko: 그 과의 의사를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it for a doctor in this department.

phrases.en: I had an exam at the OB-GYN.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병원에서 검사를 받을 때 '검사를 받다'와 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Pairs with '검사를 받다' for getting tests at the clinic.
phrases.en_equiv: to get an exam at the OB-GYN

explain_en: The hospital department for pregnancy, childbirth and women's health. Used as 산부인과에 가다.

examples.en: I brush my teeth before bed.
I brushed my teeth after eating.

explain: 이를 닦는 것이에요. 보통 '양치하다'나 '양치질을 하다'로 말해요.
explain_en: Brushing your teeth. Usually said as 양치하다 or 양치질을 하다.

en: thorough cleaning; major cleaning of a whole place

examples.en: I did a deep clean over the weekend.
We do a big clean before the Lunar New Year.

explain: 집이나 사무실 전체를 크게 청소하는 것이에요. '대청소를 하다'로 써요.

phrases.en: Today is our house's big cleaning day.
phrases.nuance_ko: 크게 청소하기로 한 날을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it for the day set aside for a big clean.

phrases.en: I finished the big cleaning in the evening.
phrases.nuance_ko: 청소가 끝났다는 것을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to say the cleaning is done.

phrases.example: 연말 대청소로 안 쓰는 물건을 버렸어요.
phrases.en: I threw away things I don't use in the year-end big cleaning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 해가 끝날 때 하는 큰 청소를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the big clean done at the end of the year.

explain_en: A thorough cleaning of a whole house or office. Used as 대청소를 하다.

examples.en: I ironed my shirt.
Please iron the clothes and wear them.

explain: 다리미로 옷의 주름을 펴는 것이에요. 신체의 '다리'나 도구 '다리미'와 헷갈리지 마세요.
explain_en: To press wrinkles out of clothes with an iron. Don't confuse it with 다리 (leg) or 다리미 (the iron itself).

examples.en: Rub your hands with soap to wash them.
I rubbed the stain, but it didn't come out.

explain: 손이나 도구를 대고 앞뒤로 비비는 것이에요. '르' 불규칙이라 '문질러요', '문질렀어요'가 돼요.

phrases.en: I rubbed and wiped the table.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문지른 뒤에 닦아서 깨끗하게 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it for rubbing and then wiping something clean.

phrases.en: Even if your eyes hurt, don't rub them.
phrases.nuance_ko: 하지 말라고 부탁하거나 말릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to ask someone not to rub something.

phrases.en: I rubbed my hands to make them warm.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문지른 방법이나 이유를 이어서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to connect the rubbing with what follows.

explain_en: To press and move something back and forth on a surface. It is a 르-irregular verb: 문질러요, 문질렀어요.

examples.en: I sweep the floor with a broom.
I'm sweeping the fallen leaves in the yard.

explain: 빗자루로 먼지나 쓰레기를 한곳으로 모을 때 써요. '바닥을 쓸다'처럼 '을/를'과 함께 써요.
explain_en: Used for gathering dust or trash with a broom. It takes an object, as in '바닥을 쓸다'.

examples.en: I put the meat in the freezer.
There is ice cream in the freezer.

explain: 냉장고에서 음식을 얼리는 칸이에요. 차갑게 보관하는 칸은 '냉장실'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: to take out of the freezer
phrases.en_equiv: to take out of the freezer

explain_en: The part of a refrigerator that freezes food. The cool (not frozen) section is '냉장실'.

examples.en: I checked the expiration date on the milk.
I threw away the bread that was past its date.

explain: 가게에서 그 식품을 팔 수 있는 마지막 날이에요. '유통기한이 지나다'로 자주 써요.

phrases.en: to be past the expiration date
phrases.en_equiv: to be past the expiration date

explain_en: The last date a food can be sold in stores. Often used as '유통기한이 지나다' (to be past the date).

examples.en: I bought a floral dress.
The floral pattern on this curtain is pretty.

explain: 꽃 모양으로 된 무늬예요. '꽃무늬 원피스'처럼 다른 명사 앞에 붙여 써요.
explain_en: A pattern made of flowers. It often comes before another noun, as in '꽃무늬 원피스'.

examples.en: My pants got torn.
It's a jacket with a torn sleeve.

explain: 종이나 옷이 저절로 또는 힘을 받아 갈라질 때 써요. 사람이 찢으면 '찢다', 그 결과는 '찢어지다'예요.
explain_en: Used when paper or cloth tears. '찢다' is to tear something; '찢어지다' is for the thing that ends up torn.

en: to send out; to let out

examples.en: I sent the kids outside.
I let the puppy out into the yard.

explain: 안에 있는 사람이나 동물을 밖으로 나가게 할 때 써요. 회사에서 사람을 그만두게 할 때도 써요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 다른 사람에게 부탁할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when asking someone else to do it.

phrases.en: Please don't send the child outside alone.
phrases.nuance_ko: 하지 말라고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to say not to do this.

phrases.en: I let the puppy out and closed the door.
phrases.nuance_ko: 내보낸 다음에 이어지는 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to link what happens after sending something out.

explain_en: Used for making a person or animal go from inside to outside. It can also mean to let someone go from a job.

examples.en: I decorated the room anew.
I study with the feeling of a fresh start.

explain: '새롭게'와 뜻이 비슷해요. 말할 때보다 글에서 더 자주 써요.

phrases.en: I decorated the room in a new way.
phrases.nuance_ko: '새로이'와 뜻이 같고 말할 때도 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as '새로이' and natural in speech too.

phrases.nuance_ko: 말할 때 가장 많이 쓰는 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The easiest and most common form in everyday speech.

phrases.en: The shop newly opened its doors.
phrases.nuance_ko: 새로 시작하는 일을 글처럼 정중하게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it in a formal, written-like way for something starting fresh.

explain_en: Similar to '새롭게'. It appears more in writing than in speech.

examples.en: We use the spoken style in conversation.
This novel is written in a colloquial style.

explain: 말할 때 쓰는 말투예요. 글을 쓸 때 쓰는 '문어체'와 짝이 돼요.

phrases.en: This book has many spoken-style expressions.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말할 때 쓰는 말을 가리킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it for expressions used in speech.

phrases.en: I wrote a letter to my friend in a spoken style.
phrases.nuance_ko: 글을 말하듯이 쓸 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it for writing the way you would speak.
phrases.en_equiv: to write in a spoken style

phrases.en: Spoken style and written style are different.
phrases.nuance_ko: 두 문체를 함께 비교할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when comparing the two styles.

explain_en: The style used in speaking. It pairs with '문어체', the style used in writing.

examples.en: We write reports in the written style.
News articles are close to the written style.

explain: 글을 쓸 때 쓰는 문체예요. 말할 때 쓰는 '구어체'와 짝이 돼요.

phrases.en: This sentence is a written-style expression.
phrases.nuance_ko: 글에서 쓰는 말을 가리킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it for expressions used in writing.

phrases.en: Exam questions have many written-style sentences.
phrases.nuance_ko: 글처럼 딱딱한 문장을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it for formal, text-like sentences.

phrases.en: Try changing the spoken style into the written style.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말투를 글 말투로 고칠 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it for turning spoken wording into written wording.

explain_en: The style used in writing. It pairs with '구어체', the style used in speech.

examples.en: Forsythia blooms in spring.
The roadside is full of yellow forsythia.

explain: 이른 봄에 노란 꽃이 피는 나무예요. 한국에서는 봄을 알리는 꽃으로 많이 말해요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 나무가 아니라 꽃을 말할 때 '꽃'을 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add '꽃' when you mean the flower, not the whole shrub.

phrases.en: The forsythia fades and the cherry blossoms bloom.
phrases.nuance_ko: 꽃이 떨어지고 끝날 때는 '지다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '지다' when flowers fall and finish blooming.

phrases.en: I went to the park to see the forsythia.
phrases.nuance_ko: 꽃을 보러 갈 때 '구경'을 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '구경' for going out to see flowers.

explain_en: A shrub with yellow flowers in early spring. In Korea it is a well-known sign that spring has come.

examples.en: I tend my garden every weekend.
My grandmother carefully tends her vegetable patch.

explain: 식물이나 얼굴, 몸을 정성 들여 보기 좋게 만들 때 써요. '정원을 가꾸다', '피부를 가꾸다'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: to take care of one's skin
phrases.en_equiv: to take care of one's skin

explain_en: Used for taking care of plants, skin, or looks so they stay nice. For example, '정원을 가꾸다' or '피부를 가꾸다'.

examples.en: The leaves turned light green.
I wore a light green T-shirt.

explain: 노란빛이 도는 연한 초록색이에요. 봄에 막 나온 잎의 색을 말할 때 자주 써요.

phrases.en: In spring, light yellow-green leaves are pretty.
phrases.nuance_ko: '연두색'과 같은 색인데 빛깔의 느낌을 말해요. 표준 맞춤법은 '연둣빛'이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same color as '연두색', with more of a sense of hue. The standard spelling is '연둣빛'.

phrases.en: Yellow-green leaves came out on the tree.
phrases.nuance_ko: 새로 나온 잎의 색을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used for the color of newly sprouted leaves.

phrases.nuance_ko: 색을 고르고 칠할 때 '으로'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add '으로' when choosing a color to paint with.

explain_en: A light green with a yellow tint. Often used for the color of fresh spring leaves.

examples.en: A sprout came up in the pot.
Sprouts come up in spring.

explain: 씨에서 막 나온 어린 싹이에요. 새로 시작하는 사람이나 일을 비유할 때도 써요.

phrases.en: for a sprout to come up
phrases.en_equiv: for a sprout to come up

explain_en: A young shoot that has just come out of a seed. It is also used figuratively for newcomers or new beginnings.

en: to be rough; to be unrefined

examples.en: It's a rough-looking bowl, but I like it.
He has a blunt way of speaking.

explain: 모양이나 말투가 거칠고 세련되지 않을 때 써요. 꼭 나쁜 뜻만은 아니고, 소박하고 정겨운 느낌을 줄 때도 있어요.

phrases.en: This cup looks rough and unrefined.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉모습이 거칠고 세련되지 않을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when something looks rough and unrefined.

phrases.nuance_ko: 거칠지만 정겨운 느낌으로 말할 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Can carry a rough but warm, affectionate feeling.

phrases.en: The taste is rustic, but it's really delicious.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉은 거칠어도 좋은 점이 있다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to say that despite being rough, it has a good side.

explain_en: Describes a look or manner that is rough and not refined. It isn't always negative; it can feel plain and homely.

examples.en: Flowers are blooming by the roadside.
I parked the car by the roadside.

explain: 길의 가장자리예요. '길가에', '길가의 꽃'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: They sell fruit on the side of the road.
phrases.nuance_ko: '에서'를 붙이면 그곳에서 하는 일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add '에서' to say what happens there.

phrases.en: I bought coffee at a roadside shop.
phrases.nuance_ko: 길 옆에 있는 가게를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it for a shop right next to the road.

phrases.en: I stood by the roadside and waited for my friend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 길 가장자리에 서 있을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it for standing at the edge of the road.

explain_en: The edge of a road. Used as in '길가에' (by the roadside) or '길가의 꽃'.

examples.en: The child drew on the ground with a stick.
I walked leaning on a stick.

explain: 가늘고 긴 나무나 쇠 조각이에요. '막대기로 ~을 하다'처럼 도구로 자주 써요.

phrases.en: I picked up a wooden stick in the yard.
phrases.nuance_ko: 무엇으로 만든 막대기인지 말할 때 앞에 재료를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put the material before the word to say what the stick is made of.

phrases.en: The teacher pointed at the board with a stick.
phrases.nuance_ko: 막대기를 도구로 쓸 때는 '-(으)로'와 함께 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: When the stick is used as a tool, it goes with '-(으)로'.

phrases.en: Grandfather walks holding a long stick.
phrases.nuance_ko: 모양이나 크기를 설명하는 말을 앞에 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add a word for shape or size in front to describe the stick.

explain_en: A long, thin piece of wood or metal. Often used as a tool, as in '막대기로 ~을 하다'.

examples.en: The test result is normal.
I climbed to the top of the mountain.

explain: '正常'은 이상이 없는 보통 상태이고, '頂上'은 산의 가장 높은 곳이에요. 소리는 같고 뜻은 달라서 문장을 보고 구분해요.
explain_en: '正常' means a normal state with nothing wrong; '頂上' means the highest point of a mountain. They sound the same, so context tells them apart.

examples.en: A half moon is in the night sky.
I cut the fruit into half-moon shapes.

explain: 반만 둥글게 보이는 달이에요. 모양이 반달 같은 것도 '반달 모양'이라고 해요.
explain_en: A moon that looks half round. Anything shaped like it can be called '반달 모양'.

examples.en: I rested warmly in front of the brazier.
We grilled meat over the brazier at the campsite.

explain: 숯이나 불을 담아 방을 데우거나 고기를 굽는 그릇이에요. 요즘은 캠핑장이나 전통 식당에서 자주 봐요.
explain_en: A container that holds burning charcoal or fire for heating or grilling. Today you mostly see one at campsites or traditional restaurants.

examples.en: It is hard to predict the weather.
Experts predicted next year's economy.

explain: 자료나 경험을 바탕으로 앞일을 미리 말할 때 써요. '예상하다'보다 근거가 있다는 느낌이 강해요.
explain_en: Used when you say what will happen based on data or experience. It feels more evidence-based than '예상하다'.

examples.en: I expected the result.
The traffic was worse than I expected.

explain: 앞으로 어떻게 될지 미리 짐작할 때 써요. 좋은 일에도 나쁜 일에도 쓰고, 보통 '예상보다'와 같이 많이 말해요.
explain_en: Used when you guess in advance how something will turn out, good or bad. It often appears as '예상보다' (than expected).

examples.en: I went to the Namsan observation deck on the weekend.
You can see all of Seoul at a glance from the observation deck.

explain: 높은 곳에서 경치를 볼 수 있게 만든 곳이에요. 산이나 높은 건물에 있어요.

phrases.en: to go up to the observation deck
phrases.en_equiv: to go up to the observation deck

explain_en: A place built high up so you can look at the view. You find them on mountains and tall buildings.

examples.ko: 재즈바나 라이브 카페에 가 보고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to try a jazz bar or a live music cafe.
On a weekend evening, I listened to music at a jazz bar.

explain: 재즈 음악을 들으면서 술이나 음료를 마시는 가게예요. '재즈 + 바'가 합쳐진 말이에요.
explain_en: A bar where you drink while listening to jazz. It is '재즈' (jazz) plus '바' (bar).

en: to receive a recommendation; to be recommended

examples.en: I got a recommendation from a friend.
I went to the restaurant I was recommended.

explain: 다른 사람이 좋다고 소개해 준 것을 받을 때 써요. '친구한테 추천받다'처럼 누구에게 받았는지 같이 말해요.
explain_en: Used when someone suggests something good to you. You usually say who gave it, like '친구한테 추천받다'.

examples.en: The teacher praised my pronunciation.
Praising someone's cooking makes them happy.

explain: 잘한 일이나 좋은 점을 말로 좋게 이야기할 때 써요. 칭찬받는 사람에게는 '칭찬을 받다'라고 해요.
explain_en: Used when you say good things about someone's work or qualities. The person who gets praised uses '칭찬을 받다'.

en: to judge; to evaluate; to screen

examples.en: At the cooking contest, the judges evaluate the dishes.
They reviewed the documents carefully.

explain: 대회나 서류를 보고 좋고 나쁨이나 합격 여부를 정할 때 써요. 심사하는 사람은 '심사위원'이라고 해요.
explain_en: Used when you look at entries or documents and decide quality or pass/fail. The person doing it is a '심사위원' (judge).

en: to be appropriate; to be suitable

examples.en: The amount of sauce is just right.
I chose suitable words for the meeting.

explain: 상황에 잘 맞아서 알맞다는 뜻이에요. '적당하다'와 비슷하지만 더 격식 있는 말이에요.
explain_en: Means fitting the situation well. It is similar to '적당하다' but a bit more formal.

examples.en: I won the case in court.
I saw news that the company won the lawsuit.

explain: 재판에서 이기는 것을 말해요. 반대말은 '패소하다'예요.
explain_en: Means to win a case in court. The opposite is '패소하다'.

examples.en: I wrote a statement using AI.
The company released a statement yesterday.

explain: 어떤 일에 대한 공식적인 생각이나 입장을 글로 쓴 것이에요. 회사나 유명인이 문제가 생기면 발표해요.
explain_en: A written statement of someone's official stance on an issue. Companies or public figures release one when a problem comes up.

examples.ko: 대행사에 맡겼는데 접수가 안 돼 있었어요.
examples.en: I left it with the agency, but it had not been submitted.
I work at an advertising agency.

explain: 다른 사람이나 회사를 대신해서 일을 처리해 주는 회사예요. 여행, 광고, 비자 신청 등에서 많이 써요.

phrases.en: to leave it to an agency
phrases.en_equiv: to leave it to an agency

explain_en: A company that handles tasks on behalf of others. Common for travel, advertising, and visa applications.

examples.ko: 한국에 입국할 때 여권을 보여 줬어요.
examples.en: I showed my passport when entering Korea.
I plan to arrive in the country tomorrow afternoon.

explain: 다른 나라에서 우리가 가려는 나라로 들어가는 것을 말해요. 반대말은 '출국하다'예요.
explain_en: Means to enter a country from abroad. The opposite is '출국하다'.

en: to transfer (to another line or vehicle)

examples.en: I transfer to Line 2 at Seoul Station.
You can transfer to a bus at the next station.

explain: 지하철, 버스, 비행기를 다른 것으로 갈아탈 때 써요. 일상에서는 '갈아타다'도 많이 말해요.
explain_en: Used when you switch to another subway, bus, or flight. In daily speech, '갈아타다' is also common.

dis.h: formal Sino-Korean; used in announcements

p.n: Same meaning; 갈아타다 is the plain everyday verb.

examples.en: I went to get a saju reading with a friend.
My saju said this year's luck is good.

explain: 태어난 해, 달, 날, 시간으로 운명을 보는 한국의 전통 방법이에요. '사주를 보다'라고 말해요.
explain_en: A traditional Korean way of reading fate from the year, month, day, and hour of birth. You say '사주를 보다'.

examples.en: They say marriage luck is coming next year.
I was curious about my marriage luck, so I had my fortune read.

explain: 결혼에 관한 운을 말해요. 운세나 사주에서 '결혼운이 좋다/나쁘다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: Luck related to marriage. In fortune telling you say '결혼운이 좋다/나쁘다'.

examples.en: My love luck was good in today's horoscope.
They say it is a time when love luck rises.

explain: 연애에 관한 운을 말해요. 운세에서 '연애운이 좋다/나쁘다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: Luck related to romance. In fortune telling you say '연애운이 좋다/나쁘다'.

examples.en: I felt jealous because my friend won a prize.
Everyone feels jealous sometimes.

explain: 다른 사람이 가진 것이나 사랑받는 것을 보고 샘이 나는 마음이에요. '질투하다', '질투가 나다'로 써요.
explain_en: The feeling you get when someone has what you want or gets more love. Used as '질투하다' or '질투가 나다'.

examples.en: I spoke with the child's feelings in mind.
I left early, taking the traffic into account.

explain: 어떤 사정을 미리 생각에 넣고 판단할 때 써요. 보통 '~을/를 감안하면'이나 '~을/를 감안해서' 형태로 많이 써요.
explain_en: Used when you factor a circumstance into your judgment. It often appears as '~을/를 감안하면' or '~을/를 감안해서'.

examples.en: I am sorry I overlooked that person's feelings.
If you overlook a small problem, it gets bigger later.

explain: 중요한 것을 대수롭지 않게 보고 지나칠 때 써요. 보통 '중요한 점을 간과하다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: Used when you pass over something important without giving it enough attention. A typical phrase is '중요한 점을 간과하다'.

en: to be late (for school or work)

examples.en: I was late for school because of the rain.
Please don't be late tomorrow.

explain: 학교나 회사에 정해진 시간보다 늦게 도착할 때 써요. 친구와의 약속에는 보통 '늦다'를 써요.

phrases.en: The traffic is bad, so I think I'll be late.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아직 늦지 않았지만 늦을 것 같을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when you aren't late yet but think you will be.

phrases.en: I was late for work yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: '지각하다' 앞에는 늦은 장소를 '에'로 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put the place you were late for before the verb with '에'.

phrases.en: You must not be late on exam day.
phrases.nuance_ko: 늦으면 안 된다고 말할 때 쓰는 말투예요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is how you say that being late is not allowed.

explain_en: Used when you arrive after the set time for school or work. For meeting a friend, people usually say 늦다.

examples.en: On Lunar New Year, we pay our respects to our ancestors.
We are here thanks to our ancestors.

explain: '조상'을 높여 부르는 말이에요. 명절이나 제사 이야기를 할 때 자주 써요.

phrases.en: On the holiday, we bow to our ancestors.
phrases.nuance_ko: 높임을 나타내는 조사 '께'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It goes with the honorific particle '께'.

phrases.en: Our ancestors lived in this village.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 분을 말할 때 '-들'을 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add '-들' to talk about more than one ancestor.

phrases.en: On Chuseok, I prepare food while thinking of my ancestors.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조상을 기억하고 감사하는 마음을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it for remembering and being grateful to one's ancestors.

explain_en: A respectful way to say 조상 (ancestors). It often comes up when talking about holidays and memorial rites.

examples.en: There is a drama shoot today.

examples.ko: 여기서는 사진 촬영을 할 수 없어요.
examples.en: You can't take photos here.

explain: 사진이나 영화, 드라마를 찍는 일을 말해요. '촬영하다'로 동사처럼 써요.
explain_en: Refers to filming or photographing, such as for movies, dramas, or photos. It becomes a verb as 촬영하다.

en: to be active; to be lively

examples.en: My younger sibling has a lively personality.
The classroom atmosphere is very lively.

explain: 사람의 성격이나 분위기가 힘차고 적극적일 때 써요. '활발한 성격'처럼 자주 써요.
explain_en: Describes a person or atmosphere that is energetic and outgoing. It is often used as 활발한 성격 (an outgoing personality).

en: to be absurd; to be ridiculous; to be preposterous

examples.en: That's really ridiculous.
I heard that story and laughed in disbelief.

explain: 너무 뜻밖이라 기가 막히고 말이 안 나올 때 써요. 친구와 말할 때는 '어이없어'라고 해요.
explain_en: Used when something is so unexpected or ridiculous that you are left speechless. With friends, you say 어이없어.

examples.en: I had the tooth pulled at the dentist after anesthesia.
It may hurt when the anesthesia wears off.

explain: 수술이나 치료 때 아픔을 못 느끼게 하는 일이에요. '마취하다', '마취를 하다'로 써요.
explain_en: Making a patient unable to feel pain during surgery or treatment. It is used as 마취하다 or 마취를 하다.

examples.ko: 지금 인도네시아에서 엄청 큰 산불이 났어요.
examples.en: A huge forest fire has broken out in Indonesia right now.

examples.ko: 산에서는 불을 피우면 산불이 날 수 있어요.
examples.en: Lighting a fire on a mountain can start a forest fire.

explain: 산에서 나는 불이에요. '산불이 나다'로 자주 말해요. '산'과 '불'이 합쳐진 말이에요.

phrases.en: to put out a forest fire
phrases.en_equiv: to put out a forest fire

explain_en: A fire burning on a mountain or in a forest. It is often said as 산불이 나다. It joins 산 (mountain) and 불 (fire).

en: to care about; to pay attention to; to worry about

examples.en: I'm fine, so please don't worry about me.

examples.ko: 시험 때문에 요즘 건강에 신경 쓰고 있어요.
examples.en: I've been taking care of my health lately because of the exam.

explain: 어떤 일에 관심을 두고 마음을 쓰거나 걱정할 때 써요. '신경 쓰지 마세요'는 '걱정하지 마세요'라는 뜻이에요.

phrases.en: to be on one's mind; to bother
phrases.en_equiv: to be on one's mind; to bother

explain_en: Means to pay attention to something or worry about it. 신경 쓰지 마세요 means 'Don't worry about it.'

examples.en: I went to the botanical garden with my family on the weekend.
There are many pretty flowers in the botanical garden.

explain: 여러 가지 식물을 모아 기르고 보여 주는 곳이에요. 보통 '식물원에 가다'로 말해요.

phrases.en: I took many flower photos at the botanical garden.
phrases.nuance_ko: 식물원에서 한 일을 말할 때는 '식물원에서'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '식물원에서' to say what you did there.
phrases.en_equiv: to take photos at the botanical garden

phrases.en: There is no big botanical garden in our town.
phrases.nuance_ko: 크기를 설명하는 말을 앞에 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put a size word in front to describe it.

phrases.en: Today I looked around the botanical garden.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가서 둘러보는 일을 '구경'과 함께 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Pair it with '구경' to talk about going around to look.

explain_en: A place that grows and displays many kinds of plants. People usually say 식물원에 가다.

en: to talk; to have a conversation

examples.en: I talked with my parents.
I want to talk with my friend for a long time.

explain: 서로 이야기를 주고받을 때 써요. '~와/과 대화하다'로 말해요. '말하다'보다 서로 주고받는 느낌이 강해요.
explain_en: Used when people exchange words with each other, as in ~와/과 대화하다. It sounds more two-way than 말하다.

dis.h: converse; two-way exchange, more formal

p.n: Same meaning; 얘기하다 sounds more casual.

en: to fade away; to go away

examples.en: The pain went away after I took medicine.
The smell faded after I opened the window.

explain: 아픔, 냄새, 피로 같은 것이 없어질 때 써요. '부모님께서 가셨어요'의 '가셨어요'는 '가다'를 높인 말이라서 이 낱말과 뜻이 달라요.
explain_en: Used when pain, smell, or tiredness fades away. The 가셨어요 in 부모님께서 가셨어요 is the honorific of 가다, which is a different word.

examples.en: I took up vegetarianism for my health.
Vegetarian restaurants are increasing.

explain: 고기를 먹지 않고 채소 중심으로 먹는 생각이나 방식이에요. 사람은 '채식주의자'라고 해요.
explain_en: The belief or practice of eating mainly vegetables and no meat. A person who follows it is a 채식주의자.

examples.en: I do my laundry at the laundromat.
I don't have a washing machine at home, so I go to the laundromat.

explain: 동전이나 카드로 세탁기와 건조기를 쓰는 가게예요. '빨래방에서 빨래를 돌리다'라고 말해요.

phrases.en: to run a load of laundry
phrases.en_equiv: to run a load of laundry

explain_en: A shop where you pay to use washing machines and dryers. People say 빨래방에서 빨래를 돌리다 for doing laundry there.

examples.en: I stayed one night at a hotel.
I'm going on a two-day, one-night trip this weekend.

explain: 한 번 자고 오는 것을 말해요. 여행 일정에서 '1박 2일'처럼 숫자와 함께 많이 써요.
explain_en: Staying one night somewhere. It is often used with numbers in trip schedules, like 1박 2일 (two days, one night).

examples.en: My friend stayed one night at our house.
It snowed a lot overnight.

explain: 하루의 밤, 즉 한 번 자는 동안을 말해요. '하룻밤 자다', '하룻밤 사이에'처럼 써요.
explain_en: A single night. It is used in phrases like 하룻밤 자다 (stay one night) and 하룻밤 사이에 (overnight).

examples.en: The stadium was full of spectators.
The crowd gave the players loud applause.

explain: 경기나 공연을 보러 온 많은 사람들을 말해요. 보통 스포츠 경기에서 써요. 영화나 연극의 사람들은 '관객'이라고 해요.
explain_en: The crowd of people who came to watch a game or event, mostly in sports. For movies or plays, people usually say 관객.

en: to watch; to view (a show, game, exhibit)

examples.en: I viewed paintings at the art museum on the weekend.
I watched a soccer game with my family yesterday.

explain: 경기, 영화, 공연, 전시 같은 것을 보러 가서 볼 때 써요. 그냥 '보다'보다 격식 있는 말이에요.
explain_en: Used for going to see a game, movie, performance, or exhibition. It is more formal than plain 보다.

dis.h: formal 'watch' for shows, films, exhibits

p.n: 보다 is the plain everyday word; 관람하다 sounds formal.

examples.en: I researched history at the library.
That teacher does research on Korean.

explain: 어떤 것을 깊이 조사하고 생각해서 새로운 것을 알아낼 때 써요. 학교에서 하는 '공부하다'와는 달라요.
explain_en: Used for investigating and thinking deeply about something to find out new things. It is different from 공부하다, which is ordinary studying.

examples.en: The base form of 먹어요 is 먹다.

examples.ko: 사전에서 단어를 찾을 때 기본형으로 찾아요.
examples.en: You look up words by their base form in a dictionary.

explain: 동사나 형용사의 어미가 바뀌기 전 모습이에요. '가다', '먹다'처럼 '-다'로 끝나요. 사전에는 기본형으로 나와요.

phrases.en: The base form of a verb ends in '-다'.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 말의 기본형인지 말할 때 '동사의', '형용사의'를 앞에 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put '동사의' or '형용사의' in front to say which kind of word it is.
phrases.en_equiv: the base form of a verb

phrases.en: If you change '갔어요' to the base form, it is '가다'.
phrases.nuance_ko: 활용한 말을 '-다' 모양으로 돌릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when turning a conjugated word back to its '-다' form.
phrases.en_equiv: to change to the base form

phrases.example: 모르는 말은 기본형을 찾아서 사전에서 봐요.
phrases.en: For words I don't know, I find the base form and look it up in the dictionary.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사전을 쓰기 전에 하는 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it for the step you take before using a dictionary.

explain_en: The form of a verb or adjective before its ending changes, like 가다 or 먹다, ending in -다. Dictionaries list words in this form.

examples.en: I freeze water.
I froze the leftover meat in the freezer.

explain: 물이나 음식을 차게 해서 얼음처럼 단단하게 만들 때 써요. 저절로 어는 것은 '얼다'예요.
explain_en: To make water or food freeze solid by chilling it. When something freezes on its own, the verb is 얼다.

en: to become clear; to clear up

examples.en: The sky clears up in the afternoon.
The rain stopped and the air became clear.

explain: '맑다'에 '-아지다'가 붙어 맑게 변한다는 뜻이에요. 날씨나 물, 공기가 깨끗해질 때 써요.

phrases.en: The sky will clear up tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞으로 맑게 변할 거라고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to say something will become clear in the future.

phrases.en: The rain has stopped and the sky is clearing up.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 조금씩 변하는 중일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when the change is happening right now, little by little.

phrases.nuance_ko: 맑게 변하지 않을 때 부정형으로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the negative form for when it doesn't become clear.

explain_en: This is 맑다 plus -아지다, meaning to become clear. It is used for weather, water, or air becoming clear.

examples.en: Please explain and give your reasons.
That story has no basis at all.

explain: 어떤 말이나 생각이 맞는 이유가 되는 것이에요. '근거를 들다', '근거가 있다'로 많이 써요.
explain_en: The grounds or evidence that make a statement or idea reasonable. It is often used as 근거를 들다 (give grounds) or 근거가 있다 (have grounds).

examples.en: You'll be fine after resting a day or two.
Please wait just a day or two.

explain: 하루나 이틀 정도의 짧은 기간을 어림해서 말해요. 숫자를 나란히 붙이면 '대략'이라는 느낌이 나요.
explain_en: Means roughly 'a day or two'. Putting two numbers side by side gives a loose, approximate feel.

examples.en: I met a friend after a long while.
I slept well for the first time in a while.

explain: '오랜만에'를 줄여서 편하게 하는 말이에요. 주로 말할 때 쓰고, 글에서는 '오랜만에'가 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: A casual, shortened form of '오랜만에'. Common in speech; '오랜만에' is more natural in writing.

en: long time no see; it's been a long time

examples.en: Long time no see! Have you been well?
It's been a really long time since I was in this neighborhood.

explain: 오랫동안 못 만난 사람을 만났을 때 하는 인사예요. 친구에게는 '오랜만이야', 높여서는 '오랜만이에요'라고 해요.

phrases.en: We met after a long time
phrases.en_equiv: We met after a long time

explain_en: A greeting for someone you haven't seen in a long time. Use '오랜만이야' with friends and '오랜만이에요' politely.

examples.en: I study at a study room before exams.
A study room is quiet, so it's easy to focus.

explain: 조용히 공부하도록 칸막이 책상을 빌려주는 곳이에요. 도서관과 달리 보통 돈을 내고 이용해요.

phrases.en: I go to a study room every exam period.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자주 오래 가는 곳이라서 '가다' 대신 '다니다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Because you go regularly, '다니다' is used instead of '가다'.
phrases.en_equiv: to go to a study room regularly

phrases.en: The study room desk is small but comfortable.
phrases.nuance_ko: 독서실의 칸막이 책상을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it for the partitioned desk in a study room.

phrases.en: My friend said, "Let's go to the study room together."
phrases.nuance_ko: 친구에게 하는 반말 제안이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is a casual suggestion to a friend.
phrases.en_equiv: let's go to the study room

explain_en: A quiet paid place with partitioned desks for studying. Unlike a library, you usually pay to use it.

en: to take notes; to jot down

examples.en: I take notes during class.
I write down important points in my notebook.

explain: 들은 내용이나 중요한 내용을 손으로 적는 것을 말해요. '필기시험'은 글로 쓰는 시험이에요.
explain_en: To write down what you hear or what matters. '필기시험' means a written exam.

examples.en: I regret not saying anything then.
I'll work hard so I won't regret it.

explain: 이미 한 일이나 하지 못한 일이 마음에 걸려서 '그러지 말걸' 하고 생각하는 거예요. '-(으)ㄴ 걸 후회하다' 형태로 자주 써요.
explain_en: To wish you had done something differently. Often used as '-(으)ㄴ 걸 후회하다'.

examples.en: I imagine myself going on a trip.
It's much bigger than I imagined.

explain: 눈앞에 없는 것을 머릿속으로 그려 보는 거예요. 목적어에는 '을/를'이 와요.
explain_en: To picture in your mind something that isn't in front of you. Takes the object particle 을/를.

dis.h: picture something in your mind

p.n: 공상 means idle, unrealistic daydreaming; 상상 is neutral imagining.

en: to refuse; to turn down; to reject

examples.en: I turned down the invitation.
It's hard to refuse a favor.

explain: 부탁이나 제안, 초대를 받아들이지 않는다고 말하는 거예요. 당하는 쪽은 '거절당하다'라고 해요.
explain_en: To say no to a request, offer or invitation. The passive-like form is '거절당하다' (to be turned down).

dis.h: turn down a request or invitation

p.n: 거부하다 sounds harsher and more final than a simple turn-down.

examples.en: I suggested to my friend that we exercise together.
I proposed a new method at the meeting.

explain: 어떤 생각이나 방법을 다른 사람에게 말해서 해 보자고 하는 거예요. '-자고 제안하다'로 자주 써요.

phrases.en: I got a suggestion from a friend to travel together.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다른 사람이 제안한 것을 들었을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when someone else made the suggestion to you.

phrases.en: If you have a good idea, try suggesting it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대방에게 말해 보라고 권할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to encourage someone to put forward an idea.

phrases.en: That is a really good suggestion.
phrases.nuance_ko: '제안하다'의 명사형 '제안'을 써서 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: This uses the noun '제안' made from the verb.

explain_en: To put forward an idea or plan to others. Often used as '-자고 제안하다'.

en: to rely on; to fall back on

examples.en: I rely on my family when things are hard.
You shouldn't depend only on other people.

explain: 힘들 때 다른 사람이나 물건에 기대는 거예요. '에게/에' 앞에 대상을 써요. 소리가 같은 '의지(will)'와 뜻이 달라요.

phrases.en: to be someone to lean on
phrases.en_equiv: to be someone to lean on

explain_en: To lean on a person or thing for support; the target takes 에게/에. Don't confuse it with the noun 의지 (will).

examples.en: I cheer for our team.
I cheered my friend on to do well on the exam.

explain: 경기나 시험을 앞둔 사람이 잘하도록 소리치거나 말로 힘을 주는 거예요.
explain_en: To encourage someone, by shouting at a game or by words, so they do well.

en: to wrap; to gift-wrap; to pack

examples.en: I wrap the gift nicely.
Please pack up the leftover food for me.

explain: 물건이나 음식을 종이나 상자 등으로 싸는 거예요. 식당에서 남은 음식을 싸 갈 때도 써요.
explain_en: To wrap or pack goods or food. Also used for taking leftovers or an order to go.

examples.en: This rule is unfair.
I felt it was unfair, so I said something.

explain: 대우나 기회가 똑같지 않은 것을 말해요. 보통 '불공평하다'로 쓰고, 명사 앞에서는 '불공평한'이 돼요.
explain_en: Treatment or opportunity that is not equal. Usually used as the adjective '불공평하다'; before a noun it becomes '불공평한'.

examples.en: I know nothing about that field.
I made a mistake out of ignorance.

explain: 어떤 것을 전혀 몰라서 아는 게 없는 상태예요. 보통 '무지하다'로 쓰고 조금 딱딱한 말이에요. 말할 때 쓰는 '무지 크다(아주 크다)'와는 달라요.
explain_en: The state of knowing nothing about something; usually '무지하다' and a bit formal. Different from the casual adverb 무지 meaning 'very'.

examples.en: They fought through nonviolence.
The nonviolence movement changed the world.

explain: '비-'는 '아닌'이라는 뜻이라 폭력을 쓰지 않는다는 말이에요. '비폭력 운동', '비폭력 저항'처럼 명사 앞에 붙여 써요.
explain_en: '비-' means 'non-', so this is not using violence. It often modifies nouns: '비폭력 운동', '비폭력 저항'.

examples.en: I feel like an outsider in the new city.
He lived in the village like a stranger.

explain: 다른 곳에서 왔거나 그 무리에 속하지 않는 사람이에요. 외국인이 아니어도 '낯설고 겉도는 사람'이라는 느낌으로 써요.
explain_en: A person from elsewhere or one who doesn't belong. It can also mean feeling like an outsider, even if not a foreigner.

examples.en: The kids race in the park.
There's a bicycle race today.

explain: 달리기나 자전거처럼 누가 빠른지 겨루는 시합이에요. '경주'는 도시 이름이기도 해서 문장을 보고 구분해요.
explain_en: A contest to see who is fastest, like running or cycling. 경주 is also a city name, so tell them apart by context.

examples.en: We play a match against another school on the weekend.
Our team played a match yesterday and won.

explain: 운동 등에서 승부를 가리려고 겨루는 거예요. '-와/과 시합하다'로 상대를 말해요.
explain_en: To compete in a match, usually sports. The opponent goes with -와/과.

en: boiling briskly / with a gurgling sound

examples.en: The stew is bubbling away.
I'm so angry I'm seething inside.

explain: 액체가 크게 끓거나 거품이 일 때 나는 소리와 모양이에요. 화가 나서 속이 끓는 느낌에도 비유해서 써요.

phrases.en: I put the ramen into the boiling water.
phrases.nuance_ko: '끓는'과 함께 물이나 국이 세게 끓는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '끓는', it describes water or soup boiling hard.

phrases.example: 그 말을 들으니까 속이 부글부글 끓어요.
phrases.en: Hearing that makes my insides boil with anger.
phrases.nuance_ko: 화가 나는 마음을 비유해서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it as a figure of speech for feeling angry.

phrases.en: Bubbles are foaming up noisily in the pot.
phrases.nuance_ko: 거품이 계속 크게 올라오는 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it for bubbles rising up continuously and strongly.

explain_en: The sound and look of liquid boiling hard or foaming. Also used figuratively for seething with anger.

examples.en: I bought a colorful umbrella.
The flower bed is full of colors.

explain: 여러 가지 색이 섞여 있는 모양이에요. '알록달록하다', '알록달록한 옷'처럼 활용해서 써요.
explain_en: Describes a mix of many colors. Used as '알록달록하다' or '알록달록한 + noun'.

examples.en: I tie my shoelaces tightly.
I go to work wearing a tie.

explain: 끈이나 넥타이, 벨트처럼 묶어서 고정하는 거예요. 가방은 어깨에 걸치니까 '메다'를 써서 '가방을 메요'라고 해요.

phrases.en: I carry a bag on my shoulder
phrases.en_equiv: I carry a bag on my shoulder

explain_en: To tie or fasten things like laces, ties or belts. A bag on the shoulder uses the different verb 메다: '가방을 메요'.

examples.en: Let's meet around ten o'clock.
Flowers bloom around the time spring comes.

explain: 어떤 때의 근처를 말해요. 앞에 때를 나타내는 말이나 '-(으)ㄹ'이 오고, 띄어 써요. '무렵'과 비슷해요.
explain_en: Means 'around the time of'. Comes after a time word or a '-(으)ㄹ' clause, written with a space. Similar to 무렵.

examples.en: The flowers smell nice.
The room is full of the scent of coffee.

explain: 꽃, 차, 음식처럼 기분 좋은 냄새를 말해요. '향기가 나다'로 자주 써요.
explain_en: It means a pleasant smell, like that of flowers, tea, or food. It is often used as '향기가 나다'.

examples.en: Cross when the green light comes on.
I wait a little for the green light.

explain: 신호등에서 건너가도 된다는 초록색 불이에요. '초록불이 켜지다'로 자주 써요.
explain_en: The green light on a traffic signal that means you may cross. It is often used as '초록불이 켜지다'.

examples.en: I went to a gukbap restaurant for lunch.
This gukbap restaurant is always crowded.

explain: 국밥을 파는 식당이에요. '-집'은 그 음식을 파는 가게를 뜻해요.
explain_en: A restaurant that sells gukbap, rice served in hot soup. The suffix '-집' means a shop that sells that food.

examples.en: I drink tea with a friend at a tea house.
There is a small tea house in the alley.

explain: 차를 마시는 가게예요. 조용하고 전통적인 분위기의 가게를 말할 때가 많아요.

phrases.en: I went to a traditional tea house in Insadong.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한국식 차를 파는 옛날 분위기의 가게를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it for an old-style shop that sells Korean traditional tea.

phrases.en: We decided to meet at a tea shop.
phrases.nuance_ko: 만나는 장소를 말할 때 '찻집에서'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '찻집에서' to say where you meet.
phrases.en_equiv: to meet at a tea shop

phrases.en: The tea shop owner is kind.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가게를 하는 사람을 말할 때 '주인'을 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add '주인' to talk about the person who runs the shop.

explain_en: A shop where you drink tea. It often suggests a quiet, traditional place.

examples.en: I put training wheels on the child's bike.
You can take the training wheels off now.

explain: 어린이 자전거가 넘어지지 않게 옆에 다는 작은 바퀴예요. '보조바퀴를 달다/떼다'로 써요.

phrases.en: to take off the training wheels
phrases.en_equiv: to take off the training wheels

explain_en: The small side wheels on a child's bike that keep it from tipping over. Used as '보조바퀴를 달다/떼다'.

examples.en: The bicycle wheel is big.
I walked one lap around the park.

explain: 자동차나 자전거처럼 굴러가는 둥근 부분이에요. '운동장을 한 바퀴 돌다'처럼 한 번 도는 횟수를 셀 때도 써요.
explain_en: The round part that rolls on a car or bike. It also counts laps, as in '한 바퀴 돌다' (go around once).

examples.en: Cars are whizzing by.
The winter wind is blowing hard.

explain: 바람이 세게 불거나 차가 빨리 지나갈 때 나는 소리와 모습이에요. '쌩쌩 불다', '쌩쌩 달리다'로 써요.
explain_en: The sound and look of strong wind or fast-passing vehicles. Used as '쌩쌩 불다' or '쌩쌩 달리다'.

en: to blow in; to blow toward the speaker

examples.en: A cool breeze blows in from the sea.
The wind blows in through the window.

explain: 바람이 이쪽으로 불어서 오는 것이에요. 주로 '바람이 불어오다'로 써요.

phrases.en: The wind blowing in is cool.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 바람을 꾸미는 모양이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the form that modifies a noun like 'wind'.

phrases.en: A cold wind suddenly blew in.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이미 일어난 일을 말하는 과거형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the past form for something that already happened.

phrases.en: The wind will blow in this evening.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞으로 일어날 일을 말하는 미래형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the future form for something that will happen.

explain_en: Wind blowing toward the speaker. It is mostly used as '바람이 불어오다'.

en: to be ticklish; to be itchy

examples.en: The soles of my feet are very ticklish.
My arm itches from a mosquito bite.

explain: 몸에 무언가 살짝 닿아서 웃음이 나거나 긁고 싶은 느낌이에요. 'ㅂ' 불규칙이라 '간지러워요'가 돼요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 꾸밀 때는 '간지러운'이 돼요.
phrases.nuance_en: Before a noun it becomes '간지러운'.

phrases.en: The soles of my feet aren't ticklish.
phrases.nuance_ko: 간지럽지 않다는 부정형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the negative form, saying it isn't ticklish or itchy.

phrases.en: My friend touched me, and I laughed because it tickled.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이유를 말하는 '-아서/어서' 모양이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the '-아서/어서' form that gives a reason.

explain_en: The feeling of a light touch on your body that makes you laugh or want to scratch. It is a ㅂ-irregular adjective: '간지러워요'.

examples.en: The road is slippery, so be careful.
I am careful when I drive.

explain: 나쁜 일이 생기지 않게 주의하는 것이에요. 보통 '조심하다'나 '조심하세요'로 써요.
explain_en: Paying attention so that nothing bad happens. It is usually used as '조심하다' or '조심하세요'.

examples.en: I wear a helmet when I ride a bike.
A helmet is a must at a construction site.

explain: 머리를 보호하려고 쓰는 단단한 모자예요. '헬멧을 쓰다'로 말해요.
explain_en: A hard hat that protects your head. You say '헬멧을 쓰다' (wear a helmet).

examples.en: I moved into a newly built apartment.
This building was newly constructed last year.

explain: 건물을 새로 지은 것이에요. 집을 구할 때 '신축 아파트'처럼 자주 써요. 오래된 건물은 '구축'이라고 해요.
explain_en: A newly built building. Common when looking for housing, as in '신축 아파트'. An older building is '구축'.

examples.en: Listening to music makes me smile without trying.
The weather is nice, so my mood lifts on its own.

explain: 일부러 하지 않아도 저절로 그렇게 된다는 뜻이에요. '절로 웃음이 나다'처럼 써요. '저절로'와 비슷해요.
explain_en: Something happens on its own without trying. Used as '절로 웃음이 나다'. Similar to '저절로'.

examples.en: The door opens when you tap the key card.
I got two key cards at the hotel.

explain: 호텔이나 사무실 문을 여는 카드예요. 카드키를 '대다'라고 말해요.
explain_en: A card that opens a door at a hotel or office. You say '카드키를 대다' (tap the card).

en: to be released; to be lifted (a lock, ban, restriction)

examples.en: When the lock is released, the door opens.
The emergency alert has been lifted.

explain: 잠금, 경보, 금지 같은 제한이 풀리는 것이에요. 사람이 풀면 '해제하다'예요.
explain_en: A lock, alarm, or restriction is released. When a person does it, the verb is '해제하다'.

en: to take (a pet) for a walk

examples.en: I walk my dog every morning.
Many people walk their dogs in the park.

explain: 강아지 같은 동물을 데리고 걷는 것이에요. '강아지를 산책시키다'처럼 목적어가 필요해요.

phrases.en: I will take the dog for a walk this evening.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞으로 할 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it for something you plan to do.
phrases.en_equiv: I will take it for a walk

phrases.en: I'm walking the dog in the park right now.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 하는 중일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it for something happening right now.

phrases.en: I'll be late, so please take the dog for a walk.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다른 사람에게 부탁할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to ask someone else to do it.
phrases.en_equiv: please take it for a walk

explain_en: To walk an animal such as a dog. It needs an object, as in '강아지를 산책시키다'.

examples.en: I was tired, so I ordered dinner for delivery.
We order fried chicken and eat it.

explain: 음식을 집으로 가져다 달라고 주문하는 것이에요. '음식을 배달시키다'로 써요. '배달하다'는 가져다주는 사람이 하는 일이에요.
explain_en: To order food to be brought to you. Used as '음식을 배달시키다'. '배달하다' is what the delivery person does.

en: to take a bath; to bathe

examples.en: I take a bath at night.
Taking a bath in hot water relieves fatigue.

explain: 몸을 물로 씻는 것이에요. 보통 욕조에 들어가 씻을 때 써요. 샤워는 '샤워하다'라고 해요.
explain_en: To wash your body with water, usually in a bathtub. For a shower, use '샤워하다'.

en: to be square; to be box-shaped

examples.en: My desk is square.
I put it on a square plate.

explain: 모양이 네모 같다는 뜻이에요. 꾸밀 때는 '네모난 상자'처럼 써요.
explain_en: Something has a square or rectangular shape. When modifying a noun: '네모난 상자'.

examples.en: Our company makes applications.
I installed a new application.

explain: 휴대폰이나 컴퓨터에서 쓰는 프로그램이에요. 보통 줄여서 '앱'이라고 말해요.
explain_en: A program used on a phone or computer. People usually shorten it to '앱'.

examples.en: Various things are lying on the desk.
I bought a bit of everything at the market.

explain: 여러 가지 물건이나 일을 가리킬 때 써요. '이것저것 사다', '이것저것 물어보다'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: to ask about all sorts of things
phrases.en_equiv: to ask about all sorts of things

explain_en: Refers to a variety of things or matters. Used as '이것저것 사다' or '이것저것 물어보다'.

examples.en: My desk is beige.
I bought a beige coat.

explain: 밝은 갈색에 가까운 연한 색이에요. '색'을 빼고 '베이지'라고도 해요.
explain_en: A light, pale brownish color. You can also drop '색' and just say '베이지'.

en: to grip; to clench; to hold tightly

examples.en: I grip the knife handle.
The child held my hand tightly.

explain: 손가락을 오므려서 꽉 잡는 것이에요. '주먹을 쥐다', '손잡이를 쥐다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: To close your fingers tightly around something. Used as '주먹을 쥐다' or '손잡이를 쥐다'.

examples.en: Paper is a very useful thing.

examples.ko: 이 낡은 가방은 이제 쓸모가 없어요.
examples.en: This old bag is no longer of any use.

explain: 쓸 만한 가치예요. '쓸모가 있다/없다', '쓸모가 많다'로 써요.
explain_en: Worth or value in being used. Used as '쓸모가 있다/없다' or '쓸모가 많다'.

dis.h: usefulness of a thing; worth keeping

p.n: 소용 sounds like 'no point or effect', not a worthless object.

examples.en: I fold a paper crane.
I gave my friend a paper crane as a gift.

explain: 색종이를 접어서 만든 학이에요. 소원을 빌며 천 마리를 접는 풍습이 있어요.
explain_en: A crane folded from colored paper. There is a custom of folding a thousand of them while making a wish.

en: to paint; to coat; to apply (paint, polish)

examples.en: I paint the wall white.
I put nail polish on my nails.

explain: 물감이나 페인트 같은 것을 표면에 바르는 것이에요. '벽을 칠하다'처럼 칠하는 곳에 '을/를'을 쓰고, '손톱에 매니큐어를 칠하다'처럼 '에'를 쓰기도 해요.
explain_en: To spread paint or a similar substance over a surface. The surface can take 을/를 ('벽을 칠하다'), or 에 when the thing applied takes 을/를 ('손톱에 매니큐어를 칠하다').

dis.h: paint or coat a surface with color

p.n: 바르다 is for spreading things like lotion or glue, not for painting a wall a color.

examples.en: I dip the brush in black ink.
I ate squid ink pasta.

explain: 붓글씨에 쓰는 검은 물이에요. 오징어나 문어가 내뿜는 검은 액도 먹물이라고 해요.

phrases.en: My mouth turned black because of the squid ink.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음식에 들어가는 먹물을 말할 때 앞에 동물 이름을 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put the animal's name in front when talking about ink in food.

phrases.en: I dip the brush in ink and write.
phrases.nuance_ko: 붓이나 손에 먹물이 묻게 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when you get ink on a brush or your hands.

phrases.en: I shook the brush and the ink splashed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 먹물이 사방으로 튀는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: It describes ink splashing around.

explain_en: The black ink used in brush calligraphy. The black fluid squid and octopus release is also called 먹물.

examples.en: The teacher writes on the blackboard with chalk.
The chalk is all worn down.

explain: 칠판에 글씨를 쓰는 하얀 막대예요. '분필로 쓰다'처럼 도구에는 '(으)로'를 써요.
explain_en: A white stick for writing on a blackboard. The tool takes (으)로, as in 분필로 쓰다.

examples.en: I accepted my friend's apology.
It is hard to accept change.

explain: 다른 사람의 의견, 제안, 사실을 그대로 인정하고 받는 것이에요. 물건을 받을 때는 '받다'를 써요.
explain_en: To accept someone's opinion, offer, or a fact. For receiving a physical object, use 받다 instead.

examples.en: There is a lot of gravel on the road.
My feet hurt from walking on pebbles.

explain: 길이나 강가에 있는 작고 단단한 돌이에요. 보통 '자갈이 많다', '자갈길'처럼 써요.
explain_en: Small hard stones found on paths or riverbeds. Often used as 자갈이 많다 or 자갈길.

examples.en: The children play on the sandy beach.
There is a wide sandy beach in front of the sea.

explain: 바다나 호수 옆에 모래가 넓게 깔린 곳이에요. '모래밭'이라고도 해요.

phrases.en: The kids build sandcastles on the sand.
phrases.nuance_ko: '모래사장'과 거의 같은 뜻이에요. 놀이터의 모래 놀이 공간에도 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means almost the same as '모래사장', and also fits a sandbox at a playground.

phrases.en: I walked along the beach in the evening.
phrases.nuance_ko: '을/를' 뒤에 '걷다'를 붙여 지나가는 곳을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '을/를' with '걷다' for the place you walk along.
phrases.en_equiv: to walk on the sandy beach

phrases.en: Jeju Island has a white sandy beach.
phrases.nuance_ko: 모래의 색을 말하는 말을 앞에 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put a color word in front to describe the sand.

explain_en: A wide area of sand beside the sea or a lake. Also called 모래밭.

examples.en: My gums hurt while I was brushing my teeth.
My gums are swollen.

explain: 이를 감싸고 있는 분홍색 살이에요. 발음은 [인몸]이에요.
explain_en: The pink flesh surrounding the teeth. It is pronounced [inmom].

examples.en: I run to the bus stop to catch the bus.
The child ran to their mom.

explain: 어떤 곳이나 사람을 향해 빨리 뛰어서 가는 것이에요. 장소에는 '(으)로'나 '에', 사람에게는 '에게/한테'를 써요. 말하는 사람 쪽으로 오면 '달려오다'예요.
explain_en: To run quickly toward a place or person. A place takes (으)로 or 에; a person takes 에게/한테. Running toward the speaker is 달려오다.

examples.en: I read the same sentence over and over.
If you practice repeatedly, your skills improve.

explain: 같은 일을 여러 번 되풀이하는 것이에요. 동사로 쓸 때는 '반복하다'예요.
explain_en: Doing the same thing many times. As a verb, use 반복하다.

examples.en: I made braised burdock root.
Burdock goes into gimbap.

explain: 길고 갈색인 뿌리채소예요. 김밥이나 조림에 많이 넣어요.
explain_en: A long brown root vegetable. It is often used in gimbap and braised side dishes.

examples.en: I'm going to do a temple stay this weekend.
I meditated during the temple stay.

explain: 절에서 지내며 한국 불교 문화를 경험하는 프로그램이에요. '템플스테이를 하다'라고 말해요.

phrases.en: I did a temple stay experience with my foreign friend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 해 보는 경험을 말할 때 '체험'을 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add '체험' to talk about trying it out as an experience.

phrases.en: I applied for a temple stay online.
phrases.nuance_ko: 참가하려고 미리 신청할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when you sign up in advance to take part.
phrases.en_equiv: to apply for a temple stay

phrases.en: Let's do a temple stay on this vacation.
phrases.nuance_ko: 친구에게 하는 반말 제안이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is a casual suggestion to a friend.

explain_en: A program where you stay at a Buddhist temple and experience Korean temple life. You say 템플스테이를 하다.

examples.en: I take a walk by the river.
I sat by the river and rested.

explain: 강의 가장자리, 강 바로 옆이에요. 장소를 나타낼 때 '강가에서', 가는 곳은 '강가에'를 써요.

phrases.en: I walk along the river every evening.
phrases.nuance_ko: 강을 따라 걷는 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it for walking along the river.

phrases.en: I had coffee at a cafe by the river.
phrases.nuance_ko: 장소를 꾸며 줄 때 '강가에 있는'을 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '강가에 있는' to describe where a place is.

phrases.en: I ride a bike by the river on weekends.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그곳에서 하는 일을 말할 때는 '강가에서'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '강가에서' for what you do at that place.
phrases.en_equiv: to ride a bike by the river

explain_en: The area right next to a river. Use 강가에서 for where an action happens and 강가에 for a destination.

examples.en: I parked the car in front of the building.
Can I park here?

explain: 자동차를 일정한 곳에 세워 두는 것이에요. 장소에는 '에'를 써요.
explain_en: To leave a car in a certain spot. The place takes 에.

examples.en: When it comes to cooking, I'm still a novice.
Sewage flows into the sewer.

explain: 실력이 낮은 사람을 뜻하기도 하고, 쓰고 난 더러운 물을 뜻하기도 해요. 실력이 높은 사람은 '고수'예요.
explain_en: It can mean a person of low skill, or used dirty water (sewage). A highly skilled person is 고수.

examples.en: Our city is developing quickly.
My Korean has improved a lot.

explain: 더 좋고 높은 상태로 나아가는 것이에요. 사람, 나라, 관계, 기술에 모두 쓸 수 있어요.
explain_en: To move toward a better or more advanced state. It works for people, countries, relationships, and technology.

dis.h: progress and advance; economy, technology

p.n: Both are natural; 발전하다 emphasizes moving forward.

examples.en: I have a good relationship with my friend.
That has nothing to do with me.

explain: 사람이나 일이 서로 이어져 있는 것이에요. '관계가 있다/없다'로도 자주 써요.
explain_en: A link between people or things. It is also common as 관계가 있다/없다 (to be related / unrelated).

examples.en: I roast peanuts and eat them.
I have a peanut allergy.

explain: 껍질 속에 든 작고 고소한 열매예요. 땅속에서 자라서 '땅콩'이라고 해요.
explain_en: A small, nutty-tasting seed inside a shell. It grows underground, hence the name 땅콩 (ground bean).

examples.en: They overslept and missed the bus. Serves them right.
They lied, and now look. Serves them right.

explain: 미운 사람이 안 좋은 일을 당해서 속이 시원할 때 쓰는 말이에요. 친한 사이에서만 쓰고, 윗사람에게는 쓰지 않아요.

phrases.example: 걔가 숙제를 안 해서 혼났대. 쌤통이야.
phrases.en: I heard he got scolded for not doing his homework. Serves him right.
phrases.nuance_ko: 친한 친구에게 하는 반말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is casual speech for close friends.

phrases.en: He was late for the appointment and missed the bus. Serves him right.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일이 벌어진 것을 보고 느낀 점을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when you react to something you've just seen or heard.

phrases.en: Honestly, I think it serves him right.
phrases.nuance_ko: 내 생각을 말하는 모양이지만 아무에게나 쓰지는 않아요.
phrases.nuance_en: This states your opinion, but don't use it with just anyone.
phrases.en_equiv: I think it serves him right

explain_en: Said when someone you dislike suffers and you feel satisfied. Use it only with close friends, never toward elders.

examples.en: My skin is sensitive, so I'm careful.
My younger sibling is sensitive to noise.

explain: 작은 자극이나 변화를 쉽게 느끼는 것이에요. 대상에는 '에'를 써요. 반대말은 '둔감하다'예요.
explain_en: To react easily to small stimuli or changes. The thing you are sensitive to takes 에. The opposite is 둔감하다.

examples.en: Hormones change when you are stressed.
Hormone balance is important.

explain: 몸 안에서 만들어져 몸의 상태를 조절하는 물질이에요. 건강, 다이어트 이야기에 자주 나와요.
explain_en: A substance made in the body that regulates its functions. It often comes up when talking about health or dieting.

en: to perceive; to be aware of; to recognize

examples.en: I recognized the problem quickly.
People are aware of the importance of the environment.

explain: 무엇이 있다는 것이나 어떤 상태인지를 알아차리고 이해한다는 뜻이에요. '문제를 인식하다'처럼 '을/를'과 함께 써요.
explain_en: It means to notice and understand that something exists or is a certain way. It is used with an object, as in '문제를 인식하다'.

examples.en: When my stomach feels heavy, I drink sparkling water.
I like sparkling water with lemon.

explain: 기포가 있는 물이에요. 단맛이 있는 '탄산음료'와 달라요.

phrases.en: I bought a bottle of sparkling water at the convenience store.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병 단위로 셀 때는 '한 병'을 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '한 병' to count it by the bottle.

phrases.en: Cold sparkling water is nice on a hot day.
phrases.nuance_ko: 온도를 말하는 말을 앞에 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put a temperature word in front.

phrases.en: One glass of sparkling water, please.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가게에서 주문할 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is what you say to order at a shop.
phrases.en_equiv: one glass of sparkling water, please

explain_en: It is water with bubbles in it. It is different from '탄산음료', which is sweet soda.

examples.en: I ate a lot for lunch, so I'm full.
I'm full, so I can't eat any more.

explain: 많이 먹어서 더 먹고 싶지 않은 상태예요. 반대말은 '배가 고프다'예요. '배부르다'로 붙여 쓰기도 해요.
explain_en: It describes being full after eating a lot. The opposite is '배가 고프다'. It can also be written as one word, '배부르다'.

examples.en: The spot between my eyebrows hurts.
He frowned and looked at me.

explain: 두 눈썹 사이의 부분이에요. '미간을 찌푸리다'는 기분이 안 좋거나 아플 때 하는 표정이에요.
explain_en: It is the area between the two eyebrows. '미간을 찌푸리다' means to frown, usually from displeasure or pain.

examples.en: Koreans eat a lot of shaved ice.
It was hot, so I went to eat shaved ice.

explain: 얼음을 곱게 갈아서 과일이나 팥을 올린 여름 디저트예요. '팥빙수'가 가장 유명해요.
explain_en: It is a summer dessert of finely shaved ice with toppings like fruit or red beans. '팥빙수' is the best-known kind.

examples.en: You can eat an apple with the skin on.
Please peel the apple.

explain: 과일, 달걀, 나무 등의 겉을 싸고 있는 부분이에요. 딱딱하면 '껍데기'라고도 해요.
explain_en: It is the outer covering of fruit, eggs, trees, and so on. For hard coverings, '껍데기' is also used.

examples.en: Yesterday was a substitute holiday.
It's a substitute holiday, so I'm not going to work.

explain: 공휴일이 주말과 겹칠 때 그 대신 쉬는 평일이에요. '대체공휴일'이라고도 해요.

phrases.en: This year there are two substitute holidays.
phrases.nuance_ko: '대체휴일'과 같은 뜻이고 공식적인 말에 많이 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means the same as '대체휴일' and appears often in official wording.

phrases.en: I rest on the substitute holiday on Monday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 쉬는 날을 말할 때 '에'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '에' to say when you rest.
phrases.en_equiv: to rest on the substitute holiday

phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 날이 쉬는 날로 정해졌을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when a day has been set as a day off.

explain_en: It is a weekday off given when a public holiday falls on a weekend. It is also called '대체공휴일'.

examples.en: Sparks flew, and I was startled.
The candle flame is flickering.

explain: 불에서 타오르는 빛이나 튀는 작은 불이에요. '불꽃놀이'는 하늘에 터뜨리는 불꽃을 보는 행사예요.
explain_en: It is the burning light of a fire or a small spark. '불꽃놀이' means fireworks.

en: to rise; to come to mind

examples.en: A good idea came to me.
The sun is slowly rising.

explain: 해나 달이 위로 올라오거나, 생각이 갑자기 머릿속에 생긴다는 뜻이에요. '생각이 떠오르다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It means the sun or moon rises, or a thought suddenly comes to mind. It is used like '생각이 떠오르다'.

dis.h: float up slowly; idea comes to mind

p.n: 뜨다 is plainer; 떠오르다 stresses the gradual rising motion.

examples.en: The weather feels cold today.
That friend felt close to me.

explain: '느끼다'의 피동형이에요. 내가 일부러 느끼는 게 아니라 저절로 그렇게 느껴진다는 뜻이에요.
explain_en: It is the passive of '느끼다'. It means something feels a certain way on its own, not because you chose to feel it.

en: field (of study or work); domain; sector

examples.en: I want to challenge myself in a new field.
What field do you work in?

explain: 공부나 일에서 나누어진 영역이에요. '어떤 분야', '새로운 분야'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It is a division of study or work. It is used like '어떤 분야' (what field) and '새로운 분야' (a new field).

dis.h: area of study or work; abstract domain

p.n: 필드 is a physical sports ground, so it does not fit a field of work here.

examples.en: I got a phone call in the middle of the night.
It's the middle of the night, so the street is quiet.

explain: 밤이 아주 깊은 때예요. 보통 자정 전후를 말해요. '한낮'과 반대 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: in the middle of the night
phrases.en_equiv: in the middle of the night

explain_en: It is the deepest part of the night, usually around midnight. It is the opposite in feel to '한낮' (midday).

examples.en: It's midsummer now.
In midsummer, you really need an air conditioner.

explain: 여름 중에서 가장 더운 때예요. '한-'은 '가장 한창인'이라는 뜻을 더해요.
explain_en: It is the hottest part of summer. The prefix '한-' adds the sense of 'the very height of'.

examples.en: There's a networking event this evening.

examples.ko: 네트워킹을 하면 정보를 많이 얻을 수 있어요.
examples.en: Networking gets you a lot of information.

explain: 일이나 공부에서 사람들과 관계를 만드는 활동이에요. 영어 'networking'에서 온 말이고, 보통 '네트워킹을 하다'로 써요.
explain_en: It means building connections with people for work or study. It comes from English 'networking' and is usually used as '네트워킹을 하다'.

en: to throw oneself into; to devote oneself to

examples.en: He gave himself for his country.
I threw myself into the water to save the child.

explain: 어떤 일을 위해 목숨이나 몸을 아끼지 않고 나선다는 뜻의 관용구예요. 실제로 몸을 던질 때도 쓰지만 보통 비유로 써요.

phrases.example: 아이를 구하려고 몸을 던진 사람이 있어요.
phrases.en: There is a person who threw themselves in to save the child.
phrases.nuance_ko: 용기 있게 나선 사람을 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to describe someone who bravely stepped forward.
phrases.en_equiv: a person who threw themselves in

phrases.en: He threw himself in and saved his friend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 위험을 무릅쓰고 도왔다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means helping at the risk of one's own safety.

phrases.example: 저는 이 일에 몸을 던질 거예요.
phrases.en: I will throw myself into this work.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 일에 온 힘을 다하겠다는 결심을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: It expresses a decision to give all one's effort to something.

explain_en: This idiom means to give oneself fully to something without sparing one's body or life. It can be literal, but is mostly figurative.

en: to bother; to harass; to bully

examples.en: Don't pick on your younger sibling.
Mosquitoes bothered me all night.

explain: 다른 사람을 힘들게 하거나 불편하게 만든다는 뜻이에요. 사람뿐 아니라 동물에게도 쓸 수 있어요. 반복해서 괴롭히는 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: It means to make someone suffer or feel uncomfortable, often repeatedly. It works for animals as well as people.

examples.en: I had a urine test.
The color of my urine is different from usual.

explain: 몸에서 나오는 오줌을 점잖게 부르는 말이에요. 병원에서 '소변 검사'처럼 많이 써요.
explain_en: It is the polite or formal word for urine. It is common at hospitals, as in '소변 검사' (urine test).

examples.en: I need to have a stool test.
The baby had a bowel movement today.

explain: 몸에서 나오는 똥을 점잖게 부르는 말이에요. 병원에서 '대변 검사'처럼 써요. 반대말은 '소변'이에요.
explain_en: It is the polite or formal word for stool. It is used at hospitals, as in '대변 검사' (stool test). The pair word is '소변'.

examples.en: The Taebaek Mountains are in the east of Korea.
A road runs along the mountain range.

explain: 여러 산이 길게 이어진 것이에요. 한국에는 '태백산맥'이 있어요.

phrases.en: I can see a high mountain range far away.
phrases.nuance_ko: 높이를 말하는 말을 앞에 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put a word about height in front.

phrases.en: The train runs over the mountain range.
phrases.nuance_ko: 산맥 너머로 가는 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it for going across to the other side of a mountain range.

phrases.en: A mountain range stretches long to the north.
phrases.nuance_ko: 산이 길게 연결된 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it for mountains connected in a long line.

explain_en: It is a long chain of connected mountains. Korea has the '태백산맥' (Taebaek Mountains).

examples.en: There is a risk of a natural disaster.
We need to prepare for natural disasters in advance.

explain: 태풍, 지진, 홍수처럼 자연에서 일어나는 큰 피해예요. '자연재해가 발생하다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It is major damage caused by nature, such as typhoons, earthquakes, and floods. It is used like '자연재해가 발생하다'.

examples.en: I'm staying in Seoul for a week.

examples.ko: 비가 와서 하루 종일 집에 머물렀어요.
examples.en: It rained, so I stayed home all day.

explain: 한곳에 잠시 또는 한동안 있을 때 써요. '묵다'는 숙소에서 잘 때, '머물다'는 더 넓게 써요.
explain_en: Used when you stay in a place for a while. 묵다 is for lodging; 머물다 is broader.

examples.en: The cat attacked the mouse.
Our team attacks first.

explain: 상대를 치거나 해치려고 할 때, 경기에서 점수를 내려고 나아갈 때 써요. 반대말은 '방어하다'예요.
explain_en: Used for attacking an opponent, or going on the offensive in a game. The opposite is 방어하다.

en: to become closer; to get near

examples.en: The exam is getting closer.
I've become much closer with my friend.

explain: '가깝다'에 '-아/어지다'가 붙은 말이에요. 거리, 시간, 사람 사이가 가깝게 변할 때 써요.
explain_en: From 가깝다 + -아/어지다. Used when distance, time, or a relationship becomes closer.

examples.en: Chuseok is on the 15th of the 8th lunar month.
My birthday is by the lunar calendar.

explain: 달의 모양을 기준으로 한 달력이에요. 설날과 추석은 음력 날짜예요. 반대말은 '양력'이에요.
explain_en: A calendar based on the moon. Seollal and Chuseok follow it. The opposite is 양력.

examples.en: The noise outside gets in the way of studying.
Sorry for disturbing your work.

explain: 일이 잘 안 되게 막는 것이에요. '방해하다', '방해가 되다' 형태로 자주 써요.
explain_en: Something that gets in the way of what you're doing. Often used as 방해하다 or 방해가 되다.

examples.en: My phone needs charging.
I topped up my transit card.

explain: 배터리에 전기를 채우는 것이에요. 동사는 '충전하다', 돈을 채울 때도 써요.
explain_en: Filling a battery with power. The verb is 충전하다; it's also used for topping up money on a card.

examples.en: The monkey is eating a banana.
I saw monkeys at the zoo.

explain: 나무를 잘 타는 동물이에요. 십이지의 아홉 번째 동물이기도 해요.

phrases.en: born in the year of the monkey
phrases.en_equiv: born in the year of the monkey

explain_en: An animal that climbs trees well. It's also the ninth animal of the Korean zodiac.

examples.en: The cat's movements are very fast.
Even the small movement was caught on camera.

explain: '움직이다'에 '-ㅁ'이 붙은 명사예요. 몸이나 물건이 움직이는 모습, 사회의 변화에도 써요.

phrases.en: The fish isn't moving at all.
phrases.nuance_ko: 움직이지 않는 상태를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it for a state where nothing is moving.

phrases.en: If you exercise, your body movement gets better.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람의 몸이 움직이는 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it for how a person's body moves.

phrases.nuance_ko: 빠르기를 설명하는 말과 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it with words that describe speed.

explain_en: The noun form of 움직이다. Used for how a body or object moves, and also for trends or shifts.

en: to come into contact with; to encounter; to border

examples.en: There are many chances to experience Korean culture.
Our house borders the sea.

explain: 무엇을 직접 만나거나 듣고 보게 될 때 써요. 땅이 서로 닿아 있을 때도 써요.
explain_en: Used when you come across something firsthand, or when areas share a border.

examples.en: My younger sibling took my toy away.
Games take up all my time.

explain: 남의 것을 힘으로 억지로 가져갈 때 써요. 당하는 쪽은 '빼앗기다'를 써요.
explain_en: Used when you take something from someone by force. The passive, 빼앗기다, means to have something taken.

examples.en: The ball hit the window.
I clean the windows on weekends.

explain: 유리로 만든 창문이에요. 그냥 '창문'은 유리가 아니어도 돼요.

phrases.en: The window broke because of the ball.
phrases.nuance_ko: 유리창이 부서졌을 때 '깨지다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '깨지다' when a glass window breaks.

phrases.example: 유리창 너머로 눈이 오는 게 보여요.
phrases.en: I can see the snow falling beyond the window.
phrases.nuance_ko: 창문 반대쪽을 말할 때 '너머'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '너머' for the far side of the window.

phrases.en: Sunlight comes in through the clean window.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상태를 설명하는 말을 앞에 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put a word about its condition in front.

explain_en: A window made of glass. 창문 alone doesn't have to be glass.

en: to be transparent; to be clear

examples.en: The water is very clear.
I poured juice into a clear cup.

explain: 유리나 물처럼 안이 잘 보일 때 써요. 일을 숨기지 않고 공개할 때도 써요.
explain_en: Used for things you can see through, like glass or water. Also for openness, as in an honest process.

examples.en: The company developed a new app.
They develop this land and build a park.

explain: 새 물건이나 기술을 만들 때, 땅이나 능력을 쓸 수 있게 만들 때 써요.
explain_en: Used for creating new products or technology, and for developing land or abilities.

dis.h: create a new product, plan, or area

p.n: 발달시키다 does not mean to create something new, so it is not natural here.

examples.en: I read part of the book.
Only part of this story is true.

explain: 전체 중에서 한 부분이에요. 반대말은 '전부'예요.

phrases.en: I read a part of the book.
phrases.nuance_ko: '일부분'보다 짧고 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It is shorter than '일부분' and used often.

phrases.en: I only know part of that story.
phrases.nuance_ko: 전부가 아니라 조금만 안다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to say you know only a little, not everything.

phrases.en: This is only a part of the whole.
phrases.nuance_ko: '전체'와 함께 써서 전체와 부분을 비교해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it with '전체' to compare the whole and a part.

explain_en: One part of a whole. The opposite is 전부.

dis.h: a small portion of one thing

p.n: 일부 is a bit broader; 일부분 stresses a small piece of the one book.

examples.en: Most students come by bus.
I'm mostly at home on weekends.

explain: 명사로 '대부분의 사람'처럼 쓰고, 부사로 '대부분 집에 있어요'처럼도 써요.

phrases.nuance_ko: '대부분'이 명사 앞에서 '대부분의 ~'로 쓰일 때의 모습이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Shows 대부분 used before a noun as '대부분의 ~' (most of the ...).

phrases.en: I did almost all of my homework.
phrases.nuance_ko: '대부분'과 비슷하지만 일이 거의 끝났을 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 대부분, but often used when something is almost finished.

phrases.en: Most of the customers are students.
phrases.nuance_ko: '대부분'이 명사처럼 쓰여 '~이에요'가 붙은 모습이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Shows 대부분 acting as a noun followed by '~이에요'.

explain_en: Works as a noun (대부분의 사람) and as an adverb (대부분 집에 있어요).

examples.en: Don't give up.
I gave up on the exam.

explain: '포기하다'로 많이 써요. 하던 일을 그만두거나 권리·희망을 내려놓는 것을 말해요.
explain_en: Mostly used as 포기하다. It means quitting something you were doing or letting go of a right or hope.

examples.en: That singer signed with an agency.
I called the travel agency.

explain: 연예인이나 모델 일을 관리해 주는 회사, 또는 대행 회사를 말해요.

phrases.en: That singer signed a contract with her agency.
phrases.nuance_ko: 연예인이 속한 회사를 말할 때는 '에이전시'보다 '소속사'를 더 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: For the company a celebrity belongs to, Koreans use 소속사 more often than 에이전시.

phrases.en: I work at an entertainment agency.
phrases.nuance_ko: '에이전시' 앞에 일의 종류를 붙여 어떤 회사인지 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put the type of work before 에이전시 to say what kind of agency it is.
