phrases.en: I found a job through an agency.
phrases.nuance_ko: 대행 회사에 부탁해서 일을 했다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you got something done by asking an agency to handle it.

explain_en: A company that manages entertainers or models, or one that acts on a client's behalf.

examples.en: The company is hiring full-time employees.
We hired three new employees.

explain: 회사가 사람을 뽑아서 일을 맡길 때 써요. '정규직을 채용하다'처럼 목적어를 써요.
explain_en: Used when a company picks someone and gives them a job. It takes an object, as in 정규직을 채용하다.

examples.en: My position is team leader.
Our leader is kind.

explain: 팀이나 모임을 이끄는 사람이에요. 영어 reader(읽는 사람)와 달라요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 회사에서 팀을 이끄는 사람은 '리더'보다 '팀장'이라고 많이 불러요.
phrases.nuance_en: At a company, the person who heads a team is more often called 팀장 than 리더.

phrases.en: I became the team leader this time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이끄는 역할을 맡게 되었다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone takes on the role of leading.

phrases.nuance_ko: 모임이나 그룹의 대표를 말할 때 '그룹'을 앞에 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add 그룹 before 리더 to mean the head of a group.

explain_en: A person who leads a team or group. It is 'leader', not 'reader'.

examples.en: Season 2 of this drama is out.
It's soccer season now.

explain: 드라마나 스포츠에서 한 번에 이어지는 기간이나 편을 말해요. 일 년의 네 계절은 '계절'이라고 해요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 드라마의 몇 번째 묶음인지 숫자를 붙여서 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add a number to say which batch of a drama it is.

phrases.en: The new season starts next month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 드라마나 스포츠가 새로 시작하는 기간을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the new period of a drama or sport that is about to start.

phrases.nuance_ko: 스포츠나 행사 기간이 끝났을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a sports or event period has ended.

explain_en: A period or set of episodes in a show, sport, or event. For the four seasons of the year, use 계절.

examples.en: This novel satirizes society.
I like satirical cartoons.

explain: 사회나 사람의 잘못을 웃음으로 비꼬아 말하는 것이에요. 소설, 만화, 연극에 자주 나와요.
explain_en: Criticizing society or people's faults through humor and mockery. Common in novels, comics, and plays.

examples.en: I hurt my shin playing soccer.
My shin hurts.

explain: 무릎 아래부터 발목 위까지 앞쪽 뼈 부분이에요. 다리 전체는 '다리'라고 해요.

phrases.en: My friend kicked me in the shin.
phrases.nuance_ko: 운동할 때나 싸울 때 정강이를 발로 차는 상황에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used when someone is kicked in the shin during sports or a fight.

phrases.en: I fell and got a bruise on my shin.
phrases.nuance_ko: 정강이를 부딪쳐서 파랗게 된 것을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a shin turning blue after being hit.

phrases.en: I hurt my shinbone, so I went to the hospital.
phrases.nuance_ko: 정강이 안의 뼈를 말할 때 '뼈'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add 뼈 to talk about the bone inside the shin.

explain_en: The front part of the leg between the knee and the ankle. The whole leg is 다리.

en: to lie face down; to bend forward

examples.en: I sleep on my stomach.
I rested with my head down on the desk.

explain: 배가 바닥이나 침대에 닿게 눕거나 몸을 앞으로 숙일 때 써요. 보통 '엎드려서'로 써요.

phrases.en: I am lying face down on the bed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 엎드린 상태가 계속되고 있을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone stays in the face-down position.

phrases.nuance_ko: 병원이나 운동 수업에서 정중하게 부탁할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite request, often heard at a clinic or exercise class.

phrases.en: The child lay face down on the floor.
phrases.nuance_ko: 엎드리는 동작이 이미 끝났을 때 과거형으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Past tense for when the act of lying down has already happened.
phrases.en_equiv: lay face down on the floor

explain_en: To lie with your stomach down, or bend forward. Often used as 엎드려서.

examples.en: I'm struggling because of the time difference.
Korea and the US have a big time difference.

explain: 나라마다 시간이 다른 것을 말해요. '시차 적응', '시차 때문에'처럼 자주 써요.
explain_en: The difference in time between countries. Common in 시차 적응 and 시차 때문에.

examples.en: I bought a plane ticket.
Plane tickets are too expensive.

explain: 비행기를 탈 때 필요한 표예요. '비행기 표'로 띄어 쓰기도 하지만 붙여 쓰는 것도 많이 써요.
explain_en: The ticket you need to board a plane. Written 비행기표 or 비행기 표.

examples.en: Many people took part in the event.
I want to join this group too.

explain: 행사나 활동에 함께할 때 써요. '에 참여하다' 형태로 써요.

phrases.en: I took part in the running competition.
phrases.nuance_ko: '참여하다'와 비슷한데, 대회나 시합에는 '참가하다'를 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 참여하다, but 참가하다 is more common for contests and competitions.

phrases.nuance_ko: 참여가 가능하다고 안내할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say that participation is possible.

phrases.en: I did not take part in the last meeting.
phrases.nuance_ko: 활동에 함께하지 않았다는 부정 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A negative form meaning you did not join in the activity.

explain_en: To take part in an event or activity. Used as 에 참여하다.

dis.h: take part; neutral, general use

p.n: 동참하다 sounds like joining in a shared effort that others already started; 참여하다 just says you take part.

examples.en: A snowstorm is raging outside.
The flight was canceled because of the blizzard.

explain: 바람이 강하게 불면서 눈이 휘날리는 날씨예요. '눈보라가 치다'로 자주 써요.
explain_en: Weather with strong wind and swirling snow. Often used as 눈보라가 치다.

examples.en: That voice actor has a cool voice.
I got the voice actor's autograph.

explain: 목소리로 연기하는 사람이에요. 애니메이션이나 외국 영화 더빙을 해요.

phrases.en: I want to become a voice actor.
phrases.nuance_ko: 꿈이나 직업을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used when talking about a dream or a job.

phrases.en: Who is the dubbing voice actor of this movie?
phrases.nuance_ko: 외국 영화에서 한국말 목소리를 맡은 사람을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the person who does the Korean voice for a foreign film.

phrases.en: The voice acting is really good.
phrases.nuance_ko: 목소리로 하는 연기를 칭찬할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when praising acting done only with the voice.

explain_en: A person who acts with their voice, such as in animation or dubbed foreign films.

examples.en: I want to buy figures in Japan.
I have a lot of figures in my room.

explain: 캐릭터를 작게 만든 인형이에요. 모으는 것을 좋아하는 사람이 많아요.
explain_en: A small model of a character. Many people collect them as a hobby.

en: food eaten with alcohol; bar snack

examples.en: What did you have with your drinks?
Chicken goes well with beer.

explain: 술을 마실 때 같이 먹는 음식이에요. 밥과 달리 술과 함께 먹는 음식을 말해요.
explain_en: Food eaten while drinking alcohol. Unlike a meal, it accompanies the drinks.

examples.en: I got too drunk.
You get drunk fast on this drink.

explain: 술을 마셔서 정신이 흐려질 때 써요. '술에 취하다'로 써요.
explain_en: To become dizzy or unsteady from alcohol. Used as 술에 취하다.

examples.en: Today's lunch is braised kimchi.
I eat rice with braised kimchi.

explain: 오래 익은 김치와 고기를 넣고 푹 끓여서 만든 음식이에요.

phrases.en: I made braised kimchi with pork.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 고기를 넣었는지 앞에 붙여 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put the kind of meat before the dish name to say what is in it.

phrases.en: Two servings of braised kimchi, please.
phrases.nuance_ko: 식당에서 주문할 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A phrase used when ordering at a restaurant.

phrases.en: I want to eat braised kimchi today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 먹고 싶은 음식을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say which food you want to eat.
phrases.en_equiv: I want to eat braised kimchi

explain_en: A dish of well-fermented kimchi and meat simmered until tender.

examples.en: Two servings of marinated ribs, please.
Marinated ribs are sweet and tasty.

explain: 간장 양념에 재운 갈비예요. 양념하지 않은 '생갈비'와 달라요.

phrases.en: We grill marinated ribs at the barbecue restaurant.
phrases.nuance_ko: 고기를 불에 익힐 때는 '굽다'를 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 굽다 (to grill) when cooking the meat over fire.

phrases.en: We are going to eat marinated ribs this evening.
phrases.nuance_ko: '~(으)러 가다'로 먹으러 간다고 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '~(으)러 가다' to say you are going somewhere to eat.

phrases.en: There is a great marinated ribs restaurant in this neighborhood.
phrases.nuance_ko: 양념갈비를 맛있게 하는 식당을 말할 때 '맛집'을 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add 맛집 to talk about a restaurant known for good marinated ribs.

explain_en: Ribs marinated in a soy-based sauce. Different from unseasoned 생갈비.

examples.en: The painting came up for auction.

examples.ko: 경매에서 가장 높은 가격을 내면 살 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can buy it if you bid the highest price at the auction.

explain: 가장 높은 값을 부르는 사람에게 물건을 파는 방법이에요. '경매에 나오다', '경매를 하다'로 써요.

phrases.en: I also took part in the painting auction.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건을 사려고 경매에 함께할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you join an auction to buy something.
phrases.en_equiv: to take part in an auction

phrases.en: I bought this painting at an auction.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건을 산 방법이 경매일 때 '경매로'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 경매로 to say the way you bought something was an auction.

phrases.en: There are many people at the auction house.
phrases.nuance_ko: 경매가 열리는 장소를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the place where an auction is held.

explain_en: A way of selling to whoever offers the highest price. Used as 경매에 나오다 or 경매를 하다.

examples.en: I donate a little every month.
I donated clothes I don't wear.

explain: 돈이나 물건을 어려운 사람이나 단체에 그냥 주는 일이에요. '기부를 하다'로도 써요.
explain_en: Means giving money or things to people in need or to an organization for free. You can also say '기부를 하다'.

examples.en: This series has ten books in total.
I watched that whole drama series.

explain: 드라마, 책, 영화처럼 이어지는 작품 묶음을 말해요. 한 편은 '편'이나 '권'으로 세요.

phrases.en: That movie came out as a series.
phrases.nuance_ko: 작품이 여러 편으로 이어져서 나올 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a work is released in several connected parts.
phrases.en_equiv: to come out as a series

phrases.en: This is a very popular series.
phrases.nuance_ko: 많은 사람이 좋아하는 시리즈를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a series that many people like.

phrases.example: 이 시리즈의 첫 번째 책을 샀어요.
phrases.en: I bought the first book of this series.
phrases.nuance_ko: 시리즈 안의 한 권을 가리킬 때 '시리즈의'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 시리즈의 to point to one volume inside the series.
phrases.en_equiv: the first book of the series

explain_en: A set of connected works such as dramas, books, or movies. Count single parts with '편' or '권'.

examples.en: That artist publishes a webtoon every week.
This novel was serialized in a newspaper.

explain: 웹툰, 소설, 기사를 한 번에 다 내지 않고 나누어 계속 싣는 것이에요. 보통 '~에 연재하다'로 써요.
explain_en: To publish a webtoon, novel, or article in parts over time instead of all at once. Often used as '~에 연재하다'.

examples.en: A devil appears in the movie.
That person is scary like a devil.

explain: 나쁜 일을 하게 만드는 무서운 존재예요. 아주 못되거나 무서운 사람을 비유할 때도 써요.

phrases.example: 그 선생님은 시험 때 악마 같아요.
phrases.en: That teacher is like a devil during exams.
phrases.nuance_ko: '악마처럼'과 비슷하게, 사람이 아주 무섭거나 못됐다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Like 악마처럼, used to say a person is very scary or mean.

phrases.nuance_ko: 영화나 드라마에서 악마를 연기하는 역할을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the role of a devil in a movie or drama.

phrases.en: The devil's laugh in the movie was scary.
phrases.nuance_ko: '악마의 ~' 형태로 악마가 가진 것이나 악마와 관련된 것을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The form '악마의 ~' refers to something that belongs to or is linked with a devil.

explain_en: An evil, frightening being that leads people to do bad things. Also used figuratively for a very cruel person.

en: to pretend to; to act as if

examples.en: My younger sibling pretended to sleep.
I pretend to like that person.

explain: '-는 척하다', '-(으)ㄴ 척하다'처럼 말 뒤에 붙어서, 사실이 아닌데 그런 것처럼 행동한다는 뜻이에요. '체하다'와 비슷해요.

phrases.en: to act like you know; to acknowledge someone
phrases.en_equiv: to act like you know; to acknowledge someone

explain_en: Attached after a verb or adjective, as in '-는 척하다' or '-(으)ㄴ 척하다', to mean acting as if something is true when it isn't. Similar to '체하다'.

en: to be intriguing; to be interesting

examples.en: This book is really interesting.
I heard an interesting story.

explain: 어떤 일이 재미있고 더 알고 싶게 만든다는 뜻이에요. '흥미로운 이야기'처럼 꾸밀 때는 '흥미로운'이 돼요.
explain_en: Describes something that is interesting and makes you want to know more. Before a noun it becomes '흥미로운', as in '흥미로운 이야기'.

dis.h: intriguing; sparks curiosity, more formal

p.n: 흥미롭다 means curiosity-sparking. 재미있다 means enjoyable or fun.

examples.en: Our company has a free dress code.
I have some free time.

explain: 하고 싶은 대로 할 수 있고 막는 것이 없다는 뜻이에요. 꾸밀 때는 '자유로운'이 돼요.
explain_en: Means being able to do as you like with nothing holding you back. Before a noun it becomes '자유로운'.

en: streaming down; fluently; one after another

examples.en: Rainwater streams down the window.
The child recites the poem fluently.

explain: 물이 길게 계속 흐르는 모습이나, 막힘없이 술술 읽거나 말하는 모습에 써요.
explain_en: Describes liquid flowing down in a long stream, or reading and speaking smoothly without stopping.

en: gently; softly (of a breeze or swaying)

examples.en: A breeze blows gently.
The puppy wags its tail gently.

explain: 바람이 부드럽게 불거나 꼬리, 잎이 가볍게 흔들리는 모습이에요. 기분 좋고 약한 움직임에 써요.
explain_en: Describes a soft breeze or a tail or leaves swaying lightly. It suggests a gentle, pleasant movement.

examples.ko: 튜브가 물 위에 둥둥 떠 있어요.
examples.en: The tube is floating on the water.
The drum sounds boom-boom.

explain: 물이나 공중에 가볍게 떠 있는 모습이에요. 북을 치는 소리로도 써요.
explain_en: Describes something floating lightly on water or in the air. It is also the sound of a drum.

examples.en: The baby's cheeks are soft.
This blanket is soft and warm.

explain: 만지면 부드럽고 연한 느낌이에요. 보통 '보들보들하다'로 써요. 아기 피부, 동물 털에 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: Describes a soft, tender feel to the touch. Usually used as '보들보들하다', for example with baby skin or animal fur.

examples.en: A wave smacks against the rock.
I hear the splashing sound at the beach.

explain: 파도가 부딪치는 소리나 세게 때리는 소리예요. 계속될 때는 '철썩철썩'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: The waves keep slapping against the shore.
phrases.nuance_ko: 파도 소리가 계속될 때는 '철썩'을 두 번 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Repeat the word as 철썩철썩 when the wave sound continues.

phrases.en: My friend slapped my back with a smack.
phrases.nuance_ko: 손으로 세게 한 번 치는 소리를 나타낼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the sound of a single hard hit with a hand.

phrases.en: There was a splashing sound from the water.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물이나 몸에 부딪치는 소리가 들렸다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say a slapping or splashing sound was heard.

explain_en: The sound of waves hitting or of a hard slap. When it keeps going, say '철썩철썩'.

examples.en: Red is my favorite color.
The traffic light turned red.

explain: 불이나 사과 같은 색이에요. '빨간색'과 같은 말이고, 꾸밀 때는 '빨간'을 써요.
explain_en: The color of fire or an apple. Same as '빨간색'; before a noun use '빨간', as in '빨간 사과'.

dis.h: short noun form, red as a name

p.n: Same meaning; 빨간색 is the more common full form.

examples.en: I wore navy blue pants.
The sky turns deep blue in the evening.

explain: 아주 진한 파란색이에요. 교복이나 청바지 색을 말할 때 많이 써요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 물건의 색을 설명할 때 '~이에요'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add '~이에요' to describe the color of an object.

phrases.en: I bought a dark navy blue bag.
phrases.nuance_ko: 색이 더 어둡다는 것을 '진한'으로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 진한 to say the color is darker.

phrases.en: I painted the wall navy blue.
phrases.nuance_ko: '으로'를 붙여서 어떤 색으로 바꾸는지 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add 으로 to say which color something is painted.

explain_en: A very dark blue. Often used for the color of uniforms or jeans.

examples.en: The old paper is yellowish.
The rice has ripened to a yellowish color.

explain: 완전한 노란색은 아니고 조금 누런 빛이 난다는 뜻이에요. 오래된 종이나 익은 곡식에 잘 써요.

phrases.en: I wrote a letter on yellowish paper.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 꾸밀 때는 '누르스름한'으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Before a noun, the form is 누르스름한.

phrases.nuance_ko: 색이 조금씩 변했을 때 '-해지다'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add -해지다 when a color has gradually changed.

phrases.en: In autumn the rice plants ripen to a yellowish color.
phrases.nuance_ko: 곡식이 익으면서 빛이 조금 누렇게 변하는 모습에 '-게'를 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add -게 to describe grain turning slightly yellow as it ripens.

explain_en: Means slightly yellow, not a full yellow. Often used for old paper or ripening grain.

examples.en: I stroke the cat with my hand.
The mother stroked the child's head.

explain: 손으로 부드럽게 여러 번 만지는 것이에요. 동물, 아이의 머리나 등에 많이 써요.

phrases.nuance_ko: '-아/어 주세요'를 붙여 부드럽게 부탁할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add '-아/어 주세요' to make a polite request.

phrases.en: I read a book while petting my cat.
phrases.nuance_ko: 쓰다듬으면서 다른 일도 함께 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you do another thing while stroking.

phrases.nuance_ko: 위로하거나 사랑을 보여 줄 때 등을 쓰다듬어요.
phrases.nuance_en: People stroke someone's back to comfort them or show love.

explain_en: To touch something gently with your hand again and again. Often used for animals or a child's head or back.

examples.en: I look down at the village from the mountain.
If you look down out the window, you can see the street.

explain: 높은 곳에서 아래를 본다는 뜻이에요. 반대말은 '올려다보다'예요.
explain_en: To look down at something from a high place. The opposite is '올려다보다'.

examples.en: Raindrops fall from the sky.
A raindrop fell on my face.

explain: 비가 되어 떨어지는 물방울 하나하나예요. '빗방울이 떨어지다'로 자주 써요.
explain_en: Each individual drop of rain. Commonly used as '빗방울이 떨어지다'.

examples.en: Rainwater runs down the window.
Rainwater collected on the road.

explain: 비가 와서 고이거나 흐르는 물이에요. '빗방울'은 한 방울, '빗물'은 모인 물이에요.
explain_en: Water from rain that collects or flows. '빗방울' is a single drop, while '빗물' is the water as a whole.

examples.en: When it rains, I wear rain boots.
The child bought yellow rain boots.

explain: 비 오는 날 신는, 물이 안 들어오는 긴 신발이에요. '장화를 신다'로 써요.
explain_en: Long waterproof boots worn on rainy days. Used as '장화를 신다'.

examples.en: Children are playing on the sand.
It feels warm when you sit on the sand.

explain: 모래가 넓게 깔린 곳이에요. 바닷가나 강가, 놀이터에서 쓰고, '모래사장'과 비슷해요.
explain_en: A wide area covered with sand, such as a beach, riverbank or playground. Similar to 모래사장.

examples.en: I picked up shells at the beach.
I like grilled clams.

explain: 바닷가에 사는, 딱딱한 껍데기가 있는 동물이에요. 먹는 조개도 있고 바닷가에서 줍는 조개껍데기도 있어요.
explain_en: A sea animal with a hard shell. It can mean the clam you eat or the shell you pick up at the beach.

examples.en: I throw away the eggshell.
The seashell is really pretty.

explain: 조개, 달걀, 곡식처럼 속을 싸고 있는 딱딱한 겉부분이에요. 부드러운 과일 껍질은 '껍질'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: to shell; to peel off the shell
phrases.en_equiv: to shell; to peel off the shell

explain_en: The hard outer covering of a clam, egg or grain. For soft coverings like fruit skin, use 껍질.

examples.en: Seawater tastes salty.
The salty taste of this soup is too strong.

explain: 소금처럼 짠 맛이에요. '짠맛이 나다', '짠맛이 강하다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: A salty taste, like salt. Used in phrases like 짠맛이 나다 and 짠맛이 강하다.

examples.en: I watched the sunset at the sea.
The sunset is really beautiful.

explain: 저녁에 해가 질 때의 해, 또는 그때 비치는 붉은 빛이에요. 하늘이 붉게 물든 모습은 '노을'이라고 해요.
explain_en: The setting sun, or the reddish light it gives off in the evening. The red glow across the sky is called 노을.

en: to be made up of; to be structured; to be composed

examples.en: Korean food is made up of rice and side dishes.

examples.ko: 우리 반은 열 명으로 구성되어 있어요.
examples.en: Our class consists of ten people.

explain: 여러 부분이 모여 하나가 되는 것을 말해요. 'A은/는 B(으)로 구성되다' 형태로 써요.
explain_en: Describes something formed from several parts. Used as 'A은/는 B(으)로 구성되다'.

en: to surrender; to yield; to submit

examples.en: The enemy finally surrendered.
My younger sibling gave in to the tickling.

explain: 싸움이나 경기에서 졌다고 인정하고 그만두는 것이에요. 전쟁뿐 아니라 일상에서 '졌다'는 뜻으로도 써요.
explain_en: To admit defeat and give in to the other side. Used for war, but also casually for 'I give up'.

examples.en: I eat carrots with a crunch.
This cabbage kimchi is crisp.

explain: 싱싱한 채소나 과일을 씹을 때 나는 소리나 느낌이에요. '아삭아삭하다'로도 써요.
explain_en: The crunchy sound or feel of biting fresh vegetables or fruit. Also used as 아삭아삭하다.

examples.en: I eat an apple with a crisp crunch.
I write with a pencil, scratching softly.

explain: 사과나 배를 씹는 소리, 연필로 종이에 쓰는 소리처럼 가볍고 바삭한 소리예요.

phrases.example: 과일을 먹을 때 사각사각 소리가 나요.
phrases.en: A crisp crunching sound comes out when I eat fruit.
phrases.nuance_ko: 소리가 난다고 설명할 때 '소리가 나요'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add 소리가 나요 to say that the sound is heard.

phrases.en: I crunch and eat the pear.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바삭하고 시원한 과일을 씹을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when chewing crisp, fresh fruit.

explain_en: A light, crisp sound, like biting an apple or a pencil writing on paper.

examples.en: Snow is coming down heavily.
The balloons popped one after another.

explain: 눈이 많이 쏟아지거나 무엇이 터지는 소리를 나타내요. 눈이 올 때 '눈이 펑펑 오다'를 가장 많이 써요.
explain_en: Describes snow falling heavily or a popping sound. 눈이 펑펑 오다 is the most common use.

en: sinking in deep again and again (mud, snow)

examples.en: My feet sink deep into the snow with every step.
My legs kept sinking into the mudflat.

explain: 눈이나 진흙에 발이 깊게 자꾸 빠지는 모양이에요. '푹푹 빠지다'로 자주 써요.

phrases.en: to be sweltering hot and humid
phrases.en_equiv: to be sweltering hot and humid

explain_en: Describes feet sinking deep into snow or mud again and again. Often used as 푹푹 빠지다.

dis.h: sinking in again and again, step by step

p.n: 푹푹 means sinking repeatedly with each step; 푹 is a single sinking.

examples.en: Rain is dripping down.
Sweat is dripping.

explain: 물이나 눈물이 방울져 계속 떨어지는 모양이에요. '뚝뚝 떨어지다'로 써요.
explain_en: Describes liquid falling in drops, such as water or tears. Used as 뚝뚝 떨어지다.

examples.en: The rain is pouring steadily.
Tears are streaming down.

explain: 비가 길게 줄기차게 내리는 모양이에요. 눈물이나 땀이 흐를 때도 써요.

phrases.en: Since morning the rain has been pouring down.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비가 오래 많이 올 때 '내리다'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with 내리다 when rain falls heavily for a long time.

phrases.en: It is hot, so sweat is streaming down.
phrases.nuance_ko: 땀이나 물이 길게 흐르는 모양에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for sweat or water flowing in a long stream.

phrases.example: 주룩주룩 오는 비 때문에 못 나갔어요.
phrases.en: I could not go out because of the pouring rain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '비'를 꾸미는 말로도 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: It can also describe the noun 비 (rain).

explain_en: Describes rain pouring down in long, steady streams. Also used for tears or sweat running down.

examples.en: A fine drizzle is falling.
I got caught in the light drizzle.

explain: 비가 가늘고 조용하게 내리는 모양이에요. 약하게 내리는 봄비에 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: Describes rain falling softly in fine drops. Fits gentle spring rain.

en: leisurely, without hurry; (슬슬 ~해야겠다) it's about time to ~

examples.en: Shall we get started?
I think it's about time I head home.

explain: 서두르지 않고 천천히 하는 모양이에요. '슬슬 ~할까요?'는 이제 시작할 때가 됐다는 뜻이에요.
explain_en: Doing something slowly, without rushing. '슬슬 ~할까요?' means it's about time to start.

examples.en: I need wrapping paper for the gift.
Please tear open the wrapping paper.

explain: 선물이나 물건을 싸는 종이예요. '포장'은 싸는 일, '-지'는 종이를 뜻해요.
explain_en: Paper used to wrap gifts or goods. 포장 means wrapping and -지 means paper.

examples.en: The stew is bubbling away.
Bubbles are rising up.

explain: 찌개 같은 음식이 끓을 때 나는 소리나 모양이에요. 거품이 생기는 모양에도 써요.
explain_en: The sound or look of stew bubbling as it boils. Also used for foam forming.

en: rubbing or wiping lightly and quickly

examples.en: I wipe the table with a dishcloth.
I rub it with my hand.

explain: 무엇을 가볍게 문지르거나 빠르게 닦는 모양이에요. '슥슥'은 비슷한 말이에요.
explain_en: Describes rubbing or wiping something quickly and lightly. 슥슥 is a similar word.

en: to be stinging; to be prickly; to be scorching (sun)

examples.en: The sunlight is so scorching.
Shampoo got in my eyes and it stings.

explain: 바늘로 찌르는 듯 아프거나 햇볕이 뜨겁게 느껴질 때 써요. 'ㅂ' 불규칙이라 '따가워요'가 돼요.
explain_en: Used for a pricking pain or strong, burning sunlight. It is a ㅂ-irregular adjective: 따가워요.

examples.en: After the shower, my body feels fresh and dry.
The laundry dried soft and fluffy.

explain: 물기가 없이 보드랍고 산뜻한 모양이에요. 씻은 뒤의 몸이나 마른 수건에 써요. '보송보송하다'로도 써요.
explain_en: Dry, soft and fresh-feeling. Used for skin after a bath or a dry towel. Also 보송보송하다.

examples.en: The rabbit hops along.
The child hops along.

explain: 토끼처럼 가볍게 뛰는 모양이에요. 아이들이 신나서 뛸 때도 써요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 한 번만 가볍게 뛸 때는 '깡충'만 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use just 깡충 for a single light hop.

phrases.nuance_ko: 여기저기 계속 뛰는 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for jumping around from place to place.

phrases.nuance_ko: 뛰면서 다른 일도 함께 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when doing something else while hopping.

explain_en: Describes light hopping like a rabbit. Also used for kids bouncing with joy.

examples.en: This coffee is sweet.
I want some sweet bread.

explain: 맛이 기분 좋게 달다는 말이에요. '달다'보다 말할 때 편하게 써요.
explain_en: Means pleasantly sweet. It is a casual, spoken version of 달다.

examples.en: The bread is neatly arranged.
Please line up your shoes neatly.

explain: 여러 물건이 줄을 맞춰 깔끔하게 놓인 모양이에요. '가지런히 놓다', '가지런히 놓이다'로 써요.
explain_en: Describes things lined up neatly in order. Used as 가지런히 놓다 or 가지런히 놓이다.

examples.en: The crumble-top bread is delicious.
I bought a crumble-top bun at the bakery.

explain: 위에 바삭한 가루 반죽을 올려 구운 빵이에요. 한국 빵집에서 흔히 볼 수 있어요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 빵집에서 빵의 수를 셀 때 '개'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 개 to count pieces of bread at a bakery.

phrases.nuance_ko: 좋아하는 빵을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say which bread you like.

phrases.en: I had crumble-top bread and milk.
phrases.nuance_ko: '이랑'으로 같이 먹은 음식을 이어 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 이랑 to connect foods eaten together.

explain_en: A bun topped with crumbly, crunchy dough. A common item in Korean bakeries.

examples.en: It is full of sweet red bean filling.
I put sweet red bean filling inside the bread.

explain: 팥을 설탕과 함께 달게 삶은 것이에요. 빵이나 떡의 속에 많이 들어가요.
explain_en: Red beans boiled with sugar until sweet. Often used as filling in bread and rice cakes.

examples.en: I roll the ball on the floor.
The child rolls a snowball.

explain: 공이나 바퀴처럼 둥근 것을 움직여서 돌게 할 때 써요. 스스로 구르는 '구르다'와 달리 누군가 굴리는 거예요.

phrases.en: to think hard; to use one's brain
phrases.en_equiv: to think hard; to use one's brain

explain_en: Use it when you make a round object roll. Unlike 구르다 (something rolls by itself), 굴리다 needs someone doing the rolling.

en: opening and closing the mouth (like a fish)

examples.en: The goldfish opens and closes its mouth.

examples.ko: 물고기가 물 위에서 뻐끔뻐끔 숨을 쉬어요.
examples.en: The fish breathes at the surface, mouth opening and closing.

explain: 물고기가 입을 열었다 닫았다 하는 모습을 나타내요. 담배를 피우는 모습에도 쓰지만 물고기에게 가장 많이 써요.

phrases.en: The fish opens and closes its mouth.
phrases.nuance_ko: 입을 계속 열었다 닫는 모습을 '입을 벌리다'와 함께 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a mouth repeatedly opening and closing, with 입을 벌리다.

phrases.en: The goldfish keeps opening and closing its mouth.
phrases.nuance_ko: '뻐끔뻐끔'에 '-거리다'를 붙인 동사로, 같은 모습을 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: A verb made from 뻐끔뻐끔 plus -거리다, describing the same motion.

phrases.en: The fish eats its food in little gulps.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물고기가 먹이를 입으로 받아 먹는 모습에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a fish takes food into its mouth.

explain_en: It describes a fish opening and closing its mouth. It is also used for puffing on a cigarette, but fish are the most common use.

examples.en: The fish swim here and there.
I ran around looking for my keys.

explain: 여러 방향으로 계속 움직일 때 써요. 한 곳이 아니라 이쪽저쪽으로 가는 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: to look over from all sides
phrases.en_equiv: to look over from all sides

explain_en: Used when something keeps moving in many directions. It suggests going this way and that, not staying in one place.

examples.en: Please don't drop rice grains.
You have rice grains stuck around your mouth.

explain: 밥 한 알 한 알을 말해요. 보통 '밥알이 붙다', '밥알을 흘리다'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: I did not leave a single grain of rice.
phrases.nuance_ko: 밥을 다 먹지 않고 조금 남길 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you leave a bit of rice uneaten.

phrases.en: A grain of rice fell on my clothes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 밥알이 아래로 떨어졌을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a rice grain drops down.

phrases.en: Do not throw away even one grain of rice.
phrases.nuance_ko: '하나도' 앞에 써서 '조금도'의 느낌을 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used before 하나도 to give the feeling of 'not even a bit'.

explain_en: A single grain of cooked rice. It is often used in phrases like 밥알이 붙다 (rice sticks) or 밥알을 흘리다 (drop rice).

examples.en: I tap you lightly on the shoulder.
The rain taps on the window.

explain: 가볍게 두드리거나 작은 것이 튀거나 떨어지는 모양이에요. 한 번이면 '톡'이에요.
explain_en: Describes light, repeated tapping or small things popping or dropping. A single tap is 톡.

examples.en: Get up quickly.
It's raining. Let's go inside right away.

explain: 기다리지 말고 빨리 하라고 할 때 자주 써요. '얼른 와요', '얼른 먹어요'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: Often used to urge someone to do something without delay, as in 얼른 와요 (come quickly).

dis.h: right away, without delay

p.n: 어서 is a more welcoming, encouraging 'come on'.

examples.en: Brush your teeth after eating.
I brushed my teeth in the morning.

explain: 이를 닦는 소리나 모양을 나타내요. 주로 어린이에게 '치카치카 해요'라고 말해요.
explain_en: Imitates brushing teeth. It is mostly child-directed speech, as in 치카치카 해요.

examples.en: I brush my molars too.
My molar hurt, so I went to the dentist.

explain: 입 안쪽에 있는 크고 넓은 이예요. 음식을 씹고 갈 때 써요.
explain_en: The large, wide teeth at the back of the mouth, used for chewing and grinding food.

examples.en: My hands are sticky.
The honey is sticky.

explain: 손에 붙는 것처럼 끈끈한 느낌이에요. '끈적끈적하다'로도 써요.
explain_en: Describes a gooey, clingy feel. It also works as the verb-like form 끈적끈적하다.

examples.en: The rabbit twitches its ears upright.
The puppy perks up its ears at the sound.

explain: 귀나 뾰족한 끝이 위로 서서 움직이는 모양이에요. 토끼나 강아지 귀에 많이 써요.
explain_en: Describes ears or pointed tips standing up and twitching, typically a rabbit's or puppy's ears.

examples.en: The snack is crispy.
I fried the chicken until crispy.

explain: 튀김이나 과자처럼 마르고 가볍게 부서지는 느낌이에요. '바삭바삭하다'로도 써요.
explain_en: The dry, light crunch of fried food or snacks. Also used as 바삭바삭하다.

examples.en: My teeth ache when I drink cold water.
My hands get cold and achy in winter.

explain: 찬 것 때문에 이나 손발이 아프고 저린 느낌이에요. '이가 시리다', '손이 시리다'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: eyes sting (from bright light or cold wind)
phrases.en_equiv: eyes sting (from bright light or cold wind)

explain_en: A sharp cold ache in teeth, hands or feet. Typical uses: 이가 시리다, 손이 시리다.

examples.ko: 비 온 뒤에 달팽이가 많이 나와요.
examples.en: Lots of snails come out after the rain.
A snail is on the leaf.

explain: 등에 껍데기가 있고 아주 천천히 기어가는 동물이에요. 비 온 뒤에 자주 볼 수 있어요.

phrases.example: 잎 위에 달팽이 한 마리가 있어요.
phrases.en: There is one snail on the leaf.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동물은 '마리'로 세요.
phrases.nuance_en: Animals are counted with 마리.

phrases.en: I walk slowly like a snail.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아주 느린 모습을 비유할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used as a comparison for something very slow.

phrases.nuance_ko: 달팽이 등에 있는 집을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the shell on a snail's back.

explain_en: A slow animal that carries a shell on its back. You often see them after rain.

examples.en: The snail goes along slowly.
Grandfather walks slowly.

explain: 동작이 느리고 급하지 않은 모양이에요. '천천히'보다 굼뜬 느낌이 있어요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 천천히 움직이는 동물이나 사람에게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for animals or people who move slowly.

phrases.nuance_ko: 말이 느리고 급하지 않을 때도 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Can also describe slow, unhurried speech.

phrases.nuance_ko: '-하다'를 붙여 상태를 설명할 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add -하다 to describe a state.

explain_en: Describes slow, unhurried movement. It feels more sluggish than 천천히.

examples.en: I picked up a turban shell on the beach.
Hold the shell to your ear.

explain: 바다에 사는 동물이고, 돌돌 말린 단단한 껍데기가 있어요. 소라 껍데기는 귀에 대면 바다 소리가 나는 것 같아요.
explain_en: A sea snail with a hard, spiral shell. Held to the ear, the shell seems to sound like the sea.

en: to put in; to stuff in

examples.en: I stuffed my phone into my bag before the test.
I put the toys into the box.

explain: 무엇을 잡아서 안에 넣을 때 써요. '넣다'보다 급하게 또는 힘주어 넣는 느낌이 있어요.

phrases.en: I put the book in my bag.
phrases.nuance_ko: '집어넣다'보다 급하거나 힘주는 느낌 없이 평범하게 넣을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A plain, neutral word for putting something in, without the hurried or forceful feeling of 집어넣다.

phrases.en: It was cold, so I stuffed my hands in my pockets.
phrases.nuance_ko: 손이나 작은 물건을 주머니에 빨리 넣을 때 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for quickly sticking your hands or a small item into a pocket.

phrases.en: Please don't stuff trash in here.
phrases.nuance_ko: 무엇을 함부로 넣지 말라고 부탁하거나 말할 때 쓰는 존댓말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite way to tell someone not to shove or stuff things into a place.

explain_en: To pick something up and put it inside. It feels a bit quicker or more forceful than 넣다.

dis.h: stuff in quickly with the hand

p.n: 넣다 is neutral; 집어넣다 stresses a quick, casual push.

en: to be damp; to be moist

examples.en: The ground is damp after the rain.
The laundry is still damp.

explain: 물기가 조금 있어서 마르지 않은 느낌이에요. 젖은 정도는 '젖다'보다 약해요.

phrases.en: If you wear damp clothes, you'll catch a cold.
phrases.nuance_ko: '축축하다'를 명사 앞에서 꾸미는 모양(~ㄴ)으로, 물건 이름 앞에 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The adjective form placed before a noun to describe something as damp.

phrases.en: My shoes are damp, so they're uncomfortable.
phrases.nuance_ko: 축축한 이유를 말하고 뒤 내용을 이어 갈 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to give dampness as a reason and connect to the next part of the sentence.

phrases.nuance_ko: 물기가 다 말랐을 때 쓰는 부정 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form, used when something has dried out.

explain_en: Slightly wet and not dry. It is less wet than 젖다 (soaked).

examples.en: The snail crawls along.
The baby crawls toward the toy.

explain: 몸을 땅에 가까이 대고 천천히 가요. 아기, 벌레, 달팽이에게 써요.
explain_en: To move slowly with the body close to the ground. Used for babies, insects and snails.

en: it's a big problem; we're in trouble

examples.en: If I lose my wallet, I'm in trouble.
I overslept. I'm in big trouble!

explain: 나쁜 일이 생기거나 생길 것 같을 때 써요. '큰일 났다', '큰일 나다'로도 말해요.
explain_en: Said when something bad has happened or is about to. Also used as 큰일 났다 / 큰일 나다.

examples.en: Hail fell.
The car was damaged by the hail.

explain: 비와 함께 떨어지는 작고 단단한 얼음 알갱이예요. '우박이 떨어지다', '우박이 내리다'로 써요.

phrases.en: Hail suddenly fell in the afternoon.
phrases.nuance_ko: '우박이 떨어지다'와 같은 뜻이고, 날씨를 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means the same as 'fall' for hail and is common in weather talk.

phrases.en: I got hit by hail and it hurt.
phrases.nuance_ko: 우박이 사람이나 물건에 떨어졌을 때 '맞다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 맞다 when hail actually hits a person or thing.

phrases.en: The hail stopped and the sun came out.
phrases.nuance_ko: 우박이 멈췄을 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the hail stops falling.

explain_en: Small hard pieces of ice that fall from the sky. Use 우박이 떨어지다 or 우박이 내리다.

examples.en: I jumped over the puddle.
I was busy, so I skipped lunch.

explain: 가운데 하나를 빼고 다음으로 가거나, 어떤 곳을 뛰어서 넘을 때 써요. 순서나 계획에도 써요.
explain_en: To jump across something, or to skip one item and go to the next. It also works for order or schedules.

examples.en: I want to become a scientist.
The scientist is doing an experiment.

explain: 과학을 연구하는 사람이에요. 직업을 말할 때 '과학자예요'라고 해요.

phrases.en: My older sister is a scientist.
phrases.nuance_ko: 직업을 소개할 때 쓰는 해요체 문장이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite sentence ending used to say someone's job.

phrases.en: I met a famous scientist yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: '유명한'을 앞에 붙이면 어떤 과학자인지 더 말할 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 유명한 in front tells what kind of scientist it is.

phrases.nuance_ko: '들'을 붙여서 과학자가 여러 명일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 들 makes it plural, for more than one scientist.

explain_en: A person who studies science. To state the job, say 과학자예요.

en: to die by suicide; to kill oneself

examples.ko: 자살하고 싶은 생각이 들면 상담 전화에 연락하세요.
examples.en: If you have thoughts of suicide, call a counseling hotline.
I heard a story on the news about a person who died by suicide.

explain: 스스로 목숨을 끊는다는 뜻이에요. 뉴스나 글에서 쓰고, 일상 대화에서는 조심해서 말해요.

phrases.example: 자살한 사람의 가족을 도와 주는 모임이 있어요.
phrases.en: There is a group that helps the families of people who died by suicide.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스나 글에서 쓰는 말이에요. 일상 대화에서는 조심해서 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in news and writing; be careful using it in everyday talk.

phrases.en: The school gives suicide prevention education.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자살을 막으려는 활동이나 교육을 말할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for programs or education that aim to prevent suicide.

phrases.en: Even when things are hard, ask for help so that you don't die by suicide.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자살을 막으려는 목적을 말할 때 쓰는 연결 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A connecting phrase that states the aim of preventing suicide.
phrases.en_equiv: so as not to die by suicide

explain_en: It means to take one's own life. It appears in news and writing, and people use it carefully in conversation.

examples.en: That country is a communist country.
I learned about communism at school.

explain: 재산을 모두가 함께 가지자는 생각이나 정치 체제예요. '-주의'는 생각이나 이념을 뜻해요.
explain_en: It is the idea or political system in which property is shared by everyone. '-주의' means an ideology or -ism.

examples.en: My grandmother prays to God every day.
God will protect us.

explain: 기독교에서 믿는 신을 높여 부르는 말이에요. 같은 뜻으로 '하나님'도 써요.

phrases.nuance_ko: '하느님'과 같은 뜻이에요. 개신교에서는 보통 '하나님'을 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 하느님; Protestant churches usually use 하나님.

phrases.nuance_ko: 종교를 말할 때 '믿다'와 함께 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used with 믿다 when talking about religion.

phrases.en: They say God's love has no end.
phrases.nuance_ko: '의'를 붙여서 하느님에게서 오는 것을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 의 shows something that belongs to or comes from God.

explain_en: It is the respectful word for the God worshipped in Christianity. '하나님' is also used with the same meaning.

examples.en: My younger sibling often complains about the food.
Don't complain, let's do it together.

explain: 마음에 들지 않는 일을 말로 드러내는 거예요. 보통 '~에 대해 불평하다', '~을 불평하다'로 써요.
explain_en: It means to voice your dissatisfaction about something. It is used as '~에 대해 불평하다'.

examples.en: I have a habit of biting my nails.
You should fix bad habits quickly.

explain: 자기도 모르게 자주 하는 행동이에요. '습관'은 좋고 나쁨에 모두 쓰지만 '버릇'은 주로 고치고 싶은 행동에 써요.
explain_en: It is a behavior you repeat without noticing. '습관' can be good or bad, but '버릇' is mostly used for habits you want to fix.

dis.h: casual; unconscious quirk, often a bad one

p.n: 습관 is more neutral and formal; 버릇 sounds like a personal quirk.

examples.en: I hurt my leg and got treated at the hospital.
If you get treatment, you will get better soon.

explain: 치료를 받는다는 뜻이에요. 의사는 '치료하다', 환자는 '치료받다'를 써요.

phrases.en: I'm receiving treatment at the hospital now.
phrases.nuance_ko: 치료가 아직 계속되고 있을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the treatment is still going on.

phrases.en: If it hurts a lot, get treated quickly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대에게 치료를 권할 때 쓰는 존댓말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite way to advise someone to get treatment.

phrases.en: After getting treatment, I got much better.
phrases.nuance_ko: 치료가 끝난 다음의 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to talk about what happened after the treatment.

explain_en: It means to get medical treatment. Doctors 치료하다; patients 치료받다.

examples.en: The hospital bill is too expensive.
I have insurance, so I paid only a small part of the hospital bill.

explain: 병원에서 내는 돈이에요. '-비'는 돈, 비용을 뜻해요.
explain_en: It is the money you pay at a hospital. '-비' means cost or fee.

en: to become soft; to become gentle

examples.en: The ground became soft after the rain.
My personality became gentler as I got older.

explain: '부드럽다'에 '-아/어지다'가 붙어 상태가 변한다는 뜻이에요. 물건, 소리, 성격에 써요.
explain_en: It adds '-아/어지다' to '부드럽다' to show a change of state. It works for objects, sounds, and personality.

examples.en: When spring comes, new leaves grow on the trees.
One new leaf came out on the potted plant.

explain: 봄에 나무에서 새로 나오는 잎이에요. '새-'는 '새로 나온'이라는 뜻이에요.
explain_en: It is a leaf newly growing on a tree in spring. '새-' means 'newly'.

examples.en: When spring came, the grass sprouted.
New sprouts are coming out on the branch.

explain: 싹, 새잎, 털 같은 것이 겉으로 나온다는 뜻이에요. 보통 '싹이 돋아나다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It means that something like a sprout or leaf comes out on the surface. Typical use: '싹이 돋아나다'.

examples.en: Many pretty flowers bloom in spring.
The cherry blossoms have already bloomed.

explain: 꽃이 열려서 모양이 보인다는 뜻이에요. '꽃이 피다'로 써요. 반대말은 '지다'예요.
explain_en: It means a flower opens up. Use it as '꽃이 피다'. The opposite is '지다' (to fall).

dis.h: basic word; flowers opening

p.n: Same meaning; 피어나다 feels more gradual and vivid.

en: to become light; to become lighter

examples.en: I took things out, so my bag became lighter.
After talking about it, my heart felt lighter.

explain: '가볍다'에 '-아/어지다'가 붙어 가볍게 변한다는 뜻이에요. 무게나 마음의 짐이 줄 때 써요.
explain_en: It adds '-아/어지다' to '가볍다' and means becoming light. It is used for weight or a burden on the mind.

en: to be sultry; to be humid and hot

examples.en: Summer in Korea is hot and humid.
On sultry days, I drink cold water.

explain: 날씨가 습하고 몹시 덥다는 뜻이에요. 'ㅂ' 불규칙이라서 '무더워요', '무더운'이 돼요.
explain_en: It means the weather is humid and very hot. It is a ㅂ-irregular adjective: '무더워요', '무더운'.

examples.en: Cicadas sing on summer mornings.
A cicada is clinging to the tree.

explain: 여름에 나무에서 크게 우는 곤충이에요. 한국 여름 소리를 말할 때 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is an insect that sings loudly in trees in summer. It often appears when describing Korean summer sounds.

examples.en: A dog barks loudly at night.
The puppy barked at a stranger.

explain: 개가 큰 소리로 소리를 낸다는 뜻이에요. 보통 '개가 짖다'로 써요.
explain_en: It means a dog makes a loud sound. Usually used as '개가 짖다'.

examples.en: Birds chirp every morning.
I can hear birds chirping outside the window.

explain: 새가 가볍고 높은 소리로 계속 운다는 뜻이에요. 새 소리에만 써요.
explain_en: It means a bird keeps making light, high sounds. It is used only for birds.

examples.en: I go around looking for good restaurants.
I went around looking for a house all day.

explain: 무엇을 찾으려고 여러 곳을 다닌다는 뜻이에요. 한 번 찾는 '찾다'와 달리 계속 돌아다니는 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: I went around looking everywhere for my lost cat.
phrases.nuance_ko: '여기저기'를 붙이면 여러 곳을 다니는 모습이 더 잘 보여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 여기저기 makes the picture of going to many places clearer.

phrases.en: These days I'm going around looking for a job.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일자리를 구하려고 여러 곳에 가 볼 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for visiting many places to look for work.
phrases.en_equiv: to go around looking for a job

phrases.en: I don't have to go around looking for restaurants anymore.
phrases.nuance_ko: 더 이상 돌아다니며 찾을 필요가 없을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when there's no longer any need to wander around searching.
phrases.en_equiv: don't need to go around looking

explain_en: It means going to many places to look for something. Unlike '찾다', it suggests moving around continuously.

examples.en: I put clothes in the suitcase.
The suitcase is too heavy.

explain: 바퀴가 달린 여행용 가방을 말해요. 영어 'carrier'에서 온 말이고 '여행 가방'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: It is a travel bag with wheels. It comes from English 'carrier', and '여행 가방' means the same.

examples.en: This gym requires a membership.
If you sign up for the membership, it's 10% cheaper.

explain: 가게나 서비스에 가입해서 혜택을 받는 자격이에요. '멤버십에 가입하다', '멤버십이 있다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: A status you sign up for to get benefits from a shop or service. Used as '멤버십에 가입하다' or '멤버십이 있다'.

examples.en: I pay a 30,000 won membership fee a month.
The membership fee includes the towel charge too.

explain: 모임이나 시설의 회원이 되려고 내는 돈이에요. 보통 '회원비를 내다'로 써요.

phrases.en: I pay the membership fee on the 1st of every month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 회원비를 낼 때 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common phrase for paying a membership fee.

phrases.en: How much is the membership fee at this pool?
phrases.nuance_ko: 가격을 물어볼 때 쓰는 질문이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A question used to ask the price.
phrases.en_equiv: how much is the membership fee?

phrases.en: That gym's membership fee is expensive.
phrases.nuance_ko: 회원비가 많이 든다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say the membership fee costs a lot.

explain_en: Money you pay to be a member of a club or facility. Usually used as '회원비를 내다'.

examples.en: The cat gave birth to three kittens.
A baby bird is chirping in the tree.

explain: 동물의 어린 것을 말해요. 사람에게 '새끼'라고 하면 욕이 될 수 있으니 조심해야 해요.
explain_en: The young of an animal. Calling a person '새끼' can be an insult, so be careful.

examples.en: I want to make Korean content.
This channel's content is fun.

explain: 영상, 글, 사진처럼 인터넷이나 책에 담긴 내용이에요. '콘텐츠를 만들다', '콘텐츠를 보다'로 써요.
explain_en: Videos, writing, or photos made for the internet or media. Used as '콘텐츠를 만들다' or '콘텐츠를 보다'.

dis.h: digital media like videos and articles

p.n: 콘텐츠 is media as a product; 내용 would only mean the substance of something.

examples.ko: 한국어를 배우는 데 노력이 많이 들어요.
examples.en: Learning Korean takes a lot of effort.
If you work at it, you can definitely get good.

explain: 무언가를 이루려고 힘을 쓰는 것이에요. '노력하다'로도 쓰고, '노력이 들다'는 힘이 많이 필요하다는 뜻이에요.
explain_en: Putting in energy to achieve something. Also used as the verb '노력하다'; '노력이 들다' means it takes a lot of effort.

dis.h: striving toward a goal

p.n: 수고 means the toil or trouble taken, not striving toward a goal.

examples.en: The singer steps onto the stage.
I was surprised because the stage was so big.

explain: 공연을 하는 높은 곳이에요. '무대에 서다', '무대에 올라가다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: The raised area where performances happen. Used as '무대에 서다' or '무대에 올라가다'.

examples.en: My dad wanted to retire in three years.
That player retired last year.

explain: 일이나 활동을 그만두는 것이에요. 직장뿐 아니라 운동선수나 가수에게도 써요.
explain_en: To stop working or active service. Used for jobs, but also for athletes and singers.

examples.en: The lobster is too expensive.
We went to eat lobster.

explain: 바다에 사는 큰 새우 같은 갑각류로, 비싼 요리 재료예요. '바닷가재'라고도 해요.
explain_en: A large sea crustacean used in expensive dishes. Also called '바닷가재'.

examples.en: There are many American football stadiums in the US.
I like soccer more than American football.

explain: 손으로 공을 들고 달리는 미국식 축구예요. 발로 하는 '축구'와 달라요.

phrases.en: I went to watch an American football game on the weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: '경기'를 붙여서 시합을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 경기 refers to a game or match.

phrases.en: He is an American football player.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이 운동을 하는 사람을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a person who plays this sport.

phrases.en: I play American football with friends in the park.
phrases.nuance_ko: 운동을 직접 할 때는 '하다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 하다 when you play the sport yourself.

explain_en: The American sport where players carry the ball. It differs from '축구' (soccer), which is played with the feet.

examples.en: You must not hit your friend.
The child beats the drum.

explain: 손이나 물건으로 세게 치는 것이에요. '누구를 때리다'처럼 쓰고, 사람에게는 폭력이라서 조심해야 해요.
explain_en: To strike someone or something hard with a hand or object. Used as '누구를 때리다'; hitting a person is violence, so be careful.

dis.h: everyday hit or beat, by a person

p.n: 가격하다 makes it formal and written, like a report of a blow.

examples.en: You must not throw your racket.
I bought a new racket.

explain: 테니스나 배드민턴에서 공을 치는 도구예요. '라켓을 들다', '라켓으로 치다'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: The tennis racket is too heavy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 운동의 라켓인지 앞에 운동 이름을 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put the sport's name in front to say which racket it is.

phrases.nuance_ko: 배드민턴을 칠 때 쓰는 라켓이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The racket used for playing badminton.

phrases.en: I borrowed a racket from a friend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자기 라켓이 없을 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common phrase when you don't have your own racket.

explain_en: The tool used to hit the ball in tennis or badminton. Used as '라켓을 들다' or '라켓으로 치다'.

examples.en: The clothes in this shop all look alike.
The three of them are all about the same height.

explain: 여럿이 서로 거의 같다는 뜻이에요. '비슷하다'보다 여러 개가 다 닮았을 때 써요.

phrases.en: There are many bags with similar shapes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 여러 개가 서로 닮았다고 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Placed before a noun to say that many things look alike.

phrases.en: The twins' faces are so alike that I get confused.
phrases.nuance_ko: 너무 닮아서 구별하기 어렵다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when things are so alike that they're hard to tell apart.
phrases.en_equiv: they're all alike, so it's confusing

phrases.en: From far away, they all look similar.
phrases.nuance_ko: 눈으로 보기에 닮았다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when things seem similar to the eye.

explain_en: Means several things are nearly the same. Compared with '비슷하다', it fits when many items all look alike.

examples.en: I put the cat in the cage.
You need a cage on the plane.

explain: 동물을 넣어 두는 상자나 우리예요. 고양이나 강아지를 이동시킬 때 많이 써요.
explain_en: A box or enclosure for keeping animals. Often used when carrying a cat or dog.

examples.en: There is a pop-up store in Seongsu-dong.
I'm going to a pop-up store this weekend.

explain: 짧은 기간만 여는 가게예요. '팝업스토어를 열다', '팝업스토어에 가다'로 써요.
explain_en: A shop that opens for only a short time. Used as '팝업스토어를 열다' or '팝업스토어에 가다'.

examples.en: The plan changed, but anyway, let's meet tomorrow.

examples.ko: 길이 막혀요. 아무튼 거의 다 왔어요.
examples.en: The road is jammed. Anyway, I'm almost there.

explain: 앞의 이야기와 상관없이 말하고 싶은 것을 이어 말할 때 써요. 이야기를 돌릴 때도 써요.
explain_en: Used to move on to the point regardless of what came before, or to change the subject.

examples.en: The witch in the fairy tale rides a broom.
The kids wore witch costumes.

explain: 동화에 나오는 마법을 쓰는 여자예요. 사람에게 쓰면 나쁜 말이 될 수 있어요.

phrases.en: I wore a witch hat on Halloween.
phrases.nuance_ko: 마녀 옷차림을 말할 때 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing when talking about a witch costume.

phrases.en: I read a story with a witch in it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동화나 영화의 내용을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe the content of a fairy tale or film.

phrases.en: That fairy tale also has a good witch.
phrases.nuance_ko: 마녀가 나쁘지 않을 때 '착한'을 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add 착한 when the witch is not evil.

explain_en: A woman with magic in fairy tales. Calling a real person this can be insulting.

examples.en: There's a saying, '운칠기삼'.
I think exams are also about 70% luck.

explain: 일의 결과는 운이 70%, 실력이 30%라는 뜻이에요. 운이 중요하다고 말할 때 써요.

phrases.en: Grandpa says life is 70% luck and 30% skill.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다른 사람이 한 말을 전할 때 쓰는 말투예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A form used to report what someone else said.

phrases.en: This game really is mostly luck.
phrases.nuance_ko: 결과를 보고 운이 컸다고 느낄 때 쓰는 말투예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you see a result and feel luck played the bigger part.

phrases.en: For exams, skill matters, but luck matters too.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사자성어를 쓰지 않고 쉬운 말로 같은 뜻을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A plain-language way to say the same idea without the idiom.

explain_en: Means success is 70% luck and 30% skill. Used when saying luck matters a lot.

examples.en: I pray for my family every morning.
I prayed that I would do well on the exam.

explain: 신에게 빌거나 좋은 일을 간절히 바라는 것이에요. '~을/를 위해 기도하다', '~기를 기도하다'로 써요.
explain_en: To pray to a god or earnestly hope for something good. Used as '~을/를 위해 기도하다' or '~기를 기도하다'.

examples.ko: 일부 사람들의 선동 때문에 시위가 커졌어요.
examples.en: The protest grew because of some people's incitement.
You must not incite people with fake news.

explain: 사람들이 어떤 행동을 하도록 부추기는 것이에요. 보통 '선동하다'로 쓰고 부정적인 뜻이에요.
explain_en: Stirring people up to act. Usually used as the verb '선동하다', with a negative meaning.

examples.en: Did you check today's weather forecast?
According to the forecast, it will rain tomorrow.

explain: 앞으로의 날씨를 미리 알려 주는 것이에요. '일기예보를 보다', '일기예보에 따르면'으로 써요.
explain_en: A report that tells you upcoming weather. Used as '일기예보를 보다' or '일기예보에 따르면'.

en: to be flat; to be even

examples.en: Boston is not flat.
This road is flat, so it's easy to walk on.

explain: 바닥이나 땅이 울퉁불퉁하지 않고 고르다는 뜻이에요. 산이나 언덕이 없는 땅에도 써요.

phrases.en: We set up the tent on a flat spot.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 꾸미는 모양이고, 울퉁불퉁하지 않은 자리를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The adjective form before a noun, describing an even, non-bumpy place.

phrases.en: I spread the blanket out flat.
phrases.nuance_ko: '평평하게'는 어떤 모양으로 하는지 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: 평평하게 is the adverb form, telling how something is done.

phrases.nuance_ko: 눈으로 보기에 고르다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when something looks even to the eye.

explain_en: Means a surface or ground is smooth with no bumps. Also used for land without hills or mountains.

examples.ko: 배를 타면 고래를 볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can see whales if you take a boat.
Whales are really big.

explain: 바다에 사는 아주 큰 동물이에요. 물고기처럼 보여도 새끼를 낳아서 키워요.

phrases.en: A whale swims in the sea.
phrases.nuance_ko: 고래가 움직이는 모습을 말할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for describing how a whale moves.

phrases.en: I'm going to see whales this weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 고래를 보려는 계획을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when talking about a plan to go see whales.

phrases.en: The child drew a picture of a whale.
phrases.nuance_ko: '고래' 뒤에 다른 명사를 붙여 새 말을 만들 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: You can attach another noun after 고래 to make a new phrase.

explain_en: A very large animal that lives in the sea. It looks like a fish, but it gives birth to live young.

examples.en: I put on a life jacket before getting on the boat.
Children must wear life jackets.

explain: 물에 빠져도 뜨게 도와주는 조끼예요. '입다'와 같이 써요.

phrases.en: I borrowed a life jacket at the boat dock.
phrases.nuance_ko: 배를 타기 전에 빌릴 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common phrase for borrowing one before getting on a boat.

phrases.en: After getting off the boat, I took off the life jacket.
phrases.nuance_ko: '입다'의 반대로, 벗을 때 '벗다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of 입다; use 벗다 for taking it off.
phrases.en_equiv: to take off a life jacket

phrases.en: A children's life jacket is small in size.
phrases.nuance_ko: 누가 입는 조끼인지 앞에 붙여서 말할 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: You can put who wears it in front of the word.

explain_en: A vest that keeps you afloat in water. Use it with the verb 입다.

examples.en: I like seafood.
Today I'm having a seafood pancake.

explain: 바다에서 나는 먹을거리예요. 해물탕, 해물파전처럼 음식 이름에 많이 들어가요.
explain_en: Food that comes from the sea. It appears in dish names like 해물탕 and 해물파전.

examples.en: I like blueberries.
I put blueberries in my yogurt.

explain: 파란빛이 도는 보라색의 작은 과일이에요. 요거트나 잼에 자주 넣어요.

phrases.en: I bought blueberry jam at the supermarket.
phrases.nuance_ko: 블루베리로 만든 잼을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for jam made from blueberries.

phrases.en: I drink blueberry juice in the morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음식 이름 앞에 블루베리를 붙여 쓰는 흔한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing where blueberry is put in front of a food name.

phrases.nuance_ko: '맛'을 붙이면 과일이 아니라 맛을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 맛 refers to the flavor, not the fruit itself.

explain_en: A small bluish-purple fruit. It is often put in yogurt or jam.

examples.en: Please give me half-and-half chicken (half seasoned, half fried).
The chance of winning is fifty-fifty.

explain: 절반씩 나눈 것을 말해요. 치킨 반반처럼 주문할 때, 또 가능성이 50%일 때도 써요.
explain_en: Split into two equal halves. Used when ordering, like 치킨 반반, and also for a fifty-fifty chance.

examples.en: That family has a vacation house by the sea.
I went to the villa and rested on the weekend.

explain: 휴가나 주말에 쉬러 가는 두 번째 집이에요. 보통 바다나 산 근처에 있어요.

phrases.en: In summer, we stay at the villa.
phrases.nuance_ko: 별장에서 며칠 동안 머물 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for staying at the villa for a few days.

phrases.en: We spent a night at a villa in the mountains.
phrases.nuance_ko: 별장이 어디에 있는지 앞에 붙여서 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put the location in front to say where the villa is.

phrases.en: I rented a villa with my friends.
phrases.nuance_ko: 잠깐 쓰려고 빌릴 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common phrase for renting one for a short stay.

explain_en: A second home you visit for holidays or weekends, usually near the sea or mountains.

examples.en: There are duck boats on the Han River.
I rode a duck boat with a friend.

explain: 오리 모양으로 만든 작은 배예요. 발로 페달을 밟아서 움직이고, 공원 호수에서 많이 타요.

phrases.en: Tomorrow we're going to the lake to ride a duck boat.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-(으)러 가다'로 타려는 목적을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The -(으)러 가다 pattern states the purpose of going.
phrases.en_equiv: to go ride a duck boat

phrases.en: Riding a duck boat on the lake is fun.
phrases.nuance_ko: '타기'를 붙이면 활동 이름처럼 말할 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 타기 turns it into the name of an activity.

phrases.en: We rented a duck boat for an hour.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돈을 내고 잠깐 쓸 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common phrase for paying to use one for a short time.

explain_en: A small duck-shaped boat moved by pedaling. People ride them on park lakes.

examples.en: A long time ago, that country had a dictatorship.
People opposed the dictatorship.

explain: 한 사람이나 한 집단이 혼자 나라를 다스리는 것이에요. '독재자', '독재 정치'로도 많이 써요.
explain_en: Rule of a country by one person or one group. Often seen in 독재자 and 독재 정치.

examples.en: Please think about it carefully.
I answered after thinking it over.

explain: 깊이 오래 생각하는 모양이에요. 주로 '생각하다'와 함께 써요.

phrases.example: 한 번 더 곰곰이 생각해 봐.
phrases.en: Think about it carefully once more.
phrases.nuance_ko: 친구나 아랫사람에게 쓰는 반말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A casual, informal form used with friends or younger people.

phrases.en: Thinking it over carefully, it was my fault.
phrases.nuance_ko: 깊이 생각한 뒤에 알게 된 것을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to introduce what you realized after thinking deeply.

phrases.nuance_ko: 생각한 다음에 다른 행동을 이어서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to link careful thinking to the next action.

explain_en: Describes thinking about something deeply and for a long time. Mostly used with 생각하다.

dis.h: think carefully, at length

p.n: 곰곰이 suggests taking time to think something over; 깊이 just means deeply.

examples.en: Dark clouds have gathered in the sky.

examples.ko: 먹구름이 몰려와서 곧 비가 올 거예요.
examples.en: Dark clouds are rolling in, so it will rain soon.

explain: 비가 올 것 같을 때 하늘에 끼는 어두운 구름이에요. '먹구름이 끼다'로 자주 써요.
explain_en: Dark clouds in the sky when rain is coming. Often used as 먹구름이 끼다.

examples.en: That child is a math genius.
Even a genius has to make an effort.

explain: 아주 뛰어난 재능을 타고난 사람이에요. '천재다', '천재 같다'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: That friend is a music genius.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 분야의 천재인지 앞에 붙여서 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put the field in front to say what the genius is in.

phrases.example: 그림을 이렇게 잘 그리다니, 천재 같아요.
phrases.en: To draw this well, you seem like a genius.
phrases.nuance_ko: 잘하는 모습을 보고 천재처럼 대단하다고 칭찬할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to praise someone as being so impressive that they seem like a genius.

phrases.en: I'm not a genius, so I study hard.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자기가 보통 사람이라고 말할 때 쓰는 부정 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A negative form used to say you're an ordinary person.

explain_en: A person born with outstanding talent. Used like 천재다 or 천재 같다.

examples.en: The police are investigating the case.
I looked up information for my homework.

explain: 어떤 일을 자세히 살펴서 알아내는 것이에요. 사건, 원인, 자료 등과 같이 써요.

phrases.en: I'll look up the weather on the internet.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-아/어 보다'를 붙이면 한번 알아본다는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding -아/어 보다 gives the feeling of trying to find out.

phrases.en: They are investigating the cause of the fire.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사고나 문제의 이유를 알아낼 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for finding out the reason for an accident or problem.

phrases.en: The investigation results come out tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: '조사하다'의 명사 쓰임으로, 알아낸 내용을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The noun use, referring to what was found out.

explain_en: To look into something closely to find out facts. Used with things like cases, causes, and data.

dis.h: look into or survey; general use

p.n: 수사하다 makes it a formal criminal investigation.

examples.en: There is a walking path in the park.
I walk along the trail every evening.

explain: 산책하기 좋게 만든 길이에요. 공원이나 강가에 많아요.

phrases.en: I walked along the path while looking at the river.
phrases.nuance_ko: 길을 끝까지 따라가며 걸을 때 '따라'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 따라 when you walk along the length of a path.

phrases.en: Let's meet at the entrance of the walking path.
phrases.nuance_ko: 산책로가 시작되는 곳을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the place where the path begins.

phrases.en: There are many flowers on the riverside walking path.
phrases.nuance_ko: 산책로가 어디에 있는지 앞에 붙여서 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put the location in front to say where the path is.

explain_en: A path made for taking walks. You find them in parks and along rivers.

examples.en: Please put a clip on the documents.
I sent that video clip to a friend.

explain: 종이를 끼우는 작은 물건이에요. 짧은 영상 조각도 '클립'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: I put a clip on the papers.
phrases.nuance_ko: 종이 여러 장을 모아서 고정할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common phrase for holding several sheets of paper together.

phrases.en: Please take the clip off the documents.
phrases.nuance_ko: 끼워 둔 클립을 뺄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when removing a clip that was attached.

phrases.en: Please send me just one short clip.
phrases.nuance_ko: 영상 조각을 말할 때 길이를 앞에 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: For video clips, put the length in front.

explain_en: A small item for holding papers together. A short piece of video is also called a 클립.

examples.ko: 그는 항상 사람을 의심하는 것 같아요.
examples.en: He seems to always suspect people.
I didn't doubt that story.

explain: 맞지 않는다고 생각하거나 믿지 못하는 것이에요. '사람을 의심하다', '의심이 들다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: To not trust something or someone, or to think something may be wrong. Used like 사람을 의심하다 or 의심이 들다.

examples.en: The child hid behind the door.
The cat is hiding under the bed.

explain: 남이 못 보게 어디에 들어가 있는 것이에요. 자기가 숨을 때 써요. 다른 것을 숨길 때는 '숨기다'예요.
explain_en: To go somewhere so others cannot see you. For hiding something else, use 숨기다.

examples.en: I bought a beginner's guide to cooking.
I started learning the guitar last year.

explain: 어떤 분야를 처음 배우기 시작하는 것을 말해요. '입문하다', '입문서', '입문자'처럼 많이 써요.
explain_en: It means starting to learn a field for the first time. It often appears as 입문하다, 입문서 and 입문자.

examples.en: I went to learn archery on the weekend.
Korean archers are really good.

explain: 서양식 활로 과녁을 맞히는 운동이에요. 한국은 양궁을 아주 잘하는 나라로 유명해요.
explain_en: It is the sport of shooting at a target with a Western-style bow. Korea is famous for being very good at archery.

examples.en: I'm going to a national park this weekend.
Korea has twenty-three national parks.

explain: 나라가 자연을 지키려고 정한 큰 공원이에요. 설악산, 지리산 같은 산이 국립공원이에요.

phrases.en: I took a walk in the national park on the weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: '국립공원'에 장소를 나타내는 조사 '에서'가 붙어서 그곳에서 한 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The particle '에서' marks the place where an action happens, so use it to say what you did in the national park.

phrases.en: There are many pretty trails inside the national park.
phrases.nuance_ko: '안'을 붙이면 공원의 안쪽이라는 뜻이 분명해져요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '안' makes it clear you mean the inside of the park.

phrases.en: We keep the national park clean.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자연을 보호한다는 뜻으로 '국립공원'과 자주 함께 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing that means to protect nature in the park.

explain_en: It is a large park the state designates to protect nature. Mountains like Seoraksan and Jirisan are national parks.

en: to utilize; to make use of

examples.ko: 배운 단어를 말할 때 활용해 보세요.
examples.en: Try using the words you learned when you speak.

examples.ko: 시간을 잘 활용하면 일이 빨리 끝나요.
examples.en: If you use your time well, the work finishes quickly.

explain: 가지고 있는 것을 알맞게 쓴다는 뜻이에요. '이용하다'보다 능력, 자료, 시간처럼 잘 살려 쓰는 느낌이 강해요.
explain_en: It means to put something you have to good use. Compared with 이용하다, it stresses using skills, materials or time effectively.

examples.en: The puppy is wagging its tail.
The cat's tail is long.

explain: 동물의 몸 끝에 길게 달린 부분이에요. 강아지가 기분이 좋으면 꼬리를 흔들어요.
explain_en: It is the long part at the end of an animal's body. A happy dog wags its tail.

examples.ko: 이 요리 레시피 좀 알려 주세요.
examples.en: Please tell me the recipe for this dish.
This is my own recipe.

explain: 음식을 만드는 방법이에요. '나만의 레시피'는 나만 아는, 내가 만든 방법이라는 뜻이에요.
explain_en: It is the method for making a dish. '나만의 레시피' means a recipe that is your very own.

en: to tend to be; to be rather

examples.en: My pillow is on the small side.
I tend to get up early in the morning.

explain: '작은 편이다'처럼 앞말 쪽에 가깝다고 말할 때 써요. 아주 그렇다는 뜻은 아니에요.
explain_en: Used as in '작은 편이다' to say something leans toward that quality. It does not mean extremely so.

examples.en: Is there a wait by any chance?
This restaurant has a long wait.

explain: 식당 앞에서 차례를 기다리는 것을 말해요. 가게에서 '웨이팅 있어요?'라고 물어보면 기다려야 하는지 알 수 있어요.
explain_en: It means waiting for your turn, usually outside a restaurant. Asking '웨이팅 있어요?' checks whether you must queue.

examples.en: Please follow me.
The puppy followed me.

explain: 앞사람 뒤에서 같이 온다는 뜻이에요. 말하는 사람 쪽으로 올 때 써요. 가는 쪽이면 '따라가다'예요.
explain_en: It means to come along behind someone toward the speaker. If you move away from the speaker, use 따라가다.

en: to to calculate; to to pay (a bill)

examples.en: Calculate the numbers slowly.
I'll pay.

explain: 수를 셈한다는 뜻이고, 가게에서는 값을 낸다는 뜻으로도 많이 써요. '계산할게요'는 '제가 낼게요'라는 말이에요.
explain_en: It means to work out numbers, and in shops it also means to pay. '계산할게요' means 'I'll pay.'

en: to clean up; to move out of way

examples.en: In winter, I clear the snow every morning.
Please clear the table.

explain: 물건을 다른 곳으로 옮기거나 깨끗이 정리한다는 뜻이에요. '눈을 치우다'는 쌓인 눈을 없앤다는 말이에요.
explain_en: It means to move things away or tidy up. '눈을 치우다' means to clear away the snow.

examples.en: I went to a club with a friend on the weekend.
I joined a book club.

explain: 음악을 들으며 춤추는 곳을 말해요. 같은 취미 모임도 클럽이라고 해요. '클럽에 가다'로 써요.
explain_en: It means a place to dance to music, and also a group with a shared hobby. It is used as '클럽에 가다'.

examples.en: That company developed the technology on its own.
We need to find our own method.

explain: 다른 것에 기대지 않고 혼자 한다는 뜻이에요. '독자적으로'는 부사처럼, '독자적인'은 뒤에 명사를 꾸밀 때 써요.
explain_en: It means doing something on one's own without relying on others. '독자적으로' works like an adverb, and '독자적인' modifies a noun.

examples.en: I'll start studying in earnest from tomorrow.
Summer has properly arrived.

explain: 어떤 일을 제대로, 크게 시작하거나 한다는 뜻이에요. '본격적으로 시작하다'처럼 자주 써요.
explain_en: It means doing something properly and in earnest. It is often used as '본격적으로 시작하다'.

examples.en: I'm meeting a client today.
The client likes the design.

explain: 일을 맡기는 손님이나 회사를 말해요. 법률 분야에서는 '의뢰인'이라고 해요. 일상에서는 '고객'도 많이 써요.
explain_en: It means a customer or company that hires you for work. In law it is called 의뢰인, and 고객 is common in daily speech.

examples.en: This picture looks a little flat.

examples.ko: 평면적인 설명으로는 문제를 풀 수 없어요.
examples.en: A simplistic explanation can't solve the problem.

explain: 평평한 면처럼 깊이가 없다는 뜻이에요. 생각이나 설명이 단순할 때도 써요. '평면적인 설명'처럼 '-인'을 붙여 꾸며요.
explain_en: It means flat, without depth. It also describes thinking or explanations that are simplistic. Add '-인' to modify a noun, as in '평면적인 설명'.

examples.en: Don't treat a child like an adult.
I treat customers kindly.

explain: '을/를 대하다'는 어떤 사람을 어떤 태도로 만난다는 뜻이에요. '~에 대해'는 '~에 관해'라는 뜻으로 따로 자주 써요.

phrases.en: to treat in a relaxed way
phrases.en_equiv: to treat in a relaxed way

explain_en: '을/를 대하다' means to deal with or treat someone in a certain way. '~에 대해' (about) is a separate, very common form.

examples.en: Everyone pursues happiness.
This company seeks quality over profit.

explain: 목표나 가치를 끝까지 따라가며 얻으려고 한다는 뜻이에요. '행복을 추구하다', '이익을 추구하다'처럼 추상적인 것에 써요.
explain_en: To keep going after a goal or value. It is used with abstract things, like 행복을 추구하다 (pursue happiness) or 이익을 추구하다 (seek profit).

examples.en: In summer, I eat chicken baekseok with my family.
This restaurant's duck baekseok is delicious.

explain: 닭이나 오리를 물에 푹 삶아 만든 음식이에요. 보통 '닭백숙'이라고 하고, 오리나 능이버섯을 넣기도 해요.
explain_en: A dish of chicken or duck slowly boiled in water. It is usually called 닭백숙, and sometimes duck or neungi mushrooms are added.

examples.en: Someone stole my wallet.
He wiped away his tears and smiled.

explain: 남의 물건을 몰래 가져간다는 뜻이에요. 땀이나 눈물을 손으로 닦을 때도 써요. '훔쳐 가다'는 몰래 가져간다는 말이에요.
explain_en: To secretly take someone else's things. It also means to wipe away sweat or tears with a hand. 훔쳐 가다 means to steal and take away.

examples.en: Water flows in the valley between the mountains.
The valley is full of fog.

explain: 산과 산 사이에 깊고 좁게 들어간 곳이에요. '계곡'은 그곳에 흐르는 물을 포함해서 말할 때 많이 써요.
explain_en: A deep, narrow low area between mountains. 계곡 is often used when you also mean the stream running through it.

examples.en: I speak up actively in class.
That student has a proactive personality.

explain: 스스로 나서서 열심히 하는 모습이에요. '적극적으로 + 동사'나 '적극적인 + 명사'로 써요.
explain_en: Taking the initiative and putting in effort. It is used as '적극적으로 + verb' or '적극적인 + noun'.

examples.en: Contracts have a lot of legal terms.
I don't know what this term means.

explain: 어떤 분야에서 쓰는 말이에요. '법률 용어', '전문 용어'처럼 분야 이름과 함께 써요.
explain_en: A word used in a particular field. It goes with a field name, like 법률 용어 (legal term) or 전문 용어 (technical term).

en: to be unjust; to be unfair

examples.en: If a deal feels unfair, report it.
I was treated unfairly at work.

explain: 옳지 않거나 이치에 맞지 않다는 뜻이에요. '부당한 대우', '부당한 거래'처럼 뒤에 명사가 와요.
explain_en: Not right or not reasonable. It usually comes before a noun, as in 부당한 대우 (unfair treatment).

examples.en: I pick up side dishes with chopsticks.

examples.ko: 뭐가 문제인지 콕 집어서 말해 주세요.
examples.en: Please tell me exactly what the problem is.

explain: 손가락이나 젓가락으로 잡아서 든다는 뜻이에요. '콕 집어서'는 여러 개 중에서 딱 하나를 짚어서 말한다는 표현이에요.
explain_en: To pick something up with fingers or chopsticks. '콕 집어서' means singling out exactly one thing from several.

dis.h: pick up with fingers, chopsticks, or tongs

p.n: 줍다 cannot be used for grasping with chopsticks or tools.

examples.en: I take out my contact lenses before bed.
I bought a new camera lens.

explain: 눈에 끼는 콘택트렌즈나 카메라의 렌즈를 말해요. 눈에 쓸 때는 '렌즈를 끼다', 뺄 때는 '렌즈를 빼다'라고 해요.
explain_en: Means a contact lens or a camera lens. For contacts, you say 렌즈를 끼다 (put in) and 렌즈를 빼다 (take out).

en: to play (tricks); to put on (airs); to handle (an animal or worker)

examples.en: The child acts spoiled with its mother.
My younger sibling is being stubborn again.

explain: 어떤 행동이나 태도를 겉으로 드러낸다는 뜻이에요. '어리광을 부리다', '고집을 부리다', '꾀를 부리다'처럼 정해진 명사와 같이 써요.
explain_en: To show a certain behavior or attitude. It pairs with set nouns: 어리광을 부리다 (act spoiled), 고집을 부리다 (be stubborn), 꾀를 부리다 (play tricks).

en: to be fierce; to be intense

examples.en: The two teams fought fiercely.
The entrance exam competition is really intense.

explain: 경쟁이나 싸움이 아주 뜨겁고 힘들다는 뜻이에요. '치열한 경쟁', '치열한 경합'처럼 써요.
explain_en: Describes competition or conflict that is very heated and hard. Typical uses are 치열한 경쟁 and 치열한 경합.

en: to be sharp; to be pointy

examples.en: It's a house with a pointed roof.
The pencil tip is too sharp.

explain: 끝이 날카롭고 가늘다는 뜻이에요. 앞에 올 때는 '뾰족한 지붕'처럼 '뾰족한'으로 바뀌어요.
explain_en: Having a thin, sharp tip. Before a noun it becomes 뾰족한, as in 뾰족한 지붕 (pointed roof).

examples.en: I drink lukewarm water.
The coffee has cooled down and is lukewarm.

explain: 차갑지도 뜨겁지도 않고 조금 따뜻하다는 뜻이에요. 물이나 국, 커피에 자주 써요.
explain_en: Neither cold nor hot, just slightly warm. It is often used for water, soup, and coffee.

examples.en: When my stomach feels bloated, I drink sparkling water.
I ate too much, so my stomach feels bloated.

explain: 먹은 것이 소화가 안 돼서 배가 가득 찬 느낌이에요. '속이 더부룩하다'로 자주 말해요.
explain_en: The uncomfortable full feeling in your stomach when food isn't digesting. It is usually said as 속이 더부룩하다.

examples.en: I take a bite of the apple.
I cut my finger on a knife.

explain: 칼처럼 날이 있는 것으로 자르거나 상처가 난다는 뜻이에요. '베어 물다'는 음식을 이로 한입 물어서 끊는다는 말이에요.
explain_en: To cut with something sharp, or to get cut. 베어 물다 means to bite off a piece of food with your teeth.

en: the third cousin of one's in-laws

examples.en: Even the most distant relatives came to the wedding.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 저랑 사돈의 팔촌쯤 돼요.
examples.en: That person is a very distant relative of mine.

explain: 아주 먼 친척을 뜻하는 관용구예요. '사돈의 팔촌까지'는 먼 친척까지 모두라는 뜻으로, 많은 사람을 말할 때 써요.
explain_en: An idiom for a very distant relative. '사돈의 팔촌까지' means even the most distant relatives, used to say a huge number of people.

en: to get (an answer) right; to hit (a target)

examples.en: I got the quiz answer right.
I hit the target with an arrow.

explain: 답이나 목표를 정확하게 맞게 한다는 뜻이에요. '맞다'와 헷갈리기 쉬워요. 사람이 정답을 '맞히다', 답 자체가 옳으면 '맞다'라고 해요.
explain_en: To get an answer or target exactly right. Don't mix it up with 맞다: you 맞히다 an answer, while an answer itself is 맞다 (correct).

en: to be dark; to be thick

examples.en: He is wearing a dark brown coat.
Thick fog set in this morning.

explain: 색이나 안개, 화장 등이 보통보다 진한 것이에요. 명사 앞에서는 '짙은 갈색'처럼 '짙은'이 돼요.
explain_en: Describes color, fog, or makeup that is deep or heavy. Before a noun it becomes 짙은, as in 짙은 갈색 (dark brown).

examples.en: Go ahead. I'll follow you.
Responsibility comes with this job.

explain: 앞사람 바로 뒤에서 따라가거나 어떤 일 다음에 이어서 생긴다는 뜻이에요. '뒤따라'는 '뒤따라 가다/오다'처럼 쓰는 연결형이에요.
explain_en: To follow right behind someone, or to come as a result after something. 뒤따라 is the linking form, as in 뒤따라 가다/오다.

examples.en: The kids got into a fight over a toy.
The race for first place is very intense.

explain: 서로 이기려고 말이나 힘으로 다투는 것이에요. '싸움이 나다', '싸움을 하다'처럼 쓰고, '1등 싸움'은 1등을 두고 겨루는 경쟁이에요.
explain_en: Fighting or quarreling to beat each other. '1등 싸움' means a close race for first place.

en: to be hit; to be run over

examples.en: I almost got hit by a car on the road.
The puppy was hit by a car.

explain: 차나 무거운 것에 부딪히거나 깔리는 것이에요. '차에 치이다'처럼 쓰고, 일이나 사람에 시달릴 때도 써요.
explain_en: To be hit or run over by a car or something heavy. It is also used for being worn down by work or people.

examples.en: My knee doesn't hurt anymore.
It isn't raining today.

explain: 동사나 형용사 뒤에 '-지 않다'를 붙여 부정해요. '안'과 뜻이 같은데, '안'은 동사 앞에, '-지 않다'는 뒤에 와요.
explain_en: Add '-지 않다' after a verb or adjective to make it negative. It means the same as '안', but '안' goes before the verb and '-지 않다' goes after it.

en: to be stuck in; to be inserted

examples.en: Candles are stuck in the cake.
Lots of books are lined up on the bookshelf.

explain: 무엇이 어디에 박히거나 끼워지는 것이에요. 상태를 말할 때는 '꽂혀 있다'라고 해요. 한 가지에 마음이 쏠릴 때도 '꽂히다'를 써요.
explain_en: For something to be stuck or inserted into a place. For the resulting state, say '꽂혀 있다'. It is also used when you get hooked on one thing, as in '그 노래에 꽂혔어요'.

en: to open wide; to spread apart

examples.en: Please open your mouth wide.
Don't spread your legs too far apart.

explain: 입이나 다리처럼 닫힌 것의 사이를 넓게 하는 것이에요. '벌다(돈을 벌다)'와 헷갈리지 마세요.

phrases.en: The child sleeps with its mouth open.
phrases.nuance_ko: 입이 열린 상태가 계속될 때 '-고'를 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add '-고' to describe a mouth that stays open.

phrases.en: My friend spread their arms and hugged me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 입뿐만 아니라 팔에도 쓸 수 있어요. 팔을 양옆으로 넓게 펼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It is not only for the mouth; you can also use it for arms spread out wide to the sides.

phrases.nuance_ko: 운동할 때 다리 사이를 넓게 하는 것을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: It describes widening the space between the legs, for example when exercising.

explain_en: To open or spread something wide, like a mouth or legs. Don't confuse it with '벌다' (to earn money).

dis.h: make a gap, or open wide

p.n: 열다 is general; 벌리다 stresses stretching it wide apart.

examples.en: Cherry blossoms bloom a lot in spring.
The cherry blossoms have already fallen.

explain: 봄에 피는 벚나무의 꽃이에요. 꽃이 피면 '벚꽃이 피다', 떨어지면 '벚꽃이 지다'라고 해요.
explain_en: The flowers of the cherry tree in spring. They 'bloom' (피다) and then 'fall' (지다).

en: the inside of a house; family

examples.en: It's very quiet inside the house.
I cleaned the house on the weekend.

explain: 집의 안쪽이나 한 가족 전체를 뜻해요. '온 집안'은 집 전체를 말해요.
explain_en: The inside of a house, or the whole family. '온 집안' means the entire house.

en: to rummage through; to fall behind

examples.en: I searched the whole bag, but the key isn't there.
Our team is behind by one point.

explain: 무엇을 찾으려고 여기저기 샅샅이 살피는 것이에요. 경기나 실력에서 남보다 못할 때도 써요.
explain_en: To search every corner for something. It also means to be behind others in a game or skill.

examples.en: There is private insurance too.
I work at a private company.

explain: 나라나 정부가 아닌 보통 사람이나 회사 쪽을 말해요. '민간 보험', '민간 기업'처럼 써요.
explain_en: Refers to ordinary people or companies, not the government. Used in phrases like '민간 보험' (private insurance).

examples.en: The overall atmosphere is nice.
Overall, it was very good.

explain: 전체를 보았을 때라는 뜻이에요. '전체적인 + 명사', '전체적으로 + 서술어'로 써요.

phrases.example: 전체적으로 보면 이 방이 제일 좋아요.
phrases.en: Overall, this room is the best.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 가지를 모두 생각해서 결론을 말할 때 앞에 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put it before a conclusion that takes everything into account.

phrases.en: This shop has a warm feeling overall.
phrases.nuance_ko: '전체적인' 뒤에 명사가 와서 전체의 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A noun follows '전체적인' to describe the whole picture.

phrases.en: The two photos are similar overall.
phrases.nuance_ko: 작은 부분은 달라도 전체는 같다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when small parts differ but the whole is alike.

explain_en: Means 'looking at the whole'. Used as '전체적인 + noun' or '전체적으로 + predicate'.

examples.en: I had a dream about a ghost last night.
I watched a movie with ghosts in it.

explain: 죽은 사람의 영혼이나 무서운 존재를 말해요. '귀신 들리다'는 귀신이 몸에 들어왔다는 뜻이에요.

phrases.en: to be possessed by a ghost
phrases.en_equiv: to be possessed by a ghost

explain_en: A ghost or spirit. '귀신 들리다' means to be possessed by a ghost.

en: to wrap around; to put on

examples.en: It's cold, so I wrap a scarf around my neck.
I put a towel around my neck.

explain: 스카프나 수건을 몸에 둘러서 감는 것이에요. 팬에 기름을 고르게 바를 때도 써요.

phrases.en: to coat a pan with oil
phrases.en_equiv: to coat a pan with oil

explain_en: To wrap something like a scarf or towel around yourself. Also used for coating a pan with oil.

examples.en: This restaurant has unlimited meat refills.
The universe is infinite.

explain: 끝이나 한계가 없는 것이에요. 식당의 '무한 리필'은 더 달라고 해서 계속 먹을 수 있다는 뜻이에요.
explain_en: Having no end or limit. '무한 리필' at a restaurant means unlimited refills.

examples.en: The mother is carrying the baby on her back.

examples.ko: 다리가 아파서 친구가 저를 업어 줬어요.
examples.en: My leg hurt, so my friend carried me on their back.

explain: 사람을 등에 올려 몸에 붙이는 것이에요. 업혀 가는 쪽은 '업히다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: to be carried on someone's back
phrases.en_equiv: to be carried on someone's back

explain_en: To carry someone on your back. The person being carried is described with '업히다'.

examples.en: This clothing breathes well.
A ventilated seat is cool in summer.

explain: 바람이 잘 통하는 것이에요. '통풍이 잘 되다'로 많이 써요. 병 이름 '통풍(gout)'은 한자가 달라요.
explain_en: Air flowing through a space. Often used as '통풍이 잘 되다'. The disease 통풍 (gout) is a different word with the same sound.

examples.en: This road is very steep.
The slope is gentle, so it's good for walking.

explain: 비스듬히 기울어진 정도나 그런 곳을 말해요. 한자가 다른 '경사(慶事)'는 기쁜 일이라는 뜻이에요.
explain_en: The tilt of a surface, or a sloped place. A different word, 경사 (慶事), means a happy event.

examples.en: The director came to the classroom.
I talked with the academy director.

explain: 학원, 병원, 유치원 같은 곳의 책임자예요. 부를 때는 '원장님'이나 '원장 선생님'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: The hospital director is seeing a patient.
phrases.nuance_ko: '원장'이 어느 곳의 책임자인지 앞에 장소를 붙여서 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put the place before '원장' to say whose director it is.

phrases.en: The kindergarten director likes children very much.
phrases.nuance_ko: 유치원의 책임자를 높여서 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A respectful way to refer to the head of a kindergarten.

phrases.en: I will tell the director about this.
phrases.nuance_ko: 원장에게 말할 때는 '께'와 '말씀드리다'로 높여 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: When speaking to a director, show respect with '께' and '말씀드리다'.

explain_en: The head of an academy, clinic, or kindergarten. Address them as '원장님' or '원장 선생님'.

examples.en: It's food they made themselves.
Honey, what should we eat today?

explain: 앞에 나온 사람 자신을 가리켜요. 연인이나 부부 사이에서 '자기야'라고 부르기도 해요.
explain_en: Refers back to the person already mentioned. Couples also call each other '자기야' like 'honey'.

examples.en: I listened to a piano performance.
That person plays the violin.

explain: 악기로 음악을 들려주는 것이에요. '연주하다'로 동사처럼 쓰고, 못할 때는 '연주하지 못하다'라고 해요.
explain_en: Playing music on an instrument. Use '연주하다' as a verb; 'cannot play' is '연주하지 못하다'.

examples.en: Thank you.
I read a book.

explain: 받침이 없으면 -ㅂ니다, 받침이 있으면 -습니다를 붙여요. 인사, 발표, 뉴스처럼 격식 있는 말에 써요.
explain_en: Add -ㅂ니다 after a vowel and -습니다 after a consonant. It is used in formal speech such as greetings, presentations and news.

examples.en: Please go ahead.
Please sit here.

explain: 받침이 없으면 -세요, 있으면 -으세요를 붙여요. 부드럽게 부탁하거나 시킬 때, 또 높여야 할 사람의 행동을 말할 때 써요.
