explain_en: Use -세요 after a vowel and -으세요 after a consonant. It makes polite requests and commands, and also honors the subject's action.

examples.en: Thanks for today. See you next time.
Class is over. See you next time.

explain: 헤어질 때 다음 만남을 기약하는 인사예요. '또'는 '다시'라는 뜻이에요.

phrases.nuance_ko: '다음에'를 빼고 짧게 말해요. 시간을 넣어서 말하기도 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A shorter version without '다음에'. You can add a time word.

phrases.example: 오늘은 바빠서 가요, 다음에 또 봐요.
phrases.en: I'm busy today so I'm leaving, see you next time.
phrases.nuance_ko: '만나요' 대신 '봐요'를 써서 더 편하게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Using '봐요' instead of '만나요' sounds more casual.

phrases.en: Let's meet again at school tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: '다음에' 대신 '내일'처럼 날짜를 넣으면 약속이 더 분명해져요.
phrases.nuance_en: Replacing '다음에' with a day like '내일' makes the plan clearer.

explain_en: A goodbye that looks forward to meeting again. 또 means "again."

examples.en: One matcha latte, please.
I like matcha ice cream.

explain: 녹차 가루로 만든 음료나 디저트 재료예요. 카페에서 '말차 라테'처럼 자주 써요.
explain_en: Powdered green tea used in drinks and desserts. Common in cafe menus, like 말차 라테.

en: Did you eat?; How have you been?

examples.en: Did you eat? Let's eat together.

examples.ko: 아직 밥 안 먹었어. 같이 먹자.
examples.en: I haven't eaten yet. Let's eat together.

explain: 친한 사이에서 쓰는 반말이에요. 진짜 식사 여부보다 안부를 묻는 인사로도 써요. 윗사람에게는 '식사하셨어요?'라고 해요.
explain_en: Casual speech between close people. It often works as a greeting asking how you are, not only whether you ate. To elders, say 식사하셨어요?

en: Let's grab a meal sometime; see you around

examples.en: Long time no see. Let's grab a meal sometime.
Let's grab a meal sometime soon.

explain: 헤어질 때 인사처럼 많이 써요. 꼭 날짜를 정하자는 말은 아니에요. 윗사람에게는 '식사 한번 해요'라고 해요.

phrases.en: Let's have a meal together sometime.
phrases.nuance_ko: 윗사람이나 어른에게도 쓸 수 있는 공손한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite version you can also use with elders or superiors.

phrases.example: 시간 있을 때 밥 한 번 먹어요.
phrases.en: Let's eat together when you have time.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-자'보다 부드러운 해요체라서 친하지 않은 사람에게도 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: This 해요체 form is softer than '-자', so you can use it with people you are not close to.

phrases.example: 제가 다음에 밥 한 번 살게요.
phrases.en: I'll treat you to a meal next time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 내가 밥값을 내겠다는 뜻이 들어 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means you will pay for the meal.
phrases.en_equiv: I'll treat you to a meal.

explain_en: Often said when parting, like 'let's catch up'. It usually isn't a firm plan. To elders, say 식사 한번 해요.

en: can't eat because of worry; to have no appetite

examples.en: I have so many worries that I can't eat.
Before an exam, I can't get food down.

explain: 걱정이나 스트레스 때문에 음식을 먹기 힘들 때 써요. 음식이 목에 걸린다는 뜻이 아니에요.

phrases.example: 나쁜 소식을 듣고 밥이 안 넘어갔어요.
phrases.en: I couldn't eat after hearing the bad news.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과거에 걱정 때문에 먹지 못했을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it for a past time when worry kept you from eating.

phrases.en: I couldn't eat, so I only drank water.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-서'를 붙여서 먹지 못한 일 뒤에 이어지는 일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add '-서' to connect it with what happened because you couldn't eat.

phrases.en: I have a lot of worries these days, so I have no appetite.
phrases.nuance_ko: 먹고 싶은 마음이 없다는 뜻이에요. 꼭 걱정 때문이 아니어도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means you don't feel like eating, and it doesn't have to be because of worry.

explain_en: Used when worry or stress makes it hard to eat. It doesn't mean food is physically stuck in your throat.

examples.en: I show my friend a photo.
Please show me your passport.

explain: 무엇을 다른 사람이 볼 수 있게 해요. 받는 사람에게는 '에게'를 써요.

phrases.en: I'll show you my family photos.
phrases.nuance_ko: 내가 보여 주겠다고 약속하거나 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when you promise or offer to show something.

phrases.en: I showed my homework to the teacher.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이미 보여 준 일을 말하는 과거형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The past form, for something you already showed.

phrases.example: 친구에게 우리 집을 보여 주고 싶어요.
phrases.en: I want to show my friend my house.
phrases.nuance_ko: 보여 주고 싶은 마음을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: It expresses that you want to show something.

explain_en: You let someone see something. Use 에게 for the person who is shown.

examples.en: After I eat, I drink coffee.
After I do my homework, I sleep.

explain: 앞의 일이 끝난 다음에 뒤의 일을 한다는 뜻이에요. 순서가 중요할 때 써요.

phrases.en: I go home after class ends.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-고 나서'와 뜻이 비슷하고, 말과 글에 두루 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar in meaning to -고 나서; used in both speech and writing.

phrases.en: I take medicine after I eat.
phrases.nuance_ko: 순서를 말할 때 쓰고, 일상 대화에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it for order of events; it is common in everyday talk.

phrases.en: I did my homework. After that, I slept.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문장 사이에서 '앞의 일을 한 다음에'라는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it between sentences to mean 'after doing that'.

explain_en: The first action is finished, and then the second one happens. Use it when the order matters.

examples.en: What does this word mean?
What does '도착' mean?

explain: 모르는 말의 뜻을 물을 때 써요. 앞에 궁금한 말을 붙여요.
explain_en: Use it to ask the meaning of a word you don't know. Put the word before it.

examples.en: I brush my teeth before I sleep.
I wash my hands before I eat.

explain: 뒤의 일을 먼저 한다는 뜻이에요. 앞 동사는 과거형으로 쓰지 않아요.

phrases.en: I wash my hands before a meal.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동사 대신 명사 뒤에 붙여서 써요. 이때는 '-기'가 필요 없어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Attach it to a noun instead of a verb; '-기' is not needed.

phrases.nuance_ko: 앞에서 말한 일보다 먼저라는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means earlier than the thing mentioned before.

phrases.en: I always turn off the light before I go out.
phrases.nuance_ko: '꼭'을 넣어서 반드시 해야 하는 일을 강조해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '꼭' stresses something you must do.

explain_en: The action after it happens first. The verb before it is never in the past tense.

examples.en: I imitate the teacher's pronunciation.
I want to copy my friend's dance.

explain: 다른 사람의 말이나 행동을 보고 그대로 해요. 맞춤법으로는 '따라 하다'로 띄어 써요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 선생님이 학생에게 해 보라고 할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Teachers often use it to ask students to try.

phrases.en: I watched a video and followed along to cook.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이미 따라서 한 일을 말하는 과거형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The past form, for something you already copied.

phrases.nuance_ko: 행동이 아니라 들은 말을 그대로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it for repeating words you heard, not actions.

explain_en: You do what someone else says or does, just as they do it. The standard spelling has a space: 따라 하다.

examples.en: If it rains, I stay home.
If you have time, let's eat together.

explain: 조건이나 가정을 말해요. 받침이 없으면 -면, 있으면 -으면을 써요.

phrases.en: You must not take photos here.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조건 뒤에 '안 돼요'를 붙여서 하면 안 되는 일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add '안 돼요' after the condition to say what is not allowed.

phrases.nuance_ko: 그렇게 하기만 하면 충분하다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means doing just that is enough.
phrases.en_equiv: all you need to do is ~

phrases.en: It's good if you sleep early.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그렇게 하면 좋다고 권하거나 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to suggest or say that something is good to do.

explain_en: Used for conditions or assumptions: 'if' or 'when'. Use -면 after a vowel and -으면 after a consonant.

en: to plan to; to intend to

examples.en: I plan to meet a friend this weekend.
I'm going to have kimchi stew for dinner.

explain: 무엇을 하려는 마음이나 계획을 말해요. 받침이 없으면 -려고, 있으면 -으려고 해요.

phrases.en: I came to Korea in order to study.
phrases.en_equiv: I came to Korea in order to study.

explain_en: Expresses an intention or plan to do something. Use -려고 하다 after a vowel and -으려고 하다 after a consonant.

examples.en: I'm going to New York tomorrow.
I will read a book this weekend.

explain: 앞으로 할 일이나 계획, 짐작을 말해요. 받침이 없으면 -ㄹ 거예요, 있으면 -을 거예요를 써요.
explain_en: Talks about future plans or guesses. Use -ㄹ 거예요 after a vowel and -을 거예요 after a consonant.

en: to decide to; to agree to

examples.en: I'm meeting a friend tomorrow (we agreed to).
I decided to exercise every day from now on.

explain: 무엇을 하기로 정했거나 약속했다고 말해요. 보통 '-기로 했어요'처럼 과거형으로 많이 써요.

phrases.en: We promised to meet early tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다른 사람과 함께 정한 약속이라는 뜻이 더 분명해요.
phrases.nuance_en: It makes clear that the plan was agreed with another person.

phrases.en: We decided to watch a movie, but it's raining.
phrases.nuance_ko: 계획을 말한 뒤에 다른 상황을 이어서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to state a plan and then continue with a different situation.

phrases.en: I decided not to drink coffee anymore.
phrases.nuance_ko: 하지 않겠다고 정했을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when you decide not to do something.

explain_en: Says you decided or agreed to do something. It is most often used in the past form, -기로 했어요.

en: to buy and eat; to eat out

examples.en: I usually eat lunch out.

examples.ko: 집에 음식이 없어서 김밥을 사 먹었어요.
examples.en: There was no food at home, so I bought kimbap and ate it.

explain: 집에서 만들지 않고 밖에서 음식을 사서 먹는다는 뜻이에요. 배달 음식이나 식당 음식에도 써요. 맞춤법으로는 '사 먹다'로 띄어 써요.

phrases.en: Shall we buy dinner instead of cooking?
phrases.nuance_ko: 같이 밖에서 먹자고 제안할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to suggest eating out together.

phrases.nuance_ko: '사 먹다'와 비슷하지만 사는 일보다 먹는 장소에 중심이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to '사 먹다', but the focus is on where you eat rather than buying.

phrases.en: Can I buy a snack and eat it at school?
phrases.nuance_ko: 사서 먹어도 되는지 허락을 물을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to ask permission to buy and eat something.
phrases.en_equiv: Is it okay to buy and eat?

explain_en: Means to buy food instead of making it at home. It is used for eating at restaurants or buying ready-made food. The standard spelling has a space: 사 먹다.

examples.ko: 제 친구는 비건이라서 고기를 안 먹어요.
examples.en: My friend is vegan, so they don't eat meat.
This restaurant has a vegan menu.

explain: 고기, 생선, 달걀, 우유 같은 동물성 음식을 먹지 않는 사람이나 그런 음식을 말해요. '채식주의자'는 더 넓게 쓰는 말이에요.
explain_en: A person who eats no animal products such as meat, fish, eggs or milk, or food like that. 채식주의자 (vegetarian) is a broader word.

examples.en: I'm busy today, so I can't go.

examples.ko: 저는 매운 음식을 먹을 수 없어요.
examples.en: I can't eat spicy food.

explain: 능력이나 상황 때문에 할 수 없다고 말해요. 반대 표현은 -(으)ㄹ 수 있다예요.
explain_en: Says you cannot do something because of ability or circumstances. The opposite is -(으)ㄹ 수 있다.

examples.en: It's the weekend, so there are many people.
I'm a student, so I get a discount.

explain: 명사 뒤에 붙어서 이유를 말해요. 받침이 없으면 -라서, 있으면 -이라서를 써요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 뒤에서 이유를 말하는 다른 말이에요. 뒤에 명령이나 제안도 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Another way to give a reason after a noun; a command or suggestion can follow.

phrases.en: It's because today is a holiday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이유를 설명하는 대답으로 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used as an answer that explains the reason.

phrases.en: I'm not a student, so there's no discount.
phrases.nuance_ko: '아니다'가 들어간 부정의 이유예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A negative reason using '아니다'.

explain_en: Attached to a noun to give a reason: 'because it is ...'. Use -라서 after a vowel and -이라서 after a consonant.

examples.en: It's raining, so I'm staying home.
I like Korean food, so I eat it often.

explain: 앞의 일이 뒤의 일의 이유가 돼요. 이유로 쓸 때는 뒤에 '-세요', '-ㅂ시다'를 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: The first clause is the reason for the second. When it means 'because', the second clause can't be a command or a suggestion.

en: I think I will; it seems it will

examples.en: I think it will rain tomorrow.

examples.ko: 오늘 저녁에는 드라마를 볼 것 같아요.
examples.en: I think I'll watch a drama tonight.

explain: 앞으로 일어날 일을 짐작해서 말해요. 확실하지 않을 때 써요.

phrases.example: 오늘은 비가 올 것 같지 않아요.
phrases.en: I don't think it will rain today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그렇게 되지 않을 것 같다고 짐작할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when you guess that something won't happen.
phrases.en_equiv: it doesn't seem like it will

phrases.en: It's weather that looks like rain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤에 명사가 와서 그 명사를 꾸며 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: A noun follows and is described by the guess.
phrases.en_equiv: N that seems like it will ~

phrases.en: It looks like it will snow tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 보고 느낀 것을 말하듯이 부드럽게 짐작해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A soft guess, as if sharing what you see and feel now.

explain_en: Used to guess about the future when you are not sure.

en: it seems; I think it is

examples.en: This bag seems expensive.
My friend seems to be sleeping now.

explain: 지금의 상태나 지나간 일을 보고 짐작해서 말해요. 형용사는 -(으)ㄴ 것 같다, 동사 현재는 -는 것 같다를 써요.

phrases.en: It seems my friend has already left.
phrases.en_equiv: It seems my friend has already left.

explain_en: Guesses about a present state or past event. Use -(으)ㄴ with adjectives and -는 with present-tense verbs.

examples.en: I want to go to a cafe this weekend.
I want to cook Korean food.

explain: 동사 뒤에 붙어서 내가 하고 싶은 일을 말해요. 다른 사람의 마음에는 보통 '-고 싶어 해요'를 써요.
explain_en: Attach it to a verb to say what you want to do. For another person's wish, use '-고 싶어 해요'.

examples.en: Studying Korean has gradually become fun.
The weather got cold.

explain: 형용사 뒤에 붙어서 상태가 바뀌었다는 뜻이에요. 어려운 상태가 되면 '어려워지다'예요.

phrases.en: It gets warm when spring comes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 형태로, 자주 있는 변화나 앞으로의 변화에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The present form, for regular changes or changes that will come.

phrases.en: The weather is getting colder and colder.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 변하는 중이라는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means something is changing right now.

phrases.en: When the weather gets warm, I'll go for a walk.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상태가 바뀌는 것을 조건으로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when a change of state is the condition for what follows.

explain_en: Attach it to an adjective to say a state has changed. 어렵다 becomes 어려워지다, 'to get difficult'.

en: while doing (and then something else happens); in the middle of doing

examples.en: I fell asleep while studying.
I met a friend on my way home.

explain: 하던 일을 멈추고 다른 일이 이어질 때 써요. 앞 행동이 끝나기 전에 뒤의 일이 생기는 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: If you keep practicing, you'll get good.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 일을 계속하다가 어떤 결과가 생긴다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to say a result appears as you keep doing the same thing.

phrases.en: I opened the door and then closed it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞의 행동이 끝난 뒤에 반대되는 행동이나 다른 일이 이어질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when the first action is done and then an opposite or different action follows.

phrases.en: I was reading a book and stopped halfway.
phrases.nuance_ko: 하던 일을 끝내지 않고 멈췄다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means you stopped before finishing what you were doing.

explain_en: Use it when an action is interrupted or switched to another. The first action is not finished before the next thing happens.

examples.en: It's raining, so take an umbrella.
I'm hungry, so let's eat quickly.

explain: 뒤에 명령이나 제안이 올 때 이유를 말하기 좋아요. '-아서/어서'는 뒤에 명령·제안을 쓸 수 없어요.

phrases.en: Why aren't you going? Because it's raining.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이유를 묻는 말에 짧게 대답할 때 끝에 '요'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add '요' at the end to give a short answer to a question asking for the reason.

phrases.en: We've eaten a lot, so let's rest now.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이미 끝난 일을 이유로 말할 때 과거형으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use the past form when the reason is something already done.

phrases.en: It's Sunday, so let's rest together.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 뒤에 붙여서 이유를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Attach it after a noun to give a reason.

explain_en: Good for giving a reason before a command or suggestion. '-아서/어서' cannot be followed by a command or suggestion.

en: while doing; at the same time as

examples.en: I studied while listening to music.
We talk while drinking coffee.

explain: 두 가지 행동을 같은 시간에 할 때 써요. 앞뒤 문장의 주어가 같아야 해요.

phrases.en: I listen to music while cleaning.
phrases.nuance_ko: '하다'가 있는 명사 뒤에 '-하면서'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '-하면서' after a noun that goes with '하다'.

phrases.en: Please don't talk on the phone while walking.
phrases.nuance_ko: '걷다'는 '걸으면서'로 바뀌어요.
phrases.nuance_en: '걷다' changes to '걸으면서'.

phrases.nuance_ko: 말하는 모습처럼 같이 하는 행동을 더해 줄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to add a second action, like how someone speaks.

explain_en: Use it for two actions happening at the same time. The subject of both clauses must be the same.

examples.en: I sprinkled chili on the pizza.
I added a lot of chili, so it is too spicy.

explain: 서양 요리에서 쓰는 매운 고추나 그 가루를 말해요. 한국 요리에서는 보통 '고추'나 '고춧가루'를 써요.
explain_en: Hot chili pepper or its powder, used in Western-style cooking. Korean cooking usually uses 고추 or 고춧가루 instead.

examples.en: I add a little cooking wine to the meat.
If you don't have cooking wine, you can use soju.

explain: 고기나 생선의 냄새를 없애고 맛을 좋게 하려고 요리에 넣는 술이에요. 마시는 술이 아니라 조미료예요.

phrases.en: I add one spoonful of cooking wine to the meat.
phrases.nuance_ko: 요리법에서 양을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used in recipes to give the amount.

phrases.en: You can add soju instead of cooking wine.
phrases.nuance_ko: 맛술이 없을 때 다른 것을 쓰자고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when suggesting a substitute because you have no cooking wine.

phrases.en: I sprinkle cooking wine on the fish to remove the smell.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음식 위에 조금씩 뿌릴 때 '뿌리다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '뿌리다' when sprinkling a little over food.

explain_en: A cooking wine added to remove the smell of meat or fish and improve flavor. It is a seasoning, not a drink.

examples.en: A new pizza place opened in our neighborhood.
Let's meet at the pizza place in the evening.

explain: '-집'은 음식을 파는 가게를 뜻해요. 치킨집, 빵집, 국밥집처럼 써요.
explain_en: The suffix -집 means a place that sells a certain food, as in 치킨집 (chicken place) and 빵집 (bakery).

examples.en: On cold days, I want to eat shabu-shabu.

examples.ko: 샤브샤브는 채소를 많이 먹을 수 있어요.
examples.en: With shabu-shabu you can eat a lot of vegetables.

explain: 끓는 국물에 고기와 채소를 살짝 익혀 먹는 요리예요. 소스에 찍어 먹어요.

phrases.en: I went to a shabu-shabu restaurant nearby.
phrases.nuance_ko: 샤브샤브를 파는 식당을 말할 때 '집'을 붙여 한 낱말처럼 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Attach '집' to refer to a restaurant that serves shabu-shabu, written as one word.

phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 고기를 쓰는지 앞에 붙여서 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put the kind of meat in front to say what is used.

phrases.en: I dip the meat in the shabu-shabu sauce and eat it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 샤브샤브를 먹을 때 찍어 먹는 소스를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: It refers to the sauce you dip food in when eating shabu-shabu.

explain_en: A dish where you quickly cook thin slices of meat and vegetables in boiling broth and dip them in sauce.

examples.en: I don't want to eat anything today.
I don't want to go out on the weekend.

explain: 동사 뒤에 붙어 하고 싶지 않은 마음을 말해요. '-고 싶다'의 반대이고, 주어가 3인칭이면 '-고 싶어 하지 않다'를 써요.

phrases.en: I don't want to work today.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-고 싶지 않다'보다 싫은 마음이 더 강하게 느껴져요.
phrases.nuance_en: It feels like a stronger dislike than '-고 싶지 않다'.

phrases.en: I didn't want to go out yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과거에 하고 싶지 않았던 마음을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: It expresses not wanting to do something in the past.

phrases.en: I don't want to go, but I have to.
phrases.nuance_ko: 하기 싫어도 해야 하는 상황을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it for a situation where you must do something you don't want to.

explain_en: Attach it to a verb to say you don't want to do something. It is the negative of -고 싶다. For a third person, use -고 싶어 하지 않다.

en: to tend to be ...; to be rather ...

examples.en: I tend to eat breakfast well.
This restaurant is rather cheap.

explain: 어떤 성질이나 행동이 그쪽에 가깝다고 말할 때 써요. 동사는 '-는 편이다', 형용사는 '-(으)ㄴ 편이다'를 써요.

phrases.en: I'm not on the tall side.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그쪽에 가깝지 않다고 부드럽게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to say gently that something isn't close to that side.

phrases.en: I was rather quiet when I was young.
phrases.nuance_ko: 예전의 성질을 말할 때 과거형으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use the past form to describe how someone used to be.

phrases.example: 저는 키가 작은 편인데 농구를 좋아해요.
phrases.en: I'm rather short, but I like basketball.
phrases.nuance_ko: 성질을 말한 뒤에 다른 이야기를 이어갈 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to state a trait and then continue with something else.

explain_en: Use it to say something is more on one side than the other, not absolutely. Verbs take -는 편이다 and adjectives take -(으)ㄴ 편이다.

examples.en: I eat breakfast and then go to school.
I am tall and my younger sibling is short.

explain: 동사나 형용사 뒤에 붙어 두 문장을 이어요. 동작이 차례로 일어나거나 두 내용을 나란히 말할 때 써요.

phrases.example: 저는 사과를 좋아해요. 그리고 바나나도 좋아해요.
phrases.en: I like apples. And I like bananas too.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-고'는 문장 안에서 잇고, '그리고'는 문장과 문장 사이에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: '-고' joins parts inside a sentence, while '그리고' joins two sentences.

phrases.en: It rained yesterday and it's sunny today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞 내용이 과거일 때는 앞에 '-았/었'을 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add '-았/었' when the first part is in the past.

phrases.en: This place is tasty, and it's cheap too.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-고' 뒤에 '요'를 붙여서 말 중간에 부드럽게 쉬고 내용을 더해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '요' after '-고' makes a soft pause and adds more information.

explain_en: Attach it to a verb or adjective to join two clauses. It links actions in order or lists two facts side by side.

examples.en: I'll buy the coffee.
I'll have this one.

explain: 말하는 사람이 지금 하겠다고 약속하거나 알릴 때 써요. 주어는 '나'만 가능하고, 명령이나 일반적인 질문에는 쓰지 않아요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 친한 사이에 반말로 약속할 때 쓰고, 어른께는 '-(으)ㄹ게요'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The casual form for close friends; use -(으)ㄹ게요 with elders.

phrases.nuance_ko: 먼저 떠난다고 알리는 인사말처럼 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common way to tell people you are leaving first.

phrases.nuance_ko: 다시 오겠다고 약속하며 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to promise that you will come back.

explain_en: Used when the speaker promises or announces what they will do right now. The subject can only be the speaker, and it isn't used for commands or ordinary questions.

en: to be scheduled to; to plan to

examples.en: I'm planning to move next week.
I'm scheduled to meet a friend tomorrow.

explain: 이미 정해 둔 계획이나 일정을 말할 때 써요. '-(으)ㄹ 거예요'보다 조금 더 격식 있고 계획이 확실한 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: I am scheduled to graduate next month.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-예정이에요'보다 더 격식 있는 말투로, 발표나 소개할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A more formal ending, used in announcements or introductions.

phrases.en: I was planning to meet a friend yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 계획이 있었지만 그대로 되지 않았을 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a plan that existed in the past, often one that did not happen.

phrases.example: 이번 주말에는 여행 갈 예정이 없어요.
phrases.en: I have no plan to travel this weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 계획이 없다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say you have no plan.

explain_en: Used for a plan or schedule that is already set. It sounds a bit more formal and definite than -(으)ㄹ 거예요.

examples.en: That person scammed a friend.
Watch out for people who scam others online.

explain: 거짓말로 사람을 속여서 돈이나 물건을 얻을 때 써요. '사기를 치다'에서 조사 '를'을 빼고 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: Used when someone lies to trick people out of money or things. The particle 를 is often dropped in speech.

examples.en: I have to get up early tomorrow.
I have to go home now.

explain: 꼭 해야 하는 일을 말할 때 써요. '-아야/어야 하다'와 뜻이 같고, 말할 때는 '되다'를 많이 써요.
explain_en: Used for things you must do. It means the same as -아야/어야 하다, and 되다 is common in speech.

examples.en: It is hot, but I have to go.
This outfit is expensive, but it is pretty.

explain: 앞의 말과 반대되거나 다른 내용을 이을 때 써요. 동사와 형용사 어간에 바로 붙여요.

phrases.en: It was cold yesterday, but it's warm today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지난 일을 말할 때 과거형 '-았/었'을 붙여서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add the past marker -았/었 when talking about the past.

phrases.en: Sorry, but may I sit here?
phrases.nuance_ko: 부탁하거나 물어보기 전에 공손하게 먼저 하는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite opener before asking for something.

phrases.nuance_ko: 문장 맨 앞에서 앞 문장과 반대되는 내용을 이어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used at the start of a sentence to contrast with the previous one.

explain_en: Connects two contrasting ideas. Attach it directly to the verb or adjective stem.

examples.ko: 이번 주말에 등산을 해 볼까 해요.
examples.en: I'm thinking of trying hiking this weekend.
I'm thinking of starting something new.

explain: 아직 정하지 않았지만 한번 해 볼 생각이 있을 때 써요. 말할 때는 '-아/어 볼까 해요'를 많이 써요.

phrases.en: I bought it thinking I might try eating it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 해 볼 생각 때문에 어떤 행동을 했다고 이유를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Gives the thought of trying something as the reason for an action.

phrases.en: I was thinking of trying to learn Korean.
phrases.nuance_ko: 전에 생각만 했던 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for something you had considered earlier.

phrases.example: 새 휴대폰을 사 볼까 생각 중이에요.
phrases.en: I'm thinking about buying a new phone.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 고민하고 있다는 뜻을 더 분명하게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Makes it clear you are considering it right now.

explain_en: Used when you are considering trying something but haven't decided yet. In speech, -아/어 볼까 해요 is common.

en: it seems that; it looks like

examples.en: It looks like it is raining outside.
It seems my younger sibling is sleeping in the room.

explain: 보거나 들은 것을 바탕으로 추측할 때 써요. 동사에는 '-는 모양이다', 형용사에는 '-(으)ㄴ 모양이다'를 써요.

phrases.en: it seems you're busy these days
phrases.en_equiv: it seems you're busy these days

explain_en: Used to guess based on what you see or hear. Use -는 모양이다 with verbs and -(으)ㄴ 모양이다 with adjectives.

en: to end up (doing); to come to (do)

examples.en: It turns out I'm moving next month.
It turns out I'm going abroad on a business trip.

explain: 내가 정한 것이 아니라 상황 때문에 어떤 일이 그렇게 될 때 써요. 보통 '-게 됐어요'처럼 과거형으로 말해요.

phrases.example: 다음 주부터 새 학교에 다니게 돼요.
phrases.en: I'm going to attend a new school from next week.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞으로 그렇게 될 일을 말할 때 현재형으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Present form used for something that will come about.

phrases.en: I've ended up going to Seoul this time.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-게 됐어요'보다 격식 있는 말투예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A more formal version of -게 됐어요.

phrases.en: You will soon get good at Korean.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞으로 변화가 생길 것이라고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to predict a future change.

explain_en: Used when something comes about through circumstances rather than your own decision. Usually in the past form, -게 됐어요.

examples.en: It suddenly started to rain.
I started eating salad yesterday.

explain: 어떤 일이나 상태가 처음 시작될 때 써요. 주로 과거형 '-기 시작했어요'로 말해요.

phrases.en: It's starting to rain. Take an umbrella.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 막 시작되는 일을 말할 때 현재형으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The present form is used for something that is just starting now.

phrases.en: I started learning Korean, and it's fun.
phrases.nuance_ko: 시작한 뒤의 일이나 느낌을 이어서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to continue with what followed after starting.

phrases.en: I will start working from tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞으로 시작할 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for something you will begin in the future.

explain_en: Used when an action or state begins. It is mostly used in the past form, -기 시작했어요.

en: I found that…; I saw that…

examples.en: The food at that restaurant was really good, I found.
When I went there yesterday, I saw there were many people.

explain: 내가 직접 보거나 겪은 일을 상대에게 이야기할 때 써요. 어간에 바로 붙여요.

phrases.en: That movie was really fun, I found.
phrases.nuance_ko: 친한 친구에게 반말로 내가 겪은 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The casual form for telling close friends what you experienced.

phrases.en: I found that the store was closed yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이미 끝난 일을 직접 보고 알게 되었을 때 과거형으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Past form for something you saw and learned about directly.

phrases.en: It was colder than I thought.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기대와 달랐던 경험을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used for an experience different from what you expected.

explain_en: Used to tell someone about something you saw or experienced yourself. Attach it directly to the stem.

examples.en: Please don't take photos here.
Please don't drink too much coffee.

explain: 동사 뒤에 붙여서 '하지 말라'고 정중하게 부탁하거나 말릴 때 써요. '안 ~세요'가 아니라 '-지 마세요'라고 해야 해요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 친한 사이나 아이에게 반말로 말릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The casual form for friends or children.

phrases.nuance_ko: 상대를 안심시킬 때 아주 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A very common phrase to reassure someone.

phrases.en: Don't go to bed too late.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-지 마세요'보다 조금 부드럽고 편한 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A little softer and more relaxed than -지 마세요.

explain_en: Attach it to a verb stem to politely ask someone not to do something. Use -지 마세요, not 안 ~세요, for this meaning.

examples.en: I had to pack my bags.
I have to get up early tomorrow.

explain: 꼭 해야 하는 일을 말할 때 써요. 어간의 마지막 모음이 ㅏ, ㅗ이면 -아야, 그 외에는 -어야를 붙여요.
explain_en: Use this for things you must do. Attach -아야 after stems ending in ㅏ or ㅗ, and -어야 otherwise.

examples.en: I do my grocery shopping at the supermarket on weekends.

examples.ko: 저녁 먹기 전에 장을 봐야 해요.
examples.en: I have to buy groceries before dinner.

explain: '장을 보다'는 먹을 것이나 생활에 필요한 물건을 사는 것을 말해요. 옷이나 신발을 살 때는 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: '장을 보다' means buying food or household items. It isn't used for clothes or shoes.

examples.en: I drink coffee too.
I also eat rice with chopsticks.

explain: '도'는 '또한'이라는 뜻이에요. 은/는, 이/가, 을/를 자리에 쓰고, 다른 조사 뒤에도 붙일 수 있어요.
explain_en: 도 means 'also'. It replaces 은/는, 이/가, 을/를, and can also follow other particles.

examples.en: I am a student.
This person is a teacher.

explain: '이다'의 격식체예요. 명사 뒤에 붙이고, 받침이 있어도 없어도 '입니다'를 써요. 질문은 '입니까?'예요.
explain_en: The formal form of 이다. Attach it to a noun whether or not it ends in a consonant. The question form is 입니까?

examples.en: I go to the restaurant to eat lunch.
I came to meet a friend.

explain: 동사 뒤에 붙어서 가거나 오는 목적을 말해요. 받침이 있으면 '-으러', 없으면 '-러'를 쓰고, 뒤에는 '가다, 오다' 같은 이동 동사가 와요.

phrases.en: I go to the library to study.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가는 목적을 말할 때 가장 기본으로 쓰는 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic form for saying the purpose of going.

phrases.en: I went to the market to buy clothes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이미 다녀온 일의 목적을 말할 때 과거형으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Past form for the purpose of a trip already made.

phrases.en: I come to Korea to learn Korean.
phrases.nuance_ko: 오는 목적을 말할 때 '오다'와 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with 오다 to give the purpose of coming.

explain_en: Attach it to a verb stem to say the purpose of going or coming. Use -으러 after a final consonant and -러 after a vowel; it must be followed by a movement verb like 가다 or 오다.

examples.en: I'm going to watch a movie.
I go to the park to exercise.

explain: 가는 목적을 말할 때 '동사 + -(으)러 + 가다'로 써요. '오다'로 바꾸면 오는 목적을 말해요.
explain_en: Use verb + -(으)러 + 가다 to say what you are going somewhere to do. Swap in 오다 to say what you are coming to do.

examples.en: I usually have breakfast at seven.
I had bread for breakfast.

explain: 아침에 먹는 밥을 말해요. 보통 '아침식사를 하다'라고 해요.
explain_en: The meal you eat in the morning. It usually goes with 하다: 아침식사를 하다.

examples.en: Excuse me, where is the bathroom?
Where is the bathroom in the subway station?

explain: 화장실 위치를 물을 때 써요. '화장실' 자리에 다른 장소를 넣어서 길을 물을 수 있어요.

phrases.en: I want to go to the bathroom.
phrases.en_equiv: I want to go to the bathroom.

explain_en: Use this to ask where the bathroom is. Swap in other places to ask for directions.

examples.en: I'm at school now.
I was at home yesterday evening.

explain: 장소 뒤에 '에'를 붙이고 '있다'를 써서 사람이나 물건이 어디에 있는지 말해요. 과거는 '있었어요'예요.
explain_en: Put 에 after a place and add 있다 to say where a person or thing is. The past form is 있었어요.

examples.en: I made a mistake in front of everyone and lost face.
My father worried about losing face.

explain: 다른 사람 앞에서 부끄러운 일을 해서 체면이 깎일 때 써요. 반대말은 '체면을 지키다'예요.
explain_en: Used when you do something embarrassing in front of others and lose your social standing. The opposite is '체면을 지키다' (to save face).

en: to be not so good; to be meh

examples.en: I don't feel so good today.
That movie wasn't good.

explain: 기대보다 좋지 않다고 말할 때 써요. 보통 '별로예요'라고 하고, 조금 부정적인 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: Use it to say something is not as good as you hoped. It is usually said as '별로예요' and sounds a bit negative.

en: to be a mess; to be terrible

examples.en: The room is a mess.
The rain ruined our plans.

explain: 물건이나 상황, 기분이 아주 나쁘고 정리가 안 된 상태를 말해요. '엉망이 되다'도 자주 써요.
explain_en: Describes things, situations or moods that are very bad or out of order. '엉망이 되다' (to get ruined) is also common.

examples.ko: 월요일은 대체 휴일이라서 학교에 안 가요.
examples.en: Monday is a substitute holiday, so we don't go to school.
Thanks to the substitute holiday, we get a longer break.

explain: 공휴일이 주말과 겹칠 때, 그 대신 쉬도록 정한 평일이에요. 보통 월요일이에요.

phrases.en: We don't go to school on a substitute holiday.
phrases.nuance_ko: '대체 휴일'과 같은 뜻으로, 공식적인 말로 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 대체 휴일; it is the more official term.

phrases.en: My company is closed on the substitute holiday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그날 쉰다는 말을 할 때 '에'를 붙여서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add 에 to say you rest on that day.

phrases.en: This year's substitute holiday is on Monday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 대체 휴일이 언제인지 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say which day the substitute holiday falls on.

explain_en: A weekday off given when a public holiday falls on a weekend. It is usually a Monday.

examples.en: Take an umbrella. Otherwise you'll get wet.
Go to bed early. Otherwise you'll be tired.

explain: 앞에서 말한 일을 하지 않으면 어떻게 되는지 말할 때 써요. '그렇지 않으면'의 줄임말이에요.
explain_en: Used to say what happens if you don't do what was just mentioned. It is a short form of '그렇지 않으면'.

examples.en: Large dogs need a lot of walks.
I want to have a large dog.

explain: 몸집이 큰 개를 말해요. 몸집이 작은 개는 '소형견'이라고 해요.
explain_en: A dog with a large body. A small dog is called '소형견'.

examples.en: There is a Chinatown in Boston.
I ate dumplings in Chinatown on the weekend.

explain: 중국 사람들이 많이 모여 사는 거리나 동네예요. 도시 이름과 함께 '보스턴 차이나타운'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: Have you been to Incheon's Chinatown?
phrases.nuance_ko: 도시 이름을 앞에 붙여서 어느 차이나타운인지 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put a city name in front to say which Chinatown.

phrases.en: I ate jajangmyeon at a restaurant in Chinatown.
phrases.nuance_ko: 차이나타운에 있는 가게를 말할 때 명사 앞에 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put it before a noun to talk about a place in Chinatown.

phrases.nuance_ko: 길을 물을 때 쓰는 기본 질문이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A basic question for asking directions.

explain_en: A neighborhood where many Chinese people live. Often paired with a city name, like '보스턴 차이나타운'.

examples.en: This is my book.
Today is my birthday.

explain: 명사 뒤에 붙여서 친한 사이에 '~이에요/예요' 대신 써요. 받침이 있으면 '이야', 없으면 '야'를 써요. 선생님이나 어른께는 쓰지 않아요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 친한 사이에 반말로 물어볼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to ask a question in casual speech with close friends.

phrases.nuance_ko: '-(이)야'의 부정형으로, 반말에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative of -(이)야, used in casual speech.

phrases.nuance_ko: '-(이)야'를 높여서 말할 때 써요. 어른께는 이 말을 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The polite form of -(이)야; use it with elders.

explain_en: Attach to a noun to say "it is" with close friends. Use 이야 after a final consonant and 야 after a vowel. Don't use it with teachers or elders.

en: to try doing; to have done something before

examples.en: I have tried swimming.
Please try this food.

explain: 동사 뒤에 붙어서 '한번 해 보다'(시도)나 '해 본 적이 있다'(경험)를 나타내요. 과거형 '-아/어 봤어요'는 경험을 말할 때 많이 써요.
explain_en: Attach it to a verb to say you try something or have done it before. The past form -아/어 봤어요 is the usual way to talk about experience.

examples.en: You don't have to call your mom.
You don't have to come early today.

explain: 그 일을 안 해도 괜찮다는 뜻이에요. 줄여서 '안 -아/어도 되다'라고도 해요.

phrases.en: Is it okay if I don't come tomorrow?
phrases.nuance_ko: 안 해도 되는지 물어볼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to ask whether it's okay not to do something.
phrases.en_equiv: is it okay if I don't...?

phrases.en: It's okay if you don't go today.
phrases.nuance_ko: '돼요' 대신 '괜찮아요'를 쓰면 더 부드러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Using 괜찮아요 instead of 돼요 sounds softer.

phrases.en: You don't have to do the homework.
phrases.nuance_ko: 친한 사이에 반말로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The casual form for close friends.

explain_en: Means it is fine not to do something. It can also be said as 안 -아/어도 되다.

examples.en: May I open the window?
You may sit here.

explain: 해도 괜찮다고 허락하거나 허락을 물을 때 써요. '-아도/어도 돼요?'는 '해도 돼요?'라는 질문이에요.

phrases.en: May I take a photo here?
phrases.nuance_ko: 허락을 구할 때 가장 많이 쓰는 질문이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common way to ask for permission.

phrases.nuance_ko: '돼요'보다 조금 부드럽게 허락할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Gives permission a little more softly than 돼요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 친한 사이에 반말로 허락할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The casual form for giving permission to friends.

explain_en: Used to give or ask for permission. -아도/어도 돼요? means 'May I do it?'

en: it is enough to; just need to

examples.en: You just need to sign here.
You just press this button.

explain: 이것만 하면 충분하다는 뜻이에요. 방법을 쉽게 알려 줄 때 자주 써요.

phrases.en: You just need to do this.
phrases.nuance_ko: 친한 사이에 반말로 쉽게 알려 줄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The casual form for explaining something simply to friends.

phrases.nuance_ko: 방법이 맞는지 확인할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to check that a method is correct.

phrases.nuance_ko: 어떻게 하면 좋은지 공손하게 물어볼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite way to ask what you should do.

explain_en: Means that doing just this is enough. It is often used to explain something simply.

examples.en: You don't have to call today.
You don't have to go now.

explain: '-지 않아도 되다'와 같은 뜻이고 말할 때 더 자주 써요. '안'은 동사 바로 앞에 와요.

phrases.en: Is it okay if I don't come tomorrow?
phrases.nuance_ko: 안 해도 되는지 물어볼 때 말로 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used in speech to ask whether you can skip something.
phrases.en_equiv: is it okay if I don't...?

phrases.en: You don't have to buy it today.
phrases.nuance_ko: '돼요'보다 부드럽게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Sounds softer than 돼요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 친한 사이에 반말로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The casual form for close friends.

explain_en: Same meaning as -지 않아도 되다, but more common in speech. 안 goes right before the verb.

examples.en: I can read Korean.
Can we meet tomorrow?

explain: 능력이나 가능성을 말해요. 반대는 '-(으)ㄹ 수 없다'예요.

phrases.nuance_ko: '-(으)ㄹ 수 있다'의 반대로, 할 수 없을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of -(으)ㄹ 수 있다, used when you cannot do something.

phrases.nuance_ko: 친한 사이에 반말로 물어볼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A casual question for close friends.

phrases.en: I was able to get up early yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지난 일을 할 수 있었다고 말할 때 과거형으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Past form for saying you were able to do something.

explain_en: Expresses ability or possibility. The opposite is -(으)ㄹ 수 없다.

examples.en: You must not smoke here.
You must not sleep during class.

explain: 그렇게 하면 안 된다는 금지를 나타내요. 규칙이나 주의를 말할 때 써요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 친한 사이나 아이에게 반말로 말릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The casual form for friends or children.

phrases.en: You must not take photos here.
phrases.nuance_ko: 안내문이나 방송처럼 격식 있게 금지할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A formal prohibition, like on signs or announcements.

phrases.en: You must not be late tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 약속이나 시험처럼 중요한 날에 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used for important days like appointments or exams.

explain_en: Expresses a prohibition: you must not do it. Used for rules and warnings.

en: because it is; since it is

examples.en: It's Saturday, so I don't work.
I'm a student, so I have a lot of time.

explain: 명사 뒤에 붙어서 '~이라서'와 같은 이유를 말해요. 받침이 있으면 '이어서', 없으면 '여서'를 써요.

phrases.en: Because today is a holiday, there are many people.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-이어서/여서'와 뜻이 같고, 말할 때 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as -이어서/여서, but used more often in speech.

phrases.en: Because I'm a student, I get a discount.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이유를 조금 더 분명하게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to state the reason a bit more clearly.

phrases.en: Tomorrow is Sunday, so let's watch a movie together.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이유를 말하고 뒤에 제안이나 부탁을 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a suggestion or request follows the reason.

explain_en: Attach to a noun to give a reason, like ~이라서. Use 이어서 after a final consonant and 여서 after a vowel.

examples.en: I eat a meal.
I study with a friend.

explain: 일상에서 부드럽고 공손하게 말할 때 쓰는 종결어미예요. 어간 모음에 따라 '-아요/어요'를 쓰고, '하다'는 '해요'가 돼요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 이미 지난 일을 공손하게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Politely talks about something already past.

phrases.nuance_ko: 끝을 올려서 말하면 공손한 질문이 돼요.
phrases.nuance_en: Raise your tone at the end to make a polite question.

phrases.nuance_ko: '요'를 빼면 친한 사이에 쓰는 반말이 돼요.
phrases.nuance_en: Dropping 요 makes it casual speech for close friends.

explain_en: The standard polite sentence ending for everyday speech. Choose -아요 or -어요 by the stem vowel; 하다 becomes 해요.

examples.en: The chick goes cheep-cheep.
The baby bird makes a peeping sound.

explain: 병아리가 우는 소리예요. 보통 '삐약삐약'처럼 두 번 겹쳐서 말해요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 소리를 나타내는 말 뒤에 '하고'를 붙여서 그런 소리를 낸다고 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add 하고 after a sound word to say that something makes that sound.

phrases.en: I can hear a cheep-cheep sound.
phrases.nuance_ko: 두 번 겹쳐서 소리가 계속 나는 느낌을 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: Doubling gives a feeling of continuous sound.

phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 마리가 계속 울 때 '삐약삐약'을 '울다' 앞에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put 삐약삐약 before 울다 when chicks keep cheeping.

explain_en: The sound a chick makes. It is usually doubled: 삐약삐약.

examples.en: The cow goes moo.

examples.ko: 아이가 음메 하고 소 흉내를 내요.
examples.en: The child imitates a cow, saying moo.

explain: 소가 우는 소리예요. 한국어에서는 소가 '음메' 하고 울어요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 두 번 겹쳐서 소가 계속 우는 느낌을 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: Doubling suggests the cow keeps mooing.

phrases.en: I can hear a moo from far away.
phrases.nuance_ko: 소리가 들린다고 말할 때 '소리'를 붙여서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add 소리 to say you hear the sound.

explain_en: The sound a cow makes. In Korean, a cow says 음메.

examples.en: I go to the movie theater with a friend.
I buy bread and milk.

explain: '함께'나 '그리고'의 뜻이에요. 받침이 있으면 '이랑', 없으면 '랑'을 붙이고, 말할 때 많이 써요.

phrases.en: I study together with my younger sibling.
phrases.nuance_ko: '함께'라는 뜻을 더 분명하게 할 때 '같이'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add 같이 to make the meaning of 'together' clearer.

phrases.nuance_ko: 물건을 하나씩 이어서 말할 때 둘 다 뒤에 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Attach it to each item when listing things.

phrases.en: I watch a movie with a friend.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-(이)랑'과 뜻이 같아요. '-(이)랑'은 주로 말할 때, '-하고'는 말과 글에 두루 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as -(이)랑. -(이)랑 is mostly spoken, while -하고 works in both speech and writing.

explain_en: Means 'with' or 'and.' Use 이랑 after a final consonant and 랑 after a vowel. Common in spoken Korean.

examples.en: I'm going to get my hair done at the salon tomorrow.
Did you get your hair done? It looks really pretty.

explain: 미용실에서 머리를 자르거나 파마, 염색을 하는 것을 두루 말해요. 머리를 감는 것은 '머리를 감다'라고 해요.
explain_en: Means getting your hair cut, permed, or dyed, usually at a salon. Washing your hair is a different phrase: 머리를 감다.

examples.en: The pizza dough is chewy.
Please roll the dough out thin.

explain: 피자나 빵을 만드는 밀가루 반죽이에요. '반죽'이라는 한국어 낱말도 같이 써요.
explain_en: The flour mixture used for pizza or bread. Korean also uses the native word 반죽.

en: to feel bad; to be offended

examples.en: I feel bad because my friend forgot our plan.

examples.ko: 그 말을 들었을 때 기분이 나빴어요.
examples.en: I felt offended when I heard that.

explain: 누가 한 말이나 행동 때문에 마음이 상하고 불쾌할 때 써요. '기분이 나쁘다'처럼 '이'를 넣어도 되고, 말할 때는 줄여서 '기분 나쁘다'라고 많이 해요.

phrases.en: Please don't take it the wrong way.
phrases.en_equiv: Please don't take it the wrong way.

explain_en: Used when someone's words or actions upset or offend you. You can say 기분이 나쁘다 with 이, but in speech it's often shortened to 기분 나쁘다.

examples.en: It's okay, it's no big deal.
We fought over something trivial.

explain: '별거'는 '별것'의 입말이에요. 대수롭지 않은 일이라고 말하거나, 선물을 줄 때 겸손하게 말할 때도 써요.

phrases.en: It's not much, but please accept it.
phrases.en_equiv: It's not much, but please accept it.

explain_en: 별거 is the spoken form of 별것. Use it to say something is not a big deal, or to downplay a gift you give.

en: to be obnoxious; to be unlucky

examples.ko: 그 사람은 말투가 정말 재수 없어요.
examples.en: That person's way of talking is really obnoxious.

examples.ko: 오늘은 재수 없는 일이 계속 생겨요.
examples.en: Unlucky things keep happening today.

explain: 운이 나쁘다는 뜻도 있지만, 사람에게 쓰면 얄밉고 기분 나쁘다는 뜻이에요. 꽤 거친 말이라서 조심해서 써요.
explain_en: It can mean 'unlucky,' but said about a person it means obnoxious or off-putting. It is a harsh thing to say about someone.

en: to be thoughtful; to be considerate

examples.ko: 그 사람은 늘 다른 사람을 먼저 생각해요. 정말 사려 깊어요.
examples.en: That person always thinks of others first. They are really thoughtful.
Thank you for the thoughtful gift.

explain: 다른 사람의 입장을 깊이 생각하고 배려하는 사람을 말해요. '사려가 깊다'처럼 조사를 넣어서도 써요.
explain_en: Describes a person who thinks deeply about others' feelings and situations. You can also say 사려가 깊다 with a particle.

examples.ko: 우리 회사는 신입 사원이 순환 근무를 해요.
examples.en: At our company, new employees rotate through different departments.

examples.ko: 인턴은 3개월마다 부서를 바꾸는 순환 근무를 해요.
examples.en: Interns rotate departments every three months.

explain: 직원이 여러 부서나 지역을 순서대로 돌아가며 일하는 것이에요. '순환 근무를 하다', '순환 근무제'처럼 써요.
explain_en: Employees take turns working in several departments or locations. Common forms are '순환 근무를 하다' and '순환 근무제'.

examples.en: It has been seven days since the baby was born.
I traveled for eight days.

explain: 날수를 세는 옛 고유어예요. 이레(7일), 여드레(8일), 아흐레(9일)가 이어져요. 요즘은 '7일'을 더 많이 써요.
explain_en: A native Korean word for counting days. 이레 is 7 days, 여드레 is 8, and 아흐레 is 9. In daily speech, '7일' is more common.

examples.en: I went on a two-day, one-night trip to Busan with friends.
I went to Jeju Island for two days and one night.

explain: 하룻밤 자고 이틀 동안 하는 여행이에요. 영어와 달리 '박'(밤)이 먼저 나와요. 읽을 때는 '일 박 이 일'이라고 해요.
explain_en: A trip of two days with one overnight stay. Unlike English, the nights come first. It is read 'il bak i il'.

examples.en: I got a bonus on top of my salary.

examples.ko: 이 가격에 플러스 알파가 붙을 수 있어요.
examples.en: Something extra might be added to this price.

explain: 기본에 더해지는 조금의 추가분을 말해요. 정확한 양은 말하지 않고 '그 이상 조금 더'라는 느낌으로 써요. '+α'로도 써요.
explain_en: A small extra amount added on top of the basic one. It doesn't give an exact amount; it means 'and a bit more'. It can also be written '+α'.

examples.en: The teacher is coming to the classroom.
My father is reading the newspaper.

explain: 동사나 형용사 어간에 붙여서 행동하는 사람을 높여요. 받침이 없으면 -시-, 있으면 -으시-를 쓰고, 오시다·가시다·하시다처럼 써요.

phrases.en: Please eat a lot. (드시다 = honorific of 먹다)
phrases.en_equiv: Please eat a lot. (드시다 = honorific of 먹다)

explain_en: Attach it to a verb or adjective stem to show respect for the person doing the action. Use -시- after a vowel and -으시- after a consonant, as in 오시다, 가시다, 하시다.

examples.en: Today is Friday, right?
This person is the new teacher, right?

explain: 이미 아는 것을 확인하거나 동의를 구할 때 써요. 명사 뒤에는 -이지, 받침이 없으면 -지로 쓰고, 높이면 -(이)지요를 써요.

phrases.nuance_ko: '-(이)지요'를 줄인 말로, 말할 때 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A shortened -(이)지요, very common in speech.

phrases.nuance_ko: 친한 사이에 반말로 확인할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with close friends to confirm something.

phrases.en: The weather is nice, isn't it?
phrases.nuance_ko: 형용사나 동사 뒤에 붙여서 동의를 구할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Attached to adjectives or verbs to ask for agreement.

explain_en: Used to check something you already know or to ask for agreement, like 'right?'. After a noun use -이지 (-지 if no final consonant); the polite form is -(이)지요.

en: to be worried that something might happen

examples.en: I'm worried that it might rain.
I'm worried that I might fail the exam.

explain: 아직 일어나지 않은 나쁜 일이 생길까 걱정될 때 써요. 동사나 형용사 어간에 -(으)ㄹ까 봐를 붙이고 뒤에 걱정이 되다를 이어요.

phrases.en: I took a taxi because I was afraid of being late.
phrases.en_equiv: I took a taxi because I was afraid of being late.

explain_en: Used when you worry that something bad might happen. Add -(으)ㄹ까 봐 to a verb or adjective stem, then follow with 걱정이 되다.

examples.en: The child sleeps hugging a stuffed animal.
There are a lot of plush toys in the room.

explain: 천으로 만들고 안에 솜을 넣은 인형이에요. 보통 붙여서 '봉제인형'이라고 써요.

phrases.en: The teddy bear plush is cute.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 동물인지 앞에 붙여서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put the animal in front to say what kind it is.

phrases.en: I bought a big plush toy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 크기를 말하는 말을 앞에 붙여서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put a size word in front of it.

phrases.en: I gave my friend a plush toy for their birthday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 봉제인형은 선물로 자주 주고받아요.
phrases.nuance_en: Plush toys are often given as gifts.
phrases.en_equiv: give a plush toy as a gift

explain_en: A toy made of fabric and filled with soft stuffing. It is usually written as one word, 봉제인형.

examples.en: I think this food is delicious.
I think that person is a teacher.

explain: 내 생각을 말할 때 써요. 형용사에는 '-다고', 동사에는 '-ㄴ/는다고', 명사에는 '-(이)라고'를 붙여요.
explain_en: Used to state your opinion. Attach '-다고' to adjectives, '-ㄴ/는다고' to verbs, and '-(이)라고' to nouns.

examples.en: I like reading books.
My younger sibling likes singing.

explain: 하는 일을 좋아한다고 말할 때 써요. 동사 뒤에 '-는 것을'을 붙이고, 말할 때는 '-는 걸'로 줄여요.
explain_en: Used to say you like doing an activity. Add '-는 것을' to a verb; in speech it is shortened to '-는 걸'.

examples.en: It might rain tomorrow.
This book could be difficult.

explain: 그럴 가능성도 있다는 뜻이에요. '-(으)ㄹ 수 있다'에 '도'가 붙어서 '다른 경우도 있다'는 느낌이 있어요.

phrases.example: 어쩌면 오늘 늦게 끝날 수도 있어요.
phrases.nuance_ko: '어쩌면'을 앞에 붙이면 '혹시 그럴지도 모른다'는 느낌이 더 분명해져요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '어쩌면' (maybe) at the front makes the sense of 'perhaps so' clearer.

phrases.example: 그럴 수도 있어요, 저도 가끔 잊어요.
phrases.en: That could happen. I forget sometimes too.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대방의 말에 '그런 경우도 있다'고 부드럽게 대답할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to gently reply to someone, meaning 'that can happen too'.

phrases.example: 눈이 올 수도 있지만 저는 갈 거예요.
phrases.en: It might snow, but I'm going.
phrases.nuance_ko: '가능성은 있지만 그래도'라고 뒤에 다른 말을 이을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to say 'it's possible, but...' and then continue with a contrasting statement.

explain_en: Says something is also a possibility. It adds '도' (also) to '-(으)ㄹ 수 있다', suggesting other outcomes are possible too.

examples.ko: 저는 김치를 만들어 본 적이 없어요.
examples.en: I have never made kimchi.
I have never been to Jeju Island.

explain: 그 일을 해 본 경험이 없을 때 써요. 경험이 있으면 '-아/어 본 적이 있다'를 써요.
explain_en: Used when you have no experience of doing something. For the opposite, use '-아/어 본 적이 있다'.

examples.en: I'll go even if it rains.
I do my homework even when I'm tired.

explain: 앞의 일이 있어도 뒤의 일은 달라지지 않을 때 써요. '있다'는 '있어도', '가다'는 '가도'가 돼요.
explain_en: Used when the second clause holds regardless of the first. 있다 becomes 있어도 and 가다 becomes 가도.

en: to get annoyed; to be irritated

examples.ko: 일이 잘 안 돼서 짜증 나요.
examples.en: I'm annoyed because things aren't working out.
My younger sibling annoyed me.

explain: 일이나 사람 때문에 기분이 나빠질 때 써요. '짜증이 나다'로도 쓰고, 다른 사람에게 화를 내면 '짜증을 내다'예요.

phrases.en: There are a lot of annoying things.
phrases.en_equiv: There are a lot of annoying things.

explain_en: Used when something or someone puts you in a bad mood. Also said '짜증이 나다'; showing irritation to others is '짜증을 내다'.

en: to be glad that one can ...

examples.ko: 바다를 직접 볼 수 있어서 좋아요.
examples.en: I'm glad I can see the sea in person.

examples.ko: 가족을 자주 만날 수 있어서 좋아요.
examples.en: I'm glad I can see my family often.

explain: 할 수 있어서 기분이 좋을 때 써요. 동사 어간에 붙여요. 받침이 있으면 '-을 수 있어서', 없으면 '-ㄹ 수 있어서'를 써요.

phrases.en: I'm happy that I can meet my friend.
phrases.nuance_ko: '좋다' 대신 '기쁘다'를 쓰면 기분이 더 크게 느껴져요.
phrases.nuance_en: Using '기쁘다' (happy) instead of '좋다' makes the feeling sound stronger.
phrases.en_equiv: to be happy that one can ...

phrases.en: I was glad that I could travel together.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이미 지난 일을 돌아보며 말할 때 과거형으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use the past form when looking back on something that already happened.

phrases.example: 한국어로 말할 수 있게 되어서 좋아요.
phrases.en: I'm glad that I've become able to speak in Korean.
phrases.nuance_ko: 전에는 못 했는데 이제 할 수 있게 되어서 좋을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when you couldn't do something before but are happy that you can now.
phrases.en_equiv: glad to have become able to ...

explain_en: Use it to say you are glad you are able to do something. It attaches to a verb stem: -을 수 있어서 after a consonant, -ㄹ 수 있어서 after a vowel.

en: superficial understanding; only skimming the surface

examples.en: I studied for the exam only superficially.

examples.ko: 수박 겉핥기식으로 읽지 말고 천천히 읽으세요.
examples.en: Don't just skim it; read it slowly.

explain: 수박은 껍질만 핥으면 맛을 알 수 없어요. 내용을 깊이 알려고 하지 않고 겉만 대충 보는 것을 말해요.
explain_en: Licking only the rind of a watermelon never gives you the taste. It describes looking at or learning something only on the surface.

en: to have no choice but to ...

examples.ko: 비가 많이 와서 집에 있을 수밖에 없어요.
examples.en: It's raining a lot, so I have no choice but to stay home.
The roads were jammed, so being late was unavoidable.

explain: '수'는 방법이라는 뜻이에요. 다른 방법이 없어서 그렇게 할 때, 또는 당연히 그런 결과가 될 때 써요.

phrases.example: 차가 고장 나서 어쩔 수 없이 택시를 탔어요.
phrases.en: My car broke down, so I had no choice but to take a taxi.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-(으)ㄹ 수밖에 없다'와 비슷하고, 동사 앞에 붙여서 '다른 방법이 없어서'라는 뜻을 더해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to '-(으)ㄹ 수밖에 없다'; put it before a verb to mean 'because there was no other way'.

phrases.en: I had no money, so I had no choice but to walk.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이미 지난 일에서 다른 방법이 없었다고 말할 때 과거형으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use the past form to say that in a past situation there was no other way.

phrases.example: 그 상황에서는 누구나 그럴 수밖에 없어요.
phrases.en: In that situation, anyone would have no choice but to do the same.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞에서 말한 상황에서는 그렇게 될 수밖에 없다고 짧게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A short phrase meaning that, given the situation just mentioned, it can't be any other way.

explain_en: 수 means 'way' or 'method', so this means 'there is no other way'. Use it when something is the only option or the natural result.

en: over; about; regarding (a topic of debate)

examples.en: Opinions are divided over this issue.
I talked with my friend about where to travel.

explain: 어떤 일을 이야기나 논쟁의 대상으로 놓을 때 써요. 뒤에는 '다투다', '의견이 갈리다', '고민하다' 같은 말이 자주 와요.

phrases.en: We talked about this problem at the meeting.
phrases.nuance_ko: 'N을/를 두고'와 뜻이 거의 같고, 말할 때 더 자주 들려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Almost the same meaning as 'N을/를 두고', and heard a bit more often in speech.

phrases.example: 저는 두 회사를 두고 고민하고 있어요.
phrases.nuance_ko: 둘 중에서 무엇을 고를지 오래 생각할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used when you think for a long time about which one to choose.

phrases.en: The brothers are fighting over the room.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 일 때문에 서로 싸울 때 '다투다'와 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Pair it with '다투다' when people quarrel with each other about something.

explain_en: Puts something on the table as the topic of discussion or dispute. It is often followed by verbs like 다투다 or 고민하다.

examples.ko: 비싸다고 해서 다 좋은 것은 아니에요.
examples.en: Just because something is expensive doesn't mean it's all good.

examples.ko: 공부를 오래 한다고 해서 성적이 오르는 것은 아니에요.
examples.en: Studying for a long time doesn't necessarily raise your grades.

explain: 앞의 일이 사실이어도 뒤의 결과가 꼭 그렇지는 않다고 말할 때 써요. 동사는 '-ㄴ/는다고 해서', 형용사는 '-다고 해서'로 써요.

phrases.example: 돈이 많다고 해서 꼭 행복한 것은 아니에요.
phrases.en: Just because you have a lot of money doesn't necessarily mean you're happy.
phrases.nuance_ko: '꼭'을 넣으면 '항상 그런 것은 아니다'는 뜻이 더 분명해져요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '꼭' makes the meaning 'not necessarily always' clearer.

phrases.en: Just because it's famous doesn't mean it's tasty.
phrases.nuance_ko: '것은'을 '건'으로 줄인 말로, 일상 대화에서 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: '것은' shortened to '건'; more common in everyday conversation.

phrases.example: 화가 난다고 해서 소리를 지를 수는 없어요.
phrases.en: Just because you're angry, you can't shout.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞의 이유가 있어도 뒤의 행동은 할 수 없다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to say that even with the reason given, you still can't do the following action.

explain_en: Says that even if the first part is true, the conclusion doesn't automatically follow. Verbs take -ㄴ/는다고 해서; adjectives take -다고 해서.

examples.en: I'm studying Korean now.
My friend is reading a book.

explain: 지금 하는 중인 일을 말할 때 써요. '한국어를 공부해요'는 습관이나 일반적인 일, '공부하고 있어요'는 지금 하는 중이라는 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: I was sleeping at this time yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과거의 어느 때에 하는 중이었던 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it for something that was in progress at a certain time in the past.

phrases.en: The teacher is reading a book.
phrases.nuance_ko: 높여야 하는 사람이 지금 하는 중일 때 '있어요' 대신 '계세요'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '계세요' instead of '있어요' when the person doing it deserves respect.

phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 하는 중이 아니라고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to say that you are not doing something right now.

explain_en: Describes an action in progress right now. '공부해요' can be a habit, while '공부하고 있어요' means you are doing it at this moment.

en: to stay still; to keep quiet; to do nothing

examples.en: Don't move; stay still.
I get sleepy when I'm just sitting still.

explain: 움직이지 않거나 아무 말·행동도 하지 않을 때 써요. '가만히 있어'처럼 명령으로도 많이 써요.

phrases.en: The child is sitting still on the chair.
phrases.nuance_ko: '앉다'와 함께 써서 움직이지 않고 앉아 있는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with '앉다' to describe sitting without moving.

phrases.example: 가만히 있으면 안 돼요. 같이 도와요.
phrases.en: You can't just stay still. Let's help together.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아무것도 하지 않고 있으면 안 된다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to say that you shouldn't just do nothing.

phrases.example: 친구가 화를 내서 저는 가만히 있었어요.
phrases.en: My friend got angry, so I stayed quiet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이미 지난 일에서 말이나 행동을 하지 않았다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use the past form to say you didn't say or do anything in a past situation.

explain_en: Means to stay still or to say and do nothing. It is also very common as a command, like '가만히 있어'.

examples.en: I want to eat a balanced meal.

examples.ko: 이 의자는 균형이 잘 잡혀 있어요.
examples.en: This chair is well balanced.

explain: 몸, 식사, 생활처럼 한쪽으로 치우치지 않고 알맞은 상태를 말해요. '균형 잡힌 + 명사' 모양으로 많이 써요.
explain_en: Describes a diet, body or lifestyle that is not lopsided. It is often used in the modifier form 균형 잡힌 + noun.

en: to adopt or buy (a pet) from a breeder; to buy a newly built housing unit

examples.en: I got a cat from a breeder.
I want to buy a new apartment from the developer.

explain: 반려동물을 키우던 사람이나 가게에서 데려올 때 써요. 새로 지은 집을 건설사에서 살 때도 써요.
explain_en: Used when you take in a pet from a breeder or shop. It is also used for buying a newly built home from the developer.

en: I wish ...; it would be nice if ...

examples.en: I wish it would rain this weekend.
I wish the room were bigger.

explain: 앞으로 그렇게 되기를 바랄 때 써요. 받침이 없으면 '-면', 있으면 '-으면'을 붙여요.
explain_en: Expresses a hope for something to happen. Attach -면 after a vowel and -으면 after a consonant.

examples.en: Legally, this is a gray area.

examples.ko: 옳고 그름을 나누기 어려운 회색 지대가 많아요.
examples.en: There are many gray areas where right and wrong are hard to separate.

explain: 옳은지 틀린지 분명하게 말하기 어려운 부분을 뜻해요. 법이나 규칙 이야기에서 자주 써요.

phrases.en: to be in a gray area
phrases.en_equiv: to be in a gray area

explain_en: It refers to something that is hard to call clearly right or wrong. It often comes up when talking about laws and rules.

en: to think that ...; to assume that ...

examples.en: I thought it was raining.

examples.ko: 그 가게가 문을 닫은 줄 알았어요.
examples.en: I thought that store had closed.

explain: 어떤 일을 그렇다고 생각했다는 뜻이에요. 보통 '알았어요'로 써서 '생각과 달랐다'는 느낌을 줘요. 동사는 현재 -는, 과거 -(으)ㄴ, 형용사는 -(으)ㄴ을 붙여요.
explain_en: It means you thought something was the case, usually with 알았어요 and often implying it turned out to be wrong. Use -는 for present verbs, -(으)ㄴ for past verbs and for adjectives.

examples.en: I don't know how to swim.
I don't know how to drive, so I take the bus.

explain: 어떤 일을 하는 방법을 모른다는 뜻이에요. 할 수 있는지 없는지가 아니라 방법을 아는지가 중요해요. 반대는 '-(으)ㄹ 줄 알다'예요.

phrases.en: I know how to write in Korean.
phrases.en_equiv: I know how to write in Korean.

explain_en: It means you don't know how to do something. The focus is on knowing the method, not on ability in general. The opposite is -(으)ㄹ 줄 알다.

examples.ko: 저는 제주도에 가 본 적이 없어요.
examples.en: I have never been to Jeju.
I have never seen that movie.

explain: 지금까지 그 경험이 한 번도 없다는 뜻이에요. 동사 어간에 -(으)ㄴ을 붙이고 '적이 없어요'를 써요. 반대는 '-(으)ㄴ 적이 있다'예요.
explain_en: It means you have never had that experience. Attach -(으)ㄴ to the verb stem and add 적이 없어요. The opposite is -(으)ㄴ 적이 있다.

en: to stand in line; to queue

examples.en: We stand in line in front of the restaurant.
I lined up to get on the bus.

explain: '줄을 서다'에서 '을'을 빼고 '줄 서다'로도 많이 말해요. 기다리는 사람들이 한 줄로 서는 것이에요.
explain_en: People often drop 을 and just say 줄 서다 instead of 줄을 서다. It means people wait one behind another in a line.

examples.en: Every time it rains, I buy an umbrella.
Whenever I hear that song, I think of it.

explain: 같은 일이 그때마다 반복된다고 말해요. 받침이 있으면 '-을 때마다', 없으면 '-ㄹ 때마다'를 써요.

phrases.example: 한국에 갈 때마다 꼭 김밥을 먹어요.
phrases.en: Whenever I go to Korea, I always eat gimbap.
phrases.nuance_ko: '꼭'을 넣으면 그때마다 반드시 한다는 느낌이 더 강해져요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '꼭' makes it feel stronger that you definitely do it each time.

phrases.en: When it rains, I always drink coffee.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-(으)ㄹ 때마다'와 비슷하게 같은 일이 반복될 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to '-(으)ㄹ 때마다'; used when the same thing happens again and again.

phrases.example: 친구를 만났을 때마다 같이 밥을 먹었어요.
phrases.en: Every time I met my friend, we ate together.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지난 일이 반복되었다고 말할 때 과거형으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use the past form to say something happened repeatedly in the past.

explain_en: Shows something happens every time the first action or situation occurs.

examples.en: It rained while I was sleeping.
I read a book while waiting for my friend.

explain: 한 행동이 계속되는 시간 안에 다른 일이 일어난다고 말해요. 명사에는 '방학 동안'처럼 '동안'만 붙여요.
explain_en: Describes something happening during the time another action continues. With nouns, use just 동안.

examples.en: I wanted to travel, but I had no time.
I wanted to see a movie, but there were no tickets.

explain: 하고 싶었던 일을 말하고, 뒤에 잘 안 된 이유나 다른 결과를 이어요. '-고 싶었다'에 '-는데'가 붙은 말이에요.

phrases.en: I wanted to rest, but I had a lot of work.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-는데'보다 '하지만'이라는 뜻이 더 분명해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The 'but' meaning is clearer than with '-는데'.

phrases.en: I want to drink coffee, so shall we go together?
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 하고 싶은 마음을 말하고 뒤에 질문이나 부탁을 이을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to state what you want now and then continue with a question or request.

phrases.en: When I was young, I wanted to become a singer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 예전에 하고 싶었던 마음만 말하고 문장을 끝낼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to simply say what you wanted in the past, ending the sentence there.

explain_en: States what you wanted to do, then follows with why it didn't happen or what happened instead.

examples.ko: 새 정책을 두고 사람들의 의견이 갈려요.
examples.en: People are divided over the new policy.

examples.ko: 두 사람이 여행 장소를 두고 다퉜어요.
examples.en: The two argued over where to travel.

explain: 의견이 갈리거나 논쟁이 되는 주제를 말할 때 써요. 뒤에 '다투다, 논쟁하다, 고민하다' 같은 말이 자주 와요.

phrases.en: The students talked about the exam date.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-을/를 두고'와 뜻이 거의 같고, 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Almost the same meaning as '-을/를 두고', and often used in speech.

phrases.en: People are arguing about this issue.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서로 다른 생각으로 크게 이야기할 때 '논쟁하다'와 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Pair it with '논쟁하다' when people debate strongly with different opinions.

phrases.en: Opinions were divided over the new rule.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람들의 생각이 하나가 아니고 갈릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when people's opinions are split rather than united.

explain_en: Marks the topic of a debate or disagreement. It is often followed by verbs like 다투다, 논쟁하다, or 고민하다.

examples.en: My hobby is movies.
My hobby is exercising.

explain: 자기소개에서 취미를 말할 때 써요. '~' 자리에 명사를 넣고, 받침이 있으면 '이에요', 없으면 '예요'를 써요.

phrases.nuance_ko: '제 취미는 ~예요'라고 대답하게 하는 질문이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the question that you answer with '제 취미는 ~예요'.

phrases.nuance_ko: '도'를 넣으면 상대방과 취미가 같다는 뜻이 돼요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '도' means your hobby is the same as the other person's.

phrases.nuance_ko: 취미 이야기를 할 때 좋아하는 것을 말하는 쉬운 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easy expression for saying what you like when talking about hobbies.

explain_en: Use it to tell your hobby when introducing yourself. Put a noun in place of ~; use 이에요 after a final consonant and 예요 after a vowel.

en: may do; it's okay to do

examples.en: May I sit here?
You may open the window.

explain: 동사 뒤에 붙여서 허락을 구하거나 줄 때 써요. 질문하면 '해도 돼요?', 대답하면 '해도 돼요'예요.

phrases.en: It's okay even if you're a little late.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-아/어도 돼요'와 비슷하게 '그래도 문제없다'는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Like '-아/어도 돼요', it means 'it's no problem even if...'.

phrases.nuance_ko: '-아/어도 돼요?'보다 조금 더 부드럽고 정중하게 허락을 구해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Asks for permission a bit more softly and politely than '-아/어도 돼요?'.
phrases.en_equiv: would it be okay if I ...?

phrases.en: You don't have to come early tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 하지 않아도 된다고, 꼭 안 해도 된다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to say you don't have to do something.

explain_en: Attach to a verb to ask for or give permission. Ask '해도 돼요?' and answer '해도 돼요'.

examples.en: I was tired, so I went to bed early.
It's raining, so I'm staying home.

explain: 앞 내용이 뒤 내용의 이유일 때 써요. '-아서/어서' 뒤에는 '-(으)세요', '-(으)ㅂ시다'를 쓸 수 없어요. '하다'는 '해서'가 돼요.

phrases.en: It's raining. So I'm taking an umbrella.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞 문장과 뒤 문장을 따로 말하며 '그러므로'라는 뜻으로 이어 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: Links two separate sentences, meaning 'therefore'.

phrases.en: I was sick, so I couldn't go to school.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이유 때문에 할 수 없었다고 말할 때 '못'과 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use with '못' to say you couldn't do something because of a reason.

phrases.nuance_ko: 고마운 이유를 말할 때 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for stating the reason you are thankful.

explain_en: Gives the reason for what follows. It cannot be followed by commands or suggestions. '하다' becomes '해서'.

examples.en: I'm learning Korean these days.
I'm late because of traffic.

explain: 이유나 사정을 설명하거나 확인할 때 써요. '-는 것이에요'를 줄인 말이에요.

phrases.en: You're taking the exam tomorrow, right?
phrases.nuance_ko: 알고 있는 내용이 맞는지 확인할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to check that what you understand is correct.

phrases.example: 요즘 너무 바빠서 못 쉬는 거 아니에요?
phrases.en: Isn't it that you're too busy these days to rest?
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대방의 사정을 짐작하며 부드럽게 물을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to gently ask while guessing at someone's situation.

phrases.en: The thing is, I'm going home now.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-는 거예요'의 원래 형태로, 조금 더 단정한 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The full form of '-는 거예요', sounding a little more formal.

explain_en: Used to explain a reason or situation, or to confirm something. It is a contraction of '-는 것이에요'.

examples.en: May I try this on?
May I try this food?

explain: '-아/어 보다'와 '-아/어도 되다'가 합쳐진 말이에요. 옷이나 물건을 써 봐도 되는지 물을 때 써요.

phrases.en: May I try on these shoes?
phrases.nuance_ko: '-아/어 봐도 돼요?'보다 조금 더 정중하게 물어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Asks a little more politely than '-아/어 봐도 돼요?'.

phrases.en: Is it okay if I listen to this music?
phrases.nuance_ko: '돼요' 대신 '괜찮아요'를 써서 부드럽게 물어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses '괜찮아요' instead of '돼요' for a softer question.
phrases.en_equiv: is it okay if I try ...?

phrases.en: May I try using this laptop?
phrases.nuance_ko: 가게나 공식적인 자리에서 격식 있게 물을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to ask formally, such as in a shop or an official setting.

explain_en: Combines '-아/어 보다' and '-아/어도 되다'. Use it to ask if you may try something out, like clothes.

en: if you want to; if you intend to

examples.en: To get to City Hall, take the subway.
If you want to lose weight, you have to exercise.

explain: '~하고 싶으면, ~하려고 하면'이라는 뜻이에요. 뒤에는 필요한 방법이나 조건이 와요.

phrases.en: If you want to be good at Korean, practice every day.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-(으)려면'과 뜻이 비슷하고 더 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar in meaning to '-(으)려면' but easier to say.

phrases.en: What should I do to get to the airport?
phrases.nuance_ko: 목적을 이루는 방법을 물을 때 자주 쓰는 질문이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common question for asking how to achieve a goal.

phrases.en: To be good at Korean, you need practice.
phrases.nuance_ko: 목적을 이루는 데 필요한 것을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to say what is needed to achieve a goal.

explain_en: Means 'if you intend to ~'. What follows is the method or condition needed.

examples.en: I couldn't go because of the rain.
I didn't go to school because of a cold.

explain: 명사 뒤에 붙어 원인을 말해요. 보통 좋지 않은 일의 이유로 많이 써요.
explain_en: Follows a noun to give a cause. It is most often used for negative reasons.

examples.ko: 저는 아이들을 가르쳐 본 적이 있어요.
examples.en: I have taught children before.

examples.ko: 한국에서 김밥을 먹어 본 적이 있어요.
examples.en: I have eaten gimbap in Korea.

explain: 전에 해 본 경험이 있다고 말할 때 써요. '가르쳐 본 적이 있어요'는 가르친 경험이 있다는 뜻이에요.

phrases.example: 저는 제주도에 가 본 적이 없어요.
phrases.en: I have never been to Jeju Island.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그런 경험이 한 번도 없다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to say you have never had that experience.

phrases.nuance_ko: '-아/어 본 적이 있어요'보다 짧게 경험을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A shorter way to talk about experience than '-아/어 본 적이 있어요'.

phrases.en: Have you ever been to Jeju Island?
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대방의 경험을 물어볼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to ask about someone's experience.

explain_en: Says you have had an experience before. '가르쳐 본 적이 있어요' means you have taught before.

examples.en: I met my friend after three years.
I finished my homework in one hour.

explain: 어떤 일이 있고 나서 시간이 지난 뒤에 다시 일어났다고 말하거나, 걸린 시간을 말할 때 써요. '오랜만에'도 같은 말에서 왔어요. '삼 년 만에'처럼 앞말과 띄어 써요.

phrases.en: We met for the first time in a long while.
phrases.en_equiv: We met for the first time in a long while.

explain_en: Says something happened again after a stretch of time, or how long something took. '오랜만에' comes from the same word. Write it separately, as in '삼 년 만에'.

examples.en: You are the only one I trust.
I only did what I was told.

explain: 명사 뒤에는 'N뿐이다', 동사·형용사 뒤에는 '-(으)ㄹ 뿐이다'를 써요. 그것밖에 없다는 뜻이고, 조금 부족하다는 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: Attach to a noun (N뿐이다) or a verb/adjective stem (-(으)ㄹ 뿐이다) to say "only that, nothing more." It often suggests it is not enough.

en: it looks like; it seems that

examples.en: It looks like there is traffic.
My younger sibling seems to be tired.

explain: 눈에 보이는 상황을 보고 그럴 것이라고 추측할 때 써요. '-는 것 같다'보다 근거가 보이는 느낌이고, 말할 때는 조금 딱딱해요.
explain_en: Used to infer something from visible evidence. It feels a bit more formal than -는 것 같다 and suggests you are going by what you see.

en: among; out of; in the middle of

examples.en: Among fruits, I like apples the most.
A call came during the meeting.

explain: 여러 개 가운데에서 고를 때 'N 중에'를 써요. 어떤 일을 하는 도중이라는 뜻으로도 써요.

phrases.en: Which of the two do you like more?
phrases.en_equiv: Which of the two do you like more?

explain_en: Use N 중에 to pick from several options. It can also mean "in the middle of" doing something.

en: not N but; other than N; instead of N

examples.en: I'll have tea, not coffee.
Please give me that one, not this one.

explain: 앞의 명사는 빼고 다른 것을 말할 때 써요. 뒤에 '다른 거'나 새로운 선택을 말해요.
explain_en: Use it to exclude one thing and name another. What follows is the alternative you want.

examples.en: I drink coffee after eating.
I meet my friend after class.

explain: 앞의 일이 끝난 다음에 뒤의 일을 할 때 써요. 동사 뒤에는 '-(으)ㄴ 후에', 명사 뒤에는 'N 후에'를 써요.

phrases.en: I watch TV after I do my homework.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-(으)ㄴ 후에'와 뜻이 같고, 순서를 말할 때 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as '-(으)ㄴ 후에'; often used to describe order.

phrases.en: I meet my friend after class ends.
phrases.nuance_ko: '후에'와 같은 뜻으로 바꿔 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Can be swapped with '후에' with the same meaning.

phrases.en: I take a shower right after I come home.
phrases.nuance_ko: '바로'를 넣으면 곧이어 한다는 뜻이 더해져요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '바로' adds the meaning 'immediately after'.

explain_en: Use it when the second action happens after the first is finished. After a verb: -(으)ㄴ 후에; after a noun: N 후에.

en: as much as; to the extent that

examples.en: I'm as tall as my older sister.
I ate until I was full.

explain: 명사 뒤에서는 붙여 써서 '그 정도로'라는 뜻이에요. 동사·형용사 뒤에서는 '-(으)ㄹ 만큼'으로 쓰고 앞말과 띄어 써요.

phrases.en: You get as much as you put in.
phrases.en_equiv: You get as much as you put in.

explain_en: After a noun it is attached and means "as much as." After a verb or adjective use -(으)ㄹ 만큼, written with a space.

en: in the way of N; N-style

examples.en: You shouldn't do it this way.
Try greeting in the Korean way.

explain: 어떤 방법이나 방식으로 한다는 뜻이에요. '이런 식으로', '그런 식으로'처럼 자주 써요.
explain_en: Means "in the manner of N." It is common in set phrases like 이런 식으로 (this way) and 그런 식으로 (that way).

examples.en: I was late because the road was jammed.
It's because I like Korean.

explain: 앞 문장의 이유를 뒤에서 설명할 때 써요. '-기 때문에'는 이유를 앞에, '-기 때문이다'는 문장 끝에 써요.

phrases.en: I can't go because I'm busy.
phrases.en_equiv: I can't go because I'm busy.

explain_en: Used at the end of a sentence to explain the reason for what was said before. -기 때문에 puts the reason first instead.

en: to tend to be ~; to be rather ~

examples.en: I tend to get up early in the morning.
This restaurant is on the cheap side.

explain: 딱 잘라 말하기 어려울 때, 대체로 어느 쪽에 가깝다고 말해요. 동사는 -는 편이다, 형용사는 -(으)ㄴ 편이다를 써요.
explain_en: Says something falls on one side in general, without being absolute. Use -는 편이다 with verbs and -(으)ㄴ 편이다 with adjectives.

examples.en: One vanilla latte, please.
I like vanilla ice cream.

explain: 아이스크림, 라떼, 케이크 같은 음식의 맛이나 향을 말할 때 써요. 외래어라서 소리 나는 대로 써요.

phrases.en: The vanilla-flavored ice cream is tasty.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음식의 맛을 말할 때 '맛'을 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add '맛' (flavor) when talking about the taste of food.

phrases.nuance_ko: 냄새나 향기를 말할 때 '향'을 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add '향' (scent) when talking about smell or fragrance.

phrases.en: I ate a vanilla cake on my birthday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음식 이름 앞에 붙여서 어떤 맛인지 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put it before a food name to say what flavor it is.

explain_en: Used for the flavor or scent of ice cream, lattes and cakes. It is a loanword.

examples.en: I have a vocabulary test tomorrow.
I tried testing the new app.

explain: 시험이나 검사를 말해요. '테스트를 하다', '테스트를 보다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: Means a test or a check. Used as '테스트를 하다' or '테스트를 보다'.

examples.en: I'm going to a language exchange meetup on the weekend.
I talk in Korean with my language exchange partner.

explain: 서로의 언어를 가르쳐 주고 배우는 활동이에요. 보통 '언어교환 모임'이나 '언어교환 친구'로 써요.
explain_en: An activity where two people teach each other their languages. Often used as '언어교환 모임' or '언어교환 친구'.

examples.en: There is a lot of fog, so visibility is bad.

examples.ko: 키가 큰 사람 때문에 시야가 가려져요.
examples.en: A tall person is blocking my view.

explain: 눈으로 볼 수 있는 범위예요. '시야가 좋다', '시야가 넓다', '시야를 가리다'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: to have a wide field of view
phrases.en_equiv: to have a wide field of view

explain_en: The range that the eyes can see. Used as '시야가 좋다', '시야가 넓다', '시야를 가리다'.

examples.en: I bought a new electric toothbrush.
I go to school on an electric scooter.

explain: 전기의 힘으로 움직인다는 뜻이에요. 보통 다른 명사 앞에 붙어서 '전동 칫솔', '전동 휠체어'처럼 써요.
explain_en: Means powered by electricity. It usually comes before another noun, as in '전동 칫솔' or '전동 휠체어'.

examples.en: This plan is not complete yet.
I totally messed up the test.

explain: 모자란 것 없이 다 갖춘 상태예요. 대화에서는 '완전'만 부사처럼 써서 '아주, 정말'이라는 뜻으로도 많이 말해요.
explain_en: The state of being complete with nothing missing. In casual talk, 완전 alone is also used like an adverb meaning 'totally' or 'really'.

en: end of the school day; after school

examples.en: I go to the library after school.

examples.ko: 방과 후 수업이 세 시에 시작해요.
examples.en: The after-school class starts at three.

explain: 학교에서 그날 수업이 끝나는 것을 말해요. 거의 '방과 후'로 붙여서 써요.
explain_en: The end of the school day's classes. It is almost always used in the phrase '방과 후' (after school).

examples.en: Keep going north.
There are many mountains in the north of Korea.

explain: 방향 중에서 북쪽을 말해요. 보통 '북쪽', '북부'처럼 다른 말과 붙여서 써요. 두드리는 악기 '북(drum)'은 소리가 같은 다른 낱말이에요.
explain_en: The direction north. It is usually combined as '북쪽' or '북부'. The drum '북' is a different word that sounds the same.

examples.en: That player has a great physique.
My body was weak, so I started working out.

explain: 몸의 체격이나 운동 능력을 말해요. '피지컬이 좋다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: Refers to a person's build or athletic ability. Used as '피지컬이 좋다'.

examples.ko: 일주일에 한 번 피아노 레슨을 받아요.
examples.en: I take a piano lesson once a week.
The next lesson is on Friday.

explain: 악기, 운동, 언어 등을 배우는 수업이에요. '레슨을 받다', '레슨을 하다'로 써요.
explain_en: A lesson for learning an instrument, a sport or a language. Used as '레슨을 받다' or '레슨을 하다'.

examples.en: I often drink milk tea.
One taro milk tea, please.

explain: 홍차에 우유를 넣은 음료예요. 타로 밀크티, 흑당 밀크티처럼 맛 이름을 앞에 붙여요.

phrases.en: It was cold, so I drank a warm milk tea.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜨거운 음료일 때 앞에 '따뜻한'을 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put '따뜻한' (warm) in front when the drink is hot.

phrases.en: It was hot, so I ordered an iced milk tea.
phrases.nuance_ko: 차가운 음료일 때 앞에 '아이스'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put '아이스' (iced) in front when the drink is cold.

phrases.en: I make milk tea at home.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음료를 직접 만들 때 '만들다'와 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Pair with '만들다' when you make the drink yourself.

explain_en: A drink made of tea with milk. Put the flavor name before it, as in 타로 밀크티 or 흑당 밀크티.

en: medical care; medical service; medical treatment

examples.en: Korea has good medical services.
There are few medical facilities in the countryside.

explain: 병을 치료하는 일이나 그와 관련된 서비스를 말해요. '의료 서비스', '의료 시스템'처럼 다른 명사 앞에 많이 써요.
explain_en: Medical treatment and related services. Often placed before another noun, as in '의료 서비스' or '의료 시스템'.

examples.en: This building has a sprinkler system.
The new payment system is convenient.

explain: 여러 부분이 모여 움직이는 체계나 방식이에요. '교육 시스템', '결제 시스템'처럼 앞에 분야를 붙여요.

phrases.en: This restaurant's reservation system is convenient.
phrases.nuance_ko: '예약'처럼 분야 이름을 앞에 붙여서 어떤 시스템인지 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put a field name like '예약' in front to say what kind of system it is.

phrases.nuance_ko: 방식이나 체계가 새로워졌을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when a method or structure has become new.

phrases.en: It's convenient if you use this system.
phrases.nuance_ko: 프로그램이나 방식을 쓸 때 '사용하다'와 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Pair with '사용하다' when using a program or method.

explain_en: An organized setup or method made of several parts. Add the field before it, as in '교육 시스템' or '결제 시스템'.

examples.en: The soldiers do combat training.
There was a big battle in that area.

explain: 군대나 사람들이 무기를 가지고 싸우는 것이에요. '전투 훈련', '전투가 벌어지다'처럼 써요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 싸움의 결과를 말할 때 '이기다, 지다'와 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Pair with '이기다' or '지다' to talk about the result of a fight.

phrases.en: After the battle ended, the soldiers rested.
phrases.nuance_ko: 싸움이 끝났을 때 '끝나다'와 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Pair with '끝나다' when a fight is over.

phrases.en: This movie has many battle scenes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 영화나 게임에서 싸우는 장면을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it for fighting scenes in movies or games.

explain_en: Fighting with weapons between armies or groups. Used as '전투 훈련' or '전투가 벌어지다'.

examples.en: I bought a used car.
I'm going to a used car lot.

explain: 이미 다른 사람이 쓴 자동차예요. 새 차는 '신차'라고 해요.

phrases.en: Used car prices are cheaper than new cars.
phrases.nuance_ko: '신차'와 비교해서 값을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used when comparing prices with a new car ('신차').

phrases.en: I sold my used car to buy a new one.
phrases.nuance_ko: 쓰던 차를 돈을 받고 다른 사람에게 넘길 때 '팔다'와 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Pair with '팔다' when you hand over a car you used to someone else for money.

phrases.en: I'm looking into used cars these days.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사기 전에 어떤 차가 있는지 찾아볼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when you search for what cars are available before buying.

explain_en: A car that someone else has already used. A new car is called '신차'.

examples.en: The teacher showed us a demonstration first.

examples.ko: 이 서비스는 다음 달부터 시범 운영해요.
examples.en: This service will run as a trial from next month.

explain: 본보기로 먼저 해 보이는 것이에요. '시범을 보이다', '시범 운영'처럼 써요.
explain_en: Doing something first as an example or trial. Used as '시범을 보이다' or '시범 운영'.

examples.en: I looked around the inside of the building.
This material is only for internal use.

explain: 어떤 것의 안쪽이나 어떤 조직의 안을 말해요. 반대말은 '외부'예요. '내부 일정'은 회사 안에서만 아는 일정이에요.
explain_en: The inside of something or of an organization. The opposite is '외부'. '내부 일정' means a schedule only for people inside the company.

examples.en: I decided to exercise this year.
What is your New Year's resolution?

explain: 어떤 일을 꼭 하겠다고 마음을 정하는 것이에요. '결심하다', '결심을 하다'로 써요.
explain_en: Making up your mind to definitely do something. Used as '결심하다' or '결심을 하다'.
